Once Winter left, clutching the coins tightly and looking deeply moved, Helene turned her bright emerald eyes toward Ebner, her lips curling into a mischievous smile as she asked, "And what's my annual salary?"
After spending a day or so with Ebner, Helene had used her Hunter abilities to get a decent read on his personality. She realized that, most of the time, he wasn't difficult to get along with, which made her bold enough to tease him a little.
To be fair, if I handed you back to the Black Death, I'd get at least 1,000 pounds... and yet, here you are asking me for a salary?
That said, it's true that a 'personal maid' without a salary would be odd and might raise suspicions. I'll let Harvey know that her salary will come from my private funds.
With these thoughts in mind, Ebner said casually, "You don't have any expenses right now, so I'll just hold onto it for you."
After a brief verbal skirmish with his
Red Maid,
Ebner checked the clock and saw it was nearing two o'clock. Dismissing Helene, he returned to his bedroom and sealed the room with spirituality.
If everything goes as expected, 'Sun' will ask about Amon during this Tarot meeting... But I can't tell him the truth directly. He's facing Amon's avatar head-on, and the more he knows, the more dangerous it'll be... I'll have to stick to the original plotline as closely as possible.
However, not telling Sun doesn't mean I can't tell Klein. If he gets a bit of forewarning about Amon, he'll be better prepared to deal with that troublesome kid.
As for how to deliver the information, Ebner decided to forge another page of
Roselle's Diary
before the Tarot meeting.
After spending over half an hour carefully crafting the diary entry, Ebner summoned Helene again and had her transcribe it in her handwriting. Once satisfied, he committed the awkward script to memory and waited for the upcoming Tarot meeting.
...
3:00 PM sharp.
The chimes of the clock were still reverberating when
Magician
Fors, bleary-eyed from her writing marathon, was suddenly enveloped by deep crimson light and transported to the grand, ancient palace. She appeared at the side of the old bronze table.
She glanced left and right, noticing that the top seat on her side, occupied by
Justice
Audrey, was already vacant. Hastily, she stood up and followed Audrey's lead, greeting
The Fool
:
"Good afternoon, Mr. Fool~"
Afterward, Fors watched Audrey greet
The Hanged Man,
The Tower,
The World,
and
Judgment.
When Audrey reached
The Sun,
she hesitated slightly.
Even Fors could sense that the young man from the Forsaken Land seemed unusually anxious.
Did he leak information about the Tarot Club?
Fors' mind jumped to conclusions, her chest tightening. Almost simultaneously with Audrey, she asked:
"What are you worried about?"
The Sun
Derrick hesitated for a moment, then, seeing that
The Fool
did not stop him, recounted how he had successfully pretended to be sick and was sent to the bottom of the round tower for isolation and treatment. He then asked whether the mysterious item in the round tower could detect the gray fog.
Hearing this question,
Justice,
Magician,
and the others all turned to
The Fool
with tense expressions.
How would I know... I don't even know what that thing is... But so far, nothing strange or powerful has tried to invade this space. Even the Evernight Goddess and the True Creator haven't been able to find this place... It should be fine...
Klein's fingers tapped lightly on the edge of the ancient bronze table as he calmly replied:
"Normally, it shouldn't be able to detect this place.
"But certain miraculous items have unusual effects."
Hearing this definitive answer, Derrick visibly relaxed. But then he seemed to recall something the former exploration team captain had said, and he blurted out:
"Have you ever heard of someone named Amon?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 433: Amon
chapters.content:
Chapter 433 - Amon
Amon... So the storyline hasn't changed because of my arrival... The fateful confrontation between Amon and the Fool over the "Seer" pathway is truly about to begin...
Ebner sighed inwardly.
Amon!
Xio, still disguised in her noblewoman attire, narrowed her eyes. She had seen this name in the files of the
Military Intelligence 9th Division.
It was said that the
Church of Steam
had recently "stumbled upon" a tomb belonging to the Amon family and had discovered many Beyonder materials inside.
Amon?
Klein thought for a moment and quickly remembered the source of his familiarity.
The Hanged Man
had mentioned this name in a previous Tarot meeting.
Similarly,
Justice
Audrey also turned to
The Hanged Man,
thinking,
The only time I've heard this name was from Mr. Hanged Man... and that was before Mr. Tower even joined the Tarot Club.
The Magician
Fors, on the other hand, stared blankly, realizing that the conversation had once again leaped out of her range of knowledge.
The Hanged Man
Alger frowned slightly, glancing at
The Tower
and noticing that he had no intention of speaking. Alger then asked
The Sun
in confusion:
"Did your exploration team encounter someone claiming to be Amon?"
The Sun
Derrick nodded earnestly.
"Yes. Forty-two years ago, an exploration team encountered someone claiming to be Amon in the depths of the darkness. After returning to Silver City, they gradually went mad and lost control, except for one survivor who was confined at the bottom of the round tower... right next to me."
The Hanged Man
pondered briefly, carefully organizing his thoughts before explaining the status of the Amon family in the Fourth Epoch, particularly during the Tudor Dynasty. Finally, he said:"There's a rumor passed down from Nast, the King of the Five Seas, that the Amon family are blasphemers. They possess the secret of stealing the power of gods!
"Additionally, the Amon family claims to be descendants of the Ancient Sun God."
Ancient Sun God? From the name alone, it sounds like one of the authorities of the Lord...
Derrick was left bewildered, feeling as though his brain was struggling to process all the information.
Seeing Derrick fall silent,
The Hanged Man
stroked his chin and asked:
"The Amon family is an ancient lineage stretching back one or two thousand years, almost synonymous with history. I'm very curious—why did the individual you encountered appear near Silver City? What was his purpose?"
He directed this question not at Derrick, but at
The Tower.
It was clear that he believed Derrick wouldn't know the answer, but Ebner might have an unexpected insight.
The others had the same thought and all turned their eyes toward Ebner in unison. Even
The World
was a beat late in making the same motion.
Ebner hesitated for a moment before answering simply:
"I cannot judge his purpose... But one thing is certain—the Amon family possesses an Angel of the
Marauder
pathway!
"Moreover, aside from Mr. Fool, if anyone else could possibly enter the Forsaken Land, the only one I can think of is him..."
An Angel of the Marauder pathway? Could the so-called 'secret of stealing the power of gods' be a high-sequence manifestation of this pathway? Hmm, during a past Tarot meeting, Miss Justice mentioned that the Nighthawks in Backlund once had their 'thoughts' stolen by a demigod of the Marauder pathway... Perhaps, at the peak of this pathway, one could indeed steal from a god...
Klein nodded thoughtfully under the cover of the gray fog, but no one else could see it.
A Marauder pathway... Could this be the same pathway as that elusive demigod the Nighthawks still haven't caught?
Audrey recalled the story shared by Captain Glaint and almost blurted it out.
Judgment
Xio, after some thought, said:
"The Church of Steam recently completed an exploration of an Amon family tomb near White Cliff Town in the Stratford Gulf..."
The Magician
Fors's eyes lit up. She was deeply fascinated by tales of exploration and immediately asked with curiosity:
"Miss Judgment, could you tell us more about the Church of Steam's exploration?"
You're not this polite when you talk to me in private...
Xio silently complained, shaking her head.
"The 9th Division only received a summary report from the Machinery Hivemind. We know they retrieved a significant amount of materials and ultimately destroyed the tomb... but there were no specific details in the briefing."
Ebner was equally surprised by Xio's account. That tomb being excavated by the Machinery Hivemind happened over a month earlier than in the original plotline...
This must be one of the butterfly effects I've caused. Perhaps because the Dragon's Tooth Tavern, where Fanny and Emma posted their exploration commission, was requisitioned due to the Conway Baron incident, which leaked the information and accelerated the exploration.
"I see..." Fors adjusted her posture, feeling slightly disappointed. However, she made a mental note to convince Xio to check the archives at the 9th Division after the meeting.
An Angel of the Marauder pathway... But Beyonders of this pathway are exceedingly rare. Of all the people I've heard about, none seem to have abilities resembling a Marauder.
Only Mr. Fool and Amon can enter the Forsaken Land... If Mr. Fool relies on sheer power, does Amon rely on stealing the authority to 'enter' such a place?
Also, if the Machinery Hivemind sent a report to the 9th Division, they must have sent one to the Mandated Punishers as well. Perhaps I can ask someone to procure it.
While Alger contemplated these possibilities, he discreetly glanced at
The Fool
and noticed that even Amon hadn't managed to stir any visible interest from the enigmatic figure. Slightly disappointed, Alger turned back to Derrick and said:
"Speak with the former team captain next door. See if you can glean any new information."
After a brief pause, he added sternly:
"But be extremely careful and cautious. I believe that person is exceedingly dangerous."
"Dangerous? Mr. Hanged Man, you think so too?" Derrick asked in surprise.
The six-member council thought the same thing!
Alger glanced up at the towering dome above and explained patiently:
Everyone else died, yet he survived. He's been confined for forty-two years and remains lucid and rational. And he's connected to someone who might be an Angel of the Marauder pathway... Isn't that suspicious enough?
Derrick finally understood and said sincerely:
"I understand.
"Thank you, Mr. Hanged Man!"
Then, he turned to Ebner and added, "Thank you as well, Mr. Tower... Also, I'll gather the materials I promised you as soon as I'm released from the round tower."
That's going to take a while... This situation won't be resolved quickly.
Ebner thought, but outwardly, he just smiled and said,
"I'm glad I could help."
With that topic concluded, the Tarot meeting proceeded as usual. Audrey submitted three pages of
Roselle's Diary,
and when
The Fool
asked what she wanted in exchange, she opted for a private discussion.
Moments later, when the other members regained their perception, they noticed
Justice
was quickly masking the excitement and astonishment on her face. Everyone couldn't help but grow curious about what she had asked
The Fool.
Only Ebner, recalling the original story, deduced that she had likely caught a glimpse of the
Black Emperor
card and truly understood what the
Mystery of Godhood
entailed.
At the same time, Ebner had already materialized three pages of the diary. One was his earlier
fabrication
, while the other two were selected from the
entertainment entries
found in Fanny's grandfather Surrey's diary.
This is to dilute any potential suspicion Klein might have... Although, at this point, I'm not too concerned if Klein realizes I'm also a "compatriot."
But it's still better to keep it under wraps. After all, if Mr. Fool loses the ability to commit his "amusing antics" during Tarot meetings, wouldn't we lose so much joy?
On the other side, Klein noticed that
Mr. Tower
had, unsurprisingly, chosen to continue accumulating contributions. He then transferred the three pages of the diary to his side and began to read them carefully. —He had already reviewed the diary submitted by
Justice
during their private exchange.
"January 25th, on a night of a blood moon, I successfully connected with Mr. Door once again.
This time, we continued our discussion about the angelic families loyal to the Tudor Dynasty—Antigonus, Amon, Jacob, and Tamara.
But he simply laughed and told me that Jacob had long since withered, Tamara had split into two factions and was barely holding on, Antigonus was in an even worse state than he was... and Amon isn't even truly a family!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 434: Diary and Transaction
chapters.content:
Chapter 434 - Diary and Transaction
Antigonus... Is that the
"Half-Fool"
Mr. Tower mentioned before? His condition is even worse than Mr. Door's... Does that mean he's also sealed or trapped somewhere?
The Hanged Man
said that Antigonus was eradicated by the
Evernight Goddess
... So it was the Goddess who took action?
The place of sealing is probably the missing
Nation of the Evernight
on the main peak of the Hornacis Mountain Range, right?
Recalling the entanglement with the Antigonus family since his initial transmigration and the whispers of
"Hornacis... Flegrea"
he heard every time he drank a potion, Klein couldn't help but make some guesses.
But... what does the last sentence mean, "Amon was never a family"... ?
With questions still lingering in his mind, Klein lowered his gaze and continued reading the rest of the contents:
"I know Jacob has long since withered. After all these years, I've never encountered anything or anyone related to this family. If it weren't for reading about them in Fourth Epoch history, I wouldn't even know they existed. They've disappeared even more thoroughly than Amon.
But the following lines went far beyond my knowledge... So I asked Mr. Door about them.
This time, Mr. Door was surprisingly willing to talk, and he told me three things.
First, Antigonus forcibly accommodated the Uniqueness and went mad long ago. He's now trapped in eternal slumber in the
Nation of the Evernight
by the
Evernight Goddess
,
unable to even wake up. Naturally, his condition is worse than Mr. Door's.
Second, because the six gods supported the Night Emperor, the Tamara family lost the Hand of Order. After the War of the Four Emperors, one faction of the Tamara family intermarried with the declining Abraham family, gaining access to the Apprentice pathway formulas. The other faction continued to insist on the Arbiter pathway, leading to an eventual split.
Third, the reason Amon is not considered a family is that every member of the Amon family is actually a clone of Amon. As a Sequence 1 Worm of Time, Amon has devoured countless Beyonders of the Marauder pathway. The number of his clones is beyond counting... Even the downfall of the Jacob family was because of him—they also held dominion over the Marauder pathway.
I was utterly stunned. If Mr. Door isn't lying, then could there be an Amon among the people around me?
Mr. Door seemed to notice my concern and laughed, telling me that Amon is actually easy to identify because his clones usually wear a monocle over their right eye. Even animals parasitized by him would have a distinctive ring around their right eye.
Apparently, this is a habit of that ancient son of the Sun God."
The page ended there, and Klein quickly flipped to the next one, hoping to gather more information... Unfortunately, what greeted his eyes was:
"May 1st, I feel somewhat tired of Madame Flonarl. Although she hasn't changed, I no longer feel the same passion when I see her..."
Emperor, you were still "laboring" on Labor Day... Truly tireless.
Klein sighed in exasperation, quickly skimmed the subsequent paragraphs, and, seeing that they were of a similar nature, flipped to the next page.
The third page was largely the same, but one line stood out:
"August 5th, my loyal captain Isacca is about to set sail on the latest steamship to search for the Forsaken Land of the Gods. Before he departed, he entrusted his wife and daughter to my care..."
I recall seeing a previous diary entry mentioning that this ship, which sought the
Forsaken Land of the Gods
,
lost contact... That incident even inspired Roselle to invent the wireless telegraph.
And Captain Isacca... If I remember correctly, wasn't there a Miss Isacca who later helped Roselle "relive his youth" or something?
What a scoundrel.
After muttering a few complaints, Klein set aside the last two pages and flipped back to the first one. He reread it word by word, his fingers tapping rhythmically on the table as he pondered:
Antigonus was indeed sealed in the
Nation of the Evernight
by the Goddess... He went mad from failing to accommodate the Uniqueness. Is that the origin of his title, "Half-Fool"?
But the truly terrifying part is that even a near-godly being can go insane. If the Goddess hadn't intervened, would we now have another evil god?
Moreover, the Apprentice, Marauder, and Seer pathways are supposed to oppose each other... So why did they all serve the Blood Emperor Tudor?
Was there a grand conspiracy behind it? Or was it merely the aggregation of Beyonder characteristics?
Lastly, just as Sun encountered Amon, I received a diary page about Amon... This feels eerily similar to my entanglement with Antigonus and the various misfortunes tied to the Twilight Hermit Order... Is this also the result of Beyonder aggregation? The pull of adjacent pathways?
But this level of attraction hasn't been so obvious before...
Could it be that the Amon in question has a significant connection to this gray fog space? Or is it simply because he possesses far too many Beyonder characteristics, amplifying this "aggregation pull"?
He didn't suspect
Tower
directly, as Derrick's question about Amon had been spontaneous. There was no way
Tower
could have prepared in advance. Besides, the handwriting on the first diary page was clearly feminine.
Which one of Tower's female friends wrote this for him?
After pondering for a while, Klein glanced at
Sun
and decided to linger in the gray fog after the meeting to observe any further developments.
I wonder if the exploration team captain in Sun's neighboring cell wears a monocle...
With these thoughts swirling in his mind, Klein allowed the diary pages to dissipate and leaned back in his chair with a smile:
"You may proceed with your transactions."
As soon as he finished speaking,
Justice
Audrey slightly raised her hand and said without concealing her intentions:
"I'm seeking three materials: a pair of Mirror Dragon's Eyes, 50 milliliters of its blood, and the fruit of the Elder Tree."
Sun
Derrick nodded seriously:
"I'll keep an eye out. Corrupted Mirror Dragons aren't uncommon... Well, in the City of Silver, there are also lingering characteristics of
Psychoanalysts
, but they're difficult to trade for and easily arouse suspicion.
"Of course, that depends on me successfully leaving the bottom of the tower first..."
At this moment, Klein manipulated
World
to make the gloomy, hoarse voice resonate:
"I'll ask around in my circles. Also, help me search for the characteristics of a
Skin Shadow
."
As for the
Thousand-Faced Hunter
, thanks to the information provided by the
Dream Labyrinth Tower
, Klein already had a target in mind. However, his recent schedule had been overwhelmingly busy, preventing him from rescuing the vampire Emlyn just yet.
"Alright."
Justice
Audrey nodded confidently before turning toward
The Hanged Man
:
"Mr. Hanged Man, I'll also keep an eye out for the
Dragon-Eyed Sea Eagle's Eyeball
that you're looking for."
She was soon to join the
Psychological Alchemy Society
, and with such a secretive organization supporting her, access to rare materials might become far less of an issue—as long as she was willing to pay the price.
World
chuckled lowly:
"Make sure you stay safe..."
Then, he turned his attention to
Judgement
:
"I've already obtained the
Golden Wings of the Gondola
. I'll deliver them to you after the gathering ends."
In truth, Sharon had already delivered the material at noon, but Klein hadn't handed it over immediately. He planned to settle everything after the Tarot Meeting.
"Alright."
Judgement
Xio sighed in relief. Although she trusted
The Fool's
fairness, she couldn't help but feel uneasy after paying without seeing any immediate response.
At this moment,
Magician
Fors inserted herself into the conversation:
"What kind of payment was required to obtain this material, Mr. World? Do you have any extra?"
She was trying to help Xio inquire further.
"2,200 pounds,"
World
responded in a low, even tone after a brief silence.
Upon hearing the price, Fors politely smiled and leaned back into her chair without asking further.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 435: Poverty
chapters.content:
Chapter 435 - Poverty
Seeing her friend shrink back into her seat, Xio almost facepalmed but also felt a bit touched. She was nearly moved to give up her materials to
Magician
, sacrificing her own gains in honor of their friendship.
However, after thinking it through, she realized that such an act would not only waste the materials used in the Sacrifice Ritual but also make her the subject of Ebner's amusement.
More importantly, it would be disrespectful to Mr. Fool.
At this moment, Ebner noticed that no one else was speaking, so he turned to
The Hanged Man
Alger beside him and said thoughtfully:
"Thank you for your assistance with that previous matter... And it was my lack of foresight. In hindsight, having you collect that bounty wasn't the best idea."
What did Mr. Tower and Mr. Hanged Man do privately?
Justice
,
Judgement
, and
Magician
all perked up their ears at these words.
"It's not an issue... Besides, just those three men brought me over 1,000 pounds in income,"
Hanged Man
Alger shook his head. Compared to the bounty, he now valued his relationship with
Tower
far more.
After all, Tower was not only well-informed and powerful but also well-connected and seemingly favored by Mr. Fool. Both professionally and personally, Alger wanted to maintain a good relationship with him.
Sometimes, taking a small loss now might yield greater rewards in the future.
Hearing this, Ebner pondered for a moment before saying:
"But you still bore some risk on my behalf... How about this: I'll share a piece of information with you as compensation for the
Silver-Tongued's
portion of the bounty."
Alger initially wanted to refuse, but seeing how serious
Tower
was, he swallowed his words and asked instead,
"What information?"
After organizing his thoughts, Ebner explained,
"You should know that consuming a Sequence 5 potion requires a corresponding ritual..."
Seeing everyone except
Magician
nodding in agreement, Ebner continued,
"The information I'll provide is the ritual requirement for the
Ocean Songster
. This way, you can prepare in advance... After all, your promotion speed is quite fast, and you might not report your progress to the Storm Church, which means you can't use their official ritual."
Alger was both surprised and delighted. Although he hadn't yet gathered the materials for Sequence 6, he was confident that he would eventually become an
Ocean Songster
. And as
Tower
mentioned, he did indeed plan to conceal his advancement speed.
"Thank you for your generosity..." Alger no longer declined and instead asked calmly,
"What are the ritual requirements?"
"Do you need a private exchange?" Ebner glanced around and asked with a smile.
"No need,"
Hanged Man
Alger shook his head. After all, this was free knowledge, and no one else in the Tarot Club followed the
Sailor
pathway. There was no need to be overly secretive.
"The ritual involves consuming the potion inside the belly of an Obnins." Ebner said casually.
Sitting at the head of the table,
The Fool
Klein noticed
Tower's
slight change in mood and couldn't help but be puzzled:
Why does Mr. Tower seem even happier about this than The Hanged Man? Does he really enjoy flaunting his knowledge that much? No... maybe sharing information is part of his acting.
In truth, Klein wasn't entirely wrong. Ebner's willingness to share this "free wool" not only repaid a favor to Alger but also reinforced his image as a scholar in the minds of the Tarot Club members.
Meanwhile, Alger's mind quickly conjured up the corresponding data:
Obnins are ancient sea monsters capable of swallowing entire sailing ships. They have enormous, twisted bodies, up to three heads, and numerous intertwined tentacles. They are the stuff of many maritime legends.
Most of these creatures are under the Storm Church's control, confined to specific territories. It's uncertain whether they possess human-like intelligence.
No wonder the Church controls Obnins rather than other sea monsters... And no wonder the Sailor pathway rarely produces Sequence 5 Beyonders among pirates. The few who do either inherit their powers or are subordinates of the King of Five Seas or the Queen of Mysteries...
Alger furrowed his brows, but he wasn't too troubled.
After all, he still had time before he reached Sequence 5 and could plan a way around the Church's monopoly.
"Thank you. This information is extremely valuable to me," Alger said sincerely.
Ebner smiled and replied,
"It's your compensation."
Then he turned to the three ladies across the table and asked,
"Ladies, could you help me purchase a new steam engine? It doesn't need to be very powerful—16 horsepower will suffice."
Justice
Audrey blinked. Although she frequently went shopping, she had never purchased a steam engine before.
She had no knowledge of specifications or performance metrics and was momentarily at a loss for words.
Similarly,
Magician
Fors, despite being a follower of the
God of Steam and Machinery
, was equally clueless about mechanical matters.
She had never paid attention to such topics in newspapers and had no idea where to start looking.
Only
Judgement
Xio, after thinking for a moment, asked:
"Would you accept a second-hand machine that's still in good condition?
MI9
recently confiscated a batch from a corrupt businessman colluding with gangs. It's the latest
Bolton-Donald Type 2
. I can try to get one for you."
"Second-hand... How much would that cost?" Ebner's eyes lit up.
"The internal price shouldn't exceed 100 pounds," Xio replied without hesitation, clearly familiar with the matter.
A brand-new machine of this model costs over 500 pounds. That's indeed a bargain!
After some consideration, Ebner nodded:
"Please help me secure one as soon as possible. I'll
sacrifice
the money to you after the Tarot meeting."
Considering that Xio had just spent a significant sum on materials, Ebner decided to pay upfront.
When his issue was settled,
Magician
Fors took a deep breath and said cautiously:
"I'd like to purchase Deep Sea Swordfish blood. I can pay in gold pounds."
Even though my savings are gone, I can still borrow from Xio and repay her when my new book comes out...
Fors silently encouraged herself.
Money truly is one of the biggest obstacles for Beyonders. How did Ebner afford all those materials back then? He's the famous Hero Detective, but it seems like he hasn't actually solved that many cases...
While she was lost in thought,
Hanged Man
Alger chuckled and said:
"I've seen Deep Sea Swordfish blood at one of the big pirate gatherings, but unfortunately, you missed that chance. Wait... no, you weren't even in the Tarot Club back then."
Then why are you mentioning it now? Are you just showing off your seniority?
Fors inwardly rolled her eyes and said sincerely:
"Mr. Hanged Man, please keep an eye out for me. I can accept a price between 300 and 400 pounds."
So... I'm on my own again? But buying materials in Backlund means they won't offer credit...
Fors nearly tilted her head back to stare at the high dome. After a moment, she looked around earnestly and asked:
"Everyone, do you know any good ways to make money?"
As soon as she spoke, an awkward silence filled the room. Only Ebner smiled and replied:
"If you're strong enough, you could try hunting bountied pirates or wanted criminals. It's dangerous, but the rewards are often substantial."
Sure... but I'd probably just become another casualty.
Fors wisely chose to shut her mouth.
She realized that aside from Mr. Fool, most of the Tarot members seemed just as strapped for cash as she was.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 436: Klein takes the blame
chapters.content:
Chapter 436 - Klein takes the blame
After a brief silence,
The Hanged Man
Alger said,
"While investigating
Vice Admiral of Ailment
, I discovered someone she had dealings with... He might be connected to the colonial slave disappearance cases. Please keep an eye out for him.
"He calls himself Barren, has reddish-brown skin with obvious Southern Continent ethnic features, but someone once overheard him speaking with a Backlund accent.
"His third tooth on the left side is missing, though it might have been replaced.
"Furthermore, he has very nondescript facial features and an average height.
"If any of you can track him down, the reward won't be an issue—at least 100 pounds or equivalent valuables."
After speaking, Alger's gaze swept across
Tower
,
World
, and
Judgement
. Although he was reluctant to provoke
Vice Admiral of Ailment
, she was only involved in transportation, and both the upstream and downstream connections were worth investigating.
Judgement
Xio carefully noted down the information, deciding to search for clues.
She was currently quite short on money, and 100 pounds was already a significant sum.
Ebner, on the other hand, knew that this Barren would appear in the
Blood Emperor's
mausoleum in the northwest outskirts of Backlund during the Great Smog Incident before New Year. However, he had no idea where the man was currently, so he simply nodded, signaling he would keep an eye out without saying anything further.
Klein, however, sighed helplessly in his heart.
With such a vague description, even divination wouldn't be able to pinpoint his location, let alone searching for him in reality...
After a few seconds of silence, seeing no one else had any transactions or commissions to offer, the gathering naturally transitioned into the
free exchange
phase.
Maintaining his enigmatic demeanor,
The Fool
Klein controlled
The World
, making him speak in a gloomy, hoarse voice:
"While investigating the
Sauron
family, I came across an interesting rumor... It's said that a Sealed Artifact numbered
0-22
from the
Sauron
family suddenly became 'alive' over a hundred years ago. Through a series of schemes, it indirectly caused the downfall of this former Intis royal family and aided Roselle in securing power over Intis."
"0-22"? So the decline of the Sauron family originated from a '0' grade Sealed Artifact's conspiracy or some sort of negative effect? That's terrifying... But this is just a rumor 'World' picked up, it might not be entirely true.
Hanged Man
Alger was shocked but still kept a healthy dose of skepticism.
He investigated this? No, he must have read it in the diary... But why bring it up now? I remember submitting related content in last month's diary...
Ebner felt puzzled but quickly hid his emotions under a layer of internal monologue.
Magician
Fors, meanwhile, was stunned by the idea that
World
was investigating such an ancient family that had existed for thousands of years.
Even if they had declined, they must still have deep foundations. Otherwise, they wouldn't have been able to make a resurgence in Roselle's later years.
I was right—the World is indeed an extremely powerful Beyonder! In the Tarot Club, he's probably one of the strongest under The Fool, maybe even stronger than Tower.
While Fors's thoughts drifted wildly,
Justice
Audrey couldn't hold back her curiosity and asked,
"What kind of artifact is it?"
Well asked, Miss Justice!
Klein inwardly praised her sharpness while controlling
The World
, who crossed his hands under his chin and said in his usual hoarse voice:
"It's called the
Calamity Seal
. Its essence is the Sequence 1 characteristic of the
Hunter
pathway—
Conqueror
..."He paused briefly before casually asking,
"Have any of you heard of it?"
"Hunter
pathway's Sequence 1 is called
Conqueror
...
Calamity Seal
? Just from the name, you can tell its negative effects must be horrifying..."
Justice
,
Hanged Man
,
Magician
, and
Judgement
all thought the same thing simultaneously.
Only Ebner furrowed his brows.
I distinctly remember that the diary I submitted didn't mention the name Calamity Seal. I only know about it because of the letter from Cullen...
Did Klein find another diary that wasn't in the original timeline? Or maybe today's diary submitted by Justice wasn't about Roselle's early 'funny anecdotes' like in the original...
However, since Klein brought up this topic himself, the Calamity Seal must have caught his attention. Could it really be hiding some deep secret?
Unfortunately, with such little information, I can't deduce anything concrete...
While Ebner was deep in thought, he noticed
The World's
gaze turn toward him, as if expecting him to say something.
It seems I accidentally revealed a trace of confusion earlier, and The Fool must have noticed... Looks like I have to say something to cover up my reaction. Hmm, I can't reveal anything directly from the diary I submitted, but I can share what Cullen wrote in his letter... It's also a good chance to probe what exactly caught Klein's attention.
After thinking it through, Ebner spoke slowly:
"I've heard about this Sealed Artifact. It's said that Roselle greatly admired it during his time as Chancellor and would often carry it with him. Even after he became
Caesar
, he considered making it his
Imperial Seal
... Unfortunately..."
He deliberately trailed off, shaking his head in mock regret.
"What happened?"
Magician
Fors immediately picked up the thread, her curiosity piqued.
The others also leaned slightly forward, eager to hear more.
Excellent. Now it seems like you're 'asking' me for knowledge and insight, solving the problem for me.
Satisfied with this turn of events, Ebner continued,
"Unfortunately, after Roselle became Emperor, the Sealed Artifact mysteriously disappeared and was never seen again."
This was something Cullen had told him. Even though Cullen had fallen out of favor in Roselle's later years, he still knew such insider information.
"That's it?"
Magician
Fors looked disappointed.
What a terrible story. I thought the artifact caused Roselle's downfall—now that would've been dramatic...
*At least let it disappear after Roselle's death; that would match my expectations. If I were writing this story, I'd turn it into an epic tale spanning several dynasties, titled
'The Cursed Artifact'.'
As Fors silently grumbled, Klein, seated at the head of the table, caught a different implication in Ebner's words.
Liu Bo disappeared suddenly? Did they have a falling out? Did Liu Bo oppose Roselle's imperial ambitions? No... After living so many lives, Liu Bo wouldn't oppose Roselle for something so simple. There must be a deeper reason I don't know about...
Or maybe Liu Bo got tired of being a Sealed Artifact and 'traveled' elsewhere...
While his thoughts swirled, Klein controlled
The World
to ask one more question:
"Do you know why it disappeared?"
It seems Klein is truly invested in the Calamity Seal. I remember it was formed after the Death Pathway god fell... Could this be related to Mr. Azik? Hmm, it's quite possible!
With his mind racing, Ebner shook his head regretfully and said,
"I don't know its whereabouts..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 437: The Fool and Amon
chapters.content:
Chapter 437 - The Fool and Amon
It turns out that Kaspars was arrested because of his identity as a
"Black Market Merchant
." In other words, the authorities don't suspect him that much. Miss
"Judgement"
also said that the source of the explosives hasn't been found.
Hmm, I'll confirm this after the Tarot Club meeting ends.
At this thought, Klein let out a slight sigh of relief, controlling
"The World"
to lean back and end the conversation.
After
"The Hanged Man"
shared some observations about Bayam, this Tarot meeting officially came to an end.
Once everyone's figures had vanished into the crimson light, Klein had the
"The World"
marionette bow to him, then transformed it into a
"Pitch-Black Eye"
and threw it into a pile of miscellaneous items.
He waited a while longer until
"Mr. Tower"
sacrificed 100 pounds for purchasing the steam engine. Only then did he
"bestow"
the money and the
"Golden Wings of Gondola"
to Miss
"Judgement"
.
After handling these matters, Klein was about to divine whether Kaspars was currently safe and whether his affairs posed a threat to him... but at that moment, illusory, overlapping prayers suddenly echoed in his ears.
Klein glanced at it and confirmed that the prayer came from
Little Sun
.
Did something happen? Is that former exploration captain really Amon's avatar?
With a slight frown, Klein extended his right hand, spread his spirituality, and touched the corresponding crimson star.
...
In the prison at the bottom of the round tower in the City of Silver, where suspected out-of-control individuals were held—
After returning to reality from the Tarot meeting,
"Sun"
Derrick cautiously sat for several seconds. Seeing no abnormal changes, he finally let out a sigh of relief.
Recalling
"The Hanged Man"
's suggestion to get more information from the former exploration team captain, Derrick walked up to the corresponding metal wall, curled his fingers, and knocked lightly.
Knock, knock.
He completed the signal, but the other side remained silent for a long time.
Asleep? Or taken to the Six-Person Council?
Derrick stared at the dull metal wall, puzzled.
At that moment, an ancient and ethereal voice suddenly came from the bed behind him:
"Are you looking for me..."
...
In the ancient palace above the gray fog, Klein's gaze froze upon seeing the scene from
"The Sun"
's prayer.
On the vague and hard-to-see body of
"The Sun"
, a transparent and illusory figure was entwined!
It had arms and legs but was coiled like a python around
"The Sun"
. Its head extended behind
"The Sun"'s
head!
In the hazy image, it wore a black classical robe, a matching pointed soft hat, and a crystal monocle on its face.
And
"The Sun"
was completely unaware!
A monocle? Is this the monocle that Mr. Door mentioned to Emperor Roselle? This really is Amon... Sequence 1, "The Worm of Time"!
Hmm, it's unlikely this is his main body after forty-two years in the City of Silver's prison. It should just be an avatar...
Klein almost sucked in a cold breath like a supporting character in some novels.
At this moment, he vaguely guessed the other party's purpose:
As a Sequence 1 Beyonder of the "Thief" pathway, adjacent to the "Seer" pathway, Amon might indeed have some connection to this mysterious space above the gray fog... So, he plans to "inhabit" "The Sun"'s spirit body, sneak into the next Tarot meeting undetected, and infiltrate the gray fog above—like a virus or a Trojan horse!
At that point, my control over this mysterious space might be taken away... No, Amon is a "Blasphemer" who even dares to steal the authority of gods... Boldly speaking, he might even steal me entirely, turning me into his avatar... After all, Mr. Door mentioned "Jacob's Decay was related to Amon"... Maybe that entire family was stolen by him?
Fortunately, fortunately, Little Sun is simple and straightforward. He immediately reported this to me, and through the corresponding crimson star, with the power of the gray fog, I was able to discover him in advance...
Klein took a deep breath, forcing himself to remain calm, and began contemplating countermeasures.
Combining his experience in purifying the black stains on "Judgement" Miss's body, he quickly devised a preliminary plan:
Using the high-level authority of the "Black Emperor" card, establish a secret contract with "The Sun" and leverage the power of the gray fog to purify Amon's avatar.
This will require "The Sun"'s cooperation... but since Amon wants to establish some connection with the gray fog above, he probably won't stop this ritual...
If this doesn't work, I'll have to temporarily 'block' "The Sun", and wait until a better method is found...
At this thought, Klein took another deep breath, spread his spirituality, and spoke in a low voice to
Little Sun
:
"I understand."
"I have something for you to do."
"Attempt to hold the following ritual..."
...
In the master bedroom of the
"Fragrant Manor"
in Bayam.
After tidying up the altar and removing the spiritual blockade, Ebner glanced at the gloomy sky outside the window and muttered to himself:
"Mr. Fool should have had his first clash with Amon by now, right?"
"It's a pity I can't help... It's true, even though I might not lose to those famous pirate generals anymore, I'm still far from the true powerhouses of this world!"
With a sigh, Ebner once again felt the urgency to advance his Sequence.
After all, I was firmly tied to "The Fool's" faction, and "The Fool's" enemies were naturally my enemies.
"And Mr. Fool's enemies are numerous and powerful!"
Shaking his head, Ebner left the bedroom and summoned Helene, who was busy verifying accounts, and together they entered the underground workshop being renovated.
As the only
"Beyonder"
in the manor besides Ebner, Helene was naturally called to assist. After all, the
"Mystical Domain"
construction in the
"Workshop"
couldn't be entrusted to ordinary people, and progress was still lagging.
Of course, the
"Teleportation Altar"
in the hidden room on one side of the
"Workshop"
was shielded by a
"Guardian Ritual"
and kept secret from her.
After a while of busy work, the
"Workshop"
finally took shape after processing some customized containers through a mystical method. It would function once the
"power core"
was installed.
At this moment, Helenecouldn't help but remark:
"I didn't expect you to be so bad at craftsmanship, yet so adept at building a workshop..."
Ebner smiled faintly:
"I've built many of these in the 'Dream Labyrinth' scenario. My skills have improved with dream practice. I'm no longer the rookie who failed to repair a hat."
...
Above the gray fog, the mysterious space returned to tranquility as if it had been silent for countless millennia.
Klein reexamined
Little Sun
through the crimson star and found that the twisted, eerie figure was no longer wrapped around him.
Whew!
He let out a sigh of relief, then displayed the
"before and after"
comparison images to
"Little Sun"
via the crimson light, letting him comprehend it himself before Klein returned to reality and fell asleep until Miss Sharon's knocking woke him up.
...
Meanwhile, in an unknown deep darkness, a flash of lightning illuminated the surroundings.
A figure dressed in a black classical robe, wearing a matching pointed hat, with black curly hair, black eyes, a broad forehead, and a thin face, stood on the edge of an abyss.
He adjusted the crystal monocle with his hand, turned his head to the left, looked into the distance, and whispered:
"As expected..."
Pausing for a moment, he curled his lips into a smile and softly uttered an ancient Feysac word:
"The Fool!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 438: All Sides
chapters.content:
Chapter 438 - All Sides
The northern region of the Kingdom of Loen, Winter County.
A towering Gothic-style black church stood amidst snow-covered mountains, occupying an expansive area.
In front of it was a sheer cliff, and all around was an endless expanse of white, devoid of any sound.
This was the headquarters of the
Church of the Evernight Goddess
—
Cathedral of Serenity
, also known as the
Sanctuary
.
Leonard Mitchell, with his dark hair and emerald green eyes, wore a black trench coat and red gloves. He was walking out of the town's post office at the foot of the mountain, intending to return to the
Cathedral of Serenity
before nightfall.
Just as he reached the town's exit, he brushed past a man wearing a hooded ceremonial robe embroidered with intricate patterns and donning a wavy, long wig.
Leonard instinctively felt that this figure was somewhat familiar. However, when he stopped and carefully observed, he confirmed that it wasn't someone he knew.
He shook his head and sighed silently:
My memory seems to be getting worse.
I keep mistaking strangers for you guys...
This wasn't the first or second time such a thing had happened, so Leonard didn't pay much attention. He turned and was about to continue walking out of the town.
At that moment, he slightly tilted his head, as if he had heard something. He stopped again and quickly turned around, scanning for the man he had seen earlier, but found nothing.
"Old man, are you serious? That man had someone else with him? But why didn't I see her?" Leonard whispered under his breath as he searched the street with his gaze.
A slightly aged voice immediately echoed in his mind:
"Ever since you learned about the
Parasite
, you've become more and more impolite...
I suggest you give up. If I'm not mistaken, the woman you missed noticing is a Saint of the
Spectator
pathway."
"A Saint of the
Spectator
pathway? Why would she come to Nighthaven Town?" Leonard asked, puzzled, but he heeded the advice and did not pursue further.
"How would I know? But considering this is the
Sanctuary
of the
Church of the Evernight Goddess
, she's certainly not here to cause trouble," the aged voice replied with a chuckle."True... Such matters aren't for me to worry about." Leonard laughed self-deprecatingly and then asked, "Does the
Spectator
pathway have stealth-like abilities?"
"It's not
true invisibility
, but a psychological effect that makes you fail to notice them," the aged voice explained.
"Old man, you seem very familiar with this ability."
"Of course, I've stolen and used it before."
...
In a two-story building in Nighthaven Town, Dunn Smith removed his disguise and the wig from his head, hanging them neatly on a coat rack. He sighed deeply and muttered in a low, steady voice:
"Leonard actually joined the
Red Gloves
... That's so unlike him... It seems what happened in Tingen really impacted him deeply."
After a brief moment, his sharp gaze fell upon the gently swaying rocking chair not far away. His expression turned serious as he asked:
"Miss Closfia, are you certain the murderer who killed forty-three people is hiding in Nighthaven Town?"
"I'm sure... I guess he thinks the most dangerous place is the safest. Unfortunately, he doesn't realize that a servant of the Evernight Goddess is practicing here and already knows of his crimes," a woman with long, golden curly hair appeared lazily from the shadows, casually reading a book as she spoke.
"A servant of the Goddess?" Dunn was visibly surprised.
If a servant of the Goddess already knew of the murderer's presence, why wait for me to handle it? Moreover, the relationship between the Church of the Earth Mother and the Church of the Evernight Goddess isn't particularly harmonious. Why would this servant allow Miss Closfia into Nighthaven Town?
"You are the loyal guardian of the Goddess in the night. Why worry about this?" Miss Closfia, or
Miss Sloth
, naturally noticed the doubts of her
tool
, smiling as she explained, "The man openly claims to be a devout follower of the Goddess, has donated large sums to the Church, and holds significant influence. Without sufficient evidence of his crimes, the Church cannot act openly."
"So, this is when a
righteous hero
becomes necessary?" Dunn said thoughtfully. At the same time, he confirmed that Closfia and the servant of the Goddess likely knew each other well; otherwise, they wouldn't have been able to handle this situation.
"But you must be careful... Because we're near the
Sanctuary
of the
Church of the Evernight Goddess
, I won't be able to assist you today. And you'll have at most five minutes." Closfia put down her book, her tone uncharacteristically serious.
"I understand." Dunn nodded, his gray eyes deep and resolute.
...
About an hour later, following a storm of
"Light"
, a man in his forties fell from mid-air like a broken puppet. The building beneath him, already half-collapsed, crumbled completely under the impact.
His limbs were mangled and torn. If not for the vest he wore absorbing some of the force, he would have been shredded by the
"Light"
.
Wearing red and gold armor, Dunn descended. He activated a
"Guidance"
charm handed to him by Miss Closfia and asked the man in a deep voice:
"Why did you kill those forty-three people?"
"Because... to silence them..." the man stammered weakly.
"Why silence them?"
"I killed my partners and their families... We discovered a ruin near the Indore Port waters in Feysac...
Suspected to be a dragon's ruin... But there was a ritual circle set up with
"Five-Colored Glorious Stones"
... We couldn't go deeper...
To keep this secret and claim the treasure for myself, I... I killed everyone who knew about it... But I felt guilty... So I came to Nighthaven Town, to the place closest to the Goddess, to confess my sins..."
After extracting details about the ruin's location and general circumstances, Dunn ended the man's life.
The dream shattered abruptly. The crumbled building returned to its original state. Only the man was truly dead—his body intact, his face peaceful.
Leaving records of the man's crimes and his own symbol, Dunn departed into the night.
Ten minutes later, a
Red Gloves
squad arrived at the scene.
...
Backlund
Night had fallen in Backlund.
In a card room at the
Bravehearts Bar
on Iron Gate Street, Maric, dressed in a white shirt and black vest, was playing Texas Hold'em with a group of zombies.
At that moment, Jane, wearing a hooded black robe, pushed open the door. She scanned the room briefly before tapping one of the zombies on the shoulder, silently commanding it to give up its seat. Without hesitation, she sat down in the now-empty chair.
Maric's pale face remained expressionless, but he tilted his chin slightly upward, speaking in his usual low, gloomy voice:
"When did
Spirit Mediums
start being able to control zombies?"
After the previous battle with the
Rose School of Thought's indulgence faction
, Jane had resolved much of her inner conflict. Her attitude towards Maric and Sharon had also softened somewhat.
On the surface, it simply seemed like they were becoming more familiar with each other...
"
Spirit Mediums
can't, but
Spirit Guides
can." Jane responded casually. She then carefully scanned the surroundings and asked with a hint of confusion, "Where's Sharon?"
She was wearing the
Hand of Mysteries
, an artifact that allowed her to see the
Threads of Spirit
, and thus, she could confirm that the
Wraith Lady
was not present."
Spirit Guide
? So you've advanced... That was quick..." Maric muttered, a flicker of daze crossing his pale face.
The little girl in front of me was someone I personally led onto the path of Beyonders just a few months ago. How has she already advanced to Sequence 6?
And honestly... I might not even be her match in combat...
Maric sighed inwardly, pushing the thought away and changing the topic. "Sharon had something to deal with... Are you looking for her?"
"Sharon's been so busy lately... She hasn't been around for several nights." Jane muttered under her breath before organizing her thoughts and saying, "I'll be heading to the Southern Continent soon to handle something for that lady... I wanted to check if you two need anything done there."
She knew that both Maric and Sharon were originally from the Southern Continent and had been unable to return due to the relentless pursuit of the
Rose School of Thought
.
Maric fell silent for a moment. Then, suppressing the emotions flickering in his eyes, he said quietly, "If possible... check on a few of our friends' families. If you can help them, please do."
He picked up a piece of paper and a pen, scribbled down a few names and addresses, and handed them to Jane.
Without the help of those companions, Sharon and I would never have escaped the pursuit, nor would we have survived long enough to receive aid from that lady... But after helping us, they were undoubtedly targeted for retaliation by the Rose School of Thought.
"Alright." Jane didn't say much more. She simply accepted the paper solemnly and carefully put it away.
...
Western District, 9 Bellotto Street, MI9 Headquarters
An elegant and mature man in a neatly pressed formal suit walked into Princess Vera's office. Smiling faintly, he addressed the sharp-eyed princess:
"Vera, there's a task for you. If everything goes smoothly, once it's done, you should have enough merit to apply for the
Imperative Mage
potion."
From his tone and demeanor, it was clear that this man was also a member of the Loen royal family—and one of higher seniority than Vera.
"I'm the
bait
, aren't I?" Vera raised her head and spoke directly.
Her status and identity were inherently misleading, making her the perfect choice as bait.
"Vera, being too clever isn't always a good thing... Nor is being too direct." The man shook his head with a smile before continuing, "But don't worry. While you're bait, Georgina will be shadowing you in secret. And you're not the only bait in play."
Hearing that a Saint would be accompanying her, Vera's expression turned more serious. She furrowed her brows and asked, "What exactly are we transporting to the Southern Continent? Why can't you simply
Travel
there directly?"
"
Traveling
has a higher risk of interception..." the man shook his head again.
At his response, Vera pondered for a moment before asking, "When?"
"Noon this Thursday. A ship will arrive at Pritz Harbor... Additionally, you can bring up to ten subordinates."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 439: The Hope of Small People
chapters.content:
Chapter 439 - The Hope of Small People
Tuesday noon, within the
"Room of Rewards"
on the sixth floor of the
Dream Labyrinth Tower.
The figures of Klein and Miss Sharon appeared here, both looking disheveled as if they had just survived a great catastrophe.
And indeed, they had. Under the overlapping disasters of a super hurricane, floods, and freezing temperatures, the city in the scenario had descended into an apocalyptic state.
If Miss Sharon were still a
Wraith
, such extreme weather conditions wouldn't have affected her much. However, on the sixth floor, she could only use her
Werewolf
abilities. Fortunately, among all Sequence 7 pathways,
Werewolves
were considered one of the strongest in terms of both survival and frontal combat capabilities.
Meanwhile, although Klein could use his full abilities, the
Magician
's physical endurance was still lacking. At the very start, he was nearly swept away by the hurricane... If not for Sharon saving him, he might have had to chant the
Fool's
honorific name on the spot to escape to the
Gray Fog.
Afterward, thanks to Klein recognizing which movie the scenario was based on, he quickly located the
protagonist
, completed the task, and returned successfully.
"This floor was dangerous, but it shouldn't have been set up by Linster... He's waiting for us on the fifth floor!" Klein said to Miss Sharon after taking a brief rest.
Sharon, her pale face still calm and emotionless, replied softly, "The timing after entering the scenario wasn't right. He tampered with it."
Klein frowned slightly at her words, silently agreeing with her judgment. Compared to the earlier scenarios, this time they had been thrown directly into the most dangerous part without any time to adapt... While it could be chalked up to the increasing difficulty of the sixth floor, Klein felt that if he hadn't known the plot, they wouldn't have had enough time to complete the task. They might have been trapped in that apocalyptic scenario until death...
Will the fifth floor be like this as well?
Sharon, wearing her small black soft hat, nodded slightly and then shook her head. "There will be arrangements... but we're more likely to encounter Linster directly."
A trap, after all... Fortunately, I can always 'leave' if necessary. I should go for it. As long as I can take down Linster, this Dream Labyrinth Tower shouldn't have any more traps targeting Sharon and me. At that point, maybe the permissions he blocked will also be restored...
Klein sighed and asked, "Do we continue?"
Sharon shook her head lightly and said in her ethereal voice, "The extraordinary items I prepared were all exhausted on the sixth floor..."
So we'll need time to replenish? Makes sense. Unlike me, she can't leave freely. Entering the fifth floor is equivalent to gambling with her life; preparation must be thorough...
With this in mind, Klein asked again, "When do you think would be suitable?"
"Next Wednesday or Thursday night. I'll inform you in advance." Sharon thought for a moment before replying succinctly.
This timing was also acknowledged by the
Dream Labyrinth Tower.
"Alright." Klein exhaled softly, then casually chose one of the
"mirrors"
and walked over to review his reward.
"Shatter extraordinary characteristics and allow spiritual contamination to evaporate?"
Holding a book titled
"Aetri's Conjecture"
, Klein showed a look of realization, followed by some helplessness.
So the reward this time really is a method to eliminate spiritual contamination from extraordinary characteristics...
But I don't have the ability to shatter characteristics! Moreover, if the Pitch-Black Eye gets shattered, the spiritual contamination from the True Creator hidden inside might erupt. Who could handle that? Should I attempt it above the Gray Fog?
The rest of the book's conjectures seemed intriguing at first glance, but upon deeper reflection, they were fraught with peril.
Was Aetri a Beyonder of the Mystery Pryer pathway? Could he have gone mad from being overwhelmed by "Knowledge"?
Closing the book, Klein turned to Sharon and found her calm blue eyes looking at him. She parted her lips slightly and said, "A method to eliminate spiritual contamination from extraordinary characteristics."
Such a coincidence? Did this tower give the same reward twice? What a scam! Is this Linster doing as well?
Klein silently complained before showing Sharon the
Aetri's Conjecture
. After a moment of silence, Sharon handed him a thin book titled
"Roselle's Memoirs V."
Seeing the title, Klein's mouth twitched. When he opened the pages, he wasn't surprised to see an intimate encounter between Roselle and a certain
Madame.
However, unlike the
Roselle Diaries
, this book was narrated in the third person.
Did Liu Bo write this? Could he have contributed to constructing this Dream Labyrinth Tower as well?
Klein quickly skimmed through the pages, finally finding the only valuable information:
Roselle had used a
"Grade 0 Sealed Artifact"
to shatter an extraordinary item and allowed the
Mysticologist
characteristic within it to recombine.
At the same time, Sharon finished reading
Aetri's Conjecture
, nodded slightly, and said, "They corroborate each other."
After a pause, she added, "The rest of the knowledge in this book is very dangerous. Don't attempt it."
Stop treating me like some lunatic who tries everything recklessly... I only attempt things when I'm confident about them.
Klein recalled Sharon's look when she first heard about the
Blasphemous Runes
incantation. With a resigned sigh, he mentally defended himself....
In a Hidden Alley in the Eastern District
Freyja, the eldest daughter of laundress Liv, led her younger sister Daisy down a shortcut after delivering freshly cleaned clothes to a customer. They wanted to get home quickly for lunch.
They often used this alley and, since it was midday, felt relatively safe despite remaining vigilant.
But suddenly, Daisy was grabbed from behind by a man in a heavy jacket and a gray-black cap. He covered her mouth with a handkerchief and dragged her into a side alley.
Another man dressed similarly, grabbed her legs. Together, they swiftly carried her away and disappeared into a waiting carriage outside the alley.
The entire process took less than two minutes. By the time Freyja turned back in a panic, the carriage had already disappeared.
Seeing her fourteen-year-old sister taken away, Freyja ran desperately, but she could only watch helplessly as the carriage vanished from her sight.
Tears streamed down her face as she screamed for help, hoping for a good Samaritan.
But this was the edge of the Eastern District. Everyone here was numb to life, and no one would respond to a girl's cries. Worse, her calls drew the attention of some ill-intentioned gang members.
Fortunately, a patrolling policeman arrived just in time, saving her from also being abducted.
Freyja clutched the officer desperately, explaining everything tearfully. But the policeman merely recorded her statement and sent her home, telling her to wait for updates.
When laundress Liv learned of her daughter's abduction, she froze momentarily before turning to Freyja with an intense determination in her eyes.
"Didn't you once tell me that Mr. Aetris, who brought back your father's ashes, said we could seek someone for help?"
Freyja's eyes brightened, and she hit her forehead hard. "I can't believe I forgot something so important!
"Mom, Mr. Aetris said he's friends with the
Hero Detective
... and we can also find a police officer named Fassing..."
Liv nodded, took out a small parcel—her husband's inheritance—and said firmly, "We'll send a telegram to Mr. Aetris, then ask where the
Hero Detective
lives."
...
In the Basement of Fragrant Manor, Bayam
A circle of crackling sparks appeared above a
Teleportation Altar
, and
Admiral of Icebergs
Edwina walked out from within.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 440: Crafting Artifacts
chapters.content:
Chapter 440 - Crafting Artifacts
Having previously communicated in the dream realm, Ebner was already waiting in the basement. When
Admiral of Icebergs
Edwina appeared on the
Teleportation Altar
, he greeted her with a smile and exchanged brief pleasantries.
Outside of academic discussions, Edwina wasn't particularly skilled at conversation. She merely nodded before reflecting on her recent experience, murmuring with lingering contemplation:
"So
this
is what traversing the
Spirit World
feels like...
"The overlapping blocks of color are like abstract oil paintings, where human concepts such as up, down, left, and right lose all meaning. Trying to navigate using those ideas would inevitably lead to getting lost... I had previously questioned the necessity of a
Teleportation Altar
... but now it's clear. Without it, I would have been lost in the
Spirit World
, unable to find an
exit
at all.
"How does
true Spirit World traversal
achieve precise navigation?"
Unfortunately, Ebner couldn't answer this question. His
Pure White Eye
seemed highly inefficient at parsing anything related to the
Spirit World
. Otherwise, he would have already attempted to learn to
Travel
himself instead of collaborating with Edwina to develop their current, expensive, and complex secret technique.
But Edwina hadn't really expected an answer from him. Through their time together in the dream realm, they had gained an understanding of each other's strengths. After thinking for a moment, Edwina temporarily set the question aside and began inspecting the newly constructed workshop.
It's worth mentioning that earlier that morning, Xio had purchased a steam engine through MI9's internal channels and offered a prayer to
The Fool
for sacrifice. However,
The Fool
had only responded around noon, meaning Ebner's power core had only recently been installed.After a tour of the workshop, Edwina's clear eyes, usually calm like spring water, revealed a rare trace of envy. She said with slight regret:
"This workshop is excellently designed... Unfortunately, there's no way to set up such a system aboard the
Golden Dream
. Ever since I learned the
Artisan
ability, I've never truly had the chance to practice it."
"You can always come here to practice. My workshop is open to you anytime," Ebner said generously.
"I'll pay rent," Edwina replied without pretense. However, as the topic turned to money, she suddenly remembered the primary purpose of her visit. She took a deposit slip from her pocket and handed it to Ebner. "To avoid drawing attention to the bounty's transfer, the money was cycled several times before being deposited in the
Lenburg Bank
. There are 8,600 Sassons in this account."
The Sasson gold from Lenburg isn't as valuable as Loen gold pounds. One gold pound is worth nearly two Sassons... So that's about 4,300 pounds? Not bad.
After a quick mental calculation, Ebner accepted the deposit slip and tucked it away.
Edwina's gaze then shifted to the steam engine Helene had purchased. After observing it carefully, she said with certainty:
"You've modified it. Are you planning to use Beyonder abilities instead of fuel?"
"I've kept the fuel option... but there's a
Pyromaniac
in my estate who plans to use this as part of her
acting
method," Ebner explained with a smile.
Edwina nodded thoughtfully and said seriously, "If I need to use this workshop in the future, I'll bring Danitz along."
...
Backlund, Garden Villa at 28 Kingst Street, Cherwood Borough
Freyja and her mother, laundress Liv, stood anxiously outside the grand and luxurious villa. They mustered the courage to press the doorbell several times but ultimately hesitated each time.
Their humble clothing felt utterly out of place in such a setting.
Finally, it was Mr. Scudder, who was about to leave the house, who noticed them. He approached them courteously and inquired about their purpose, allowing Liv to overcome her reservations and pour out their story in one breath.
When Mr. Scudder heard that her daughter had been abducted, his expression turned grave. Having experienced something similar before, he deeply understood the desperation of seeking help in such situations. He warmly invited the mother and daughter inside the villa and listened carefully to their account.
After a moment of silence, Mr. Scudder said regretfully:
"Detective Bryan is not in Backlund at the moment and cannot take your case..."
Just as Liv and Freyja were about to fall into despair, Mr. Scudder added:
"But I can contact Miss Xio Derecha on your behalf. I believe she would be willing to help."
Then, as a devout follower of the
Earth Mother Goddess
, Mr. Scudder subtly suggested:
"Additionally, if you are followers of the
Earth Mother Goddess
, I can also inform Bishop Utravsky about this matter..."
Freyja, an 18-year-old girl, brightened at the mention of
Arbiter
Xio's possible assistance. However, she didn't fully understand the implication of Mr. Scudder's words and blurted out, "I'm a follower of the Goddess..."
Before she could finish, her mother firmly grabbed her arm, took a deep breath, and said sincerely, "I am willing to listen to the teachings of the
Earth Mother Goddess
. Please introduce us to the Bishop."
Hearing this, Freyja realized the subtle meaning behind the conversation. She was about to say something when she saw Mr. Scudder smile warmly and say:
"In any case, please wait here for a while. I'll first contact Miss Xio and then report this matter to the Bishop."
...
Bayam, Basement of Fragrant Manor
After discussing mysticism knowledge with Ebner for a while longer, Edwina once again used
Teleportation
to return to the
Golden Dream.
Before leaving, she informed Ebner, "The
Golden Dream
will set sail tomorrow and is expected to reach the waters near Gulain City in East Balam by the weekend."
During this time, she suggested performing a
Teleportation
ritual once daily to test the
Edwards-Brain Teleportation Method.
As the
door
formed by sparks above the
altar
vanished, Ebner took a short break before retrieving a
Corpse Collector
characteristic he had previously obtained from the
Eternal Life Society
, along with a
Werewolf
characteristic sent earlier by Jane through a
Messenger
.
He was ready to start crafting extraordinary items in the workshop.
Of course, to ensure the power core operated normally, Helene had been called in as well. She officially began her
water-boiling
duties.
...
South Bridge District, Rose Street
Mr. Scudder arrived at
Harvest Church
by carriage. After paying the fare, he paused before the church's exterior and prayed devoutly to the
Earth Mother Goddess.
He had only left a brief message for Xio before heading straight here, so he was still early.
Inside the church, Bishop Utravsky was giving a sermon. His towering 2.2-meter frame and the loose priestly robe failed to conceal his imposing physique, yet his expression was warm and serene, radiating gratitude and reverence for life.
In front of such a
Father
, no one dared to make a sound. The small congregation sat quietly, occasionally following the elegant gestures of a beautiful priestess leading them in the
Earth Mother Goddess's
unique prayer rituals.
As a devout follower of the
Earth Mother Goddess
, Mr. Scudder found a seat near the aisle and joined in the sermon.
Beside him, a young gentleman with a thick beard glanced at Mr. Scudder, his eyes narrowing slightly as if he recognized him from somewhere.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 441: Hazel’s Decision
chapters.content:
Chapter 441 - Hazel's Decision
The bearded gentleman was none other than the renowned detective
Sherlock Moriarty
—in other words, Klein.
He discreetly observed the man sitting next to him, who was dressed in a white shirt covered by a black vest, his hair meticulously groomed. Klein found him oddly familiar.
After carefully recalling for a moment, realization dawned in Klein's eyes.
On the night I cleansed Miss "Judgement" of her black mark, this gentleman and his wife had entered "Tower's" bedroom to deliver fresh clothes, food, and drinks to the ladies...
He must be Mr. "Tower's" butler? Why is he here at Harvest Church? Could "Tower" have some connection to the Church of the Earth Mother?
Hmm... it might not be directly related to the church. Perhaps he knows someone within the church, which is why he visits frequently.
With this thought, Klein turned his gaze toward the priestess at the front of the prayer hall, Miss
Hazel Macht
. He nodded thoughtfully and stopped paying attention to the gentleman beside him.
He patiently waited, calm and composed, until the sermon concluded. Then, he gripped his cane, preparing to rise and continue his tasks.
At that moment, a man wearing the robe of the
Church of the Earth Mother
entered through the door leading to the back rooms of the church.
He appeared to be around twenty-eight or twenty-nine years old, with black hair, red eyes, a high nose bridge, and thin lips. He was handsome but not particularly masculine in appearance. It was none other than
Emlyn White
, whom Klein had seen in his prophetic dream.
Klein's mouth slowly fell open, and he nearly failed to close it again.
Isn't this guy supposed to be locked in the basement?
Didn't he shout repeatedly about holding onto his faith and refusing to submit to Bishop Utravsky's ideals?
How did he surrender so quickly?
This is beyond shameless! How am I supposed to "perform" in this situation?
While Klein was mentally ranting, Emlyn White was distributing the elements of the
Holy Communion
to the gathered believers, eventually stopping right in front of Klein.
Klein's mind raced, and he lowered his voice:
"You're Emlyn White, aren't you? Your parents hired a friend of mine to look for you..."
Emlyn White's usual haughty demeanor had disappeared, replaced by a weak smile that looked only slightly better than crying.
"Alright, Detective, stop acting... I know you're the
Clown
who visited that night... or rather, the new owner of the
Master Key
...
"Your disguise couldn't fool that little girl over there who can lift the church doors with one hand, let alone me.
"But still, even though I'm now a priest of the Earth Mother, I need to thank you..."
This response completely exceeded Klein's expectations. For a moment, he didn't know how to react and could only scream internally:
So... you really surrendered?
Last time at Harvest Church, you confidently said you worship the Moon and would never switch faiths. And now, just a short while later, you've given in?
That was fast!
Also, why is it that both you and Miss Hazel can so easily see through my disguise? I thought my disguise was pretty good...
Seeing Klein's slightly open mouth, Emlyn misunderstood his expression and smiled smugly:
"Heh, for noble vampires, every person has a unique scent, a distinctive blood characteristic. Even while I was locked in the basement, I could smell and remember your scent.
"As for Miss Hazel, the arm under her glove might have some... issues. There's something strange residing within it."
I see... The extraordinary abilities of different pathways are truly unpredictable. Fortunately, up to now, I haven't encountered someone who knows both Klein and Sherlock. Otherwise, my simple disguise wouldn't last long...
As for being identified as an extraordinary by Emlyn and Hazel, Klein wasn't too concerned.
If they recognize me, so be it. The current situation is vastly different from two months ago when I first arrived in Backlund.
Back then, I was frantic and desperate after the ambassador's incident, barely clinging to every opportunity to survive. During that time, exposure to the extraordinary world and even becoming a Beyonder wasn't entirely impossible. Even if someone discovers my Beyonder identity now, they wouldn't overthink it.
Moreover, "Tower's" teacher, Detective Isengard, maintains good relations with the police and the official organizations. He vaguely suspected I was one of them and gently tried to bring me into the fold. In that sense, I could barely count as an unofficial member of the authorities. If something happens, I won't necessarily be arrested.
And if push comes to shove, I can always reveal my identity as "The World" and ask Miss "Judgement" for help.
As Klein relaxed and began discussing with Emlyn about why he had become a priest of the Earth Mother, Mr. Scudder had already reported Liv and Freyja's tragic situation to Bishop Utravsky.
After listening to the report, Bishop Utravsky remained silent, but
Hazel
frowned and asked, "Such incidents... aren't they under police jurisdiction?"
"In the
East Borough
, such events aren't uncommon... Unless there's a major incident, the police rarely pay attention to them," Mr. Scudder explained. He had spent time wandering in the
East Borough
after arriving in Backlund and was familiar with its
rules
. The police there were far more interested in enforcing the
Poor Law
and driving away vagrants sleeping in public spaces than in preventing crime.
"How can this happen?!" Hazel, though not born wealthy like
Miss Justice
, had grown up in relative comfort and had never witnessed the true suffering of the lower classes. The most despicable things she had seen were disputes over inheritances.
However, even in the original novel, this young lady had always been warm-hearted and willing to help others. After joining the
Church of the Earth Mother
and listening to Bishop Utravsky's sermons daily, this quality had only grown stronger.
She hesitated briefly, then turned to Bishop Utravsky and asked if it was appropriate for her to get involved.
Bishop Utravsky lowered his head slightly, gazed at the priestly robes on Hazel, and said with a warm smile:
"Go, child. Follow the choice in your heart. The Mother will bless you."
Hazel hesitated and said, "If this group is so brazen, they might have powerful backing... If I act recklessly, could it bring trouble to the church?"
Bishop Utravsky maintained his gentle smile and replied:
"Every person has their mission. All will return to the earth, buried deep in the soil, sprouting anew, growing tall, and blossoming—one life after another.
"This is the fate of all things. If the
Harvest Church
suffers oppression because of this, then that oppression is simply a part of our destiny, a plan laid out by fate and the Mother."
Hazel's expression turned resolute. "If things do go wrong, I'll ask my father for help!
"There's always a way to resolve things."
...
Later, when Hazel arrived at Ebner's garden villa with Mr. Scudder, they coincidentally encountered
Xio
, who had just received the message and rushed over.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 442: Prelude
chapters.content:
Chapter 442 - Prelude
"Name:
Dagger of Gloomlight
Appearance: A 20-centimeter-long steel dagger with a black gemstone embedded in the hilt, flickering with dim light.
Abilities: The wielder's speed and strength will be moderately enhanced. It can resist the erosion of decay, cold, and the aura of death. It will also make unintelligent undead perceive the wielder as one of their own. Additionally, the wielder can directly see some malevolent spirits. When the blade strikes a spirit, it can inflict significant damage.
Negative Effects: The wielder's body temperature will continuously drop until they die and become an actual corpse.
Precautions: Do not use it for more than ten minutes at a time. After usage, it's best to bask in sunlight for half an hour or drink a cup of
Holy Solar Water.
Sealing Method: Store it in a scabbard reinforced with a
Sacred Oath.
"
In the basement workshop of
Fragrant Manor
in Bayam, Ebner fiddled with the dagger he had just crafted and asked Helene, who was wiping sweat from her forehead nearby:
"If this dagger is priced at 500 pounds, would you buy it?"
Since they were underground, Helene wasn't wearing her hat that could change her hair color. Her vibrant red hair clung damply to her forehead, making her look slightly disheveled.
Helene took a deep breath, thought for a moment, and replied seriously, "I don't need it, so I wouldn't buy it... But it has a good design, and its abilities are quite practical for Beyonders who aren't adept at dealing with the undead. If it comes with the sealing scabbard, I think someone would purchase it."
"So... it's profitable after all..." Ebner let out a sigh of relief. He decided to bring it to the next extraordinary gathering at the
Fragrant Leaf Tavern
to gauge the market for mystical artifacts in Bayam.
After carefully placing the
Dagger of Gloomlight
into a temporary scabbard reinforced with the
Ring of Light
, Ebner reflected on the lessons he had learned during the crafting process. With a smile, he said to Helene, who had just finished wiping her sweat:"Take a half-hour break, and then we'll start the next one..."
Helene's eyes went blank for a moment. She then glared at Ebner with a gaze full of resentment, nearly summoning a fire crow to smack his smug face.
...
Harvest Church
Inside
Harvest Church
, Klein chatted with Emlyn for a while and discovered that this vampire genuinely believed he could deceive Bishop Utravsky with half-hearted devotion to the Earth Mother. Klein gave him a look of pity and informed him that the bishop possessed a miraculous artifact called the
Candle of Heart's Desire
. It might have already planted subtle suggestions in Emlyn, gradually making him a true believer in the Earth Mother.
Hearing Klein's analysis, Emlyn grew visibly uneasy. Without saying another word, he dashed toward the church doors, but the half-giant bishop didn't stop him.
Klein noticed that Miss Hazel and the butler from
Tower
had already left, but he paid it no mind. Instead, he approached the bishop and mentioned Emlyn's parents hiring him to locate their son.
Bishop Utravsky looked down at him with a warm expression and said calmly:
"Emlyn may return home anytime he wishes."
Seeing that the bishop truly had no intention of preventing Emlyn from leaving, Klein leisurely walked out of the church and caught up with Emlyn, who had run some distance before circling back.
When Emlyn saw Klein, his face was twisted in frustration. He said anxiously:
