"I suddenly started missing
Harvest Church
. I miss reciting the scriptures. I miss the
Holy Emblem of Life
. I miss cleaning and tidying... Just one hour! One hour would be enough..."
Mandatory labor for an hour? The bishop has a talent for subtle conversion... Instead of forcing Emlyn to switch faiths, he's using labor to influence him imperceptibly. That Candle of Heart's Desire is said to originate from a dragon? The Spectator pathway is frightening indeed...
Klein was lost in thought when Emlyn suddenly declared with anger:
"I will resist this feeling! I'll move to Jianhai or even Feysac! I refuse to believe that if I'm far away from Backlund, I'll still want to return!"
For some reason... I feel like you'll definitely come back...
Klein internally mocked Emlyn but didn't say it aloud. Instead, he hailed a carriage and sent Emlyn back to his home on
Riverside Boulevard.
When Klein paid the fare, Emlyn bolted upstairs into his bedroom. Upon seeing that his beloved
puppets
were all safe, he let out a deep sigh of relief. Then, he returned downstairs, placed his hand over his chest, and bowed deeply to Klein:
"No matter what, I must thank you."
Klein smirked and said,
"No need to thank me.
"I'll be claiming the bounty for finding you, as well as the fare for the carriage, from your parents.
"Additionally, you'll need to prepare an extraordinary potion for me to treat a patient.
"That's the payment you owe me."
Bounty? Carriage fare? Potion? Where's your gentlemanly demeanor?
Emlyn's expression twisted, mirroring Helene's from earlier. If he could control flames, he'd likely have the same impulse she had.
...
28 Kingst Street, Cherwood Borough
When Xio Derecha arrived at the garden villa after receiving Mr. Scudder's message, she saw Hazel stepping out of a carriage in casual attire.
Xio recognized Hazel immediately. After all, this young lady had once tried to steal a bracelet from her friend and had her arm severed by Ebner in the process. The incident had left a deep impression on her.
In contrast, Hazel didn't have much memory of Xio. She had only briefly seen her when saying farewell to Ebner.
Roughly guessing why Hazel was here, Xio exchanged a few polite words with her before following Mr. Scudder into the drawing room, where Liv and Freyja were waiting anxiously.
Thanks to Xio's reputation in the
East Borough
, when Freyja heard that the petite lady before her was the famous
Arbiter
, she immediately burst into tears and recounted the events again, pleading with Xio to
"Arbitrate"
the matter.
Hazel, listening from the side, clenched her fists but quickly relaxed them, reminding herself not to act impulsively. She was unfamiliar with the
East Borough
and acting recklessly might make things worse. It was better to hear what the
Arbiter
had to say.
Meanwhile, Liv gritted her teeth and retrieved a handful of gold coins from the package sent back by Aitris, intending to offer them as a commission fee.
Though Xio was currently strapped for cash, she wasn't so desperate as to accept all of it. She symbolically took one coin, signaling her acceptance of the case, and then asked sternly:
"I recall that your neighborhood is under the
Hillary Gang's
control. They have strict oversight of their territory and rarely allow others to interfere... Have you informed them about this incident?"
Liv nodded grimly and said, "I approached them... but they said Daisy was taken from an area outside their jurisdiction..."
"The
Hillary Gang
may be more disciplined than other gangs, but they're still criminals... If someone forced them to back off, it must be someone powerful..."
With a plan forming in her mind, Xio prepared to visit her contacts in the gang. However, Hazel suddenly said, "Can I come with you? I believe I can be of help."
Xio sized her up and then chuckled. "Sure... But you can't go into the
East Borough
dressed like that."
...
In an alley outside the
East Borough
, a carriage slowly came to a stop.
A few burly men stepped out and hid in nearby corners, waiting for new
prey
to arrive.
At that moment, they spotted three women walking calmly through the alley...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 443: Xio’s Solution
chapters.content:
Chapter 443 - Xio's Solution
"Boss, there's a good catch among them... I can't see her face clearly, but her figure is far better than the ones we've caught before!"
A man in his thirties with a vicious expression stared intently at one of the three girls walking through the alley. She was wearing gloves, and his eyes gleamed with greed.
The man he called
Boss
wore a gray-black flat cap, a thick cotton coat, and had a red birthmark on his face. Hearing his subordinate's words, he squinted at the girls and nodded excitedly.
"Indeed... judging by her posture, she might have been a rich young lady once. Excellent. Take her back, and Mr. Kapin will surely reward us."
"Boss, Mr. Kapin doesn't like us calling him 'Boss'..." the vicious man reminded cautiously.
"Shut up! Get moving!" the boss snapped in irritation, then stood up, readying a handkerchief soaked in chemicals. He signaled to his men to encircle the three girls.
On the other side of the alley, the three young women walking through were none other than Xio Derecha, Hazel Macht, and Freyja, who was leading them.
Under Xio's guidance, they had earlier visited one of the
Hillary Gang's
leaders and learned that the kidnappers were backed by powerful Beyonders—possibly with official connections. They were far beyond what a gang controlling just a few streets could handle.
The gang leader didn't know the specifics but mentioned that their boss and several gang leaders had tried negotiating with the kidnappers, only for the talks to fall apart. They were then instructed not to provoke those people.
However, the kidnappers operated with a semblance of
rules
, rarely entering gang-controlled territories to abduct people. Most of their operations happened at the borders between gang territories, so the gangs hadn't retaliated too aggressively.
Hearing this, Hazel was left stunned.
Do the kidnappers fear the gangs more than the police? Does that mean the gangs are the real enforcers of order in the East Borough?
How could such an absurd thing happen?
But for Xio, this was business as usual.
In the
East Borough
, her title as the long-absent
Arbiter
carried more weight than the police.After failing to gather more clues, Xio had Freyja lead them to the scene of Daisy's abduction. They planned to follow the direction the carriage had taken and trace Daisy's whereabouts.
However, as soon as they arrived, Xio, using her
Sheriff
abilities, immediately noticed a carriage parked just outside the alley and three men lying in wait at the entrance.
Narrowing her eyes, she discreetly shielded Freyja behind her while slightly slowing her pace, allowing the distracted Hazel to walk ahead.
Just as they were about to step into the street, the three men burst out from their hiding spots. The man with the red birthmark lunged at Hazel, aiming to press the chemical-soaked handkerchief over her mouth and nose.
The other two men moved in perfect sync, preparing to grab Hazel's legs once she passed out.
But before the handkerchief even got close to Hazel, the red-marked man felt a sudden emptiness in his hand—it was gone.
Before he could react, he was lifted by an immense force and slammed violently into the ground.
The handkerchief reappeared, now pressed firmly against his own face. His head spun, and his vision grew blurry.
Meanwhile, the other two men trembled violently, their knees giving way as they collapsed to the ground.
A sharp pain struck the back of their necks, and they slumped into unconsciousness.
Xio grabbed the two men by their collars, glanced at the carriage parked nearby, and said to Hazel:
"Drag that leader onto the carriage as well. I need to
interrogate
them.
"And... maybe stop pressing his chest with that hand. You might actually kill him."
Xio had heard from Ebner about Hazel's
heroic feat
of catching a chandelier weighing hundreds of pounds with one hand. She knew how dangerous that arm could be.
Hazel snapped out of her daze and looked at the man she had instinctively pinned to the ground. Then she noticed her other hand, which was now holding money, a cigarette case, a lighter, and a box of
safety condoms
invented by Emperor Roselle. Her face immediately turned crimson.
She quickly withdrew her hand and handed everything over to Freyja, who was standing behind her.
Freyja, unfamiliar with such situations, only realized what was happening after accepting the items. She stared at the three men being dragged along the ground by Xio and Hazel, a mix of fear and hatred in her eyes.
"Are these the ones who took my sister?" she asked with trembling lips.
After tossing the two unconscious men into the carriage, Xio clapped her hands and replied,
"Maybe... but we'll need to
interrogate
them to be sure."
She turned and looked at Freyja, who was biting her lip nervously, then said thoughtfully:
"Can you keep watch near the carriage? If anyone approaches, let me know."
Interrogations were messy affairs, not something an ordinary girl like Freyja should witness.
"Okay!" Freyja agreed without hesitation.
Xio nodded and hopped into the carriage. Just as she was about to wake one of the captives and use her
Interrogator
abilities to extract information, Hazel suddenly raised her gloved arm and warned:
"It's telling me... something was done to their spirits. Any
interrogation
or
communing
methods might trigger a reaction..."
Xio's golden eyebrows furrowed as she halted her abilities. She trusted Hazel's arm, which housed an ancient alchemical spirit, to detect such things accurately.
To be sure, Xio took a golden mask from her bag, put it on, and carefully observed the three men. After a moment, she confirmed Hazel's warning.
"It feels like... the use of
Judge
abilities. But at a high Sequence... even with my
Judgement Mask
, I can't
undo
the
Law
binding them... Is there at least one Sequence 5
Disciplinary Paladin
backing them?"
This is bad... As a formal member of MI9, my actions might alert them. They could destroy evidence, and Daisy's situation might worsen...
After a brief moment of contemplation, Xio made a decision. She looked seriously at Hazel and said,
"I need to use some
special methods
to interrogate them. Please step out for a moment."
Caught off guard by Xio's sudden authority, Hazel instinctively nodded, got out of the carriage, and shut the door behind her. Only after she was outside did she realize how easily she had been persuaded. She stomped her foot in frustration but didn't return inside.
Inside the carriage, Xio sealed the space with her spirituality. Then she clasped her hands in prayer and murmured reverently:
"Fool who does not belong to this era;
Mysterious Ruler above the gray fog;
King of Yellow and Black who wields good luck.
"I beseech your help;
"I beseech you to allow me to meet Mr. 'Tower' in the hall above the gray fog..."
Yes, in this urgent situation, Xio's simplest and most effective solution was—to ask
Ebner
.
...
Minsk Street
Klein had just finalized arrangements with Lawyer Jurgen regarding a "doctor" who would visit Mrs. Doris the next day. As he stood up to excuse himself and borrow the washroom, he heard a faint and ethereal prayer.
He ascended above the gray fog and responded.
...
Bayam, Fragrant Manor's Workshop
In the workshop, Ebner had just finished crafting two more mystical artifacts using spiritual materials purchased at the
Fragrant Leaf Tavern
. He finally let Helene go rest after hours of grueling work.
As for the "werewolf" characteristics that Jane sent over by messenger, Ebner did not touch it for the time being... Such a valuable thing requires more practice, and only take action after being certain.
As a reward, he had promised to take her shopping—something explicitly written into their contract.
Just as the exhausted and relieved Helene left the basement, Ebner, still examining the two newly crafted artifacts, was suddenly surrounded by an endless gray fog.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 444: Mr. Fool’s Intervention
chapters.content:
Chapter 444 - Mr. Fool's Intervention
When his vision returned to normal, Ebner found himself, as expected, in the
Ancient Hall Above the Gray Fog
. Across the long bronze table sat Xio .
"What happened?" Ebner asked calmly.
As he spoke, he glanced around. Although he couldn't see
Mr. Fool
, he was certain that He was present.
"I need your help with something..." Xio skipped any pleasantries and quickly recounted the entire story of Liv's youngest daughter, Daisy, being kidnapped. At the end, she said with clear concern, "At this point, we must rescue Daisy before the other party realizes those three men have fallen into our hands... Otherwise, they'll likely kill her...
"But I don't know how to bypass the mental tampering placed on them to extract information..."
So that's the situation... If I directly tell her that Daisy is in the dungeon of Kapin's estate, won't that seem far too prophetic?
Ebner thought sarcastically to himself before continuing his internal analysis:
Freya and Daisy, the two pitiable sisters from the original story, have somehow become entangled with Aitris... and because of that, they've ended up at my home, pulling Xio and Hazel into this mess.
However, Xio's concerns are valid. While there are indeed members of MI9 involved in human trafficking, they are only a small faction. The majority are actually unaware. After all, such operations need to be kept hidden from the Church, and the more people who know, the more likely it is to leak.
If someone like Xio—a proper MI9 agent unaware of this dirty business—gets involved, the easiest way to maintain secrecy would be to silence her.
And silencing an official Beyonder subordinate of a princess is far harder than simply silencing the traffickers and their victims.
Kapin's death would not be mourned, but Daisy and the other kidnapped girls are likely in far more danger than in the original events.
But since I'm not at the scene and can't use Analysis, breaking through the mental tampering on those men will be extremely difficult.
Teaching Xio to set up a Teleportation Altar is also unrealistic. First, it's far too complex, and she wouldn't be able to learn it in a short time. Second, the materials required are not easily obtained. In short, it's not feasible in the short term.
So... this matter must rely on Mr. Fool.
After deliberating briefly, Ebner deliberately paused before saying to Xio,
"I don't have a great solution... I suggest you pray to
Mr. Fool
for help."
Xio was momentarily disappointed but brightened up at the suggestion. She immediately turned her gaze toward the empty seat at the head of the table, clasped her hands together, and began to pray devoutly.
Meanwhile, Klein, hidden nearby, sighed internally and muttered in his thoughts:
Why am I not surprised by Tower's suggestion? Is it because he always knows how to make the most of Mr. Fool?
However, after listening to Xio recount Liv and Freya's plight, Klein felt a deep sense of anger towards such despicable acts of kidnapping. From his heart, he wanted to intervene.
Thus, after Miss
Judgement
finished her prayer, Klein revealed himself. He appeared at the head of the bronze table, lightly tapping its edge with his fingers. With a faint smile, he addressed the two Tarot members:
"You know, I am someone who values
equivalent exchange
... So, what do you plan to offer in return for my help?"
Seeing
Mr. Fool
suddenly appear and hearing His question, Xio quickly and respectfully replied, "I will try to collect ten pages of
Roselle's Diary
and present them to you at future Tarot meetings..."
In fact, she already had three pages of the diary from a friend she met while purchasing the
steam engine
. They were originally meant for Fors, as a way to ease her guilt over keeping secrets from her friend.
Miss Judgement seems quite confident... Has she found a new source for Roselle's Diary? That's excellent news!
Unexpectedly pleased by this potential gain, Klein nodded and said, "Agreed."
Before Xio could express any praise, Klein's expression grew serious, and he gave a clear instruction:
"Offer me the lost girl's belongings as a
sacrifice
.
"Have those who need to speak recite my name.
"And ensure that they do not leak this to anyone afterward."
Xio hesitated briefly before nodding solemnly. "Your will is my command,
Mr. Fool
."
The leader of the three captured men radiated an aura of
corruption
and
evil
. Xio had no qualms about killing him afterward.
Satisfied, Klein nodded. "Good. Let's stop here for now. I will inform you when there's progress."
When it came to true villains, Klein had no hesitation in acting decisively.
...
Back in the carriage, Xio quickly arranged an altar using the materials she always carried. She placed Daisy's vocabulary notebook, which she had received from Freya, onto the altar and sacrificed it to
Mr. Fool
.
Afterward, she controlled the power of
Mental Piercing
to wake the man with the red birthmark. While he was still dazed by the ability, Xio exuded her
authority
and commanded him to recite a string of
Ancient Hermes
words.
The man, who didn't understand Ancient Hermes, instinctively repeated the words. His mind was still clouded from the pain of
Mental Piercing
, and he vaguely sensed himself entering a fog-filled space.
Moments later, he saw a paper figure that looked identical to him fly towards him and merge with his body. After that, he remembered nothing.
At the same time, Klein, seated in the
Ancient Hall Above the Gray Fog
, held the
Black Emperor
card in his hand. He extended his spirituality to touch the overlapping shadows of the man and the paper figure.
This was an application of
Covenant Mysticism
. A weak human gradually synchronized with a higher being, feeling corresponding knowledge and receiving profound spiritual insights. In this process, Klein played the role of the
Great Being
.
In this synchronized state, the exchange was reciprocal. Humans could gain knowledge from higher beings, and higher beings could bypass spiritual restrictions and extract desired information.
After a brief but intense exchange, Klein ended the
Covenant
and realized his fists were clenched tightly.
Kapin... Deputy Director of the Backlund Metropolitan Police Department... A Member of Parliament... What a filthy conspiracy!
But why would a human trafficker's house have at least four Beyonders? The strongest one, Horace, might even be Sequence 5... I don't know his pathway, but it seems similar to the Black Emperor...
Law, order, authority... An Adjudicator? If I recall, Tower classified this pathway under the Order Domain.
Based on what I saw, the restrictions only apply to the underground section of Kapin's estate, not the entire building. After all, sealing the entire house during the day would raise too many questions.
But even so, this is likely beyond Miss Judgement's abilities... And Tower isn't in Backlund... If anything goes wrong, Miss Judgement could be in grave danger... Should I intervene?
Klein wrestled with his emotions but ultimately made up his mind. He was willing to help Daisy—the bright young girl who had dared to dream of escaping poverty.
He performed a divination:
"Saving Daisy is a dangerous endeavor."
The yellow crystal pendant spun clockwise with great speed and amplitude, confirming the danger.
But it wasn't hopeless. There was a chance—a slim but real chance.
Leaning back in his chair, Klein smirked self-deprecatingly:
"Aren't you looking for an opportunity to perform proactively?
"This is it!
"As a magician, you still have to challenge yourself to do something difficult, otherwise you should be called a master of tricks instead of a magician.
"To accomplish something that seems impossible, even if the result is false, this is the image of a magician in my mind. As for whether it is one of the rules, it remains to be confirmed..."
After making up his mind, Klein once again touched the crimson stars of the Tower and Judgment with his spiritual power, and thought to himself,
"But I still need Miss Judgment's cooperation in this matter. It would be best if she could remove me to avoid suspicion from those who conduct subsequent investigations...
"Well, as the Fool, I can't be too proactive... I have to exaggerate the difficulties and let Judgment and the Tower come to me for help... Maybe I can even use this to get some knowledge out of the Tower..."
...
At the same time, Ebner, who was in the basement workshop of the Fragrant Manor, was thinking in his mind,
"Although Xio is already Sequence 7 and has a powerful Sealed Artifact, she will definitely not be able to deal with those Beyonders in the Kapin family... and with her sense of justice, I'm afraid she won't give up easily on rescuing Daisy...
"So, this matter has returned to its original trajectory, and it has to be solved by the thief 'Black Emperor'!
"I am sure that Klein will never stand idly by after learning the whole story... So, we have to give him a way out...
"Hey, maybe Klein thinks the same thing... I have to be prepared to be fleeced..."
Thinking of this, Ebner just sighed, and thick gray fog appeared in front of him again, and then he came to the ancient hall above the gray fog.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 445: Klein’s Three Questions
chapters.content:
Chapter 445 - Klein's Three Questions
Arriving at the ancient palace above the gray fog again, Ebner and Xio had just sat down when they saw Mr. Fool tapping the edge of the long table with his fingers. A series of images displaying the slave trader Capim's vile deeds began to appear before them.
There were countless images of newly captured girls crying and screaming in underground prisons.
Scenes of numb, half-naked girls offering drinks to the deputy director of the police department, members of the House of Commons, and other so-called "big shots" colluding with Capim filled the air.
Some showed them being beaten, scolded or dragged to secluded places where they were tortured.
Later, four Beyonders—Harras, Belize, Katy, and Parker—appeared one after another, demonstrating their respective abilities.
After witnessing these scenes, Xio, who had a strong sense of justice, abruptly stood up, her face filled with anger. Even Ebner, who had already been aware of this "plot," felt a deep disgust in his heart.
The written words in the book were nowhere near as impactful as these images...
he thought.
I have to invest more in this matter. It would be best if we could wipe out every single one of those bastards.
"I'm sorry, Mr. Fool... Please excuse my loss of composure" Xio took a deep breath, sat down again, and apologized sincerely.
"It doesn't matter. Things like this are bound to make people angry. I understand," Klein the Fool replied calmly.
He tapped the edge of the table again, and the haunting images gradually disappeared.
"As far as I know, Capim is a wealthy man rumored to be involved in multiple cases of missing girls. He is suspected of being a human trafficker and engaging in the slave trade in private... But because there is no clear evidence, he remains free..."
After calming herself, Xio began to analyze the situation.
"The underground seal seems to involve the ability of a Sequence 6 Judge from the Arbiter Pathways... but the strength is far greater than that of an ordinary Judge. Either Harras is a Disciplinary Paladin, or he borrowed power from a ritual or an extraordinary item.
"Logically, Capim shouldn't have been able to gain the protection of such an extraordinary figure... He shouldn't even have had the opportunity to meet them...
"Unless..."
At this point, Xio paused, her expression turning grim. If it were just a simple Sequence 5 Beyonder, she could report it to MI9 through Her Highness Vera and mobilize resources to rescue Daisy and the other girls.
But the Beyonders in Capim's villa belonged to the Arbiter Pathways. In Backlund, Mid-Sequence Beyonders from this path were typically either military personnel or descendants of nobles granted formulas by the king. In reality, most of the latter also served in the military.
It was hard for Xio not to suspect that Harras and his group were actually peripheral members of MI9—just like she herself had been at the start.
If I report this to MI9 or even the church, news will inevitably leak given MI9's intelligence network... Daisy and the others might be silenced before we can act!
I trust Her Highness Vera isn't one of them... but her influence within MI9 is limited. The number of people she can mobilize is very small.
But I can't just storm the place myself, even with Hazel's help... Hazel's metal arm is powerful, but she lacks practical combat experience. Instead of assisting me, she might end up becoming a burden.
Her thoughts raced, and Xio turned to Ebner once again, hoping he could devise a solution.
At the same time, after confirming from Miss Judgment's analysis that Harras was indeed a Beyonder from the Arbiter Pathways, Klein the Fool subtly shifted his gaze to Tower.
Mr. Tower, it's all up to how well you play your part... If this doesn't work out, I might need to have The World conveniently "log in," stumble across you two, and offer some advice.
Ebner didn't disappoint either Miss Judgment or Mr. Fool. After a brief pause, he respectfully asked Mr. Fool at the head of the table, "I wonder if your followers have the time to intervene in this matter and rescue those innocent girls? I can offer appropriate compensation... and provide assistance if necessary."
For example, some of the extraordinary items I own can be loaned out temporarily. Consider it an additional investment.
Hearing this, Xio opened her mouth as if to say she would pay the reward, but no words came out.
I already owe so many debts... I can't possibly buy more on credit...
As for the debt to Ebner? Well, I already owe him so much. I'll just have to repay it slowly in the future...
We have a good understanding, Mr. Tower!
Klein thought to himself with admiration.
Or rather, you are exceptionally skilled at utilizing The Fool's abilities.
Outwardly, his expression remained calm and emotionless as he said, "I can make the request for you."
"Thank you for your help, Mr. Fool." Xio and Ebner stood and saluted respectfully.
Mr. Fool nodded slightly, acknowledging their gratitude, before sending them out of the gray fog.
This wasn't an act. Klein had genuinely run out of time—he had already been in Lawyer Jurgen's bathroom for over twenty minutes. If he stayed any longer, the man might actually knock on the door to check on him.
...
A few minutes later, after leaving Lawyer Jurgen's house and putting on some simple makeup, Klein called a taxi and rushed to Capim's villa with a dungeon – the address was obtained through "divination."
Sitting in the carriage, he summoned the members of Judgment and Tower for the third time in the gray fog.
As soon as Xio regained her sight, she saw a figure wearing a pitch-black crown and covered in dense armor standing respectfully in front of Mr. Fool. It was obviously a follower who was willing to take over the task of saving people.
He looked very mysterious and powerful, giving people a strong sense of oppression... Could he be a saint? He was indeed the follower of Mr. Fool.
Feeling the mysterious aura of the "Follower", Xio became more respectful and also breathed a sigh of relief:
With such a powerful figure willing to help, Daisy and the other girls can definitely be rescued... I just don't know what kind of reward he wants, I hope it's not too much.
At this time, after asking Mr. Fool for instructions, the armored figure turned around and looked at Ebner and Xio, then asked in a voice full of majesty and oppression, "You are the one who needs a commission?"
It gives me a feeling that he is very similar to Nast, the "King of the Five Seas"... What a good actor! Did Klein use his spirit to contain the "Card of Blasphemy" to pretend to be the "Black Emperor", and then let the "World" dummy sit there as the "Fool"?
Guessing this in his heart, Ebner nodded calmly on behalf of Xio and said, "Yes, Your Excellency, we need your help... I wonder what reward we have to pay you to accept our request?"
The armored Favored One smiled and said, "I heard from Mr. Fool that you are very knowledgeable... So, as long as you answer three questions of mine, I will help you."
Klein's questions during this period shouldn't be difficult to answer... and this can also be considered a role play, right? Ebner thought about it, and then he had a clear idea in his mind. He said confidently, "Please ask."
"The first question is, besides shattering the Beyonder characteristics, is there any other way to remove the mental pollution within the characteristics?" Klein asked in a deep voice.
Eh? Klein got the method of shattering the characteristics from the little "Sun" after several Tarot meetings, right? What happened to the "butterfly effect" that allowed him to know in advance? Could it be my fault?
Although he was surprised, Ebner did not hesitate to answer: "You can also use the magical items of the Marauder Pathway to steal the pollution in the extraordinary characteristics, and then mix the extraordinary characteristics into a potion before the theft fails. In this way, the mental pollution will not return, but will dissipate directly."
This... is indeed something I had not thought of before... The Sealed Artifact "Blood Vessel Thief" behind the Chanis Gate in Tingen City can steal the target's extraordinary abilities, and considering mental pollution as one of them, there is no logical problem...
But the problem is that the mental pollution in the "All-Black Eye" is not from ordinary Beyonders, but from the evil god... Whether it is a Beyonder with the ability to steal or a magical item with similar properties, it is difficult to withstand such mental pollution. The former will 100% lose control on the spot, and the latter will be directly polluted...
Well, theoretically, sacrificing a similar magical item could achieve the goal, but the timing must be just right and there can't be any mistakes, otherwise both will be contaminated.
Klein quickly analyzed the feasibility of this method and admired it in his heart: It is worthy of being called the "Tower" of "erudition". The problem that has been bothering me has been solved so easily.
He quickly came to his senses, nodded with satisfaction, and then asked again: "Second question, how do we find Viscount Cullen of the vampire clan?"
Klein wasn't actually sure whether Ebner knew Cullen, but the fact that he could produce a high-level vampire tome like "Blood Feast," even if it was only half a copy, showed that he had a close relationship with the vampires... What if he just happened to know Cullen's sisters?
Cullen? What do you want to do with him? You probably only saw his name in Roselle's diary, right? But those diaries have nothing to do with you...
After hearing the question, Ebner became more and more confused. He felt that something seemed to have happened to Klein that he had not seen in the original book.
Without Cullen's consent, Ebner couldn't tell Klein about the ritual to summon Silica, so after thinking for a moment, he carefully replied,
"You can go to Mr. Azik Eggers for this matter. His daughter has a good relationship with Cullen...
"I remember that one of Mr. Fool's followers had asked me to investigate Azik before. Maybe I know that gentleman... You can go and ask him for help to introduce me."
Mr. Azik? His daughter has a good relationship with Viscount Cullen? Could it be that the lady has become a great figure above the demigod, so she is still alive today? And she has found her father?
Upon hearing this, Klein was puzzled, but he was also sincerely happy that Mr. Azik was able to find his relatives... After all, loneliness is not pleasant.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 446: Before the Rogue Appears
chapters.content:
Chapter 446 - Before the Rogue Appears
But Mr. Azik is still under the watchful eye of "0-08". Once I get in touch with him, I'm afraid I'll fall into "0-08's" arrangement again...
Under the cover of the gray fog, Klein smiled bitterly in secret and stopped thinking about it. He turned to ask the third question:
"Who is the 'Iron Man' currently active in the Kingdom of Loen?"
Ever since he obtained the novel about the new Iron Man in the "Dream Labyrinth Tower", Klein had been wondering about the connection between Iron Man and himself. However, he had no clues, so he took this opportunity to ask "Tower".
"The Tower" is "Doctor Strange," and there's a high possibility he knows the true identity of "Iron Man." After all, they're both from the Avengers!
Klein couldn't help but complain inwardly.
After hearing the question, Ebner shook his head apologetically and said, "I'm sorry... Although I know who he is, I can't tell you without his permission. Please forgive me.
"Or, could you change the question?"
One of Ebner's principles was not to reveal a friend's secrets without their permission.
Although Dunn couldn't exactly be considered Ebner's friend, the "Iron Man" was, in fact, the work of Miss Judy's mother and perhaps even a task arranged by Mother Earth herself. Naturally, Ebner wouldn't leak such a secret easily.
"Mr. Tower really knows who Iron Man is... Could it be that they actually have an organization similar to the Avengers? But what does he have to do with me? Why does the Dream Labyrinth Tower think I need to know Iron Man's story?"
Hmm... maybe I should change my thinking... What do I care about most at this stage? Apart from advancing my Sequence, it's probably revenge... So, could "Iron Man" be related to Ince Zangwill?
With his thoughts racing, Klein agreed to "Tower's" suggestion and said in a dignified tone:
"Okay... Then let me change the question. Is 'Iron Man' related to the defected bishop of the Church of Evernight, Ince Zangwill?"
Hearing this question, Ebner hesitated for a while but finally answered indirectly:
"There is a grudge between them."
"So that's it... Iron Man is Ince's enemy! He might be an important ally in my revenge. So that's why the Dream Labyrinth Tower compiled his deeds into a novel for me..."
Klein nodded thoughtfully, looked at Ebner, and said, "Very good. Thank you for your answer. I will keep my promise and rescue those kidnapped girls."
Thinking of the
"additional investment"
he had prepared, Ebner shook his head with feigned guilt and said:
"I should thank you for your tolerance... After all, I didn't answer your third question... So, to make up for that concealment, I can provide you with some material assistance for your mission."
"Material help? What's that? And this is just Mr. Tower's excuse... Judging from how indignant he was after seeing those pictures, he must want to help."
Since Ebner hadn't deliberately hidden his emotions, Klein, observing closely, quickly discerned his true intentions. However, Klein didn't feel annoyed by this; instead, he asked with interest:
"How can you help me?"
Ebner knew that Klein's spirit body could only carry a limited number of items and couldn't lift anything too heavy. Most of his magical items weren't suitable for Klein's use. The "Ring of Light" and the "Sun Brooch" had overlapping functions, and the "Tears of Lilith" wouldn't be particularly useful against the incorporeal thief "Black Emperor."
After some thought, Ebner decided to help with the "Ninth Law" spell, which he had exchanged from the "Dream Labyrinth Tower."
"The 'Ninth Law' is a high-level spell containing the power of the 'Imperative Mage.' However, it has a unique origin and can only exist in the real world for three minutes..."
Ebner explained in detail the function and usage of the "Ninth Law."
Even though it could only last for three minutes, Ebner believed that in the hands of the "Magician" Klein, he would be able to maximize its utility.
After hearing the explanation, Klein's eyes lit up. He had previously used high-level Charms like the "Flaring Sun Charm" and "Language of Foulness", so he understood their power. With such a tool, his success rate would undoubtedly increase significantly.
"But... why can it only exist for three minutes? Although I'm curious, I won't ask. After all, it's not my place."
Nodding, Klein said in a tone consistent with his current persona:
"It can indeed help me... Before the action begins, between 7 and 7:30, I will ask Mr. Fool to hand me the Charms.
"Heh, high-level Charms aren't cheap. You've spent a lot."
"It's not about money; it's about effort! Klein, you'd better catch all those bastards this time! Otherwise, my hard work will be wasted..."
After mocking himself internally, Ebner nodded to Klein's "Black Emperor" persona and said:
"I'll wait for your signal and prepare the spell as quickly as possible before sacrificing it to Mr. Fool."
Once their discussion concluded, Ebner turned to Xio, who had been silently listening, and instructed:
"Follow the normal procedures and send the three men to the police station or MI9. After all, they really did attack the daughter of a member of the House of Commons... But try to delay it until 7:30, when His Excellency the Favored One takes action."
Xio said thoughtfully, "Understood. I'll ensure the man who recited Mr. Fool's name appears to have committed suicide out of fear of punishment."
At this moment, the armored "Black Emperor" spoke again:
"Remember to ask Mr. Fool for protection later... After I rescue them, I will capture three of Capim's men. There will still be some suspicion on you, and I fear someone might use extraordinary means to investigate."
"Mr. Fool can still offer this kind of protection? He's such a kind, tolerant, and easy-to-talk-to god. No wonder Ebner trusts him so much..."
Xio was momentarily stunned before standing up to salute Mr. Fool in gratitude.
The Fool merely nodded slightly, saying nothing. After all, the fake "World" would be exposed the moment he spoke.
...
In a dimly lit carriage parked at the edge of the East Borough, Xio lifted the spiritual blockade, pushed open the carriage door, and stepped out. Behind her, the muffled screams and desperate pleas of two men still lingered in the stale air.
As for the man with the red birthmark on his face? He was already dead.
This was Freya's first encounter with such a chilling scene, and even though the figure stepping out of the carriage was much shorter than her, an overwhelming sense of awe and intimidation washed over her.
Standing nearby, Hazel, shaped by the gentle teachings of Mother Earth, felt a faint discomfort settle in her chest. She had keenly sensed the life force in the carriage fading into nothingness. However, she didn't dwell on it. Instead, she asked softly:
"Any results?"
"They are subordinates of the wealthy man Capim," Xio replied evenly, her voice carrying a steel edge.
"Who is Capim?" Hazel asked, her brows knitting together.
"A wealthy man suspected of being involved in human trafficking behind closed doors. He has deep connections with certain House of Commons members and senior officials in the Police Department..." Xio explained briefly.
"The congressmen... the police... they're all in this together?" Freya's face turned deathly pale as she pieced together the implications. It felt as if the sky above Backlund had been covered in eternal darkness, with no sunlight breaking through.
Although Hazel also felt her chest tighten with anger, she took a deep breath, forcing herself to stay composed. She asked, "What should we do now?"
"We'll take them back to MI9. Once we get a search warrant, we'll raid Capim's estate directly. After all, they dared to attack you, the daughter of a member of the House of Commons... Even with Capim's connections, he'll have to give an explanation. He might even secretly release Daisy to avoid more trouble."
Xio's words were measured, and designed to sound like a logical conclusion drawn without any prior knowledge of the unfolding plans. This way, even if someone investigated later, it wouldn't arouse suspicion.
"Okay, I'll go with you... as the 'party' who was attacked." After a moment's thought, Hazel added hesitantly, "Can't we just arrest Capim directly?"
"Capim won't see another dawn. Mr. Fool's believers will ensure that."
Though she thought this silently, Xio explained calmly, "We don't have enough solid evidence. If we act rashly, they might silence him to destroy any traces of proof."
Hazel bit her lip and turned her head away, frustration etched across her face. She wasn't angry at Xio, but rather at herself—at her own helplessness.
Understanding the weight of the situation, Freya gathered her courage and spoke up, "I... I'll also come along as a 'witness.'"
...
The Capim family's villa was located on Iris Street in the Cherwood Borough, close to the affluent West Borough.
After returning to the real world, Klein took a carriage to discreetly pass by the villa—a grand estate surrounded by a sprawling lawn, neatly trimmed gardens, marble statues, and a small fountain plaza.
Through the window of the carriage, Klein caught sight of the iron gate from his divination, guards patrolling with trained eyes, and vicious hounds pacing restlessly. Everything matched his vision perfectly—Daisy was indeed imprisoned here.
Satisfied, Klein instructed the coachman to take him to a modest hotel in the Bridge District.
In the privacy of a small, cheap room, Klein locked the door, sealed the space with his spiritual power, and checked the time on his gold-cased pocket watch.
Once certain, he took a deep breath, walked four steps backward counterclockwise, and entered the ancient, boundless gray fog.
There, he notified "Tower" that it was time to send the "Ninth Law" Charm.
...
In the dim underground chamber of Fragrant Manor, the gray fog receded from Ebner's vision as he stepped away from the ritual altar.
Wasting no time, he entered the "Dream Labyrinth Tower" and exchanged for the "Ninth Law" Charm—a temporary but immensely powerful artifact derived from the mystic principles of the "Imperative Mage."
Back in the workshop, Ebner performed a well-rehearsed sacrificial ritual, offering the Charm to "The Fool" above the gray fog.
When the glowing symbols faded and the ritual concluded, Ebner let out a long sigh of relief. His part was done. Now it was up to Klein to use the Charm wisely.
After cleaning up the ritual traces, Ebner dusted off his coat and returned upstairs. He quickly changed into casual attire and prepared to leave.
He had promised his "Red Maid" that they would visit the night market, and he had no intention of breaking that promise.
Besides, he still hadn't had dinner, so it was a good opportunity for us to go out and eat together.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 447: Capim’s Destruction
chapters.content:
Chapter 447 - Capim's Destruction
Capim House, Iris Street, Cherwood Borough
In the spacious and elegant dining room, the maids meticulously arranged gold-inlaid ceramic tableware on the long table. They placed caviar, roast chicken, stewed lamb, fried ox eye, fried dragon bone fish, cream soup, and other delicacies in an orderly sequence, adhering to refined etiquette.
Moments later, Capim, slightly overweight, emerged from his study. A false warmth spread across his face as he greeted his guests with exaggerated humility: the middle-aged Heras, cloaked in a white hood; Katie, clad in a thin shirt; and Parker, an aged man who appeared harmless and frail.
Once seated, Capim raised his glass, feigning an aristocratic air, and toasted:
"Storm is above, let's toast to a better future."
Katie brushed her fingers against the old scars lining her face, giving only a faint nod in response.
Heras said nothing but lightly raised the stem of his wine glass.
Only Parker, the elderly gentleman, responded:
"Cheers to a bright future."
Unbothered by the lack of enthusiasm, Capim turned his attention to the only lady present, speaking with ingratiating charm:
"Ms. Katie, tonight we have your favorite caviar and a roasted chicken specially prepared for you."
Katie hummed lightly in acknowledgment and began carving the roast chicken with surgical precision. Her knife moved methodically, dividing the bird into pieces of near-identical size.
Even though he had witnessed this display before, Capim still felt a chill run down his spine. Trying to mask his unease, he hurriedly cut a piece of fried dragon bone fish, dipped it in black pepper sauce, and stuffed it into his mouth.
The dinner proceeded without incident until the ornate wall clock struck 7:23.
At that moment, just as Capim was about to ask his guests if they would like dessert, he erupted into sudden, uncontrollable laughter. His laughter grew louder, his body shaking as he clutched his belly. Tears streamed down his flushed cheeks.
The dining room fell eerily silent.
The servants nearby began collapsing one by one, unconscious. Others clutched their stomachs, vomiting yellow-green bile, unable to stop.
No one was spared.
Heras, despite his calm demeanor, felt his breath grow shallow. His instincts screamed a warning: the entire room was filled with poison.
He barked sharply:
"Hold your breath! Parker, open the door! Katie, follow me—find the intruder!"
Bang!
The dining room door burst open as Parker forced it ajar, allowing fresh air to flow in. At the same time, Heras activated his spiritual vision, immediately spotting an illusory figure silently moving amidst the chaos.
The figure was cloaked in thick black armor, a black crown resting atop its head, and a black mask obscuring its face—like a spectral king emerging from the void.
It was Klein, who had phased through the wall two and a half minutes earlier.
Without hesitation, Heras raised his right hand, channeling the Judge ability to "imprison" the intruder. But before the ability could take effect, he noticed a glowing talisman clutched tightly in Klein's hand—etched with intricate symbols like the "Sword of Judgment" and an array of ancient sigils.
It wasn't just an ordinary artifact—it was a high-level spell.
Heras's eyes widened in realization. Before he could react, Klein solemnly declared in ancient Hermetic:
"It is forbidden to make rules here!"
The weight of the words echoed throughout the space.
Having witnessed the "Forbidden" combat technique during the naval battle seen in Miss Judgment and Mr. Tower's Late Night Broadcast, Klein had prepared meticulously. He confirmed with Miss Judgment that most of Capim's Beyonders followed the Arbiter Path, known for rule enforcement and restriction abilities.
To counteract this, Klein had secured the "Ninth Law" Charm from Mr. Tower—a spell specifically designed to prohibit prohibitions.
As Klein's words hung in the air, a series of dark golden runes and magic symbols spread throughout the space, weaving into the fabric of reality.
Heras immediately felt the weight of invisible chains binding him. His "imprisonment", "exile", and all other rule-based abilities became utterly useless. Even his voice was choked back, preventing him from issuing commands.
Seeing his most formidable foe effectively neutralized, Klein wasted no time. He swiftly turned and used "Scream" to repel Katie's attempted sneak attack from behind.
Without pausing, he fired several air bullets infused with holy aura directly at Heras, capitalizing on his opponent's vulnerability.
The latter dodged while pulling an iron-black metal glove from his hidden bag.
While Katie recovered and once again entangled the invading "ghost" with her pistol and whip, Heras successfully donned the glove.
In an instant, Heras felt as though he had grown taller, as if he had become a towering figure capable of determining the fate of others.
Having used this item many times before, he did not let himself be consumed by this illusory feeling. Instead, he channeled its power to forcibly break the "laws" established by his opponent's talisman and successfully
punished
them.
However, just as he delivered a glowing fist aimed at the intruder's head, the scene around him shattered into fragments.
A dream? The other party also has the ability of a "Nightmare"?!
Heras was shocked but forced himself to calm down. As he surveyed his surroundings, he found Katie and Parker lying motionless on the floor, their life or death uncertain. Worse yet, the iron-black glove was now worn on the spectral hand of the black-crowned intruder.
What frightened him even more was his current location—next to a gas pipe. The sharp smell of gas saturated the air, triggering every warning bell in his mind.
The poison gas was used to mask the smell of gas?!
Just as Heras pieced together the realization, he saw the figure wearing the black crown bow slightly to him, as if bidding farewell.
Then, a bright flame ignited!
Boom!
A deafening explosion consumed Heras's vision. Flames burst forth like a grand fireworks display, searing everything in their path.
He barely had time to shield his vital organs before the fiery wave engulfed him.
Without the iron-black glove's protection, Heras's physical resilience was far inferior. The massive impact shattered his body, breaking his internal organs and leaving him severely injured.
Yet, against all odds, he did not die. With sheer determination, Heras stood up with trembling limbs as the flames subsided.
As for the others—ordinary people like Capin had been burned to charcoal, Parker had succumbed to the poison before the explosion, and Katie, though alive, was barely holding on.
"It's so hard to kill them... Fortunately, I came well-prepared,"
Klein sighed.
As a spirit, Klein had been mostly unscathed by the explosion. He used the
Nightmare Badge
he had acquired from the
Eye of Wisdom
gathering once again, pulling all the remaining survivors in the villa into a dream world, severing their last chance of escape.
Under normal circumstances, the Beyonders might have forced themselves awake from the dream. But due to their critical injuries, they had lost that ability entirely.
With a snap of his fingers, Klein unleashed a series of air bullets, ending the evil lives of the remaining human traffickers. Then, without delay, he turned and flew toward the underground entrance.
Belis, who had been guarding the underground prison, had just woken up from the dream when he saw the black-crowned ghost descending upon him. Panicking, he raised his high-pressure steam rifle to fire.
But the iron-black glove on Klein's spectral hand glowed ominously, and in a blur of motion, it struck Belis's head with unerring precision.
With the explosion destabilizing the building, the range of Klein's
"Ninth Law"
prohibition had weakened, allowing him to utilize the iron-black glove's full capabilities.
Klein glanced at Belis's headless corpse, grimacing slightly at the messy remains. Fortunately, being in a spirit state spared him from the visceral reality.
With the guard defeated and the key item—the
Iron-Black Metal Glove
—in his possession, Klein smoothly unlocked the prison doors one by one, freeing Daisy and the other captive girls.
Some bravely ran towards the streets like Daisy, who had only recently been kidnapped and had not undergone any conditioning or training.
It was only after escaping the oppressive villa that the girls, trembling with relief and fear, turned back to look.
On the roof of the now-ruined mansion stood a figure cloaked in black armor, wearing iron-black gloves and a black crown.
With a dramatic swish, the figure's black cape fluttered in the wind before disappearing from view.
"Daisy!"
A familiar voice broke through the chaos. Daisy's eyes lit up as she saw her sister, Freya, running towards her with tears streaming down her face. Behind Freya were two elegant women, one tall and the other short.
"Freya!"
Daisy sprinted forward and embraced her sister tightly, both of them sobbing in relief.
Watching the heartfelt reunion, Xio and Hazel exchanged warm smiles.
"This is Mr. Fool's Favored One,"
Xio thought, her spirituality stirring as if touched by something profound.
At that moment, a gust of wind blew through, and a figure streaked across the sky at high speed. Almost simultaneously, an illusory door materialized in mid-air, and from it stepped a handsome man in a tailored suit.
Xio recognized them both instantly—one was the
Saint of the Augustus Family
, whom she had recently met at MI9 while reporting to Her Highness Vera, and the other was the Archbishop of the Backlund Diocese of the Church of the Storm,
"Spellsinger of God" Ace Snake.
...
In Bayam, the night market on Beldan Street was alive with energy. Bars, shops, restaurants, and amusement parks stayed open all night, drawing colonists, locals, adventurers, and even pirates.
Ebner and Helene stepped out of their carriage and into the lively streets, only to be approached by a shifty-looking man.
The man discreetly pulled out a small bottle and whispered, "Want some, sir? Only ten pounds."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 448: The Calculations Behind the Scenes
chapters.content:
Chapter 448 - The Calculations Behind the Scenes
This scene, this wording, this tone—it was exactly like the "scalpers" at train stations in his previous life before the real-name system was enforced. For a brief moment, Ebner felt a wave of nostalgia and disorientation wash over him.
Snapping back to reality, Ebner activated his Pure White Eye with a mix of curiosity and familiarity, wanting to see what exactly this man was trying to sell and why it was priced so steeply.
But moments later, Ebner's mouth twitched slightly as he realized the truth.
Do I look like a weakling?
Although his face appeared a bit pale from an entire afternoon of crafting mystical items, it was clearly not the pallor of frailty.
Moreover, the so-called potion wasn't just diluted—it was far inferior to the Health Potion Karen specially prepared for Russell. On top of that, it contained addictive substances.
Was this aimed at me? Or did Helene give herself away somehow?
Ebner glanced at Helene. She was wearing a hat that concealed her hair color and hairstyle, a veil that covered most of her face, and her demeanor was slightly altered after spending an entire day boiling water.
No... it's unlikely someone from the "Admiral of Ailment" could recognize her this quickly. In other words, this man is targeting me. But why?
Adjusting his glasses, Ebner smiled calmly and asked, "This medicine—it's from the pharmacist across the alley from the Red Theater, isn't it?"
The man's eyes widened in surprise. "You knew?"
He quickly masked his reaction, replacing it with a greasy smile. "Sir, since you know about this, you must also know that the master only produces a limited amount each day... But lucky for you, I have special access to extra stock."
Really? Darkwill, you've stayed true to your roots, haven't you? And your so-called 'special access' is just diluting the potion tenfold, isn't it?
Ebner suppressed a sigh and said plainly, "Ten pounds is far too steep. Eight pounds per bottle—how many do you have? I'll take them all."
The vendor was visibly taken aback by Ebner's generosity but quickly composed himself, eyes gleaming with greed. "It's always a pleasure to do business with someone decisive! Alright, I'll take a loss here—ten bottles, all yours. Think of it as the start of a good friendship."
So, diluted ten times over, huh? I wonder if the 'special additives' were also multiplied tenfold...
Feigning satisfaction, Ebner nodded. "Alright... but I don't have that much cash on hand. Follow me to my carriage, and I'll get the money."
As he spoke, he cast a glance at Helene.
Though she didn't fully grasp Ebner's plan, Helene was sharp enough to follow his lead. With a faint pout, she clung to Ebner's arm and complained in a coquettish tone about her wasted shopping time. Ebner comforted her with soft words, and she eventually relented, though her glare at the vendor carried a hint of hostility.
—Before heading out, Helene had changed from her maid attire and agreed with Ebner to play the role of a "lover" while they were outside.
The vendor chuckled, attempting to smooth over the tension. "Madam, you'll be the one who benefits most from your husband's purchase."
As he spoke, his gaze lingered on Helene—a mix of lust, regret, and thinly veiled anticipation.
Helene's brows furrowed in disgust. She had seen these kinds of lecherous stares before—in Trier, in Intis, and on the open seas. She thought she had grown numb to them, yet each time, they still made her skin crawl.
What kind of potion was that? How would it benefit me? And why did Detective Brian ask me to play along with this act?
While these questions spun in her mind, the trio arrived at the carriage parked on the next street. Ebner nodded to the driver, a manor servant who had stayed behind with the vehicle.
Without hesitation, Ebner grabbed the vendor by the arm, his grip iron-tight, and said in a tone that brooked no refusal, "Come inside to collect your payment."
It was only then that the vendor realized something was wrong. He hesitated, but the aura emanating from Ebner—the weight of authority and cold decisiveness—reminded him of his own terrifying boss. Fear gripped him, and his fleeting thoughts of escape dissolved into reluctant compliance.
He followed Ebner into the carriage obediently, his earlier bravado completely extinguished.
Just now, in the downtown area, it had been inconvenient for Ebner to use his abilities, wary of being detected by any high-level Beyonders who might be lurking nearby. However, now that he had reached this secluded "parking spot," such concerns no longer restrained him.
Combining "Majesty," "Bribery-Charm," and "Guidance" in the spiritual realm, Ebner easily bent the man's will to his own.
Although Helene, walking alongside him, had no idea what kind of abilities Ebner had used, she was deeply grateful to have witnessed the transformation in the man. She felt relieved that she had wisely signed the "contract" under fair terms. If she had recklessly pushed Detective Brian to use his powers back then, she might have unknowingly signed away her freedom entirely!
With that thought lingering, Helene silently followed Ebner into the carriage. After all, she was technically his "captive." Staying close and avoiding any misunderstandings seemed the safest course of action.
Inside the carriage, after Helene stepped in, Ebner sealed off the space using his spiritual power. He then simulated the "Whip of Pain", letting it hang menacingly in the man's mind as he whispered:
"Who are you?
Why did you approach me?
Who gave you these instructions?"
...
Meanwhile, on the second floor of the Fragrant Leaf Bar, a middle-aged man with the distinct look of a Bayam native knocked on the office door before entering. Inside sat the bar's hidden mastermind, "Giant Warrior" Ozil.
The man respectfully reported, "'Sea Serpent' has made contact with the target and successfully sold the item to him."
Ozil, a tall and broad-shouldered older man, swirled the wine glass in his hand and chuckled. "So the so-called 'Hero Detective' is overrated after all.
"But it's to be expected. He rose to fame at such a young age, and he's clearly a romantic soul. Even coming to Bayam on vacation, he brought his lover along... Naturally, a man like that would need
that kind of medicine
to keep up appearances."
He smirked, his eyes gleaming with ambition. "Looks like we'll soon have the 'Fragrant Manor' in our grasp."
The subordinate hesitated briefly before mustering the courage to ask, "Boss, if you want that manor so badly, why don't we just capture him outright and deal with it directly? Why go through all this trouble?"
Ozil raised an eyebrow and let out a long sigh. "I've had my eyes on that manor for quite some time, but its previous owner holds significant influence. Even the people above me warned me not to act recklessly, despite its long period of abandonment.
"Now it has a new owner... but who knows what relationship this 'Hero Detective' has with the previous master of the Aroma Manor? It's too risky to move openly. Instead, we'll make him dependent—hook him on the potion, drain his finances slowly, and finally, leave him with no choice but to sell the manor to us willingly."
After explaining his reasoning, Ozil shifted his tone, issuing a stern command: "Don't rush this operation. If he starts suspecting something and gets someone to cleanse his body of the potion's effects, all our efforts will be wasted. Tell 'Sea Serpent' not to administer doses too frequently or in quick succession. We want the addiction to creep in subtly so he doesn't notice until it's too late."
"Understood, Boss!"
...
Above the gray fog, after confirming the safety of Daisy and Miss Judgment through divination, Klein shifted his gaze to the three Beyonder Characteristics that radiated intense spiritual light, as well as an iron-black metal glove.
"This time, we've truly gained a lot,"
he mused with satisfaction.
...
Meanwhile, at MI9 Headquarters, Her Highness Vera sat across from Xio and sighed as she shook her head.
"I originally hadn't planned to bring you along on the mission to the Southern Continent...
"But for now, it's better if you stay out of the spotlight."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 449: Investigation and Speculation
chapters.content:
Chapter 449 - Investigation and Speculation
"Southern Continent?" This was the first time Xio had heard of such a place, and she looked at Vera with confusion.
"I received a mission a few days ago to escort a valuable item to a colony in the Southern Continent... There might be danger along the way, so I hadn't planned on bringing you with me. However, the Capim case is far more complicated than it seems. If I'm not in Backlund, I can't guarantee your safety..."
Vera paused briefly, refraining from elaborating further, before continuing, "You should stay in the dormitory at headquarters tonight. Tomorrow morning, say your goodbyes to your friends, pack your luggage, and meet me at the train station. We'll depart for Pritz Harbor at 1 PM."
Xio could feel Her Highness Vera's genuine concern, and her heart warmed slightly. However, after pursing her lips, she couldn't stop herself from asking, "Behind Capim... are there people from our MI9? Or perhaps high-ranking officials within the kingdom?"
"All plans were carried out in Mr. Fool's Kingdom, and the ones who took direct action were Mr. Fool's Favored Ones. I shouldn't be under suspicion... Yet, Her Highness Vera still believes they might target me. Could it be because of my father?
Is this enormous force, entrenched within MI9 and even the upper echelons of the kingdom, the true mastermind behind framing my father?"
Xio couldn't stop her thoughts from spiraling.
"You are not yet qualified to know so much," Vera said, shaking her head and refusing to answer.
The response echoed what Ebner had been telling her all along.
What had her father discovered? Why did Capim kidnap that girl? Was she meant to be sacrificed to an evil god?
After a brief silence, Xio nodded. "I understand."
"After this escort mission, you should have accumulated enough contributions to obtain the final material for advancing to 'Judge'."
Noticing Xio's gloomy expression, Vera added the reminder with a faint smile, which managed to lift Xio's spirits slightly.
After Xio left the office, Vera stood up and walked to the window. Her gaze fell upon the sprawling palaces and the towering Gothic clock tower dominating the skyline of Queens. She let out a faint sigh:
"Black Emperor? Is such sneaky, deceitful behavior truly worthy of that title?
"Let alone His Majesty Solomon... You can't even compare to Roselle's boldness."
...
Following Vera's advice, Xio didn't return home. Instead, she headed straight to the MI9 dormitory. She was no stranger to the place, having spent countless nights here after long interrogations.
After a quick wash, Xio lay down on the narrow bed. Her thoughts drifted back to the events surrounding the Capim Villa incident.
Two Saints had suddenly descended. Mr. Fool's Favored Ones had appeared on the rooftops as if deliberately provoking them, only to vanish without a trace under the Saints' watchful eyes.
The mangled bodies in the villa, tarot cards scattered across the remains...
The overwhelming blessing of Mr. Fool's Angel that had shielded her and Hazel...
The terrifying moment when they were almost taken away for "interrogation."
"If Her Highness Vera hadn't intervened personally, I'd probably still be in the custody of the Augustus Family's Saint."
These thoughts swirled in Xio's mind until, slowly, she drifted off to sleep.
She wasn't sure how long she had been sleeping when suddenly, she saw a sacred and radiant light.
The light condensed into a humanoid figure, twelve pairs of dark wings unfurling majestically from its back.
The wings folded inward, wrapping her in their embrace.
Xio woke with a start, instantly aware that she was dreaming—but not an ordinary dream. She realized that someone had invaded her dream!
She could feel something shadowy and sinister wandering in the gray sky above. Thoughts and memories surged uncontrollably from the depths of her mind, forming vivid scenes in the dream.
Most prominent were the events of the past few weeks:
Receiving a commission from Mr. Skade, investigating alongside Hazel and Freya, and capturing Capim's men who had targeted Hazel.
In her dream, Xio forced herself to remain calm. She focused her mind and attempted to control her thoughts, realizing—much to her relief—that it wasn't as difficult as she had feared.
In East Borough, Xio, whose dream was invaded by a dragon, quickly calmed down, tried to control her thoughts, and found that it wasn't difficult.
So, she hid her memories involving the Tarot Club, leaving only those parts that aligned with her actions in reality.
Of course, to cover up any flaws she might have revealed in front of the Saint, Xio rewrote the events surrounding the death of the man with red spots on his face. She made it seem like she had attempted to break through the restrictions in his mind but failed, and in anger, beat him to death before disguising it as suicide out of fear of punishment.
At that moment, Xio suddenly heard a familiar cold snort, and her dream began to turn chaotic, as if it had lost its guiding force.
She recognized this as a sign that the intruder had left.
After forcibly escaping the dream, although Xio was fully awake, she kept her eyes closed and maintained her sleeping posture to mislead potential enemies. She quietly thought:
Was that last voice... Her Highness Vera?
Can the Disciplinary Paladin also detect dream invasions?
...
In a villa not far from the Capim family estate in the Cherwood Borough, a mature middle-aged man with golden eyes looked at the embarrassed figure emerging from the void and asked with a smile, "What happened? Even entering the dream of a Sequence 7 is dangerous now?"
"Is Her Highness Vera really just a Disciplinary Paladin? If she hadn't recognized who I was, I might have been killed on the spot..." the embarrassed figure said in a low voice.
"Vera is His Majesty's youngest and most favored sister. It's entirely normal for her to carry some powerful magical items or protective charms." The middle-aged man chuckled and shook his head before asking, "Did you discover anything?"
"No... The girl from the Dere family actually knows nothing. Even Capim's men provoked them... The reason she looked uneasy when she saw you was probably because she had just accidentally killed someone."
The embarrassed figure recounted what he had seen in Xio's dream and added, "I've also verified these details in the dream of the girl named Hazel... It's essentially the same. However, there was a very powerful spirit beside Hazel... likely a creation of the Church of Mother Earth. My current embarrassment is partly thanks to it."
"A powerful spirit? What did it look like?" The middle-aged man's thoughts drifted to the black figure that had suddenly vanished, and he asked with a flash of insight.
The person who had invaded Xio's dream shook his head and said, "It couldn't have been that. It lacked the power of the Black Emperor."
"You should be aware that the ghost that attacked Capim carried the aura of a true Black Emperor. That's the main reason His Majesty ordered a thorough investigation."
The middle-aged man nodded silently, then sighed:
"That ghost's anti-divination ability is incredibly strong. Neither I, Snake, nor any other lords in the military skilled in divination have managed to uncover any useful clues... Even when we focused on the lost Roselle's Grip, we failed.
"So, the only clues we have are the Joker, who scattered tarot cards in the Lanevus case, and the Iron Man, who also appeared back then.
'Dark Emperor', 'Iron Man', 'Joker'... Is this some new organization, using tarot cards as their symbol and posing as so-called 'heroes'?"
...
After interrogating the man who sold the medicine, Ebner and Bayam roughly understood why they had been targeted. In short, their deterrent power wasn't sufficient, and they occupied a manor that others coveted, drawing unwanted attention.
I originally planned to keep a low profile during my time in Bayam... Why must you force my hand?
Ebner sighed, used the Nightmare ability to put the drug seller into a deep sleep, then lifted the spiritual blockade and opened the carriage door.
Helene, who had listened to the entire interrogation, stepped out of the carriage and couldn't help but ask, "Mr. Bryan, where are you going?"
"To 'solve' the problem, of course!" Ebner turned around and gave a "kind" smile.
(End of this Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 450: Ebner’s Attack
chapters.content:
Chapter 450 - Ebner's Attack
"Solve" the problem? Is he going to "solve" the person who created the problem?
Helene couldn't help but recall the detective in front of her, who had cleanly eliminated the "Trickster" just a few days ago. The thought lingered in her mind.
However, such methods were only possible for powerful pirate leaders like him and Tracy.
If I had that kind of strength... maybe I could do my part to revive my family...
Helene felt a pang of envy. This goal had been her driving force for so long. After all, there had never been a female demigod in the history of the Sauron family.
Noticing Helene had drifted into thought, Ebner coughed lightly to bring her attention back. He then instructed, "Take the man in the carriage back to the manor. He's just an ordinary person and won't pose a threat to you. I trust you won't let him escape easily... Also, inform the butler that I might not return until tomorrow morning."
At this point, Ebner looked at Helene with a rare apologetic expression and added, "I'm sorry, the 'reward' I promised you will have to wait. It seems you won't be able to continue shopping today."
Helene was caught off guard by Ebner's politeness. She waved her hand casually and replied, "It's okay. You can make it up to me later."
Ebner nodded slightly, said nothing more, and disappeared into the night.
Watching him leave, Helene hesitated for a moment but ultimately chose not to violate the "contract" witnessed by the gods. She obediently directed the coachman to take her and the medicine seller back to Fragrant Manor.
On the other side, Ebner, hidden in the shadows, watched the carriage head towards the suburbs and nodded in satisfaction. Then, imitating the abilities of a "Faceless Man," he transformed into the appearance of the medicine seller. His clothing also shifted to match the other man's attire.
This transformation was a simplified application of the secret technique "Roselle's Golden Armor Technique." While the armor created wasn't as sturdy as the original and lacked special abilities, its shape could be adjusted freely.
At least next time I dress up as "Doctor Strange," I won't have to ask Xio to sew costumes for me overnight...
Ebner thought self-deprecatingly.
Using the information he had extracted during the interrogation, Ebner walked purposefully towards a house near the bustling night market.
Reaching his destination, he knocked on the door in a specific pattern. Moments later, the heavy wooden door creaked open, revealing the face of a middle-aged Bayam native.
"Mr. Tula," Ebner said, lowering his head and speaking in a fake respectful tone.
"Come in," Tula replied curtly, stepping aside and leading Ebner into the dimly lit living room.
The room was shrouded in shadows, with only faint crimson light filtering through the window. Yet, Tula moved confidently to the sofa and sat down without hesitation.
An extraordinary with night vision abilities,
Ebner deduced silently.
Activating his "Pure White Eye," Ebner mimicked the "Sheriff's" sensing ability to scan the house for any hidden threats.
Since he wasn't a true "Sheriff" and couldn't establish a proper "jurisdiction," his simulation lacked precision. However, given that the enemy was unlikely to anticipate this specific detection method, it was sufficient.
"'Sea Snake,' what's the situation? Explain in detail," Tula said, lighting a cigarette and taking a deep puff.
But Ebner had already confirmed the house was empty except for Tula. It was a pure meeting point.
When he heard the question, Ebner made no move to respond. Instead, he raised his head, and twin bolts of dazzling lightning flickered in his pupils.
"Spiritual Piercing!"
Tula's face twisted in agony as the spiritual attack struck him. But his combat experience kicked in—he gritted his teeth, rolled to the side, and reached for his revolver.
However, Ebner had anticipated this move. When Tula's hand reached into his gun bag... it was empty.
Tula was stunned, thinking that the revolver had fallen off during the tumbling, and looked around hurriedly. At this moment, the revolver he cherished so much was already aimed at his head.
Stealing...
Ever since he obtained a sealed item with the characteristics of a "Dream Stealer" that could only exist in dreams in the Dream Labyrinth Tower, Ebner had been "analyzing" the ability within it while accumulating points. He used it for the first time today, and the effect was quite good.
As for why Tula did not choose to escape in pain but tried to fight back, and why he decided to look for his beloved gun after discovering that it was missing... it was naturally because he had been "combat hypnotized" by Ebner.
Tula, who had a gun pointed at his head, was not panicked at all. He calmly asked, "You are not 'Sea Snake'... Who are you? The detective?"
"If you kill me now, Lord Strongman Ozil will not let you go."
'Strongman Ozil'? You're threatening me with that loser who was killed instantly by Gehrman? Ebner sneered, not wanting to waste time talking to him. After knocking him out, he used his 'Dream Walker' ability to enter Tula's subconscious and guided him step by step to reveal the secrets hidden deep inside his mind through the different changes in his dreams.
Unlike the 'Sea Snake', who had done many bad things but was not sentenced to death, this native man, Tula, was a complete villain and butcher! There were hundreds of innocent people who died by his hands, including many of his own people who once trusted him...
In other words, this scumbag relied on the lives of his own people to please the 'Strongman Ozil' and gained the other party's trust as a native.
So, after finding out where Ozil was going to spend the night, Ebner used Tula's revolver without hesitation to end his sinful life.
After extracting the extraordinary characteristics, Ebner threw the scumbag's body into the fireplace, set it on fire, and burned it to ashes.
Then he picked up the Beyonder that was as beautiful as the night sky, opened his "Pure White Eye," and analyzed it briefly, determining that it was a 'Midnight Poet'.
That guy smoked in the living room without turning on the lights late at night. Could he be suppressing his poetic inspiration?
It's a pity that you are uneducated!
After knowing that Tula could only barely recognize all the Loen letters through the "guidance" just now, Ebner complained and then opened the "Dream Door" to send the characteristics into the lounge of the Dream Labyrinth Tower.
After doing all this, Ebner returned to the dark house without any lights, thinking to himself:
Judging from the original work and the information we've obtained so far, "Strongman" Ozil should be a Beyonder of the "Warrior" Path, either a "Pugilist" or a "Weapon Master"...
However, since he was worthy of being the host of Bayam's underground gathering, he must have some powerful items in his hands. Otherwise, he would definitely not be able to suppress those vicious pirates... In the original book, because it was an encounter, he had no time to prepare, so he was killed instantly by Gehrman...
Moreover, his background must be clarified... After all, killing him might lead to an investigation by the people behind him...
The "Warrior" path... Could it be that the "Vice Admiral Dusk" is behind him?
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 451: The story and the killing
chapters.content:
Chapter 451 - The story and the killing
Well... with my strength, even if it was a sneak attack, even if Strongman Ozil had some powerful items hidden, I could probably kill him...
So, the key is how to deal with the aftermath after killing him?
As his thoughts raced, Ebner had a rough plan in mind... it was to "kill with a borrowed knife." Although the plan was simple, he couldn't think of a better way at the moment.
As for how to "borrow," it is naturally to frame someone... No, to be more precise, it is to find someone to take the blame.
...
In a villa at No. 36 Haifang Street, Strongman Ozil walked into the study next door and sat down at the desk.
"I always feel like something is wrong... but maybe it's my illusion..." Ozil frowned, then stood up, walked to the bookshelf, rearranged a few books, and opened a secret compartment hidden behind them.
Inside the compartment was an ancient notebook made of animal skin and an ordinary crystal ball sealed by many runes.
Ozil carefully avoided touching the compartment containing the crystal ball and took out only the notebook.
Stroking its surface, he couldn't help but fall into memories.
More than ten years ago, when he was a pirate captain, he once intercepted and killed a team of Nighthawks.
This notebook and the crystal ball in the secret compartment were spoils obtained during that battle... well, so were the recipes for the Sleepless and the Midnight Poet.
Of course, with his strength, the reason he succeeded was that the team had the bad luck to encounter an attack by the King of Immortality fleet beforehand. The elites in the team had been left behind to cover the retreat...
Afterward, through the spiritual communication of his subordinates, Ozil learned that the team of Nighthawks had discovered a tomb during their mission. The notebook and crystal ball had been retrieved from there.
They originally wanted to bring the two items back to the Church of the Evernight, but unfortunately, after exiting the mausoleum, they seemed cursed and encountered increasingly severe accidents until they all perished.
After that ambush, Ozil was afraid that the Church of the Evernight would find out about him, so he changed his name, went ashore, and became the owner of the Amyris Leaf Bar.
Later, he hired an appraiser to examine the crystal ball and learned that it could bring disasters severe enough to kill designated people.
