Special operations? Isn't that based on the strategy Klein suggested to Captain Gawain? It's only been a few months, and it's already making waves in the colonies? If Klein knew about this, he'd definitely be thrilled...
Leonard quickly composed himself and raised a question, "Since the military and the Rose School of Thought both have demigods involved, wouldn't our strength be insufficient to interfere with their actions?"
The Lightning Badge shook his head and replied, "Our task is to figure out their objective, not to stop them. Moreover, in East Balam, both the Church of Storms and the Church of the Evernight Goddess have Saints stationed here, so you don't need to worry too much about safety. On the surface, we're investigating the mysterious Doctor Strange who enjoys answering questions. I believe the military won't go out of their way to target us."
"I understand," Leonard said with a nod, signaling that he had no further questions. He then quietly listened as the others raised their concerns.
After about ten minutes, once all questions had been answered, the Lightning Badge ended the meeting with a final reminder, "Our
Trident
will set sail at 3 a.m. sharp. Don't be late."
After the meeting, Leonard said goodbye to Captain Sost and hurried to the Amyris Leaf Bar. There, he dragged the sleeping "Sea Serpent" Welf into a dream and began questioning him. However, to his surprise, Welf woke up the moment Leonard asked about the identity of the person backing him.
Standing outside the bar, Leonard frowned and muttered under his breath, "Old man, what's going on?"
"It's the power of a contract notarized by the God of Knowledge. For it to be this effective, it seems the person backing Welf is likely a Blessed of the God," the ancient voice of Pales Zoroast echoed in his mind.
.....
In the Southern Continent, in the city of Gulain, Ebner had just walked out of the Wall family residence after a busy night. He planned to have breakfast with Xio when he heard a newsboy shouting, "Extra! Extra! Lieutenant Colonel Hall leads 36 warriors to defeat a thousand Intis troops!"
(Chapter End)

chapters.title: Chapter 495: Doctor Strange’s Retribution
chapters.content:
Chapter 495 - Doctor Strange’s Retribution
Xio had gone out early in the morning to buy a local Balam-style breakfast from a nearby restaurant. She seemed to be in a good mood, humming a tune as she made her way back to the rented inn.
However, the moment she stepped into her room, something felt off. Although this wasn't her "jurisdiction," her Arbiter pathway abilities, which granted extraordinary insight, allowed her to sense subtle irregularities.
"Who's there?" she asked warily.
Her words had just left her lips when Ebner emerged from the shadows. Recognizing him, Xio exhaled in relief.
After shutting the door and using her spirituality to seal the room, she cast him a sideways glance, expressing her annoyance at being startled. Then she asked, "How did you find out I was staying here?"
"You need to trust a detective's expertise. Some traces don't fade overnight," Ebner replied with a pause, before adding with a smile, "And as expected, basic stealth and shadow concealment aren't enough to completely evade an Arbiter's senses at close range."
"I'm already a Judge," Xio corrected him proudly, puffing out her chest. Then, reflecting on what she had sensed, she added, "Actually, I didn't notice your presence directly. I've just become familiar with this room after staying the night, so it wasn't hard to detect something unusual."
Ebner nodded thoughtfully, unsurprised by Xio's recent promotion. Given the dangers of her current mission, it made sense for her to boost her strength by advancing as soon as possible.
Seeing that Ebner had also brought breakfast, Xio placed it together with her own on the table. Picking up a piece of lamb rib coated with chili sauce, she took a bite and asked while chewing, "Why didn't you use Psychological Invisibility just now?"
"Psychological Invisibility can fool even Arbiter pathway demigods—I've confirmed this before. However, precisely because of the Arbiter pathway's sensory blind spots in this area, I suspect the military must have developed countermeasures specifically targeting psychological concealment.
"Instead, they're more likely to overlook something they consider their specialty," Ebner explained, biting into a piece of Balam-style flatbread. He avoided the meat, partly because Xio enjoyed it more and partly because he preferred lighter breakfasts.
When Ebner mentioned Psychological Invisibility fooling Arbiter demigods, he was naturally referring to Admiral Amelius Levitt, who had appeared in the fifth layer of the Dream Labyrinth Tower. At least under conditions where Amelius wasn't being particularly vigilant, and Ebner remained perfectly still, it had worked.
"Even so, you'll have to keep some distance," Xio said after some thought, setting down her lamb rib. "While my escort team doesn't have any overt demigods, I can't be sure there aren't hidden powerhouses following us.
"Also, I have a feeling Princess Vera isn't as simple as she seems. Don't underestimate her just because she's only Sequence 5."
"It's not surprising for a royal princess to carry powerful mystical items," Ebner replied reassuringly. He then pulled out a finely crafted silver card from his pocket and handed it to Xio. Smiling, he said, "That's why I came to find you—to give you this card. With it, I can use the Dream Labyrinth and my Bryan Reversal Descent technique to locate you from hundreds of kilometers away."
"Doctor Strange..." Xio examined the card and immediately recognized the figure depicted on it. Suddenly, everything made sense. "So the strange events in Gulain City over the past two days were your doing?"
"There were also people taking advantage of my name to scam and seduce others... I dealt with them last night," Ebner said, his tone growing colder.
When he first learned that imposters were exploiting his name in the Southern Continent, Ebner had been both amused and exasperated. He didn't mind those merely pretending to be him for flair; after all, the Nighthawks or Mandated Punishers would undoubtedly have a "chat" with such individuals eventually.
But those who used his identity to deceive and exploit others were intolerable. Not only did they tarnish Doctor Strange's reputation, but they crossed Ebner's moral boundaries. As a result, he had intentionally dragged those imposters into his dream world the previous night and "rewarded" them by overloading their minds with excessive knowledge.
Doctor Strange's help came through knowledge, and so did his retribution.
By now, the fraudsters were either insane or reduced to drooling fools.
Xio showed no sympathy for the scammers and instead clapped her hands in delight. She was, however, astonished by Ebner's ability to creatively use the Dream Labyrinth Tower's authority.
It's not just the Dream Labyrinth Tower's authority at play. It also involves the principles of the red star above the gray fog, the White Eye's added weight, the tacit approval of the God of Knowledge, and—of course—a bit of my own brilliance. That's what makes Doctor Strange's methods appear so enigmatic, even godlike.
As Ebner silently reveled in his cleverness, Xio picked up the newspaper he had brought and glanced at the front page headline. She exclaimed in surprise, "Lieutenant Colonel Hall defeats Intis Colonial Army...
"Miss Audrey's last name is 'Hall.' Could this lieutenant colonel be a member of the Earl of East Chester's family?"
This must be Alfred's crowning moment of glory,
Ebner thought slyly.
When he gets back to the Northern Continent, he'll probably lose to his sister's dog in a fight...
While entertaining this amusing thought, he replied casually, "This lieutenant colonel is Miss Audrey's second brother, and like her, he's a Beyonder of the Arbiter pathway. He's probably a Sequence 7 'Interrogator' at the moment."
In the original story, Alfred had already advanced to "Disciplinary Paladin" by the time he returned to the Northern Continent, but that was over a year later. It was impossible for him to have reached that level now.
"You seem to know Miss Audrey's family quite well," Xio remarked, casting a sidelong glance at Ebner before picking up another lamb rib slathered in chili sauce and tearing into it with her teeth.
...
In a military camp on the outskirts of the Pas River Valley, a man in a crisp military uniform sat at his desk, writing a report. His golden hair was swept back at an angle, his azure eyes as clear as a lake beneath a sunny sky. Tall and well-proportioned, he exuded an unshakable air of authority with every movement, a natural charisma that made him seem commanding even without soldiers flanking him.
Just then, a dark-haired, brown-eyed man in his late twenties entered the tent, holding a newspaper in one hand. "Alfred, you're famous!" he exclaimed.
Alfred glanced up, shook his head regretfully, and said, "I'm afraid we'll soon have to leave the special operations unit."
"Why?" the dark-haired man asked curiously, stepping further into the tent.
"Because as long as I remain in this unit, it will lose its anonymity. The enemy will no longer overlook us, and many of our surprise tactics will become impossible to execute. For a special operations force, fame itself marks failure." Alfred put down his pen and sighed.
"Is that an insight you came up with?" the brown-eyed man asked, casting a glance at the resignation letter lying on Alfred's desk.
"No... It's a suggestion written to the military by a knight named Gawain. He has a deeper understanding of special operations than someone like me, who's merely a frontline commander. Truly a knight of remarkable experience. Haha, it's said that one of his apprentices had a lot of creative ideas, many of which proved highly effective in practice." Alfred spoke with genuine respect for the knight named Gawain.
"So there are still knights from the old era who haven't been completely outpaced," the dark-haired man said with a click of his tongue. "It seems their military theories still hold some value. But why didn't they recruit his apprentice into the army?"
"I heard that apprentice died in battle while defending his hometown... The enemy was some mysterious organization," Alfred replied with a hint of regret. "Otherwise, I'd have used all my connections to bring him under my command and nurture him."
"What a pity," the brown-eyed man lamented before changing the subject. "Alfred, I came here today with some good news."
"Don't keep me in suspense, Pagni," Alfred said, shooting his friend a glance.
The man named Pagni pulled an iron box from his pocket, grinning. "Your luck is amazing. Just after you earned your accolades, the 'Gondola's Golden Feather' you needed conveniently showed up.
"Haha, I bought this from a naval officer aboard the newly arrived
Covenant
battleship in Gulain. It cost me a full 3,500 pounds to get him to part with it."
Alfred's azure eyes reflected the golden glow of the feather inside the box. Suppressing his excitement, he said steadily, "Don't worry, you won't lose out. I'll pay 4,000 pounds and give you 500 as a broker's fee."
"Deal. Just wire it to my account at the Backlund Bank," Pagni said, handing over the box. "I trust the Hall family's reputation."
"The Hall family never disappoints," Alfred said solemnly as he accepted the box.
"Come on, don't be so serious—we're friends," Pagni said with a wave of his hand. Then, as if remembering something, he hesitated before adding, "By the way, regarding the demigod dragon bones you asked me to investigate, I've come across a lead, though I'm not sure how reliable it is.
"To be precise, a merchant caravan under my family's employ heard some rumors about it in both Feysac and Winter County..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 496: Departure and Plans
chapters.content:
Chapter 496 - Departure and Plans
Since the meeting time was approaching, Xio finished her breakfast and returned to the military port to join Princess Vera and the elite members of the Loen Military Intelligence 9th Division.
Ebner, on the other hand, returned to the underground wine cellar of the Wall family. First, he conducted a simple communication with "Vice Admiral Iceberg" using the "Roselle Séance Technique." Then, after waiting for about ten minutes, a flame-bordered portal appeared on the "transportation altar," and Edwina's figure emerged.
"I've already made arrangements aboard the Golden Dream. We can set off now," Edwina said calmly, dressed in her intricate shirt and dark trousers.
Ebner didn't respond immediately but instead described in detail the series of actions taken by the military and the "Rose School of Thought" that he had learned about.
Although "Vice Admiral Iceberg" had promised to help him hunt the "Finks Lion," the current situation had changed, and it was necessary to explain everything clearly to her.
Edwina listened quietly, took out a small mirror from her pocket, manipulated it for a moment, and then said thoughtfully, "Perhaps Maria's subordinates were able to spot the 'Finks Lion' back then because its lair had been disturbed."
"You mean... the Loen military and the 'Rose School of Thought' might be targeting the original habitat of the 'Finks Lion'?
"Hmm, that does make sense... If that's the case, we should indeed follow behind the military convoy! After all, even if the lion was startled, it wouldn't have gone too far..."
Ebner suddenly understood her reasoning and couldn't help but feel a bit curious about the small mirror Edwina had taken out. Could it be the "prophecy" item bestowed by the God of Knowledge and Wisdom?
Edwina did not explain further. After putting the mirror away, she spoke with conviction: "Since I've promised to help you, I will not go back on my word... Besides, although there may be risks, I'm quite interested in the military's objective."
Lady, we're just going to hunt the 'Finks Lion,' but your curiosity could easily complicate matters...
Though he silently complained, Ebner sincerely expressed his gratitude to Edwina. He then dismantled the "transportation altar" and stored the materials in the resting chamber of the "Dream Labyrinth Tower."
Edwina assumed he was using some "space" type mystical item. Although intrigued, she didn't ask further questions.
Once everything was ready, the two of them simultaneously activated their "invisibility" abilities and left the Wall family home together.
It was worth noting that the head of the Wall family, Mr. Wall himself, had been conscripted by the military and was currently serving as a guide for Xio's team.
The two mid-sequence Beyonders of the Reader Pathway ascended through the spiral staircase, passing through Upper Lip District, Left Cheek District, Left Brow District... until they finally reached the Bald Plateau at the very top of Gulain City.
According to descriptions from Loen newspapers and travelogues, this location marked the boundary between civilization and barbarism, between prosperity and desolation. Beyond this plateau lay the forests of the wild South Continent, no longer part of the colonial city but the territory of native tribes.
—Although large numbers of native residents also lived in Gulain City, along with the chaotic and impoverished slums, the city as a whole still operated within the order established by the Loen colonial military.
Due to earlier delays, Ebner and Edwina lagged behind Xio's group by about an hour. However, they were not concerned. Instead, they waited for another ten minutes to ensure a safe distance before officially starting their journey.
...
In the fifth level of the "Dream Labyrinth Tower," within the Tingen scenario.
Klein arrived at the agreed location just in time to see Sharon, holding up the hem of her Gothic-style dress, leaping and bounding across the rooftops with a speed that rivaled a steam locomotive.
This... compared to her mysterious appearances from mirrors, Sharon's current style is entirely out of character...
Klein's mouth twitched slightly as he silently ridiculed the sight.
A "Werewolf" and a refined young lady just don't go together...
When Sharon finally landed before him and resumed her emotionless "doll" state, Klein asked, "Do you want to change into something more suitable?"
"Something easier for running and jumping, perhaps?"
"That's not necessary," Sharon replied with an unchanged expression. Then, her calm, blue eyes met Klein's as she added, "This is a dream."
A dream... are you implying that your appearance can be altered freely through some method?
Klein mused.
I mean, with the help of the Gray Fog, I could do it. But if you really had that ability, why were you still holding up your dress while running earlier?
Sharon seemed to notice Klein's internal grumbling. She pursed her lips slightly and explained, "I'm not proficient yet."
Ah, that makes sense.
Klein nodded in understanding. Letting go of these minor, irrelevant details, he began recounting his earlier experiences to Sharon. "Mr. Azik wasn't at Hoy University. According to the other professors, he left Tingen a few days ago."
"The Nighthawks received reports of ghostly activity. They'll arrive in an hour," Sharon shared her findings. After a brief pause, she added softly, "He's not an ordinary demigod."
Klein nodded in agreement with her judgment.
If Mr. Azik were just an ordinary demigod, this scenario wouldn't have excluded him... He either has a level of authority too high to simulate or possesses power that disrupts the balance!
Regardless of which was true, it meant Klein's idea of enlisting Mr. Azik's help had failed.
However, Klein wasn't disheartened. Before meeting Sharon, he had revisited the events of Tingen through the Gray Fog, carefully reviewing the situation and performing multiple divinations. After some thought, and by combining his insights into the "Dream Labyrinth Tower's" apparent rules, he had come up with a new plan.
Klein carefully considered his words before speaking under Sharon's calm gaze, "From the previous levels we've experienced, and given the restrictions placed on our abilities, it's clear that this labyrinth isn't focused on testing our combat prowess. Instead, it examines our ability to gather information, analyze logic, and use intelligence to solve problems..."
...and our ability to cheat.
Of course, Klein kept the last thought to himself.
Sharon listened silently, nodding faintly to show she agreed with his assessment.
"And I believe this level is no different... Although Linster merging with the Evil God's offspring seems overwhelmingly powerful and impossible to defeat, there must be tools or methods in this scenario designed to counter him!
"Linster hasn't attacked us or Captain Dunn right away, which suggests that the scenario has intentionally given us time to break the deadlock."
"Scenes with high difficulty are still designed to be solvable, even if they seem dire. For example, in the previous level, despite the extreme weather conditions we faced at the start, there was still a path to survival."
After listening to Klein's analysis of their predicament, Sharon remained quiet for a few seconds before speaking, "Ince... and '0-08'?"
"Exactly. I believe the key to solving this lies with '0-08.' Only by obtaining it can we rewrite the situation to our advantage. This also allows us to eliminate one enemy ahead of time, preventing a two-front battle during the final confrontation."
Klein nodded as he organized his thoughts and continued, "Moreover, the '0-08' in this dream scenario doesn't truly possess the power of a Sequence 0 Sealed Artifact. It doesn't have a high enough level of authority; it's merely mimicking abilities within this dream. So, its writings only affect entities within this dream scenario. They can't influence us directly."
"And Linster, having chosen to merge with the Evil God's offspring, has become a part of this dream. He is subject to its effects," Klein concluded.
"Are you sure?" Sharon's icy blue eyes locked onto Klein as she asked concisely.
"I'm sure," Klein replied firmly.
Before meeting Sharon, Klein had tried divining Ince's location within the dream through the Gray Fog. To his surprise, the answer had come to him with remarkable clarity. He immediately realized that the "0-08" in this scenario, as he had suspected, was merely a fabricated imitation without enough authority to disrupt his divination from the Gray Fog.
Only after confirming this through a series of divinations did Klein finalize the plan he just laid out.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 497: Rainy Night
chapters.content:
Chapter 497 - Rainy Night
In the dreamscape version of Tingen City, within a dimly lit room, "Corpse Collector" Frye, "Sleepless" Royale Reideen, and "Midnight Poet" Seeka Teown lay unconscious on the floor. The sealed artifact under Seeka's charge, the "Mutated Sun Brooch," was now in Sharon's hands.
She carefully examined the sealed artifact before handing it over to Klein.
Without delay, Klein set up a ritual, recited the incantation, and began crafting his once-reliable trump card: the "Sun Flame Charms."
This time, however, Klein was significantly stronger and more knowledgeable in mysticism than he had been during his time in Tingen. As a result, he successfully crafted three charms before feeling his spirituality nearly drained.
He calmly inspected the three Sun Flame Charms in his hands.
The golden hue on their surfaces had dulled slightly, the engravings were ancient and intricate, and a warm, soothing sensation seeped through them, flowing into his skin...
Everything seemed identical to the charms he had crafted back in Tingen.
"But I can't shake the feeling that these are fake... This scenario couldn't even simulate the authority of a '0-08,' let alone conjure a real drop of divine blood. So, they're likely just dreamscape props that only work here?"
With this thought, Klein decided to conduct an experiment. After politely excusing himself to Sharon, he brought the Mutated Sun Brooch and one of the charms into the washroom.
Then, leaving the other two charms behind, he ascended to the Gray Fog with the brooch and single charm in hand.
The moment he entered the ancient palace above the Gray Fog, Klein sharply noticed the energies within both the charm and the sealed artifact rapidly dissipating. Within just one or two seconds, the items became ordinary objects devoid of any mystical power. Shortly after, their very existence grew unstable, as if they could vanish at any moment.
This feels familiar... Right! The "Ninth Law" charm Mr. Tower gave me behaved similarly, except its energy dissipated more slowly...
Klein pondered.
Could Mr. Tower also be a climber of the Dream Labyrinth Tower? But how did he manage to bring items out of the scenarios and keep them stable for three minutes?
Since Klein and Sharon had gained access to the tower through Linster's unauthorized methods, they lacked many of the permissions regular climbers enjoyed. As a result, Klein remained unaware of the tower's point system and the ability to exchange points for items.
I suppose it makes sense. If we could exchange points for escape charms, Linster's painstakingly orchestrated revenge plot would be meaningless.
Hmm, after we clear this level and deal with Linster, I'll have The World find an opportunity to reach out to Mr. Tower... That "Four-Leaf Clover" incident I saw during my dream divinations might indeed stem from one of the Dream Labyrinth Tower's scenarios... I remember stopping my investigation back then due to a dreadful premonition.
While Klein was lost in thought, the strain of depleted spirituality caused a throbbing pain in his temple. Forced to leave the Gray Fog, he returned to the dreamscape reality.
To his surprise, the Mutated Sun Brooch and Sun Flame Charm in his hands reverted to their original state, seemingly regaining their mystical properties as if their earlier decay had been nothing but a dream.
If I stay here too long, I might start confusing dream and reality...
Klein rubbed his temples before trudging back to the room. Looking at Sharon, who silently gazed at him, he said, "I'll leave the rest to you..." Then, his legs gave out, and he collapsed onto the floor, joining the three unconscious Nighthawks in slumber.
Sharon stood silently for a few moments, as if weighing her options. Finally, she placed the Mutated Sun Brooch back in one of the Nighthawks' hands, crouched down, and effortlessly lifted Klein. Without hesitation, she leaped out the window and disappeared into the rainy night at astonishing speed.
....
Southern Continent, South of Pasu Valley, Daniel Valley.
At some point, it had begun to rain. Initially a light drizzle, the rainfall had grown increasingly dense, showing no signs of stopping.
A six-person team trudged through the rain, scouring the valley as if searching for something.
"We've dug up the ground for a mile around, but there's still no sign of the target..." A servant wiped the rain from his face as he reported to a young man standing nearby, also in the rain.
However, after delivering his report, the servant hesitated before adding, "Your Highness, we've been searching here for nearly half a month now. We even checked the lion's lair, but there's still no trace... Are we certain this is the place the military is looking for?"
The young man turned to face him, and the servant clearly saw a pair of narrow, piercing eyes beneath the shimmering water screen shielding the prince from the rain.
This was Prince Monbatten, the youngest child and seventh son of the king, and the younger brother of Prince Edessak. Unlike other members of the Augustus family who followed the "Arbiter" pathway, Monbatten had chosen the path of a "Sailor." However, his specific Sequence remained a mystery to outsiders.
Instead of answering the servant's question, the prince asked, "Irwin, do you know why this place is called Daniel Valley?"
"I've heard it used to be Daniel Lake... but a few hundred years ago, the river flowing through it suddenly changed course, causing the lake to gradually dry up and form this valley," the servant, whose name was Irwin, replied promptly, clearly having done his homework beforehand.
"This place was indeed once called Daniel Lake... but it didn't dry up because the river changed its course. It dried up because the master who created the lake, Daniel, perished!" Prince Monbatten said, scanning his surroundings before speaking.
"Master Daniel?" Irwin, his attendant, found the name familiar but couldn't recall where he had heard it.
"You might've come across his name during ceremonies. After all, the exquisite hydrosols and potions he created are still cherished by many deities," Monbatten said with a faint smile.
"Oh, that Daniel! I always thought the name referred to the Hermes word for 'caring for loved ones,' which is why it earned the favor of the gods. Kind of like how 'Amantha' means 'serenity' in Hermes..." Irwin said with a sudden realization.
"Perhaps Master Daniel did draw inspiration from Hermes when choosing his name. After all, he wasn't from the Northern Continent, so the name must've been adopted later," Monbatten explained. He paused for a moment, then continued before his attendant could press further. "The master was actually the son of a tribal chief here in the Southern Continent. He even joined the Rose School of Thought when it was still dominated by the Temperance Faction. However, after the Chained God gave birth to its progeny and the Indulgence Faction rose to power, he used unknown means to cross the untamed seas—long before any established routes—and traveled to the Northern Continent. He even studied at the universities of Lenburg and published several papers there.
"Later, it seems he discovered something remarkable in the Northern Continent. Fleeing back to the Southern Continent and his homeland, he hid those discoveries here..."
Hearing this, Irwin's face suddenly lit up as he recalled something. He asked in astonishment, "Your Highness, could it be that the item we're carrying is..."
Before he could finish, Prince Monbatten nodded. "That's right. The sealed artifact '1-025' is the legacy left behind by Master Daniel after his death. It also serves as the 'key' to his so-called 'residence.' After extensive investigations by the Ninth Military Intelligence Division, we've determined that his 'residence' is likely hidden somewhere in this valley.
"That's why we didn't hesitate to risk a confrontation with the Church of the Storms and forcibly seized '1-025.'"
"What exactly did Master Daniel discover back then?" Irwin blurted out, only to realize a moment later that his question overstepped his bounds. His voice grew quieter, and he finally lowered his head in apology under the prince's amused gaze. "I'm sorry, Your Highness, I spoke out of turn."
"It's true. That's not something you need to know..." Monbatten remarked. Then, with a meaningful glance at his attendant, he added, "Do you wonder why there are no Beyonders from the Arbiter or Lawyer pathways in our team?"
"Huh?" Irwin's face filled with confusion, but before he could figure it out, the prince gave a resonant order. "Relay everything I just told you to our companions. Now is not the time for complaints. Our comrades in the other teams are risking their lives to cover for us. We must not let their efforts go to waste!"
"Yes, Your Highness!" Irwin straightened up and responded promptly. Though still puzzled, he went off to relay the prince's words to the rest of the team.
Monbatten watched the servant's retreating figure before murmuring to himself, "The trail of the Ghost Empire... Father, is the Black Emperor not enough to shield our family from the calamities to come? Such greed... Would the Seven Gods truly allow this?
"And the responses from the Church of the Storms and the Church of Evernight have been rather strange this time... I clearly..."
....
Meanwhile, elsewhere in Pasu Valley, Jane, who had ventured alone, confronted a spirit guide that was supposed to show her the way. The translucent guide questioned her, "Are you sure this is Daniel Lake? Why do I see nothing here?"
...
To the north of the valley, Xio's squad had just repelled an assault led by a member of the Rose School of Thought commanding local militia forces. Now, amidst the pouring rain, they were regrouping, gathering the scattered soldiers.
"This isn't sustainable..." Princess Vera muttered as she glanced at the faint silhouettes of enemy scouts in the distance. She summoned the guide, Mr. Wall, and instructed, "We'll move south to Daniel Valley. You'll lead the way."
She paused, then turned to the elite squad of Beyonders by her side, adding, "The military has authorized us to retreat there if necessary and regroup with other teams."
Their deliberate and clear direction in marching would serve as a lure, once again drawing the Rose School of Thought's attention.
No one objected to this plan. After all, without proper logistical support, it was impossible to endure the continued harassment of enemy forces.
Meanwhile, Xio reached into her pocket, her fingers tightening around the silver card Ebner had given her.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 498: Various Forces
chapters.content:
Chapter 498 - Various Forces
To the southeast of Pasu Valley, another Loen military squad was similarly ambushed by armed forces led by a member of the Rose School of Thought.
However, this squad was far weaker compared to the one led by Princess Vera. They failed to repel the enemy and were instead routed, forcing them to scatter and flee in different directions.
Colonel Lloyd, his face concealed behind a "golden mask," relied on his formidable strength as a Disciplinary Paladin to carve a path through a barrage of over ten high-pressure steam rifle shots, eventually breaking free from the encirclement.
After confirming that he had shaken off his pursuers, Lloyd finally breathed a sigh of relief. While marveling at his luck—none of the bullets had hit any of his vital points—he oriented himself and began heading toward Daniel Valley.
What Lloyd didn't know was that seven or eight bullets, which were about to strike his vital areas, had been blocked by a thin layer of frost, sparing him from critical injuries.
After he disappeared into the distance, two alluring and scantily clad figures emerged from thin air at the spot where Lloyd had just been standing.
They were none other than the Saintess of White Katarina and Vice Admiral Ailment Tracy.
Although it was already November, the weather in the Southern Continent was the opposite of the Northern Continent, still oppressively hot.
"Are you sure he'll lead us to the military's true objective?" Tracy asked, her gaze following the direction in which Lloyd had fled.
"You should address me as 'Mother' first. That's the bare minimum of proper etiquette," Katarina turned her head slightly, casting a playful glance at her daughter. Her eyes sparkled with amusement as she replied with a faint smile, "If the information you extracted from him that day is accurate... then yes, I'm certain."
Tracy's face instantly turned red with both shame and anger. Glaring at her mother, her voice trembled with rage as she said, "You were the one who controlled my body to do that! It wasn't of my own free will!"
"Heh, I was merely demonstrating how to act like a proper witch. Besides, I didn't actually let him succeed, did I?" Katarina chuckled softly, covering her mouth. Seeing Tracy's expression still clouded with embarrassment and anger, she continued in her melodious, almost song-like voice, "Tormenting yourself in pain is actually good for you.
"Pity that as soon as you regained control of your body, you shoved that colonel away... Tsk tsk, his expression at that moment was absolutely priceless."
"Stop it!" Tracy snapped, cutting her mother off. She took a deep breath, attempting to change the subject. "Do you think what he said that day about eventually regrouping can be trusted?"
"Under the influence of my 'ecstasy,' there's no way he could've lied," Katarina said, her face radiating a saintly glow of purity.
"Then... before we catch up to him, can you finally share your guesses about the military's objectives? When you investigated the military's laboratories, you said you had some ideas, but you didn't tell me. If I don't understand the specifics, I won't rush into action again—there could be enormous risks involved!" Tracy glanced at her mother, who had shifted from her coquettish charm to a sweetly playful demeanor, and asked with a serious expression.
"Call me 'Mother,' and I'll tell you," Katarina replied with a soft laugh, seemingly unbothered by her daughter's tone.
Tracy hesitated for a few seconds, wrestling internally, before finally giving in with an air of resignation. "Mother," she said, her voice dripping with reluctance.
After what happened that day, I swore I'd never acknowledge her again... I'm so spineless! No... this is just a temporary measure to find Helene's whereabouts,
Tracy thought to herself, repeatedly trying to justify her choice.
Noticing her daughter's inner turmoil, Katarina nodded in satisfaction.
Yes, this is exactly the state of mind a Demoness of Affliction should have.
With that, the ageless witch—over a millennium old—used her soft, mesmerizing voice to explain:
"Nearly three months ago, an incident involving the 'Demoness of Affliction' pathway occurred in Backlund. During this incident, the Church of the Storms lost a 'Grade 1' Sealed Artifact... specifically, the one formed by the Sequence 3 trait of the 'Prisoner' pathway, the 'Disciple of Silence.' The artifact's designation is '1-025.'"
"A Sealed Artifact formed from the 'Disciple of Silence'... Is it a 'Cursed Object'?" Tracy asked, visibly surprised. This was her first time hearing about the incident. At the time, she had still been the "Plague Maiden," wandering between the Northern Continent and East Bayam's sea routes, paying little attention to events on land.
The 'Disciple of Silence' was also known as the 'Cursed Object,' a term more familiar to witches skilled in curses.
"Exactly." Katarina nodded as she crouched down, picking up a rock stained with Lloyd's blood. She continued, "That cursed object eventually ended up in the hands of the military. However, instead of returning it, they defied the pressure from the Church of the Storms and kept it for themselves."
"The military's elaborate deployment of so many 'decoys' this time is likely to ensure the safe transport of '1-025' to the Southern Continent. They plan to use it to unlock Daniel's treasure."
Hearing this, Tracy furrowed her long, straight brows and asked in confusion, "Who is Daniel? And why is the Rose School of Thought so determined to contend with the military for his treasure?"
"The Rose School likely isn't after the treasure itself; they just don't want Loen to succeed. After all, Daniel was once a member of the Rose School of Thought, and there are rumors that he was even a disciple of the Chained God. Moreover, '1-025' is the Sealed Artifact formed from his Beyonder characteristic after his death," Katarina explained, her voice taking on a dreamy quality as if lost in reminiscence.
"Speaking of Daniel, he was quite a prominent figure several centuries ago—elegant, knowledgeable, and extraordinarily charismatic. He didn't resemble the image of a prisoner at all... I only met him once. Pity we didn't have the chance to delve deeper into conversation," she sighed wistfully.
Tracy, thoroughly uninterested in her mother's nostalgia, interrupted bluntly, "And what exactly is his treasure?"
"During one of his explorations, Daniel seemed to have uncovered an incredible secret. In the end, he was forced to flee back to the Southern Continent and hide that secret. However, I'm unclear on what that secret actually was or how he ultimately met his demise...
"Oh, by the way, over a hundred years ago, Roselle visited the Southern Continent in his later years in search of Daniel's treasure. No one knows what he found, but it's assumed he didn't succeed," Katarina added.
Restoring her saintly demeanor, she smiled slightly and asked, "So, after hearing all this, are you interested in joining me to uncover the secret that led to the death of a Saint?
"You must have noticed by now that the demigods are all preoccupied with countering each other. At most, our opponents will only be at Sequence 5.
"Once we understand what that secret is, perhaps I'll even take you to catch a glimpse of that little 'Hunter' girl from afar. What do you think?"
Tracy immediately fell into a conflicted silence, while Katarina's lips curled into a knowing smirk.
...
In an underground facility about a hundred miles away from Xio's squad, Edwina was sitting cross-legged, nibbling on dry rations that Ebner had prepared as she slowly recovered the spirituality she had expended during their journey while "invisible."
This temporary underground facility had been created by the Vice Admiral Iceberg using simulated earth-element spells. Edwina's expertise in architecture was evident as the space she carved out was both hidden and comfortable, complete with ventilation. It left Ebner clicking his tongue in amazement.
Although Ebner could also use similar spells when transformed into a giant bear using "Lilith's Tears," he was nowhere near as skilled as Edwina.
Of course, even if he could do it, he wouldn't. Stripping off his clothes to transform into a bear in front of Vice Admiral Iceberg? That would be far from "polite"...
Once I become a Mysticism Magister, I absolutely need to develop a "Mansion Spell" or something similar. Traveling wouldn't feel so miserable,
he mused, letting his thoughts wander as he activated "Pure White Eye" to sense the position of Xio through the Doctor Strange Card.
"They've turned south... Their destination is likely Daniel Valley.
"The same Daniel Valley where the Finks Lion was sighted.
"Edwina, it seems your guess was correct. The military's true destination appears to be there—they're regrouping," Ebner concluded.
Not feeling in top shape...
Finally starting to resolve the plot thread around '1-025.'
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 499: The Approaching Truth
chapters.content:
Chapter 499 - The Approaching Truth
Vice Admiral Iceberg put down the dry ration in her hand and took out the small mirror she carried with her. After a long moment, she finally said,
"We are destined to encounter the Finks Lion."
Ma'am, do you realize that your way of speaking is starting to sound increasingly like a charlatan's?
Ebner silently complained to himself, but on the surface, he appeared thoughtful as he asked,
"Does this mean someone is 'arranging' things again?"
Given the interception of the "King of Immortality" fleet not long ago, his question subtly hinted at whether the God of Knowledge and Wisdom was behind this.
"I don't know." Edwina shook her head, but her expression turned pensive. She deliberated for a moment before saying,
"However, the name 'Daniel Valley' reminds me of someone."
"Who?" Ebner asked curiously.
"The founder of Lenburg University's current academic system, the pioneer of the impact factor system for academic journals, and a master of magical pharmaceutics—Mr. Daniel," Edwina explained, her face showing a trace of reverence.
"This... why have I never heard of his accomplishments?" Ebner pondered for a moment and confirmed that he had no impression of this person—neither from the original story nor from his understanding of this world after transmigrating.
Logically speaking, someone who made such contributions shouldn't be so obscure.
"According to the records I found in the 'Tower of Wisdom,' that master wasn't someone who sought fame. He seemed to 'temper' his desire for recognition, acting very discreetly. Many of his creations were published under other people's names. The only exception was a specific essential oil he named after himself, but most people didn't associate 'Daniel' with his name. They simply assumed it was the Hermesian word for 'care for one's loved ones,'" Edwina briefly introduced what she knew about Daniel.
"Daniel's essential oil?" Ebner mulled it over and finally recalled hearing about an item related to that name.
"Yes, that was indeed one of his works. It's said that rituals dedicated to the Earth Mother or the Evernight Goddess achieve better results when using this particularly fragrant essential oil as a sacrificial offering, especially the former. However, as a follower of the God of Knowledge and Wisdom, I've never personally tested this, so I can't verify its efficacy," Edwina said with a slight nod.
Hearing her description, Ebner suddenly felt a sense of familiarity. After thinking for a moment, he tentatively asked,
"Do you know the formula for Daniel's essential oil?"
All this time, whenever he conducted rituals, he either directed them toward the "Unknown Land" associated with himself, the Fool, or the omnipotent God of Knowledge and Wisdom. Aside from crafting "Holy Night Powder" on the first day of his transmigration, he'd never sought the blessings of the Evernight Goddess or Lilith. Thus, while he'd heard of Daniel's essential oil, he'd never deliberately looked into it.
Edwina nodded lightly and replied,
"I do."
Raising her right hand, she smoothed out a section of the dirt wall beside her with an earth-element spell, creating a makeshift "blackboard," and began explaining earnestly.
Since they had some time to spare, Ebner didn't interrupt her habitual "role-playing" and instead adopted a posture of attentively listening to a lecture.
However, his expression quickly turned peculiar as Edwina detailed the formula. It turned out that this so-called "Daniel's essential oil" was essentially a more advanced version of the "Silica Joy Water" he had once concocted based on a formula from the
Book of the Dead
.
The ingredients were more luxurious, and the preparation methods more intricate, but the underlying principles and approach were identical...
Based on existing information, Jane's ancestor—the Death Consul—likely began "sleeping" in Calderon City around the end of the Fourth Epoch or the beginning of the Fifth Epoch. The
Book of the Dead
must have been written before that...
Could it be... this so-called Master Daniel was merely a "plagiarist" who happened to acquire the Book of the Dead? Is that why he kept such a low profile?
But his other talents were undeniably impressive—his forward-thinking ideas in various fields were remarkable. Wait, could he have been a transmigrator too? A more modest one compared to Roselle? But then why name the essential oil after himself specifically?
The
Book of the Dead
had supposedly remained within the Grant family since the days of "Baron Conva," passed down until it was taken into the Death Consul's tomb by a descendant, and later retrieved by Jane.
Unless this Daniel was also a member of the Grant family, he would have had no chance to see it... Could it really be a coincidence that his ideas overlapped with those of the Death Consul?
Thinking this, Ebner asked Vice Admiral Iceberg, "What was this master's surname?"
"Master Daniel's origins are mysterious—he appeared suddenly and vanished just as suddenly. Even the 'Tower of Wisdom' has no record of his surname, nor does it know where he ultimately went. However, after reading the
Glimpses of the Spirit World
you brought me last time, I suspect he might have been an avatar of one of the Seven Lights of the Spirit World, perhaps even one of the rulers of the Pure Light Brotherhood." Edwina pondered for a moment, then casually erased the "essential oil formula" from the makeshift blackboard and began sketching diagrams and symbols as she spoke.
That is possible... Aside from transmigrators, the Seven Lights do often engage in guiding humanity's development... But that doesn't explain why he was so low-profile in everything else yet insisted on attaching his name to an essential oil...
This question seemed destined to remain unanswered for now, so Ebner set it aside and redirected the conversation to the initial topic. "Why did the name of that valley remind you of this master? Isn't 'Daniel' a fairly common name in Hermes?"
"The common language of the Southern Continent is Dutanese, the tongue of the former Balam Empire. Most place names here are derived from that language... Besides, after Maria told me about the Finks Lion's location, I researched that area. Once I connected the dots, I realized its naming origin aligns with Master Daniel's era," Edwina explained while writing examples of Southern Continent place names on the "blackboard."
"I see... Maybe his sudden disappearance was because he somehow crossed the yet-to-be-navigable Storm Sea and made his way to the Southern Continent..." Ebner's face showed an expression of realization, and he muttered thoughtfully.
"I suspect he originally came from the Southern Continent. His methods of crafting potions, his deliberate 'temperance' in his actions... all bear traces of the Rose School's Temperance Faction. And you mentioned that the military's transport team for a certain item has been repeatedly ambushed by the Rose School. The Seven Lights might have already mastered a way to cross the Storm Sea by then..." At this moment, Edwina fully displayed her logical and analytical abilities as a Beyonder of the Reader pathway.
The Rose School... the military... Wait, I remember the military went as far as to offend the Church of the Storms to forcibly seize "1-025." Even Xio had to return that Wind-blessed Marionette to smooth things over...
And "1-025" is essentially the characteristic of a Sequence 3 "Disciple of Silence"!
Could it be that the item the military is transporting to the Southern Continent with such effort is "1-025"?
Does it have some connection to Daniel? Or could it even be Daniel's legacy?
And is the military trying to use it to locate other relics left behind by Daniel?
With such an extravagant operation... what could it possibly be?
...
At the edge of Daniel Valley, Jane wandered through the rain, scouting the area. Aside from finding traces of human activity, she discovered nothing else.
"Although the Queen called this place Daniel Lake... it really has turned into a valley..."
"The Queen wants me to find the lair of an extraordinary creature called the Finks Lion here. According to her, that lion was deliberately released into the wild here by Emperor Roselle... And she wants me to retrieve a 'card' that might exist in its lair...
"But there's no sign of a lion here at all... let alone a lair. Could it have been hunted by others active in this area?"
Muttering to herself, Jane raised her head to look at the thick layer of clouds above. She frowned slightly, her thoughts silent as she observed the intensifying downpour.
"This rain... it seems to be getting heavier!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 500: Linster’s Faith
chapters.content:
Chapter 500 - Linster's Faith
When Klein awoke in "Tingen City," it was just past 4 a.m., and the sky was still dark. After adjusting to the faint candlelight in the room, he noticed Miss Sharron sitting quietly, reading a book.
"How long was I asleep?" Klein asked hoarsely, his voice still thick from rest.
He glanced around the room, then poured himself a glass of water from the pitcher on the table to soothe his throat—despite this being a dream, the physiological feedback of his body felt incredibly real.
Miss Sharron closed the book in her hands and answered concisely, "Four hours."
Putting down the glass, Klein's attention shifted to the cover of the book she was reading. Thanks to the
Nightmare Emblem
he wore, which provided enhanced night vision, he managed to make out the words "Ladies' Aesthetic" printed on it.
Is Miss Sharron considering swapping her gothic dress for something more combat-suitable?
Klein mused, feeling an inexplicable sense of anticipation, akin to waiting for a new skin update for a female character in one of those mobile games from his previous life.
However, Klein quickly dismissed these wandering thoughts. After ensuring that his spiritual energy had fully recovered, he composed his words and said, "After all, this is a scenario Linster created specifically for revenge. Even if the 'Labyrinth Tower' has balanced it by giving us time to investigate and prepare, that time won't last long. We need to find Ince Zangwill immediately and seize Sealed Artifact 0-08."
"Understood," Sharron replied simply.
After speaking, she pursed her lips slightly, and the outfit on her body began to transform rapidly. In mere moments, her gothic dress had changed into a sleek hunting outfit, making her appear sharp and valiant, with a beauty quite different from her usual appearance.
Noticing Klein's look of admiration and surprise, Sharron's azure eyes flickered slightly. However, she quickly suppressed any unnatural reactions and reverted to the precise demeanor of an immaculate "doll."
On the other hand, Klein had only taken a few extra glances out of curiosity. Knowing that staring at a lady in such a manner was impolite, he quickly averted his gaze, collected his "equipment," and left the room with Miss Sharron.
Instead of hiring a carriage, the two moved swiftly along the streets, finally reaching the outskirts of Tingen before dawn. There, they stood before a house surrounded by verdant lawns.
The house featured a decaying garden, whose flowers had begun to wither in early September, and a dark red chimney. Everything matched the description of the building Klein had hired a detective to search for during his time in Tingen.
"The place I once sought endlessly is so easily found in this dream version of Tingen... It seems that Ince knew my every move back then and had already made 'arrangements.' Unfortunately for you, in this dream, your fake '0-08' is useless against me!"
Though his thoughts were tinged with irony, Klein maintained his caution. He ascended to the gray fog and conducted a series of divinations before returning to reality. Facing the waiting Miss Sharron, he nodded and said, "No additional dangers... our only opponent is Ince.
"You distract him, and I'll wait for the right moment to deliver the fatal blow."
Sharron silently stared at the man who had just excused himself to the bathroom for a few seconds before nodding slightly. "Alright."
A few minutes later, Ince Zangwill, with his dark golden hair and sharply sculpted features, looked on in despair and disbelief with his remaining eye. His body collapsed to the ground, surrounded by charred pieces of internal organs burning with black flames—organs he had just vomited out moments earlier.
Klein lowered the pitch-black revolver in his hand and stared at the corpse of his nemesis. In a voice that only he could hear, he murmured,
"Ince, just like I once said to Lanrus... death is the most 'affectionate' confession I can give you."
Klein lowered the pitch-black revolver in his hand and stared at the "corpse" of his nemesis, murmuring softly to himself,
"Ince, just like I once said to Lanvus... death is the most 'affectionate' confession I can give you.
"Unfortunately, the 'you' here is nothing more than a dream-induced phantom."
After finishing his words, Klein stood up, picked up the feathered pen on the table, and curiously examined it for a moment before setting it down again. Turning to Sharron, who was quietly flipping through a notebook, he smiled and said,
"I didn't expect that after losing the advantage of '0-08,' this version of Ince Zangwill would be so weak in direct combat. I've heard that when he failed to forcibly ascend to a demigod, he suffered severe backlash. It seems likely that as a result, many of the 'Gatekeeper' and 'Spirit Guide' abilities he should have possessed are no longer available to him.
"No wonder he was so intent on weakening the Captain and the Tingen Nighthawks... No wonder he never even considered breaking into Chanis Gate while the Captain was out. Ha, in his current state, just approaching Chanis Gate would probably trigger the latent issues in his body and cause him to collapse completely."
The earlier ambush on Ince had gone so smoothly it felt almost absurd. With Klein and Sharron's seamless coordination, Ince had been rendered utterly powerless!
They hadn't even needed to use the "Sunlight Talisman." The "Black Flame" bullets from Klein's "Confession" revolver, combined with the holy light enchantment from the "Sun Brooch," had been enough to eradicate most of Ince's lingering spirits before killing him outright.
By now, Miss Sharron, who had been wearing a white lace-trimmed shirt paired with a tailored black hunting jacket earlier, had reverted to her gothic long dress. Her expression unchanged, she slid the notebook she had been reading across the table to Klein, pointing to a particular page with her slender finger.
"Look here," she said.
Detecting a note of seriousness in her tone, Klein focused his attention on the indicated section of the page. It read:
"A sense of inexplicable agitation warned Ince Zangwill of impending danger. He decided to assist Linster by accelerating his fusion with the 'Evil God's Offspring.' To this end, he split a portion of the Death's Descendant characteristics he had collected and implanted them into Megose's body, granting her the necessary strength.
"With Megose's enhanced body, Linster, who was in the midst of fusing with the 'Evil God's Offspring,' no longer needed to worry about his 'mother's' body enduring the process. What originally required several months to complete was shortened to just a few days."
As expected...
Klein thought to himself. He flipped further back in Ince's notebook, piecing together more of the story behind this dream-created scenario.
The events described were eerily similar yet clearly distinct from the ones Klein had personally experienced. In this dream version of Tingen, there was no "True Creator," no Aurora Order, and no Lanvus.
From beginning to end, the one "collaborating" with Ince was none other than Linster, the "Wraith" who had dragged both Klein and Sharron into the "Dream Labyrinth Tower"!
However, if there was no Lanvus, how had Megose come to bear the "Evil God's Offspring"? And if this so-called "Evil God" wasn't the True Creator, then who—or what—was it? Could it really be as Klein suspected, a god without clear attribution?
As this thought flitted through his mind, Klein frowned and seemed to recall something. Turning to Miss Sharron, he asked,
"What was Linster's faith within the Rose School of Thought? The 'Chained God'?"
Miss Sharron, wearing her black soft hat, remained silent for several seconds before answering in her ethereal, dreamlike voice:
"The Original Moon."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 501: Klein’s Preparations and the Appearance of the Finks Lion
chapters.content:
Chapter 501 - Klein's Preparations and the Appearance of the Finks Lion
The Primordial Moon?
Klein was no stranger to this name. Not only had "The Tower" mentioned it during the "Demoness of Affliction" incident, but two of his mysticism books,
Feast of Blood
and
The Book of Secrets
, also described this mysterious entity.
Especially in
The Book of Secrets
by Sorcerer King Klarman, there were detailed rituals for bypassing the "Crimson Goddess" and directly praying to the "Primordial Moon."
"All of this indicates that the Primordial Moon is either a high-ranking and exalted entity... or, like me, possesses some sort of 'cheat' akin to the 'mysterious space above the gray fog.'
"However, Klarman explicitly mentioned in his book that the Primordial Moon existed during the Fourth Epoch. Meanwhile, Emlyn once told me that the author of Feast of Blood, Rhine Callenrida—who was also Liu Bo in his days as a Vampire Duke—perished in the mid-to-late Fourth Epoch. This means the Primordial Moon had already existed by then, or it wouldn't have been recorded in his work.
"From the Fourth Epoch to now, at least 1,400 years have passed. Even if the Primordial Moon started as a 'fraud,' much like me, by now it must have become a near-god or even a true deity.
"In fact, I once suspected that Lilith, the ancient god recorded by the City of Silver and the progenitor of the vampires, might actually be the Primordial Moon. However, I later dismissed this theory.
"According to the Emperor's diary, Lilith was close to Liu Bo. As a deity, she even shed a tear for his death. While that might just be Liu Bo exaggerating, it does suggest their relationship was familiar.
"Meanwhile, Liu Bo's descriptions of the Primordial Moon in Feast of Blood show no respect or affection whatsoever—if anything, they are filled with disdain. This starkly contrasts with Klarman's humble tone when discussing the Primordial Moon in The Book of Secrets.
"So, it's unlikely the Primordial Moon is Lilith. Considering its traits, such as bringing dangerous outcomes to its supplicants, it might be an incarnation of some evil god or high-ranking demon."
Klein mulled over these thoughts as he turned to Sharron and began asking her a series of questions:
"Does the Rose School of Thought still harbor faith in the Primordial Moon? Doesn't the Chained God suppress it? And what do you know about the Primordial Moon?"
Since
The Book of Secrets
had been a reward from Sharron, Klein figured she probably knew more about this entity than he did.
If he could gather enough information, he could risk divining the state of the "Evil God's Offspring" above the gray fog.
Dressed once again in her elaborate and intricate long gown, Sharron remained silent for a moment before her lips moved slightly:
"The Chained God, who became the embodiment of the 'Mother Tree of Desire,' and the Primordial Moon are mortal enemies. But they both oppose and collaborate with one another.
"The faith in the Primordial Moon was introduced into the Rose School of Thought by a sorcerer-king who revered it. This belief swayed some members of the School, including Linster.
"The Rose School's attitude toward the Primordial Moon's faith is one of tolerance.
"My knowledge of the Primordial Moon also comes from
The Book of Secrets
."
"So, the Chained God resents the Primordial Moon but is powerless to stop it? Or perhaps, under the overwhelming pressure from the Seven Gods, they're forced into uneasy cooperation?"
"But what is this 'Mother Tree of Desire,' and how did the Chained God become its embodiment?"
These questions churned in Klein's mind, and he eventually voiced them aloud to Sharron.
Her deep blue eyes rippled slightly, and after a brief pause, she answered in her calm voice:
"With the start of the Fifth Epoch and the fall of the Death God, the Balam Empire's royal family gradually lost control over regions like the Star Highlands and Paz Valley. These areas birthed their own extraordinary organization—the Rose School of Thought.
"At its inception, there was no 'Mother Tree of Desire,' only the Chained God. The Rose School emphasized restraint and established a religious system of rituals, including laws. Its formal members lived austere, low-desire lives to cope with the side effects of their powers.
"But one day, the divine revelations began including words like 'indulgence.' Slowly, some members reverted to ancient, blood-soaked sacrificial traditions. Eventually, some high-ranking members secretly declared that the Chained God was the embodiment of the 'Mother Tree of Desire.'"
"It sounds as if the Chained God was gradually corrupted or replaced by this 'Mother Tree of Desire'... It even reminds me of the 'Hidden Sage' suddenly 'coming to life.'
"
"Speaking of things suddenly 'coming to life,' the Sauron family's '0'-level Sealed Artifact, formed from the 'Conqueror' characteristic, awakened because of Liu Bo's transmigration.
"Could it be... Liu Bo transmigrated into the Chained God and gradually overtook it? Hmm... no, probably not. Liu Bo, like me and the Emperor, shares similar values. Indulgence might suit him, but he'd likely reject blood-soaked rituals. It's highly unlikely."
After contemplating for a moment, Klein carefully said to Sharron,
"I need to step into the washroom. Once I return, we'll decide how to proceed."
He knew the excuse sounded suspicious, but with such a formidable enemy looming, he couldn't afford to care.
Moreover, he was starting to consider introducing Miss Sharron to the "Fool." While she seemed trustworthy, she now knew too many of his secrets. It wouldn't hurt to have a contingency plan... though he hadn't yet found the perfect opportunity.
Sharron fixed her gaze on him for several seconds before calmly replying,
"Alright."
Klein quickly entered the washroom, locked the door behind him, and took four steps counterclockwise to ascend to the gray fog.
Sitting on the high-backed chair that belonged to the "Fool," Klein took a deep breath and removed the spirit pendulum from his cuff.
"The Evil God's Offspring fused with Linster originates from the 'Primordial Moon' within the Dream Labyrinth Tower."
He silently recited this phrase seven times and then opened his eyes to observe the yellow crystal pendant. It remained completely still, unmoving.
"Divination failed?"
Klein frowned.
He tried changing the phrasing and the divination method, but the result was the same—failure.
This doesn't make sense. When I divined whether Linster was fusing with the Evil God's Offspring earlier, I received clear results... This indicates that neither Linster nor the Offspring has the rank or items to block divination...
Could it be because I mentioned the Primordial Moon? Does this mean the Primordial Moon's power isn't something simulated by the Dream Labyrinth Tower, but real?
So, the so-called Evil God's Offspring might be fake, part of the dream, but its power source is real? If that's the case... could this fake eventually become real?
Klein was startled by the thought but quickly calmed himself. Having previously faced the offspring of the Eternal Blazing Sun and the True Creator, he reasoned that the Primordial Moon couldn't possibly be more powerful than those two.
He steadied the pendulum again and recited another phrase:
"Stopping the birth of the Evil God's Offspring in the dream will bring me danger."
After seven repetitions, the yellow crystal pendant began to rotate clockwise, though slowly and with a small amplitude.
This indicated that there was indeed danger, but it was within manageable limits.
What caught Klein's attention even more was this: the divination didn't fail this time.
This proved that even if Linster's fusion with the Evil God's Offspring was nearing completion, he still hadn't obtained the Primordial Moon's power or rank and remained a "falsehood" created by the dream.
"But if the fusion is completed, things might change... Linster is, after all, a devout believer in the Primordial Moon!
"We must eliminate him as quickly as possible. If the Evil God's power truly enters the dream, I might have no choice but to escape with Miss Sharron."
With his decision made, Klein simulated the sensation of descending and returned to reality. Exiting the washroom, he walked back to the parlor where Miss Sharron was waiting.
The doll-like lady sat in a chair, flipping through another notebook that had belonged to Ince Zangwill.
When she noticed Klein's return, she raised the notebook in her hand and gestured toward Ince's lifeless body on the floor, speaking succinctly:
"His journal."
Klein wasn't particularly interested in Ince's sob stories. After confirming that the journal didn't contain any valuable information, he picked up "0-08" and wrote in the notebook:
"Madam Sharon of the Demoness Sect accidentally discovered that Megose was nurturing the Evil God's Offspring. Understanding that the child's birth would bring destruction to Tingen City and ruin her years of efforts, she used her channels to report the matter to the Machinery Hivemind and the Mandated Punishers.
"The Mandated Punishers and the Machinery Hivemind did not take the situation lightly. They immediately sent a telegram to the Nighthawks while dispatching personnel to corner Megose in her house."
To save the Captain and complete the mission, Klein paused his writing and silently apologized to the Machinery Hivemind and the Mandated Punishers, making the triangular holy emblem gesture across his chest.
This act caused Miss Sharron, who was observing him, to display a flicker of emotion in her gaze.
Fortunately, this was merely a dream. Even if the Machinery Hivemind and the Mandated Punishers were to die here, it wouldn't result in their actual deaths.
"We're heading to Megose's house now," Klein said, handing the feather pen to Sharron. He solemnly added, "This time, you'll provide support."
Sharron glanced at him, nodded slightly, and said, "Be careful."
"Don't worry... I'll approach in a different form," Klein replied with a confident smile.
"What?" Sharron's deep blue eyes held hidden emotions, and she instinctively asked.
Soon, her questions were answered when a ghostly figure clad in black armor and wearing a black crown appeared before her.
"the 'Black Emperor'!"
...
On the outskirts of Daniel Valley, Ebner and "Vice Admiral Iceberg" Edwina had no choice but to halt their progress.
The torrential rain continued to pour, turning the once-dry riverbeds into flowing streams.
As they were about to cross one such "small river," the water's surface suddenly reflected the image of a lion!
It was the Finks Lion, hiding within the stream's reflection!
"So this is the fated encounter?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 502: The Lion
chapters.content:
Chapter 502 - The Lion
"So this is the fated encounter?" Ebner murmured to himself as he quietly pulled a puppet from his shirt pocket, preparing for battle.
Beside him, "Vice Admiral Iceberg" Edwina retrieved an oil lamp. Ebner took a quick glance and immediately recognized it as the mystical item,
"Silent Winter,"
which Edwina had purchased at the Pirate Congress for 4,200 pounds.
This item emitted a light that could make living creatures' limbs icy cold and rigid, eventually freezing them completely. Without a specific countermeasure, even a demigod would be affected.
However, to their surprise, the lion reflected in the stream's surface suddenly leaped out of the water and into reality. Its body radiated a warmth akin to the sun, and though its movements were slightly uncoordinated, it dashed five meters away with impressive speed.
Just as Ebner instinctively considered simulating the speed of a "Zombie" to pursue it, the lion abruptly turned around and spoke, "Stop! Why are you humans always so eager to fight? Can't we just sit down, have a meal, and talk things over?"
Eat and talk? You're quite the sophisticated lion... but I wonder, will it be you eating me, or me eating you?
Ebner thought wryly as he exchanged a glance with Edwina.
Suppressing his hostility, Ebner raised his hands to show he was unarmed and stepped forward.
But the lion immediately took a step back, its uncoordinated rear legs causing it to stumble and fall. Even so, it continued to wriggle away, shouting, "Stop, don't come any closer!"
"Weren't you the one who suggested eating and talking? How can we do that without getting closer?" Ebner stopped in his tracks, putting on a look of innocence.
"Kid, either put that thing in your pocket away, or stay five meters away from me... I'm older than the two of you combined, and that little trick of yours won't work on me!" the lion retorted. Its fluffy face displayed an oddly human expression of cunning and disdain.
"You know?" Ebner was genuinely surprised this time. Since the lion had seen through his trick, he decided not to hide it anymore and calmly used a handkerchief to cover the puppet's eyes.
He then focused his attention on the lion, observing its features closely. Its size and appearance were no different from an ordinary lion, except for its snow-white fur and multicolored mane, which gave it a somewhat peculiar look.
Additionally, its disproportionately large head seemed mismatched with its body.
This appearance was somewhat different from the descriptions of the
Finks Lion
he had read in books."Of course I know! Kid, you're familiar with the 'Polymath,' right? That Sequence's Beyonders have an ability called
Analysis,
which allows them to discern others' strengths and weaknesses. I could tell the range of your puppet's spirit-thread manipulation at a glance..." the lion said smugly, snorting as it turned its gaze to Edwina, raising its chin. "And that little lady's 'oil lamp' over there? I know how to counter that, too."
That tone, that attitude... it's showing off, isn't it? Truly fitting as the main material for a "Mysticism Magister." But its level of Analysis seems quite advanced—it might be able to simulate and counter many pathways' abilities. This won't be easy to handle,
Ebner thought, clicking his tongue twice as he quickly devised countermeasures.
"You two are decent, though. Unlike those idiots who woke me up before, attacking me on sight without giving me a chance to speak... You know, I've been trapped here by that bastard for over a hundred years without anyone to talk to. It's been maddening..." the lion rambled on, seemingly oblivious to Ebner's calculations.
Halfway through its tirade, the lion suddenly let out a soft "Hmm?" Its expression shifted to one of surprise and delight. "You... you're both mid-sequence Beyonders of the
Reader
pathway?"
The lion's statement interrupted Ebner's train of thought. He exchanged another glance with Edwina before cautiously asking, "How do you know that?"
"You've heard of Polymaths's Exchange Technique, right? Over the past hundred years, I've developed a new mystic art based on it, specifically to detect whether any
Polymaths
are nearby!" The lion seemed incredibly forthcoming, almost eager to answer every question.
"You've heard of
Polymath's Exchange Technique,
haven't you? Over the past century, I've refined it into a new mystic art specifically designed to detect the presence of
Polymaths
nearby!" The lion seemed remarkably talkative, answering almost every question with a casual air of familiarity.
"Vice Admiral Iceberg" Edwina's lips twitched slightly, and her light blue eyes, as clear as a mountain spring, glimmered with a strong thirst for knowledge. She clearly wanted to inquire about the principles of this mystic art.
However, she understood that now wasn't the right time to ask. She refrained from acting on her curiosity, but the lion's friendly demeanor reduced her hostility, and she no longer seemed poised to attack at any moment.
"What made you come up with such a... peculiar mystic art?" Ebner asked with a strange expression. By now, his intention to attack had also diminished, and he felt there might be an opportunity to extract some significant information from this lion.
Perhaps about the so-called "bastard" who had trapped it.
Judging by the lion's behavior, it seemed like it had been holding back its grievances for years and was now desperate to vent.
"Of course, I developed it to escape..." The lion began to speak but abruptly stopped itself, forcing a "simple and honest" smile onto its furry face before countering with a question: "I'm a
Finks Lion.
Do you know what
Finks
means?"
"'Finks' originates from Ancient Feysac, and it means 'to disseminate hidden knowledge,'" Edwina answered without hesitation.
So it does. And here I thought this lion was just stalling for time.
Ebner also knew the meaning of the name, but since his companion had already spoken, he chose to remain silent and instead focused on the lion's reaction.
"Exactly! And, similar to the Sequence 5
Mysticism Magister
in the
Reader
pathway—whose acting guidelines involve 'collecting mystic arts, creating mystic arts, teaching mystic arts, and ultimately demystifying mystic arts'—I, as a
Finks Lion,
have a rule: I must pose a question about a secret to anyone I meet. If they can answer it correctly, I'll grant them a reward!"
As it spoke, the lion shot Ebner a sly wink and continued with a tempting tone, "Even if you want my brain, I'll give it to you."
What's with this lion? It's practically inviting me to take its brain... Could this be a trap? Also, the acting guidelines for a Mysticism Magister are 'collect, create, teach, and demystify mystic arts'? To reveal such critical knowledge so casually... this lion truly lives up to the name Finks, spreading secrets left and right,
Ebner thought to himself.
He glanced at Edwina, who had moved to his side. She caught his look and nodded slightly, indicating that the lion's explanation of the
Mysticism Magister's
acting guidelines was accurate.
"But if you lose your brain, won't you die? I don't believe you'd sacrifice yourself just to reward someone," Ebner said after some thought, deliberately showing a skeptical attitude to test the lion.
"If I had only one brain, of course, I wouldn't give it to you! But an extra brain is just a burden!" The lion's tone turned indignant. "That bastard fed me something that made me grow an additional brain, which is why my head is so huge! And, to make matters worse, he imposed a 'rule' that prevents me from removing or expelling it myself..."
Realizing it had said too much, the lion hurriedly tried to change the subject. "Ugh, ever since I got this extra brain, I've had trouble controlling my emotions—and I even trip over myself when I try to run!"
"So that's it. Someone imprisoned you in this valley and imposed various rules on you. These rules can only be broken with the help of a
Polymath.
Am I right?" Ebner asked with a look of sudden realization.
(Chapter End)

chapters.title: Chapter 503: Questions
chapters.content:
Chapter 503 - Questions
This feels like someone prepared a main material in advance, waiting for a Polymath to come along. No wonder Edwina's prophecy was about a "fated encounter." With everything arranged so clearly, of course, it's "fated." But who planned this elaborate scheme over a hundred years ago?
It couldn't have been that Daniel master Edwina mentioned—he perished centuries ago, the timeline doesn't match...
A hundred years ago, the most prominent figure was undoubtedly Roselle... Could it have been him? Did he "foresee" my arrival and invest in advance, hoping I'd help him rid himself of some kind of corruption once I grew strong enough?
The "Knowledge Emperor" was indeed skilled in prophecy... but could he have foreseen my transmigration?
Or perhaps this was initially Roselle's arrangement—or someone else's—made for another purpose, but it was repurposed by the "God of Knowledge" as my opportunity?
As these thoughts raced through Ebner's mind, he saw the lion curl its mouth into a wide "smile," nodding repeatedly as it said, "Yes, yes, you've guessed it all correctly. But it's all your guess—it has nothing to do with me."
Hearing this, "Vice Admiral Iceberg" Edwina felt a spark of inspiration and immediately asked, "Is it also part of the 'rules' that you can't actively reveal what restricts you, or who imposed the restrictions on you?"
Ebner, having had a similar thought, withdrew from his musings and turned his attention to the "Finks Lion."
However, the lion, now thoroughly soaked by the downpour, looked quite pitiful. Its once-pristine white fur clung wetly to its body, further emphasizing its oversized head.
The lion glanced at Ebner and Edwina, who were still shielded by their "water barrier." Muttering something under its breath, it plucked a few of its multicolored mane hairs with its paw. Suddenly, an inexplicable force surged, and the water barrier surrounding Ebner and Edwina extended outward, forming a large dome with a five-meter radius to shield against the intensifying rain.
Seizing the opportunity, the lion moved into the barrier's range but still maintained a distance of over five meters from Ebner.
After ensuring the humans wouldn't retract their abilities, the lion finally spoke, feigning a "simple-minded" tone: "With an extra brain, my
Analysis
ability became stronger, but controlling
Imitation
became far harder, with a high failure rate. So, over the past century, with nothing better to do, I've pre-prepared my mane into all sorts of 'charms' and hung them around my neck...""The charm I just used contains a mystic art I developed, adapted from the Marauder pathway. It allows me to 'steal' partial control of others' abilities."
Edwina's eyebrows twitched, and her eyes widened in disbelief. "Those multicolored mane hairs... they're all charms?"
So, it's stealing, but not fully stealing? Why are all the mystic arts this lion develops so weird...
Ebner inwardly complained. He wasn't too surprised, though—his constantly active "Pure White Eye" had long since revealed the true nature of the lion's multicolored mane.
This was also why he hadn't chosen to fight outright. After all... the lion had at least tens of thousands of charms in its mane. Such an overwhelming stockpile was absurd!
In a direct confrontation, even with Edwina's help, they might not be able to subdue it quickly and risk it fleeing to hide.
"Of course! You must understand how boring it is for a lion trapped in this valley, unable to leave and with its legs hardly functional," the Finks Lion muttered. It then cursed the one who imprisoned it before circling back to the topic at hand. "You're both right in your guesses... So, who's going to answer my 'hidden question' first?"
Ebner still couldn't determine whether this so-called "hidden question" was a trap. Edwina seemed equally cautious. After a moment of hesitation, Ebner asked again:
