"Do you want to enter now, or wait until the maze's main entrance fully opens?"
Ebner exchanged glances with the two ladies, who decisively left the decision to him.
Without shirking responsibility, Ebner pondered for a moment before asking, "What's the difference?"
"Essentially, none. Since you don't have the 'key,' even if you reach the 'deepest point,' you can't truly unlock the treasure. You'll still have to wait for those holding the key to enter through the main gate, navigate the maze, and reach the deepest point.
"Roselle could bypass Daniel's seals, but we can't.
"However, the card left by Roselle might be outside the treasure vault."
The lion explained dutifully.
"Have you ever gone inside?" Ebner asked after some thought.
"My lair is technically the reflection of a well within Daniel's Valley, but that place is outside the maze's boundaries." The lion spoke bitterly, shooting a wind blade at the punching bag, then turned to Jane.
"Fortunately, this lady answered the question Daniel set up, which lifted some of the 'rules' and 'restrictions' on me. As long as she gets that card, I'll be completely free."
Grinding its teeth, the lion continued, "Once I'm free, I'll expose all of Roselle's dirty secrets and ruin his reputation!"
"He's really dead," Jane reminded him calmly.
"Dead? That scourge wouldn't just die!" The lion sneered dismissively before swiftly changing the subject. "So, what's your decision?"
"I choose to enter now," Ebner answered without hesitation.
He had already made up his mind. The seals left by a demigod might be troublesome, but with Pure White Eye, he might be able to overcome them.
Even if they couldn't reach the treasure, they could set up measures in advance, gaining an edge when the military or the Rose School of Thought arrived with the key.
"Then go ahead. This time, I don't need to carry you. Even without 'mirror world' abilities, you can directly reach the destination. Roselle solidified that door." The lion shook its head and said.
Ebner activated Pure White Eye, analyzing the door carefully. Seeing no deception in the lion's words, he beckoned the two ladies to his side.
After a brief discussion, Edwina and Jane each grabbed one of Ebner's arms, allowing him to lift them with wind manipulation as they ascended toward the door on the ceiling.
A dizzying sensation, like passing through a teleportation gate, swept over them. When their vision cleared, they found themselves standing before a grand palace of gold and crimson, straight out of a fairy tale.
On the first step of the main hall, a solitary card lay silently.
At first, it appeared completely ordinary. But the moment the trio entered, a radiant brilliance began to rise from its surface, transforming it entirely.
Ebner's eyes focused, quickly recognizing the image of Roselle blowing a trumpet on the card.
It was a Judgment Card.

chapters.title: Chapter 513: Schemes Begin to Emerge
chapters.content:
Chapter 513 - Schemes Begin to Emerge
Jane and Edwina's gazes similarly fixed upon the radiant card, which shimmered with brilliance. Above Roselle's image, where he blew a trumpet, a line of text formed from dazzling starlight:
Sequence 0: Justiciar
"'Justiciar'... Sequence 0... So this is Emperor Roselle's 'Blasphemy Card.' So that's what 'blasphemy' truly means!" Edwina murmured, her eyes gleaming with newfound understanding.
Jane, however, appeared far less surprised. After all, she had once retrieved a "Death Card" from her ancestor's tomb. While Roselle's depiction on that card had been different, the essence remained the same.
Without moving personally, Jane donned the glove adorned with a vertical eye and commanded the wraith Steven to retrieve the card. Once she confirmed that there was no danger, she brought it closer.
Placing her finger lightly on Roselle's depiction, Jane caused the card to transform into a miniature, three-dimensional book.
The book fluttered open on its own, revealing lines of text written in ancient Feysac:
Sequence 9: Arbiter
"Possesses persuasive charm and sufficient authority, along with exceptional combat skills for handling unexpected situations..."
"Potion formula..."
Jane merely brushed her fingers across the page, prompting the book to turn itself:
Sequence 8: Sheriff
...
Sequence 7: Interrogator
...
Sequence 6: Judge
...
Sequence 5: Disciplinary Paladin
"Attacks against enemies who violate the Paladin's established rules will be enhanced by an unknown force and possess guaranteed accuracy..."
Potion formula:
Main ingredients: The stinger of an Adal Queen Bee, the forehead crystal of a Mist Tiger.
Supplementary materials: ...
Ritual: Consume the potion in the nest of a Beroth Mountain Ape.
Sequence 4: Imperative Mage
...
Sequence 3: Chaos Hunter
...
Sequence 2: Balancer
...
Sequence 1: Hand of Order
...
Sequence 0: Justiciar
Potion formula: Three portions of the Hand of Order's characteristics, along with the Uniqueness.
Ritual: Judge a deity who has violated your established rules, exact sufficient retribution, and make it public.
A succession of potion formulas and rituals flashed before them. Only after Jane finally put away the card did Edwina withdraw her gaze, sighing in awe.
"So this is the secret to godhood...
"A discovery like this would definitely 'shock' the world, but..."
"But the gods would never allow it! Neither the righteous nor the wicked ones," Lyon the lion interjected, unexpectedly entering the grand hall and seamlessly picking up the conversation.
Although Ebner and the other two had most of their attention on the Blasphemy Card, they maintained enough caution in unfamiliar territory to have noticed the lion's presence long before, so they weren't surprised by its sudden appearance.
"'Blasphemy' truly lives up to its name..." Jane nodded in agreement. Having seen another Blasphemy Card, she was far less shaken than Edwina.
As someone who already knew several pathways' godhood rituals from the original work, Ebner wasn't overly awed by the divine. In fact, he silently speculated:
"When the Night Emperor became the 'Justiciar,' which god did he judge?"
As the lion leaped onto the second-tier platform of the grand hall, it extended its paw forward, colliding with an invisible barrier.
Fixating on the rippling distortions of the barrier, it observed intently for a while before shaking its head and grumbling, "As expected, this is beyond my ability to break... Makes sense. Roselle merely exploited part of this seal's rules and still managed to trap me outside the valley for over a hundred years."
The trio had focused on the lion from the moment it acted. Hearing its remark, Jane curiously asked, "The rules that trapped you originated here? Are you free now?"
"Actually, Roselle only leveraged this seal. The true 'core' that bound me was that Blasphemy Card... When you picked it up, I was set free."
The lion leaped back to the lowest platform, flicking its tail as it spoke.
"So that's how it is..." Jane finally understood why the lion hadn't followed them inside initially. It was still constrained by the rules the Emperor had established for it.
While they conversed, Edwina carefully surveyed the grand hall, noticing its three-tiered structure. They stood on the first level, the lion had encountered the barrier on the second, and the topmost level featured two enormous high-backed chairs.
Red-tiled steps connected each platform, leading toward the golden pillars that supported the hall and ultimately to the two thrones.
After trying to break through the barrier on the second platform without success, Edwina deliberated and spoke, "This architectural style belongs to the Trunsoest Empire... But the color scheme is off.
"And this seal is incredibly advanced. I have no means to bypass it."
The Trunsoest Empire, once ruled by the Night Emperor whose consort was the Blood Moon Queen, would never have employed gold as a primary color in their palaces...
"Gold is associated with the Sun and symbolizes light. The red might represent blood and fire—or perhaps crimson... Could this be symbolic of some ritual?" Ebner mused, rubbing his chin while glancing at the lion.
"Don't look at me. I don't know either," the lion huffed. "Maybe Daniel just liked these colors."
That possibility couldn't be ruled out... but it felt unlikely.
Turning to Edwina, Ebner noted her subtle headshake, indicating she had no solution. Jane's expression was similarly resolute; despite her formidable combat prowess, she lacked expertise in mystical constructs.
"I'll give it a try," Ebner said after a deep breath, stepping toward the second platform.
The Ghost Empire's "ticket" was most likely on the top platform. Having come this far, he had to try.
Though the MI9 operatives with their "keys" could unlock the seal eventually, doing so would forfeit their current advantage.
Gently touching the invisible barrier, Ebner activated his Pure White Eye and began analyzing it intensely.
Streams of data flickered before his eyes. Several minutes later, as he circumvented a mechanism designed to thwart analysis and was on the brink of locating the barrier's weak point, a figure suddenly materialized before him.
The figure wore ornate clothing, had chestnut-brown curly hair, blue eyes, a high nose bridge, and thin lips—
It was none other than Roselle Gustav in his prime!
.....
Due to continued rainfall, the Daniel Valley was now inundated with water, with the deepest areas reaching past Xio's knees and up to Princess Vera's calves.
Their team had already joined forces with Prince Mountbatten, MI9 Colonel Lloyd, and several other squads. Among them were six Sequence 5 Beyonders and more than ten Sequence 6 combatants.
Ordinary soldiers had long since withdrawn from the valley and were now facing off against certain southern continental tribal forces at its perimeter.
Within the valley, however, MI9 personnel and their allies maintained a cautious stance toward the encroaching members of the Rose School of Thought, whose extraordinary combat strength exceeded their own.
"If you surrender the cursed item, I'll let you leave," declared an arrogant wraith, emerging from the ranks. "It's clear you've failed to find the entrance all this time, proving that Daniel's treasure was never meant for you."
His tone exuded a commanding arrogance, evidently someone accustomed to issuing orders.
"Heh, do you think that's possible, Chief Fat?" Prince Mountbatten stepped out from under the rain curtain, scoffing with disdain. "Our forces are evenly matched, and the Saints are still restraining each other in unknown areas. What gives you the right to decide?"
The wraith known as Chief Fat immediately contorted his face into a grimace upon hearing this and let out a piercing shriek. As a member of the Indulgence faction, he never bothered to suppress his temper.
Unfortunately for him, the shriek had barely begun when Prince Mountbatten opened his mouth and sang Roselle's "Serenade." The tune instantly nullified the wraith's spiritual attack on their side.
"Starting a pointless fight before we even see the treasure—don't you think that's foolish?" Mountbatten said with a smile, showing none of the typical irascibility of a Sailor pathway Beyonder.
Seeing his attack neutralized, Chief Fat's face darkened further as he prepared to unleash another powerful ability. However, an elderly bald man stepped forward and stopped him.
The old man seemed highly respected; even someone as hot-tempered as Chief Fat begrudgingly backed down, merely letting out a cold snort.
After pacifying Chief Fat, the elder turned to the MI9 forces and said, "Since you can't find the entrance, why not hand over the key to us? Isn't this just a waste of time?"
"Heh, we actually found the entrance long ago," Prince Mountbatten said indifferently. "Why do you think we're waiting here?"
The elder frowned, then his expression shifted to one of astonishment. "You mean... Daniel Lake?"
"Exactly. The rain started as soon as we entered the valley with the key, and it's been getting heavier and heavier—a clear sign!
"When Daniel Lake reappears, the treasure will be in the lake's mirrored world... No wonder your school has never found anything here for centuries," Mountbatten explained with a triumphant tone.
The elder's eyes glinted as he gave Mountbatten a half-smile. "Then we'll wait a little longer."
Battling in the mirrored world would be more advantageous for the Rose School of Thought, so there was no need to act rashly now.
Relieved, Mountbatten returned to his group and nodded at a short young man with black curly hair standing behind Ivan. "Your name's Bas, right? Good job figuring out where the true entrance is."
The young man, who seemed to be one of Ivan's subordinates, humbly replied, "It was all thanks to you and Boss Ivan, Your Highness. I merely offered an insignificant idea."
After speaking, he avoided Ivan's approving gaze, lowering his head with a subtle glint of amusement in his eyes.
...
On Sonia Island, in a Feysac Empire colonial town.
At the same time that Ebner saw Roselle's image during his parsing process, Niango Iziamai Panin, a senior deacon of the Church of the God of War, suddenly looked south as he listened to his subordinate's report. Squinting, he thought to himself:
"It's starting, huh?
"Then I should act as well... Heh, I might as well help you this time!"
But just as the thought crossed his mind, his eyes rippled violently, and it took over ten seconds for him to suppress the disturbance. Fortunately, the reporting subordinate remained bowed and unaware.
Heh, Panin, I've already gained control of your mind. You won't be getting any chances! A faint smile tugged at Panin's lips as he conversed internally with an unknown entity.
The subordinate finished his report and stood respectfully to the side, awaiting orders.
Panin rose to his feet and said casually, "Select 666 pirates from those recently captured and have them encircle the newly constructed Silent Town as a prison."
"Understood, Your Grace," the subordinate replied, perplexed but not daring to question a demigod.
After the subordinate left, Panin looked southward again, his smile deepening. "I wonder if your thousand-year-long scheme will succeed.
"I can only offer a little help at best."

chapters.title: Chapter 514: Gathering of Saints
chapters.content:
Chapter 514 - Gathering of Saints
In the deepest part of the Daniel Maze, within the grand palace, Ebner stood on the second platform and deactivated the Pure White Eye.
The "Roselle" who had just appeared before him was naturally not the real Emperor Roselle, but a mere "phantom" left behind at the core of the sealing mechanism.
Or more precisely, it was a "recording"—a "footage" captured when Roselle had "twisted" and "modified" part of the seal.
In the recording, Roselle casually adjusted the sealing effects while speaking:
"I've modified the palace's 'rules' according to our agreement. Now, the 'ticket' will only be obtainable by someone who unlocks the seal using the key. The others at most will find secondary treasures here.
"This is my repayment for the method you provided to separate the pollution... Thanks to you, I've gained more awareness of my condition, though I still can't break free from It.
"But now another problem troubles me... I can no longer tell whether I'm still normal or already abnormal.
"Sigh, your sudden departure made me sad... but you were right. Everything changed after that trip to the moon.
"Forget it, there's no point in talking about this. I recorded this message because I was sure you'd see it. So please allow me to say 'thank you' and... 'sorry.'"
As Ebner recalled this recording, he sank into deep thought:
"Who was Emperor Roselle confiding in? It sounded like a very close friend.
"This person not only provided a method to separate pollution but also seemingly advised Roselle not to go to the moon... Unfortunately, he didn't listen.
"Roselle believed this person would see the recording... Considering the rules he set for the lion and the question he left behind, it's plausible he meant either me, the lion, or Jane!
"Firstly, the lion is unlikely. Although it could be considered both Roselle's pet and friend, it was merely left to roam in the valley, not someone who voluntarily left Roselle's side, so I can rule it out.
"As for Jane, her uniqueness lies in being another contingency of the God of Death, a descendant of the Death Consul.
"Roselle personally visited that consul's tomb; perhaps they formed a connection then...
"That consul might not be truly dead—there might even be arrangements tied to Jane herself. This could explain Roselle's certainty that she would come and see this message.
"The only issue is... I was the one who actually saw it. How did Roselle know I would relay it to Jane?
"Finally, there's me. From the lion's earlier question, it's clear that Roselle anticipated the arrival of a 'fellow traveler.' This might be a result of the Knowledge Emperor's prophecy...
"But it could also be that my transmigration was within his expectations. If that hypothesis is true, then the most reasonable deduction is that the Pure White Eye has brought transmigrators to this world before, and Roselle knew its previous owner!
"This would explain why that person could warn Roselle about the dangers of going to the moon.
"Of course, this is all conjecture without solid proof... So either of the last two guesses could still be valid."
"In fact, I find the speculation about Jane more likely.
"After all, since I'm now the owner of the 'Pure White Eye,' it means the previous owner probably died not long after leaving Roselle, which is how I ended up crossing over...
"To possess such a powerful 'golden finger' and die so quietly... it seems unlikely.
"Not every transmigrator can be as useless as the 'biologist' or 'druid' who cultivated 'plants' in some idle game, right?
"Speaking of which, it's been several days. I wonder if Waver has found any clues about that person."
With that thought, Ebner shook his head, discarding the chaotic thoughts in his mind, and turned his attention to the matter at hand:
"Roselle said that only the one who holds the 'key,' perhaps the sealing item '1-025,' can get the 'ticket' after opening the 'seal'...
"Looking at it this way, I need to figure out how to get it...
"Hmm, as a formal member of the military, even if Xio gets the 'ticket,' she'll likely have to hand it over.
"Edwina's appearance is too obvious. If she snatches the 'ticket,' she will certainly be hunted down by the Loen military, and even with the Church of Knowledge backing her, she might not be able to protect herself... it would be a loss.
"As for Jane, her identity is also easy to trace. Even if she tries to keep a low profile, she is a cadre on the 'Future.' Moreover, she already took the 'Blasphemy Card' on this trip, so it wouldn't be appropriate for her to take the 'ticket' too... Perhaps neither Xio nor Edwina would mind, but if two items of the 'Judgment' path were in one place, just the combined effect could make it difficult for her to safely return to Queen Mystic.
"As for the lion, it's a good 'lion' choice, but I'm not familiar with it, so why should I hand it over?
"Therefore, the safest option is for me, the 'strange doctor' who appeared out of nowhere, to go for it."
While Ebner was thinking, Jane and Edwina walked up. Jane, curious, asked, "Any leads?"
"Yes... I've gotten some information left by Emperor Roselle." Ebner snapped back to reality, thought for a moment, and decided to tell the truth. After all, both Jane and Edwina were people he could trust.
"Emperor Roselle... What information did he leave?" Jane's eyes widened immediately upon hearing this.
On this trip to the Southern Continent, Queen Mystic had tasked her with not only retrieving the 'card' but also collecting any clues left by the emperor.
Although she didn't know the exact relationship between the queen and Roselle, it was clear from the tasks she had been assigned that the queen paid close attention to the world-changing figure from over a hundred years ago.
Beside Jane, Edwina's pale blue eyes also lit up. She had a strong curiosity for hidden secrets.
As for the lion, Leon, though it seemed indifferent, its ears had subtly perked up.
Ebner noticed their expressions, and after teasing their curiosity, he restated Roselle's words, rephrased for clarity.
— In a way, this was also a performance of the 'learned scholar,' so he made sure to be serious.
"Pollution... Was the emperor corrupted in his later years?" Edwina recalled some manuscripts left by her great-grandfather that mentioned the emperor's abrupt change in temperament, showing a thoughtful expression.
As for Jane, she didn't think too much about it, but instead memorized the words to later report them to Queen Mystic when she returned.
As for Leon the lion, it gave Ebner a meaningful look and thought,
So you're one of the 'Calamity Seal' agents... no wonder you could answer the emperor's question.
The whole thing about "only those with the 'key' can finally get the 'ticket'" is probably just a surface-level arrangement. From what I know about the emperor and the 'Calamity Seal,' the real meaning behind this is likely that you're meant to personally use the 'key' to lead the ritual to break the 'seal'."
"Heh, the ritual involving the key must be more than just breaking the seal—there's surely a significant secret tied to it."
Though the lion often referred to Roselle as "that guy" or "bastard," deep down, it always regarded him as "the Emperor."
Even the lion itself hadn't realized this.
Just as the lion suspected, Ebner soon shared his plan—to take the lead in seizing Sealed Artifact 1-025 when MI9 and the Rose School arrived, while the others remained hidden to assist as needed.
Neither Jane nor Edwina objected to the plan, but their gazes naturally shifted toward Leon the Lion.
The lion, seeing their expectant stares, quickly raised its paw to indicate its agreement, expressing its willingness to sign a contract.
Ebner then took out various materials and even borrowed some from Lyon's lair before activating the Pure White Eye and leveraging the hall's existing seal to begin his elaborate preparations.
...
Back in the Daniel Valley, the rainfall continued to pour relentlessly until the water level finally surpassed a critical threshold.
Suddenly, the dark water's surface emitted shimmering lights, and before MI9 and the Rose School members could react, most were swept into the glow and vanished.
Only two figures remained atop the lake.
One was the bald elder from the Rose School who had tried to mediate earlier, and the other was Princess Vera of the Loen royal family.
Just before the lights appeared, Vera had only managed to toss a mystical item into Xio's hands before helplessly watching as her subordinates were drawn into the mirrored world of the lake.
"It seems this Daniel treasure only selects mid- to low-sequence Beyonders," the bald elder mused, nodding thoughtfully before sneering at Vera.
"You Loen folks are truly deceitful. We agreed that Saints wouldn't participate, yet here you are, a demigod!"
Vera's expression remained steady as she retorted, "And you're any different?"
Both simultaneously launched attacks—not at each other but toward the water's surface at their sides.
Webs formed from threads and ice materialized out of thin air, effortlessly blocking their strikes.
A figure gradually emerged—a woman clad in a simple, pure white robe with high slits, revealing flawless legs.
This was none other than the "White Saintess" Katharina, who had secretly followed MI9 Colonel Lloyd.
"Don't be so enthusiastic... I can't handle it," Katharina teased with a voice as melodious as a song.
"The Unaging Witch? Even the Demoness Sect is involved?" The elder and Vera both frowned simultaneously.
...
Meanwhile, atop a distant mountain more than a thousand miles away, a group of over a dozen demigods gathered in three distinct factions, observing the center of the Daniel Valley through a massive mirror.
"When did Her Highness Vera become a demigod?" Duchess Georgina, dressed in a black evening gown, exchanged a glance with another Augustus Saint beside her, both filled with confusion.
They were also somewhat relieved—had Vera not already become a demigod, it would have been nearly impossible for them to offer swift support from a thousand miles away.
So they bypassed the contract and secretly arranged for a demigod... the Rose School really can't be trusted!
On the opposite side, Rose School Saint Mahmosi, Disciple of Silence , turned to question the royal faction demigod from the Spirit Cult that had unexpectedly joined them:
"Was the Demoness Sect your doing?"

chapters.title: Chapter 515: The Labyrinth
chapters.content:
Chapter 515 - The Labyrinth
The Spirit Cult's royal faction had dispatched three demigods this time, ostensibly to oversee the actions of the Loen military and the Rose School. Although Daniel Valley was located in the Pass River Valley, it bordered the southern region and wasn't far from the Balam Restoration Army's territory.
The leader among the three was a stately, elegant lady in her thirties, with long black hair and brown eyes. Facing the Silent One Mahmosi's questioning, she remained indifferent and said:
"Though the Demoness Sect was once a close ally of our Balam Empire, that relationship ended long ago with the disappearance of our god.
"We no longer have control over them."
Mahmosi stared at her for a long moment, seemingly employing some ability to verify her words. After a while, he slowly nodded:
"Bruna, it seems you're not lying.
"The Demoness Sect may have caught wind of this on their own... or perhaps Loen leaked information.
"After all, they did previously use a demoness' ship as a cover—getting noticed is only natural."
Mahmosi refrained from further questioning Loen. Unlike the Spirit Cult in the southern continent, Loen was a true enemy.
Since they were enemies, it was only natural for Loen to resort to any means necessary.
Satisfied that the Spirit Cult wasn't deliberately intervening, Mahmosi retrieved a gold nail intricately engraved with patterns from his pocket and pierced it through his lips, fastening his mouth shut.
As a Silent One, speaking required him to pay the corresponding price.
This spectacle puzzled Loen's demigods, but Bruna, unfazed, turned her gaze northward toward Daniel Valley, her thoughts stirring:
"Roselle, after all these years, I still can't decipher your schemes.
"You asked me to conceal that lion's whereabouts, yet specifically instructed me not to stop Maria if she discovered it.
"Even stranger, Her Majesty the Empress approved my actions this time...
"What exactly did you foresee?
"What are you plotting?
"Even in death, you refuse to let us rest in peace."
As Bruna pondered, Duchess Georgina, leader of the Loen delegation, proposed:
"Since there's been an incident at Daniel Lake, standing here in a standoff is meaningless and might let the Demoness Sect take advantage. Why not work together to break through Daniel's setup?"
The Rose School didn't object and even invited the Spirit Cult to join them.
Bruna readily accepted their proposal.
...
In the mirrored world of Daniel Lake, as Xio sensed herself landing on the "ground," she instinctively raised her black revolver in one hand and gripped a transparent dagger adorned with dozens of interlinked star-like lights in the other, assuming a battle stance.
She soon realized, however, that she was alone in a roughly 100-square-meter space with no signs of other people or objects—just six inconspicuous doors embedded in the six walls of this cubic room.
A message echoed in her ears, explaining her current situation.
This shadowy world beneath the lake was called the "Daniel Labyrinth," constructed by a long-fallen Saint. Hidden in its depths were the Saint's lifetime collection of treasures.
All the mid- to low-sequence Beyonders who had been confronting each other outside were now scattered across different parts of the labyrinth. By choosing any door, they would enter a similar space and face another choice of doors.
However, the path to the deepest part was singular—only by selecting the "correct" door at every juncture could one reach the ultimate destination.
Each mirrored space contained hidden clues to indicate which of the six doors led closer to the true path.
Of course, abilities such as divination, prophecy, or luck manipulation could bypass the need to search for clues, allowing one to reach the depths more quickly.
Similarly, those with "mirror-jumping" abilities could remember the coordinates of specific spaces and shuttle between them to systematically test each door, employing brute force to find the path.
This place has both "rules" and the possibility of exploiting "loopholes."
After processing the information from the space, Xio, though still vigilant, was no longer as tense. She raised the near-transparent dagger that shimmered with bright star-like lights to examine it closely.
It was a mystical item given to her by Vera at the very moment she was sucked into the lake's shadow. Due to time constraints, Her Highness hadn't had the chance to explain what this dagger was or what it could do.
But Xio instinctively believed Vera wouldn't have handed it to her without reason. The dagger must hold significant value in this space, perhaps even becoming a key asset for her survival.
Xio wasn't overly concerned about not knowing its specific function. She swept her gaze around the space, but her Arbiter intuition detected no trace of any "clues." Letting out a sigh, she muttered to herself:
"I'm far better at tracking, infiltrating, or fighting... I'm really not good at finding clues—that's a detective's job.
"If Ebner were here, he'd probably be looking all smug, already 'knowing' the answer."
Imagining Ebner's "proud" expression made Xio chuckle. Then, she softly recited the title of the Fool:
"The Fool who does not belong to this world..."
Yes, she wasn't worried at all—because she had "external support" to call on, whether for identification or solving puzzles.
...
6 a.m., the early dawn light barely illuminated the sky.
Klein, fast asleep, wasn't awakened by the church's customary chimes but instead by a soft and ethereal voice that roused him to sit up abruptly.
A woman's voice? Did Miss Temperance manage to organize the information about Daniel for Mr. Tower so quickly?
Or was it from another member? Hmm, it couldn't be Miss Magician—she would never be up at this hour. Besides, she just returned from a tense meeting with an Abraham descendant at Pritz Harbor and was still mentally drained.
Was it Miss Justice? Or Miss Judgment?
Though a bit grumpy from waking up, Klein got up nonetheless. The room remained cold, but his body felt comfortably warm without the usual chill of leaving the covers.
"Miss Sharron's potion is remarkable. I thought I'd be sick for days... I'll have to ask her where she bought it next time."
After a brief moment of admiration, Klein skipped washing up, reversed four steps, and entered the space above the gray fog.
Seated in the Fool's high-backed chair, he activated the crimson star representing Miss Judgment and was immediately surprised:
"The mirror world? How did Miss Judgment end up there? My Beyonder abilities don't touch that domain at all...
"Forget it for now... Is it to identify an item? That I can handle. But can a normal sacrificial ritual even work in the mirror world?
"Let me think... From my previous tests, mirror divinations can tap into the power of the gray fog, forming a spectral pathway to me... There's no reason a 'sacrifice' wouldn't work...
"Still, I should divine whether that item poses any danger first."
...
In a private room at the Braveheart Bar, Sharron had sent Maric away and now placed a neatly transcribed document on the altar.
After a brief hesitation, she recited a name that still stirred a tinge of fear within her:
"The Fool who does not belong to this era..."

chapters.title: Chapter 516: He’s Become Someone Else
chapters.content:
Chapter 516 - He's Become Someone Else
In the ancient palace above the gray fog, Klein sat at the head of the bronze table, awakening from a dream before enthusiastically playing with that transparent dagger strung together by a dozen or so bright star-like points.
"I didn't expect this to be not only a high-sequence item but also forged using the characteristics of two different pathways." Klein sighed as he placed the dagger on the table.
Other than the sealed artifact 0-08 he had used in the Dream Labyrinth and Azik's copper whistle, which only served to summon a messenger while having the side effect of "attracting" undead, this was his first time seeing another high-sequence item, naturally sparking his curiosity.
Through a recent "dream divination," Klein had roughly understood the dagger's functions.
It possessed five primary abilities:
First, it could "record" "Laws" in the dozen or so bright stars on it.
By channeling spirituality into the stars, the user could unleash the recorded Laws, which were comparable in power to Ninth Law charms.
After releasing a Law, the star would re-record a new one within a day. The effect could be specified by the user or would otherwise randomly record a previously released Law.
Second, anyone who violated the released Laws would be "banished" to coordinates associated with the star that recorded them.
The coordinates could be pre-set by the user but could not exceed a thousand kilometers from the dagger's current location.
Third, carving a "door" anywhere with the dagger would allow the user to step through for a random teleportation.
The destination was uncontrollable, with a maximum range of a thousand kilometers—though with bad luck, it could be high in the sky or deep underground.
Fourth, any stab to a target with the dagger would cause severe damage far beyond a typical piercing strike.
Fifth, the dagger could be used as an "astrology" tool to guide the user toward their sought objective.
"What a powerful weapon... Even ignoring the rest, just the self-replenishing Laws hold immense strategic value.
"By comparison, its negative effects are troublesome but still within an acceptable range."
As Klein pondered, two vivid scenes from his divination surfaced in his mind:
In the first, an indistinct woman activated a Law with the dagger, successfully banishing a formidable foe to an unknown location. However, shortly after, she attempted suicide multiple times but was forcibly stopped by her strong willpower. She finally regained her composure after an hour.
In the second, the same woman became disoriented two hours after using the dagger's astrology function. Even slightly complex terrains caused her to lose her way for the next twelve hours. Fortunately, her divination skills prevented significant delays.
Klein concluded that the dagger likely induced a suicidal impulse after using a Law, lasting about an hour. The intensity was unknown, as he couldn't gauge the woman's mental resilience.
However, as long as Miss Judgment promptly came above the gray fog, it wouldn't be a significant problem.
Additionally, prolonged use of the astrology function led to disorientation lasting half a day, reminiscent of his "Master Key." Was this "getting lost" trait common among Apprentice pathway Beyonders?
If I recall correctly, Sequence 5 of that pathway is called "Traveler"... How do you travel if you're always getting lost? Or is it that once you start a journey, you'll never find your way back home?
Klein muttered a sarcastic comment before preparing to share the divined scenes and the dagger with Miss Judgment.
However, just then, the crimson star representing Miss Temperance began expanding and contracting.
"Has she already sorted the information Mr. Tower requested?"
After listening to Miss Sharron's prayer through his extended spirituality, Klein tapped his fingers on the table and activated Mr. Tower's crimson star, signaling him to prepare for the ritual to receive the information.
Unexpectedly, Mr. Tower responded that he was currently unable to hold the ritual and requested permission to ascend directly to view the documents, hoping the Fool would consent.
Klein tapped his finger on the long bronze table, an idea forming in his mind:
"Mr. Tower wants to read the materials. Miss Judgment seeks assistance related to the Mirror World. And Miss Temperance, being a Wraith, is particularly familiar with the Mirror World...
"In that case, why not bring Tower, Judgment, and Temperance up here for a 'small meeting'?"
Once he made up his mind, Klein extended his spirituality to the corresponding crimson stars and sent out invitations.
After receiving confirmations from the three Tarot Club members, three figures appeared on either side of the ancient bronze table as crimson light blossomed.
...
Ebner had just finished setting up the ritual extended from the "seal" with the help of Edwina and Lion Leon when he received the Fool's proposal.
After pondering for a moment and consulting the lion, who informed him that the military and the Demoness Sect wouldn't reach the hall for a while, he hid within the ritual setup along with the two ladies and the lion, using "resting" as an excuse to be pulled into the mysterious space above the gray fog by Klein.
The Fool first introduced Miss Temperance to Miss Judgment, mentioning her specialties. He then placed the manifested "Daniel" materials before Ebner and displayed the divination results to Xio before letting them discuss freely.
The three first watched the divination projection together. As they moved on, Ebner flipped through the materials while listening to Xio explain her situation to Sharron.
Yes, since Xio hadn't disguised herself for this ascent to the gray fog, Miss Sharron was dressed in her signature intricate black Gothic court dress, with soft blonde hair peeking out from under her small hat.
They recognized each other immediately, having formed lasting impressions during the Conva Baron incident.
However, since Sharron was naturally reticent and Xio was known for keeping her friends' secrets, they tacitly chose not to expose each other's identities. Xio had even kept Mr. Tower's identity from Fors—though her "joyful" deception had somewhat deviated from its original intent.
Their relationship instantly became closer, and they quickly engaged in a meaningful discussion about the Mirror World.
Ebner, meanwhile, devoted most of his attention to the materials on "Daniel," or rather, "Dannet Tinekerr."
Most of the contents aligned with what he'd learned from Edwina and Lion Leon, but the initial section piqued his interest:
"Dannet Tinekerr was referred to as the 'Left Hand of God' by the Rose School of Thought from birth, ranking even above his sister Reinette, a favored one.
"From birth, he was emotionally detached, nearly devoid of humanity. His relationship with his parents and sister wasn't bad but was very ordinary.
"However, this condition changed abruptly before the Chained God issued the decree of 'Indulgence.'
"Dannet suddenly seemed to awaken, gradually developing emotions. After the decree was issued, he completely abandoned his responsibilities and positions, leaving the Southern Continent.
"Regarding him, Reinette once said:
"'My brother was never truly alive, but one day he came to life.
"'I thought it was God... but I was wrong.
"'The godly part of him had died. He had become someone else.'"

chapters.title: Chapter 517: He is everywhere
chapters.content:
Chapter 517 - He is everywhere
The Left Hand of God? Isn't that the title of the Dark Angel Sasrir? Tolzna, just because you were once part of the Rose of Redemption doesn't mean you can blatantly engage in bootlegging...
Though to be fair, even the Creator of Silver City borrowed those titles from elsewhere.
Judging from the title "Left Hand of God" and Miss Reinette's description of her brother, Dannet's initial role for the Chained God might have been similar to that of the Dark Angel for the Creator of Silver City — a contingency plan.
This suggests that the Chained God was prepared for the Mother Tree of Desire's invasion.
Hmm, based on Dannet's transformation, I can think of three possibilities.
First, the Chained God's arrangement activated after being corrupted, making Dannet the contingency. But this seems unlikely... Miss Reinette did say she thought he was a god but was mistaken.
Second, the Mother Tree of Desire might have discovered Dannet and corrupted him, leading to a new personality. But if that were the case, why would he immediately flee, running all the way to the Knowledge God's domain?
Third, which builds upon the second theory, is that he was indeed discovered by the Mother Tree of Desire, who sent someone to deal with him. However, after his "death," an unknown entity took over his body — perhaps a transmigrator!
After all, the changes he brought to Lenburg — such as modern university systems and the impact factor system for journals — have a distinctly transmigrator flavor.
I had my suspicions before, but reading these accounts has made me even more convinced. Dannet likely "died," only to have a transmigrator inhabit his body afterward!
But if he died centuries ago, how did he connect with the Emperor? Could it be that the Emperor found his relics somewhere and decided to help fulfill a wish?
It's possible... Maybe he even read the "original work" and left letters in his relics for the Emperor, including methods to separate "pollution" and warnings about the dangers of lunar exploration.
However, after investigating, the Emperor may have found that Dannet had dealings with the Knowledge God and was scheming something, thus growing suspicious and ignoring the warnings. This aligns with the footage the Emperor left in the sealed area.
Thinking along these lines, Ebner flipped to the last few pages of the material. He discovered that Dannet had been active on the Northern Continent for over two centuries, from the birth of a "divine abomination" more than 920 years ago to the 20-Year War over 700 years ago. Although not famous, he'd achieved quite a bit during that time.
It was also apparent that Miss Reinette still had lingering concerns for her "brother"; otherwise, she wouldn't have gathered such detailed information.
Of course, as an angel of the Temperance Faction, she might have other motives for doing this.
"The 20-Year War..." Seeing this time point, a flash of inspiration struck Ebner.
He quickly recalled that the Conva Baron, who had long coveted the Sefirah Castle, received his title during that war over 700 years ago!
It's highly likely that this suspected transmigrator, Dannet, had connections with Baron Conva. After all, the baron's diary was encrypted using the Book of the Dead, and the elixirs created by Dannet were similar to those recorded in that book.
"Mr. Azik once mentioned that Baron Conva's peculiar state was the result of some kind of experiment.
"Could it be... that the one conducting experiments on him was Dannet, backed by the Knowledge God?
"And was the experiment's purpose... to separate 'pollution'?!
"Using a simulation of the Three-Headed Cathedral and Dream Weaver's core abilities, combined with the chaos sea Baron Conva encountered beneath that ancient castle... to develop a secret technique for separating pollution?"
"Probably not enough... the God of Knowledge and Wisdom and Dannet must have employed other methods or techniques that I'm unaware of...
"Thinking back now, the Roselle I encountered in the Dream Labyrinth Tower—his condition was quite similar to that of Baron Conva. Both retained only a youthful state, endlessly repeating a segment of their lives.
"Hmm, similar but fundamentally different. Perhaps Roselle refined the method on his own.
"But as Roselle mentioned in his message, this method couldn't completely rid one of pollution... so Baron Conva's obsession with Sefirah Castle was likely due to Dannet, who had read the original work, telling him about it, right? After all, it's indeed the only reliable way to resolve pollution... maybe that was compensation for using him as an experiment subject?"
After pondering for a while, Ebner gradually pieced things together, though several questions remained unanswered.
For instance, what was Dannet's grand objective in going through all this trouble?
What role did the Death Consul, who slumbered in Calderon City, play in all of this? Despite never appearing directly in these events, his influence seemed to be everywhere.
Baron Conva was his descendant, Dannet's distillation techniques likely originated from his book, Roselle had entered his tomb, and even the mysterious queen's nurturing of Jian was likely due to him.
Ebner refused to believe it was all a coincidence!
However, with insufficient information to complete the puzzle, he could only analyze up to this point. Reluctantly, he turned his attention toward the discussion between "Judgment" and "Temperance."
Meanwhile, seated at the head of the table, Klein had finished reading Dannet's records. Unlike Ebner, he didn't have so many questions. Only two words echoed in his mind: "Liu Bo!"
He's everywhere! So modern university systems were his "contribution"? I thought it was Roselle...
Haha, is this some kind of "transmigrator aggregation effect"? I always seem to come across information about him.
Klein chuckled self-deprecatingly and focused on the situation described by Miss Judgment, who had finished narrating her predicament. The three formally began their discussion.
Miss Temperance rested her left palm on her right elbow, supporting her chin with her right hand. Though expressionless, it was clear she was contemplating seriously.
After a dozen seconds, she offered a suggestion: "The Mirror World is a reflection of reality. Even if sealed and modified, it won't change too drastically."
What does that mean? Xio blinked, not quite grasping the point, and instinctively looked toward Ebner.
Noticing her reaction, Sharon's azure eyes shifted subtly as if something had come to mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 518: Analysis
chapters.content:
Chapter 518 - Analysis
Seeing Xio looking over, Ebner pondered for a moment and hesitantly asked:
"Miss Temperance, do you mean that the complete 'Daniel's Labyrinth' is actually a projection of the geography of Daniel Valley, just segmented into small mirror worlds... perhaps with the arrangement of these segments shuffled?"
"Yes," Miss Sharon nodded lightly, simply adding, "The 'doors' connect non-adjacent mirror worlds."
Connecting non-adjacent mirror worlds through doors essentially shuffles their order, doesn't it? Or perhaps she means that the mirror worlds inherently rely on doors for connection, making the concept of sequence irrelevant?
Talking with Miss Sharon is really challenging—Klein must have quite the talent for always understanding her correctly.
Ebner silently complained, then relayed his judgment and knowledge of mirror worlds to Xio. Only then did she grasp Sharon's meaning but remained puzzled.
"How does this help us?" she asked.
"We were drawn into the labyrinth at dawn," Sharon reminded her.
"Dawn?" Xio frowned, turning back to Ebner.
After a moment of contemplation, Ebner's eyes lit up. "The position of the rising sun and the setting crimson moon? Or perhaps their reflection on the lake surface?"
As he spoke, he recalled the dominant colors of the grand hall deep within the labyrinth—gold and red.
They likely symbolized the sun and the crimson moon.
Sharon said nothing, merely nodding silently to affirm his deduction. As for why she was sure the treasure was at the sun or crimson moon's reflected position, she did not elaborate.
However, from the information he'd read earlier, Ebner had a guess—Dannet was born at sunrise and died on a crimson night.
"Considering the season is November and the latitude of Daniel Valley... it should be near the direct solar point at dawn.
"The sun's reflection should be positioned slightly eastward...
"So, the hint is actually the direction and angle of the light?
"Just keep choosing the doors in the direction of the light source?"
Hearing Ebner's analysis, Xio's eyes brightened with realization, though she still asked, "What if the light comes from the intersection of multiple angles? What if there are three possibilities?"
Each segmented mirror world was a hexagonal cube, so light entering from the intersection of three walls was plausible.
In fact, in the initial space where Xio found herself, light came from the shared edge between the floor and the front wall.
"Luck," Sharon answered concisely.
Xio looked troubled at that. Her luck was sometimes good but often terrible. This wasn't Backlund, and she couldn't use the Solomon Gold Coin here either.
Ebner chuckled, "If you're unsure, use that magical item your superior lent you for 'astrology.' I suspect that's why your superior entrusted it to you. Just make sure you reach the deepest part of the labyrinth within two hours."
With both the 'Blasphemy Card' and the Ghost Empire's ticket—two top-tier treasures of the Justiciar pathway present, a magical item imbued with the traits of an Imperative Mage would naturally exhibit a convergence effect. Even without using 'astrology,' it had a high chance of guiding her to the labyrinth's deepest part.
Of course, after two hours, when the dagger's negative effects kicked in, who knew where she'd end up 'wandering'?
Xio's eyes sparkled as she finally understood why Princess Vera had handed her the dagger. She promptly thanked the Fool, Miss Temperance, and the Tower while inquiring about Sharon's preferred form of compensation.
As for how she'd repay the Fool and Tower, she planned to submit additional pages of Roselle's diary for the former, while the latter could be discussed privately—no need to bring it up in the fog.
"One page of Roselle's diary," Sharon requested without hesitation.
Xio pressed her lips together, feeling a bit troubled. Due to the Capim case, she still owed the Fool diary pages and had none to spare for Sharon.
But how did Miss Sharon know that the Fool needed Roselle's diaries? Could she have also been brought in by Ebner? Did he, like when I was about to join the club, tell her all about the Tarot Club?
No, probably not... Ebner has been away from Backlund lately, theoretically not having time to meet Miss Sharon.
But then again, he can use teleportation, so who knows...
As Xio's thoughts drifted far off course, Ebner called her back to the present. Seeing her snap out of it, he nodded toward her meaningfully.
Xio quickly understood what Ebner was signaling. Turning her head toward Sharon, she said, "I'll get you a diary page as soon as possible."
Since Xio hadn't disguised herself, her distinctive features would surely be recognized by Miss Sharon. Given that Sharon would easily deduce her identity after attending a few Tarot gatherings, Ebner saw no point in hiding their friendship.
As for the diary... that lion had spilled so much dirt on Roselle, including some highly useful "insider facts." With that as a basis, it wouldn't be too far-fetched to "compose" a few diary entries.
Besides, the lion might actually possess genuine Roselle diaries. It wouldn't hurt to ask when they returned.
Sharon looked at the two silently for a few moments, then unexpectedly found herself feeling less intimidated by this meeting organized by the Fool. After all, aside from Sherlock, running into two familiar faces in succession made things feel less mysterious and daunting.
"Alright," Sharon eventually agreed calmly.
Ebner then reminded Xio to be cautious of other labyrinth participants before requesting the Fool to end the gathering.
Xio, however, was brimming with confidence. With a mystical item bearing the power of a Level 1 Sealed Artifact in hand, it was the others who should be careful, not her.
After the three members rose and saluted, the Fool raised his hand slightly, making them vanish from the ancient palace.
Following that, the Fool tossed the transparent dagger linked by radiant stars through the Door of Summoning, "bestowing" it to Miss Judgment. He then manifested pen and paper, summarizing the Roselle "ramblings" heard in the Dream Labyrinth Tower and quickly arrived at some plausible "conclusions."
"Roselle, as someone from over a hundred years ago, definitely wouldn't have seen my 'Master Key.' After all, it only recently came into existence.
"Given that Roselle wouldn't have mentioned it without reason, I can boldly speculate:
"The reason Linster, as a Tower Climber, was able to connect with the sealed Roselle at the base of the Dream Labyrinth Tower... was likely due to the 'Master Key' itself!
"Come to think of it, I deliberately linked the Master Key to Azik's Copper Whistle on a keychain to draw Linster's attention before launching a sneak attack using Full Moon Murmurs, which clinched my victory.
"And Full Moon Murmurs was the second phrase Roselle mentioned.
"From Roselle's diaries, what I learned from Tower, and Magician's experiences, it's evident that Full Moon Murmurs originated from Mr. Door, the ancestor of the Abraham family.
"As the King of Angels, he was exiled by the combined forces of the Evernight Goddess and Lord of Storms, which must have been for a reason... Given Roselle's corrupted state, perhaps Mr. Door is the incarnation of the evil god 'Primordial Moon'? Or was he corrupted by the Primordial Moon and, after exile, tried to save himself by contaminating Roselle through their full-moon conversations?
"In any case, when Linster heard the Full Moon Murmurs, he unintentionally established contact with the sealed Roselle—or the corrupted part of him. Desperate, Linster followed Roselle's instructions, sacrificing his own soul and granting partial authority to Sharon and me in hopes of revenge.
"In the end, he was just a pawn manipulated by that corrupted Roselle all along."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 519: The Beginning
chapters.content:
Chapter 519 - The Beginning
"Even if Mr. Door isn't the Primordial Moon, he's definitely connected to Emperor Roselle's current corrupted state. When Miss Magician advances to higher sequences and directly confronts the Murmurs, I must remind her to be extra cautious."
With this thought in mind, Klein continued reviewing the conclusions he had jotted down:
"Emperor Roselle probably received warnings and a method to separate himself from corruption from Liu Bo, who is the Calamity Seal.
"Unfortunately, due to Liu Bo's cooperation with an entity called 'Two-Faced Dragon,' the emperor didn't fully trust him. This led to regret after Roselle did something that caused him to be corrupted. Roselle sought Liu Bo's help afterward, but by then, Liu Bo had likely long since departed.
"As a result, Roselle left certain items in the ruins or tomb of Liu Bo's past incarnations, hoping that a future version of Liu Bo would find them, appreciate his 'investment,' and help him escape corruption.
"But who is this 'Two-Faced Dragon'? Sounds like a dragon, but it could just be a title... though who would willingly use a title like 'Two-Faced'? Even my Tarot Club wouldn't openly flaunt that term."
Klein quipped, then his gaze shifted to two other terms: "Blasphemy Card" and "Three Lights."
"'Blasphemy Card' should refer to the card with the codename 'Mother.' I wonder which pathway it corresponds to...
"'Three Lights'—is that a name? To be mentioned alongside Bernadette, Roselle's eldest daughter, it must hold great significance to him. But this name doesn't sound like a woman's...
"Next Tarot meeting, I'll have The World casually inquire about it."
After tapping his finger on the table in contemplation, Klein made the manifested pen and paper disappear, left the gray fog, and returned to reality.
As he prepared breakfast, Klein remained on alert, ready to return to the gray fog to provide Justiciar with any necessary assistance.
Originally, he had planned to head out and scout for a suitable fraudster target today. After all, he had accepted Miss Hazel's commission fee on Monday, and it was already the weekend with no progress made.
But compared to his professional ethics, the safety of Tarot Club members naturally took precedence.
....
In the Daniel Labyrinth...
Guided by the mystical dagger borrowed from Vera, Xio moved swiftly between portals connecting different mirror worlds.
Suddenly, just as she leaped from the "ceiling" into a new world, a figure charged toward her at a speed rivaling a steam locomotive.
In her mind, a vivid scene played out: a man with distinctly southern continent features slammed his palm atop her head, freezing her body with frost before shattering it.
—This was the prediction provided by her Ring of Foresight.
Without hesitation, Xio relied on her petite frame to roll sideways, narrowly evading the strike.
The man's expression grew even more bloodthirsty and twisted as frost spread from his hands, chasing after Xio.
However, a solemn voice speaking in ancient Hermes rang out beside him:
"Ice-based spells are forbidden here!"
With the declaration, the frost rapidly dissipated, and the ice creeping toward Xio's feet melted into vapor.
Xio seized the opportunity. Her golden mask radiated dawn-like brilliance as she declared once more:
"Those who violate the rules must be punished!"
Before the man's expression could change, Xio closed the distance at an impossible speed and angle, thrusting the transparent dagger formed by dozens of radiant stars into his neck.
The man initially sneered, intending to endure the blow with his formidable defenses while tearing Xio apart.
But to his shock, the dagger sliced through his skin—capable of withstanding cannon blasts—as though it were paper, severing his throat and sweeping sideways, cleanly decapitating him.
His hands, which had grasped Xio's waist in preparation to crush her, went limp and dropped lifelessly.
Standing upright, Xio glanced at the headless zombie, hesitating briefly. She was reluctant to waste the Beyonder Characteristics, yet unwilling to spend time waiting for them to precipitate.
She recalled Ebner once mentioning how he had commissioned The Hanged Man to collect bounties.
"The Fool probably wouldn't mind a corpse offering... right?"
Though uncertain, Xio decided to try. Using the zombie's blood, she hastily arranged a simple sacrificial ritual and recited the Fool's honorific name, awaiting His response.
Within seconds, the corpse vanished into the Door of Summoning. Xio quickly discerned the direction of the light and stepped through the corresponding door.
...
In another Mirror World, Prince Mountbatten reunited with his retinue, including Captain Elwin and the observant young team member, Bas, who had first identified Daniel Lake as the entrance.
"Bas, you're a remarkably meticulous person with excellent analytical skills. You picked up on the labyrinth's clues so quickly—determining that the direction of the light was the key," Prince Mountbatten praised warmly.
The short-statured young man with curly black hair remained modest, emphasizing that he was weak and needed Captain Elwin's protection. Thus, he could only contribute by analyzing clues for the prince.
As he spoke, he subtly glanced toward the other side of the mirrored space before quickly withdrawing his gaze.
After the three of them passed through the door aligned with the light source, a graceful woman's figure slowly emerged in the space they had vacated.
Dressed in a white blouse and beige trousers drenched by rain, the contours of her alluring form became faintly visible beneath her clothes.
This was Vice Admiral of Ailment, Tracy.
She and her mother, the Saintess of White Katarina, had initially watched the standoff between the Demoness Sect and the military at the outskirts of Daniel Valley. Unexpectedly, they had been "pulled" into the labyrinth.
"That black-haired young man noticed me? Heh, the military really has all sorts of scheming types. The prince might be in for some trouble.
"But his discovery about the clue does seem correct."
After silently murmuring to herself, Tracy waited at her spot for a few minutes before pushing open the same door the prince's group had entered.
.....
In yet another mirror space, Colonel Lloyd of the military, who had nearly captured Tracy in the past, wasn't as fortunate this time. He encountered the hot-tempered Chief Fate of the Rose School.
Wraiths held a significant advantage in the Mirror World as they could bypass doors and directly traverse multiple segmented spaces. As a result, Colonel Lloyd struggled to land a hit and grew progressively weaker under relentless harassment.
"Poison..." Only then did Lloyd realize the hidden tactic used against him, but it was too late—he could no longer speak.
"Wraith Possession!"
Chief Fate seized control of the colonel's body, immediately making him stab himself through the heart.
Moments later, Chief Fate cackled wildly as he gathered the Beyonder Characteristics and mystical items from the corpse. His laughter grew louder and more frenzied until all his pent-up rage was released.
Then, with renewed focus, he jumped back into a space aligned with the "correct path."
.....
In the grand palace at the labyrinth's deepest point, still contemplating the purpose behind Daniel and Roselle's intricate arrangements, Ebner suddenly noticed the palace's main doors slowly opening.
"They're here."
Hiding within the ritual formation they had set up, Ebner, Jane, and Vice Admiral Iceberg all stood ready. The lion, however, remained leisurely sprawled on the ground, occasionally casting peculiar glances at Ebner's back.
.....
Sonia Island, Silent Town.
His Excellency Nyango Iziamai Panin turned toward the south and commanded the officer under his control:
"Begin."
A thick black fog instantly engulfed the entire town. The 666 pirates imprisoned within simultaneously raised eerie smiles.

chapters.title: Chapter 520: On the Brink of Conflict
chapters.content:
Chapter 520 - On the Brink of Conflict
The grand palace, with its red-tiled floor and gold pillars, slowly opened its massive doors. First to enter were two werewolves covered in thick fur and a grotesque bat-like creature with festering boils all over its body.
They carefully scanned the hall. The bat creature sniffed the air as if trying to catch a scent but found nothing unusual. Once they confirmed no enemies were present, one of the werewolves retreated behind the door.
A few minutes later, a small team of ten members filed in. Leading them was Chief Fate, who had previously killed Colonel Lloyd.
Half a step behind him were two men and a woman, followed by six other Beyonders, including the werewolf who had gone back to report.
Among the men, one was a lean young man with deep brown skin and unsettling red eyes. Despite his otherwise handsome features, patches of swollen, festering wounds marred his face, making him look somewhat repulsive.
The other was an elderly man with white hair and beard, exuding an eerie aura surrounded by deathly energy.
The woman, dressed in a white blouse and beige trousers, was none other than Vice Admiral of Ailment Tracy. However, her expression was peculiar, and a middle-aged man's reflection flickered in her eyes—clearly, she had been possessed by another Wraith from the Rose School.
Out of the six Sequence 5 powerhouses that had entered the labyrinth, they had already lost two.
"Tracy," now under possession, lewdly ran her hands over her own body, letting out a grotesque laugh. "As expected of a Demoness, far better than any woman I've vented on... Fate, are you sure I can't add her to my tribe? She killed Damian just now, shouldn't she pay the price?"
Both the red-eyed youth and the grim elder gave her a look of disgust without responding. Chief Fate, although part of the Indulgence Faction, had no interest in such perversions. He simply replied coldly:
"Sure, as long as you can handle the retribution of a Demoness of Unaging. But don't even think of touching her until we finish the mission. Otherwise..."
He didn't finish the sentence, but his threat was clear. Even if Tracy was merely a legacy of the Temperance Faction, she was still connected to the Rose School. The Saints would never tolerate outsiders laying claim to their people without severe punishment.
Possessed Tracy begrudgingly groped herself one last time before joining the others to hear the bat creature's report.
"My lord... after our investigation, we detected a powerful seal on the first platform of the hall. It seems to require a corresponding item to unlock it," the bat respectfully informed them. Werewolves were not exactly known for their expertise in such matters.
In truth, this "seal" was an extension of the original palace arrangements, cleverly repurposed by Ebner. The real key was needed for the second platform, not the first.
Chief Fate cast a glance at the red-eyed youth and the grim elder, signaling them to verify the findings.
Although a Wraith himself, Chief Fate's hot temper had hindered his ability to study mystical knowledge, leaving him lacking in expertise.
The youth, a Scarlet Scholar, and the elder, a Gatekeeper, were far more knowledgeable in such matters.
Since Chief Fate was a student of a Saint, his status was the highest among the group. Even though the two men were also Sequence 5 Beyonders, they still obeyed his command and approached the seal set up by Ebner. After a moment of observation, both shook their heads, unable to decipher it.
Seeing this, the hot-tempered Chief Fate drew a long sword and struck at the invisible barrier of the seal. The impact merely caused a faint ripple.
"As expected of the arrangement by the Left Hand of God. Even after hundreds of years, it's beyond us to break... We'll have to wait for the Ruen folks to arrive. After all, the key is in their hands," Chief Fate sighed as he sheathed his sword.
The others did not object to this outcome and patiently waited. Only the possessed "Tracy" occasionally teased the ghouls and werewolves following them, laughing coquettishly as they grew restless but forcibly restrained themselves. Her antics continued until Chief Fate reprimanded her once again.
...
Hidden behind the barrier, Ebner wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. Chief Fate's slash had nearly broken through his setup and exposed their presence. Although their side had the genuine Sequence 5 Vice Admiral Iceberg, as well as himself and Jane, both with combat abilities not inferior to Sequence 5, they were still at a significant disadvantage compared to the Rose School's forces. Moreover, the lion's stance was unclear, and Ebner had no intention of counting on it to fight desperately for them.
"Two Wraiths, one Scarlet Scholar, one Gatekeeper, four Zombies, two werewolves, and two vampires," the lion muttered, a flash of silver in its eyes before yawning. "That's quite the lineup. Should be enough for you to have a decent fight."
"If we can rescue Tracy, she'll likely join our side," Vice Admiral Iceberg Edwina suggested, her pale blue eyes flickering with anger as she watched the Rose School Wraiths humiliate Tracy. Although Edwina was not friends with Tracy, she couldn't bear to see her treated so disgracefully.
"Once the Loen military forces arrive, there will definitely be chaos. That'll be our chance to rescue her and give the Rose School some trouble," Ebner nodded in agreement. He then warned, "That chief's sword possesses the Reaper's ability, capable of delivering deadly attacks. Be very careful."
Edwina solemnly nodded, indicating she would be cautious. Meanwhile, Jane also nodded but subtly directed her gaze toward the Gatekeeper elder, pondering: "The Queen mentioned before my departure that my opportunity to advance to Sequence 5 lies in this mission. Could she have been referring to him?"
At the same time, Ebner, having spiritually sealed the surroundings, quietly prayed to The Fool, relaying the gathered intelligence to Xio.
...
Above the gray fog, Klein pondered after conveying Ebner's information:
"Mr. Tower and Miss Judgment are both in Daniel's Labyrinth...
I had previously confirmed that they were both Climbers...
Could this labyrinth be part of the Dream Labyrinth Tower? Are they clearing a trial? But if it's not part of the Dream Labyrinth Tower and is genuinely Daniel's Labyrinth, then Mr. Tower and Miss Judgment sure have a remarkable connection with Liu Bo's remnants.
Hmm... I'll have to subtly probe the Emperor later to find out what was left there and who ultimately obtained it."
...
On Sonia Island, in the Silent Town.
As the sinister black fog engulfed the town, crimson runes emerged on the ground, and overwhelming terror spread across the faces of every resident on Sonia Island.
Standing atop an altar constructed from countless white bones, the Church of the God of Combat's senior deacon, Nyango Iziamai Panin, manipulated by the "Duke of Terror" Adabao, began sacrificing himself and the weapon imbued with the God of Combat's divine power. He offered these as tributes to the "Lord of the Abyss, the symbol of erosion and corruption, the destroyer of vast universes, The Devil Monarch Farbauti," praying for His descent.
At that moment, the Saints of the Feysac military were out on patrol, and the Church of the God of Combat's reinforcements couldn't arrive in time. The stationed soldiers and clergy had already been mentally corrupted by Adabao, turning into his unwitting allies.
It seemed that nothing could prevent the ritual's success.
However, suddenly, a pirate who hadn't been selected among the 666 in the town lifted his shirt, revealing a thin, brownish-yellow puppet embedded in his chest and abdomen.
The puppet appeared to have grown from his body, connected to his internal organs. Its eyes and mouth curved like crescent moons, and its body was adorned with dried flowers and withered grass, radiating an indescribable eeriness.
In an instant, the puppet turned blood-red, as if soaked in fresh blood.
It then visibly softened, transforming into a heap of sludge that led deep into the pirate's entrails.
From the sludge, a black, grotesque arm extended, dripping with viscous liquid. Bizarre forms bulged along its surface—skulls, spiked tongues, and three-dimensional eyes.
"Abomination" Suah!
As this divine offspring appeared, pirates, soldiers, and clergy outside the Silent Town began to mutate. Some hunched over, sprouting gray-black fur, their drooling mouths twisted into grotesque shapes. Others had their skin turn jet-black, becoming as hard as steel. A few collapsed, seemingly lifeless, only to rise again without any visible harm. Some bodies turned transparent and intangible, morphing into shadowy figures.
Merely being exposed to the offspring's aura led to collapse and death for some, while others mutated into werewolves, ghouls, and other Beyonder creatures.
Curiously, the 666 within the town remained unaffected, still bearing that eerie blend of fear and joy on their faces.
On the altar, Panin turned his head to meet Suah's gaze without fear of contamination, grinning, "As expected, you've come!"
Then he looked skyward, his lips curling into a smirk. "As agreed, it's time for you to act."
As soon as his words fell, two elder figures appeared before Suah. One looked plain and unremarkable, with completely white hair, while the other had fiery red hair exuding an aura of iron and blood.
"This isn't a necessary development for the times, Adabao," the red-haired man said after glancing at Panin.
The ordinary-looking elder merely smiled without speaking.
"But it doesn't hinder the development of the times, does it? Besides, this is something the Chairman would be pleased to see," Panin replied with a smile as he continued presiding over the ritual. "Moreover, you owe me one."
"Ten minutes. I'll help for only ten minutes," the red-haired man stated calmly, glancing at the writhing black, sticky mass that formed Suah's body.
"No problem," Adabao replied confidently.
Suddenly, another area nearby became vividly colored, and a pustule-covered monster emerged from it. After surveying the scene, it spoke in a grating voice:
"The Mother Tree's judgment was correct. Paz Valley was merely a diversion. This is your true goal! Demons, you're trying to help Farbauti break free!"
Panin's face remained indifferent, his tone dismissive: "Yes, you're absolutely right. But you can't stop us."
The pus-covered monster let out a hideous laugh, sneering, "Do you think the Mother Tree wouldn't be prepared?"
As soon as the words fell, branches entwined around the monster, tightly binding it. Instead of weakening it, this only made its aura surge even stronger.
The Chained God had transmitted power from afar!
...
Meanwhile, Xio had regrouped with Prince Mountbatten and his team, and together they stepped into the grand palace at the deepest level of the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 521: Unsealed
chapters.content:
Chapter 521 - Unsealed
Due to the lack of mirror-world traversal abilities, the number of Beyonders gathered around Prince Mountbatten was far fewer than that of the Rose School. Including Xio, there were only six.
The other members were either still wandering within the maze or had already been killed by the Rose School.
Among the six, three were Sequence 5 powerhouses: Priest of Light Irwin, the Prince's direct subordinate and Reaper Myron, and Baron Larry, a Disciplinary Paladin who originally served as the captain of a bait team.
With the temporary leadership of the Ocean Songster Prince Mountbatten, they barely managed to match the Rose School in high-end combat power.
Unfortunately, the remaining three Beyonders included only Xio at Sequence 6, while the other two were Sequence 7 members directly under the Prince's command: Seafarer Cade and the sharp-minded black-haired young man Bass.
Upon stepping into the grand hall at the maze's deepest point, their group was immediately encircled by the Rose School members. Had Prince Mountbatten not been holding up a puppet, his finger pressed against a badge on it, the Rose Schoolers would have attacked right away.
Prince Mountbatten swept his gaze over the enemies, feeling heavy-hearted but maintaining a composed demeanor as he spoke, "Chief Fate, I'll say it again—fighting before seeing the treasure is extremely foolish."
"You think you're in any position to negotiate?" Chief Fate rubbed his bald head, sneering.
Having vented his earlier rage, he was now in a more level-headed state to handle matters.
"Why not? If I release the seal on '1-025,' it will kill everyone here," Prince Mountbatten stated in a tone laden with subtle menace.
"If it means denying you access to the treasure, offering myself to the gods would be worth it!" Chief Fate spoke defiantly but had clearly softened his stance.
He knew full well that he could indeed resort to such a desperate move, but his fellow Sequence 5 members likely lacked the same unwavering faith.
Prince Mountbatten recognized his shift in tone but chose not to point it out, chuckling, "I believe in your resolve... but wouldn't it be better to hold onto that resolve until after we've seen the treasure?
"What if there's nothing inside, and it's just a trap laid by Master Daniel? Dying now would only let him have the last laugh."
Seeing that the Prince had extended an olive branch, Chief Fate feigned hesitation before signaling to Tracy and the pustule-faced youth beside him, instructing them to clear a path to the first platform. "The seal's up there."
Prince Mountbatten guarded the rear with "1-025" in hand, leading his subordinates up the steps to an invisible barrier.
Priest of Light Irwin stepped forward, examined it briefly, and turned back, reporting, "Prince, it's just as the records describe. Place '1-025' on the stone platform to the left, and the barrier will be lifted."
As a Priest of Light, Irwin had only a rudimentary understanding of rituals, but even that made him more reliable than the Reaper, Ocean Songster, or Disciplinary Paladin in such matters.
The black-haired, curly-headed young man Bass glanced at the barrier, a faint smile curling his lips before quickly fading. He lowered his head without saying anything.
Prince Mountbatten cautiously approached the barrier, holding "1-025" in one hand while flipping a coin with the other, seemingly confirming something.
Afterward, he vibrated the air in a particular way, transmitting his voice exclusively to his companions, ensuring that the outsiders heard nothing: "Once the seal is lifted, the Rose School will likely attack immediately. Be prepared.
"Additionally, the information we have suggests that the maze will collapse shortly after the seal is broken. The previously blocked passages connecting to reality will reopen. So, whoever gets the ship ticket must immediately use a mirror to return to reality.
"Rest assured, Master Daniel probably left a safe way out for the treasure's inheritor. You'll likely reappear far from Loen or the Southern Continent, but it shouldn't be too dangerous.
"Afterward, regardless of where you end up, regroup at Pritz Harbor. Alternatively, return directly to MI9 headquarters in Backlund."
This last remark was directed at Baron Larry and Xio.
The group had no objections. Xio nodded and discreetly scanned the area, but she couldn't spot Ebner.
—Because of concerns about any mind-reading Beyonders in the group, Ebner hadn't disclosed his plan to her.
Xio had only gleaned from the information Ebner sent via The Fool that he was likely hiding nearby.
After briefing everyone, Prince Mountbatten prepared to place "1-025" on a stone platform to the left.
There were similar stone platforms on both the left and right across all three platforms, but the right-side ones held ornate decorations, while the left remained empty.
"Your Highness, lifting the seal might be dangerous. Let me handle it." Seafarer Cade suddenly suggested, "I'm also a Sailor-pathway Beyonder and can undo the seal on '1-025' anytime if they make a sudden move."
He spoke loudly, deliberately letting the Rose School members hear. They responded with sneers but no action.
Prince Mountbatten glanced at his aide, hesitated briefly, and then nodded, "Very well."
Carefully, he handed "1-025" to Cade.
At the same time, Chief Fate whispered to his team, "The moment the seal lifts, attack immediately. Don't let them near the third platform."
"Understood," the pustule-faced red-eyed youth and the cold, deathly old man replied succinctly.
The Wraith controlling Tracy's scantily clad body asked in surprise, "What if they unleash '1-025'?"
"Is your brain filled with nothing but women? Once the seal lifts, the treasure will be right in front of us. They'll definitely want something from inside. Why would they start by mutually destroying everyone?"
Chief Fate cursed under his breath before falling silent, appearing relaxed but fully prepared to strike.
...
On the second platform, within the seal arranged by Ebner, he and his companions, along with the lion, remained hidden by the ritual, waiting for the chaos of battle to seize "1-025" and unlock the true seal of the grand hall.
As the Seafarer took a deep breath and placed the puppet on the stone platform, Ebner swiftly adjusted the ritual, voluntarily lifting the seal he'd set on the first platform.
Immediately, the Scarlet Scholar leaped into the air, transforming into a full moon. All the werewolves and undead on the scene howled with extreme malice and charged toward the first platform at unprecedented speed, swiftly blocking Prince Mountbatten and his team's attempt to seize the treasure.
