Your nose is really sharp. You remembered my scent from a single meeting at the police station over six months ago? That's almost on par with the 'Pure White Eye's' ability to extract traces.
Suppressing his inner thoughts, Ebner maintained a polite smile and replied, "I've been in Feysac until recently."
Feysac...? But I've never been to Feysac... Could that sense of familiarity and kinship really be just an illusion?
Emlyn pondered for a few seconds but decided not to dwell on it further. Instead, after some hesitation, he solemnly asked, "Mr. Specter, may I trouble you with a favor?"
—Max Specter was the alias Ebner used for his current identity as a lover of the Countess. When he visited yesterday, he had introduced himself by this name to Bishop Utravsky, Hazel, and Emlyn.
"What kind of favor? Go ahead," Ebner asked curiously.
He had never known Emlyn to be this familiar with strangers. His current identity should be little more than an acquaintance to him.
"I want you to keep an eye out for this doll... It's my favorite, a masterpiece by Grandmaster Tano from a hundred years ago... But a few days ago, it suddenly disappeared!
"If you see it in any shop, market, or exhibition, please let me know!"
As he spoke, Emlyn took out a thick piece of cardboard with an illustration of a doll drawn on it. Then, gritting his teeth, he added, "If I find out who took it, I will make them pay!
"Did they think that leaving money behind makes it any less of a theft?!"
At that moment, Ebner struggled to keep his expression from turning strange—because the doll in Emlyn's drawing was identical to the one he had just seen in the mirror of the washroom!
....
Klein left Lina and Shoko's café and returned to Minsk Street in the Chorwood district. The sky had already turned completely dark, and the glow of gas street lamps was even brighter than the faintly visible crimson moon overhead.
He initially planned to visit Lawyer Jurgen's house for a free meal and to pet his cat. However, just as he strolled up to No. 15, his spirituality was suddenly stirred—he sensed that someone had been inside his home.
Who could it be? That fake Baron Larry? Did he come looking for me after failing to find me elsewhere?
Klein performed a divination and determined that there was no immediate danger. Only then did he cautiously unlock the door, step inside, and scan the room warily. Soon, his gaze landed on an envelope placed on the coffee table.
Lowering his eyes, he scrutinized the envelope for a moment, then pulled out a pair of black gloves and put them on before picking it up and tearing it open.
Inside was a thin piece of stationery. The moment he unfolded it, dark red letters came into view, accompanied by a faint, lingering scent of blood.
On the letter, words written in dried blood read:
"You will all die!"
A threat? From who?
They used the word 'you all'... The only case I've publicly worked on with others was the Demon Hound serial murder case... Could it be the owner of that dog seeking revenge?
Klein's heart tightened as he swiftly analyzed the situation.
Later, in his bedroom, he found another blood-written threat letter. This time, he did not hesitate—he immediately chose to report it to the police.
During this process, he took advantage of a trip to the police station's washroom to enter the world above the gray fog. Through "The World," he informed Miss "Justice" of his predicament.
Miss "Justice" did not hesitate and assured him that she would rush to Minsk Street as soon as possible to provide covert protection.
With Sharon's promise, Klein felt visibly relieved. Though he didn't know what the Demon Hound's owner was planning, one thing was certain: the enemy could not possibly be a demigod. With Sharon's assistance, even if they couldn't win, they should at least be able to protect themselves.
However, upon his cautious return to Minsk Street, he found that one detective after another was showing up at his home.
Among them was Detective Isengard Stanton, who was seriously injured.
From his account, Klein finally gained a clearer understanding of the enemy he was facing.
.....
A few streets away from Minsk Street, in a safe house—undoubtedly one rented by Xio—Ebner and Xio successfully rendezvoused. There, Xio handed him a Sealed Artifact that could briefly block the influence of "0-08."
It was a pair of earrings, named:
"The Primordial Trick" and "The Final Conspiracy."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 620: Arrodes Finally Found Its Master
chapters.content:
Chapter 620 - Arrodes Finally Found Its Master
The materials used to craft these earrings were incredibly peculiar. Even "Pure White Eye" couldn't immediately analyze their composition, only determining that their essence was extremely high—possibly something not even originating from this planet.
Moreover, they were named "The Primordial Trick" and "The Final Conspiracy" with such an imposing flair because they were tainted with the divine blood of two gods!
One of them, Ebner was certain, came from the "Primordial Demoness." As for the other—whether it belonged to the "Blood Emperor" or the "God of Death"—he couldn't tell.
Ebner's intuition suggested the latter. These earrings were likely crafted after the Pale Disaster, during which both the "Primordial Demoness" and the "God of Death" were severely wounded by the Seven Gods, making the presence of divine blood entirely reasonable.
In terms of essence alone, these earrings absolutely rivaled a "Grade 0 Sealed Artifact." However, due to the extraordinary craftsmanship of their creator and the unique properties of the materials, the earrings sealed each other, maintaining a delicate balance that reduced their potential harm by ninety percent.
Of course, this balance and sealing also stripped them of almost all their abilities, leaving only a single function: providing "Concealment of Conspiracy" for Beyonders of the "Hunter" and "Witch" pathways.
This was likely an advanced application of the "Conspirator" and "Instigator" abilities, refined to a level approaching true godhood.
Notably, only "Hunter" and "Witch" pathway Beyonders could use them due to the intricate sealing structure of the earrings.
When their own pathway's aura activated their power, the balance could still barely hold. But if another pathway's aura contaminated them, the equilibrium would break, briefly lifting the earrings' seal.
And once "The Primordial Trick" and "The Final Conspiracy" were unsealed, their negative effects were terrifying—ordinary demigods wouldn't even survive the ensuing calamity. Most would perish before they could even attempt to wield them...
After gaining a preliminary understanding of the artifact through "Pure White Eye," Ebner became intrigued by its origins.
Unfortunately, his "Pure White Eye" currently only provided analysis, not insight. To uncover the full story of these earrings, he would likely have to rely on "The Fool" to recklessly experiment with them.
Seeing Ebner set the earrings down, Xio forcefully suppressed an inexplicable sense of anticipation in her gaze and instead asked seriously, "Ebner, can you use them?"
You're actually wondering if I can use my 'Magic Mirror'-pastured spirit to imitate a 'Witch,' right? Xio, when did you start enjoying this kind of entertainment?
After internally complaining for a few seconds, Ebner thought for a moment before giving a definitive answer. "Yes!"
As he spoke, he stroked the magic mirror in his pocket, and his entire aura instantly became enchanting... At the same time, his facial features started adjusting on their own, his body shape and bone structure shifting as well...
Within seconds, Xio was left dumbfounded as she watched Ebner transform into her exact likeness—except taller, with a better figure, more refined curves, and an even more captivating presence...
This was actually the image Xio had envisioned for herself in her dream last night, just without the "Witch's" inherent allure. Ebner had been too lazy to adjust his appearance, so he conveniently borrowed her idealized self-image. It was definitely not meant to be some kind of subtle mockery...
And the moment Ebner, in this transformed state, put on the earrings, his entire presence vanished!
Xio tried using various methods, even amplifying her detection abilities with mystical items, but she still couldn't sense anything—not even though he was right in front of her.
The concept of "Unperceivable Brewing Conspiracy," derived from the "Conspirator" pathway's power, was nearly equivalent to divine authority. For someone like Xio, who wasn't even a demigod, failing to detect anything was perfectly normal.
After all, with the right ritual, even "0-08" could be momentarily deceived.
Xio examined Ebner's "new appearance," but she didn't suspect anything. After all, she couldn't actually see what she looked like in her own dreams.
At this point, her amusement had faded, replaced by a tinge of envy...
Maybe I should use this appearance in the next Tarot Meeting?
Just as Xio's thoughts began to drift, gunshots suddenly rang out from House No. 15 on Minsk Street. Almost immediately, a viscous black liquid seeped through the walls and vanished into the night.
Had it not been for Ebner using the "Tudor Emblem" to distort the propagation of "light" and magnify the scene as if the house were right in front of them, they would never have noticed the "black liquid" at all.
"They really came... That 'Desire Apostle' is truly bold! And he actually managed to retreat unscathed from Klein, Sharon, and my teacher..."
Klein now possessed several powerful Beyonder artifacts that he didn't have at this point in the original timeline. Even an ordinary Sequence 5 would struggle against him. Detective Isengard, besides his own Sealed Artifacts, also had the "Ring of Light" that Ebner had lent him for protection.
Miss Sharon could be set aside for now—official Beyonders were lying in ambush nearby. Unless Klein was truly in mortal danger, she likely wouldn't intervene...
But even so, for the "Desire Apostle" to escape so smoothly despite this lineup... How many mistakes had they made during the battle?
...
On the rooftop of a seven-story building, five or six blocks away from Minsk Street, Vera gently brushed aside a lock of hair lifted by the night wind and smiled to herself.
"From Xio's report on the arrangements around Baron Larry, I already suspected that a Saint of the 'Spectator' pathway was helping my dear brother orchestrate his schemes... And as expected, I was right! It turns out to be that royal advisor... However, his skills still need some polishing... Personally stepping in to 'suggest' things? That's not how a true 'Spectator' should act! But this works in my favor... Ariehogg is in need of a catalyst right now..."
...
Inside House No. 15 on Minsk Street, Klein stared at the bullet holes in the walls with a pained expression as he, Detective Isengard Stanton, and another female detective, Caslana, discussed the series of tactical errors they had made during their battle with the "Desire Apostle." Caslana was a Beyonder of the "Arbiter" pathway, likely connected to either the military or nobility.
As they talked, Caslana, the weakest of the three and somewhat sentimental, suddenly became somber. With a sigh, she said, "This was the most dangerous incident I've ever been caught up in. I don't know if I would have survived in the end. If... if I were killed by the 'Desire Apostle,' I hope my tombstone would say: 'She had a great mother.'" Her voice grew softer, and the usual firmness in her expression was replaced by a rare gentleness.
Isengard nodded in deep agreement. "This was also the most dangerous enemy I've ever faced." But then, he chuckled. "Still, I don't plan on dying so easily... In fact, if our teamwork had been a little smoother, we could have kept him here."
Besides, my student and my friend are nearby. If anyone should be worried, it's that 'Desire Apostle.'
...Stop recklessly setting up death flags! And not just one, but multiple kinds of flags... Are you trying to jinx us all? Good thing Detective Isengard didn't throw in a dramatic 'Who can kill me?'
Klein opened his mouth slightly, unsure how to even begin ridiculing the two detectives in front of him.
Maybe I should follow up with, 'After this case, I'll go back home and get married'—just to complete the cliché?
But unfortunately, I don't even know how to return home...
Isengard glanced at Klein, who had suddenly fallen into a low mood, and asked with a mix of curiosity and concern, "Sherlock, are you worried? Or do you have some wish you'd like someone to fulfill?"
With my bodyguard lady here, there's no way I'd die... And if I had a wish, I'd fulfill it myself!
Klein glanced at the ordinary mirror he carried, where Sharon was resting her chin on her hands, listening to their conversation. He sighed and said, "I just hope to be buried in a nice cemetery with a good view, with my body intact, sprinkled with holy water and fresh flowers..."
Basically, no cremation! Future Sherlocks who may end up with multiple graves...
Sharon, listening through the mirror, instinctively gave him a new nickname.
The three fell into silence until the sound of a doorbell rang outside.
Moments later, a deacon from the Machinery Hivemind, Ikonser Bernard, entered, carrying an ancient silver mirror with intricate patterns.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 621: Before the Action
chapters.content:
Chapter 621 - Before the Action
In the washroom, behind a locked door, Klein recalled the words that the silver mirror named "Arrodes" had secretly shown him and pondered:
"'Your loyal and humble servant, Arrodes, at your service'?"
"What's going on? That mirror was just coldly toying with the Machinery Hivemind's Deacon, Ikonser... How did it suddenly change its attitude?"
Klein found the situation both amusing and puzzling. It was unclear whether he was speaking to himself or addressing someone unseen.
As soon as he finished his sentence, the image in the half-body mirror above the sink rippled and shifted, transforming into a woman in a black court dress—Miss Sharon.
She rested her chin on her hand and contemplated briefly before simply stating, "You are a Blessed."
So, you're saying that the silver mirror has some connection to the spirit world... and the mysterious space above the gray fog also seems intertwined with the spirit world. Since I am the Blessed of the 'Fool'... I carry the aura of the gray fog, which that mirror, Arrodes, detected?
After "translating" Sharon's words in his mind, Klein found the reasoning quite plausible—and it also served as a convenient excuse...
With that thought, he said to Sharon, "Watch over my body for a moment. I need to... report this matter."
"Alright." Sharon nodded lightly and watched as Sherlock murmured the honorific name of "The Fool" in an almost inaudible voice, then took four steps backward. Moments later, he became motionless.
"Those four steps... are they part of a ritual to please 'The Fool'?"
Sharon pondered as she stepped out from the mirror.
In the mysterious space above the gray fog, Klein, seated in the Fool's position, first extended his spirituality to listen to Miss Justice's request.
—The reason he had entered the washroom and ascended to the gray fog was precisely because he had heard Justice's prayers.
As expected, her request was about finally passing the preliminary evaluations of the Psychological Alchemy Society. That very night, she would face the final test and needed the Fool's protection.
Klein was already well-versed in the process of the "Paper Angel's Blessing," so he followed the usual procedure. Before long, he flicked a roughly cut but slightly improved paper figurine forward.
As expected, the paper figurine gathered the power stirred by the "Black Emperor" card above the gray fog and transformed into a giant angel with twelve pairs of black wings. Through the crimson star, it enveloped Miss Justice in its embrace.
After finishing this task, Klein turned his attention to another crimson star that pulsed with expansion and contraction—it belonged to Mr. Tower.
It doesn't seem urgent... just a message?
Hmm, has he found a way to save Talim?
With that thought, Klein tapped the crimson star and read the message. Upon finishing, his brows furrowed.
"Talim is afflicted with a curse that only an angel-level entity can remove?"
"And Mr. Tower actually managed to get an 'angel' to help him?"
"Just what is his true identity...? Could he really be a Blessed of the Earth Mother?"
Sharon had once suggested this possibility, though she herself wasn't entirely certain.
The more Klein thought about it, the more he felt a headache coming on—not because he was worried about Mr. Tower's background. After all, having spent so much time together in the Tarot Club, he trusted this "erudite" gentleman.
However, rescuing Talim was proving to be far more challenging than he had expected. This wasn't something that could be repaid with mere intelligence on Baron Larry...
Although Mr. Tower hadn't mentioned any additional compensation and had even asked him to keep it a secret from Miss Judgment...
"The World" couldn't just play dumb and offer nothing in return. That would go against "The Fool's" principle of equivalent exchange.
The only question now was—what could "The World" offer that would be enough to repay the favor of an angel's intervention?
Sigh, I'll have to ask Mr. Tower privately during the next Tarot Meeting... Hopefully, he needs some high-level knowledge that I possess.
With that thought, Klein exhaled and allowed his spirit body to descend back into reality.
Seeing Sharon's deep blue eyes turn toward him, Klein coughed lightly and said, "'The Fool' says... don't concern yourself with that mirror."
Because worrying about it is pointless...
Sharon nodded slightly, her figure gradually fading until she disappeared completely.
Because it wouldn't make a difference anyway...
Sharon nodded slightly, her figure gradually fading before disappearing altogether.
Klein washed his hands, returned to the living room, and stared at the bullet hole in the wall, lost in thought.
Should I cover them with a cheap oil painting, patch them up, or repaint?
Or ask Mr. Tower's mentor to inquire if the Machinery Hivemind will reimburse renovation costs? After all, this damage technically resulted from their ambush...
...
Hillston Borough, Seventh Avenue, at the home of Escalante, a member of the Psychological Alchemists.
With the "Angel's Blessing" from Mr. Fool, Audrey successfully passed the final assessment of the two men before her and officially became a member of the Psychological Alchemists.
—One of the men was Gilbert Alucard, a psychologist introduced to her by Lady Norma, the sister of Nigen Duchess, Emma's mother. The other was Stephen Humphreys, the convener of the previous psychology seminar.
Both were key members of the Psychological Alchemists.
Afterward, the two men provided Audrey with an overview of the organization's history and ideology, mentioning Hermes and the "Mind Dragon." Finally, they presented her with a potion—Telepathist Potion.
However, no one noticed that when those two names were spoken, something silently infiltrated their mental islands.
Leaving Escalante's house with the potion in hand, Audrey remained quiet along the way, speaking little. It wasn't until she entered her room and briefly dismissed her personal maid, Annie, that she turned to the golden retriever, Susie, and smiled.
"Your potion is ready~"
Susie wagged her tail happily at the sight of the Telepathist Potion.
"When you become a Telepathist, I have another gift for you," Audrey said with a smile, glancing at the gold-rimmed glasses hanging around Susie's neck.
"Audrey, what gift?" Susie tilted her head curiously.
"A pair of earrings called 'Dragon's Eyes.'"
Audrey had worn them a few times after purchasing them from Miss Judgment. However, since they were an outdated design, Annie would never allow her to wear them outside—after all, it might make people suspect that the Hall family was facing financial trouble, leading to misunderstandings.
But what was the use of wearing mystical items at home? After thinking it over, Audrey decided to temporarily entrust them to Susie.
"Earrings? What do they do?" Susie asked in confusion.
Audrey thought for a moment and then answered confidently, "With them, those stray dogs that try to court you won't dare to come near!"
After all, they carried the "Dragon's Might"...
Hearing this, Susie wagged her tail even more joyfully.
...
At 2 AM, inside the lounge of the Dream Labyrinth Tower.
Holding a pair of earrings, Ebner transformed under Xio's gaze into a beautiful woman with jet-black curls and deep blue eyes.
"Tracy?" Xio recognized the Vice Admiral of Ailment from their encounter in the palace at the deepest part of Daniel's Labyrinth.
"Yes... Since Talim's situation involves a Demoness's curse, I might as well take the form of another Demoness with powerful backing to rescue him. Even if the enemy uses special means to investigate, they'll suspect Tracy instead."
"If they start turning on each other, that's a win for us..."
Ebner explained with a faint smile.
This expression made Xio momentarily dazed. She turned her head slightly and asked, "You set up teleportation altars in two locations but only showed me the one outside the city... Is the one inside the city a one-time use?"
"The one in Cherwood Borough is meant to be abandoned. I set it to self-destruct upon activation... Teleporting within Backlund is too dangerous.
"Meanwhile, the one outside the city is necessary for my return and is in a good location for long-term use," Ebner explained while changing into pirate attire.
That was Tracy's style... though it might be a bit chilly outside—Backlund was in the depths of winter.
"Where do you plan to take him?" Xio asked curiously, trying to keep her gaze steady.
"To Edwina's ship... I already spoke to her.
"She's quite satisfied with Talim's academic background."

chapters.title: Chapter 622: Talim, Who Boarded a Pirate Ship
chapters.content:
Chapter 622 - Talim, Who Boarded a Pirate Ship
In a hidden room, a man and a woman were entangled in passion, their heavy breaths filling the space.
The man had striking features, but one of his eyes was blind—he was none other than Ince Zangwill. Just as he was about to reach the peak of pleasure, he caught a glimpse from the corner of his eye: the quill on the desk had unexpectedly broken free from its "seal" and was writing in the open diary on its own.
Ince's heart jolted. He immediately lost all interest in pleasure, pushing aside the woman beside him and leaping to the desk, seizing the quill.
The woman on the bed, a beauty with a hint of laziness in her demeanor, let out a dissatisfied hum. She then dressed herself and walked over to Ince in no particular hurry, pouting, "I even skipped overseeing that 'Desire Apostle' just to keep you company, and this is how you treat me?"
You skipped overseeing the "Desire Apostle" because "Arrogance" was with them, didn't you? Do you think I don't know?
Though that thought crossed her mind, Ince Zangwill did not argue; instead, he said grimly, "Something unexpected happened!"
"What kind of unexpected event?" the woman—Despair Nightingale, Panatia—swept her gaze over to the diary and saw a few freshly written lines:
"...Talim suddenly woke up from his dream. He seemed to have seen something and looked quite surprised.
"Talim was confused by something. Under an unknown pull, he left his residence in Cherwood Borough and walked toward South Riverside Street along the Tasok River.
"Talim entered the vacant house at No. 23..."
The quill had stopped writing at this point, as Ince had already grasped it. He crossed out the last sentence and replaced it with a new one:
"The target has decided to kill Talim immediately using a curse. She had already considered this when collecting his blood, so this development is reasonable."
"Talim? That subordinate of Prince Edsack? He shouldn't know anything..." Panatia mused.
"He indeed knows nothing, but that doesn't stop certain people from deducing things through him! Especially since someone has managed to block '0-08's' perception..." Ince shook his head before continuing, "You'd best accelerate your plan to avoid any unforeseen complications."
"The preparations aren't complete yet. Even if we speed things up, we still need at least ten more days..." Panatia said as she finished putting on her jewelry and shoes.
"Are you heading to South Riverside Street?" Ince frowned slightly. "Be careful—it might be a trap."
"Are you worried about me?" Panatia flashed an intoxicating smile, but when her eyes met Ince's cold, one-eyed gaze, she couldn't help but click her tongue. "Tch, boring man!" she muttered under her breath.
With that, she walked toward the door but turned back before leaving. "I'm about to impersonate that Desire Apostle to lure away the Spellsinger of God... Do me a favor—have a few Mandated Punishers conveniently discover the anomaly at that house on Riverside Street. I want to use 'Jason Beria's' identity to eliminate them while conducting a quick investigation there...
"This way, the mastermind trying to take Talim away might just end up bearing the wrath of the Spellsinger of God for me."
Ince Zangwill pondered for a moment before nodding. "Alright."
"Then, I'll let you enjoy the pleasure we left unfinished once I return." Panatia threw him an ambiguous air kiss, and her figure gradually faded, as if erased by an invisible hand.
...
In Bayam, inside the underground chamber of Fragrant Manor.
Ebner watched as the doll he had placed on Talim suddenly cracked all over. Tiny black flames emerged from the fissures.
As expected, mere distance couldn't block a curse of this level... Fortunately, the "Chained God"—no, the "God of Spiritual Creature"—had taken on the burden of the curse for him.
While he was deep in thought, the flames within the cracks slowly gathered into thin black strings, tightly binding the doll.
Moments later, the intangible flames solidified, as if they had truly turned into ropes binding the doll, losing all supernatural traces.
After glancing at Talim, who remained completely unaware of his predicament due to Ebner's "hypnosis," Ebner reverted to his original form, stowed away the doll, and once again led him into the "circle of fire" that had suddenly appeared on the teleportation altar.
—Speaking of which, the reason Ebner didn't teleport directly to the "Golden Dream" but instead made a stop at Fragrant Manor was to return to his original appearance and change into a new outfit.
After all, it was one thing for Xio to see his "Tracy" disguise, but there was no need to spread it any further...
...
When Talim regained consciousness once more, a beautiful lady with light blue eyes appeared before him.
I remembered that the last time I woke up, I also saw an extremely beautiful woman, but it definitely wasn't this one...
Is this a dream? But why does it feel so real?
Could it be like Sherlock always jokes... that I'm just waking up the wrong way?
Before the dazed Talim could make sense of the situation, the woman in front of him calmly asked, "Which university did you graduate from, and what was your major?"
"Beyonder University, Economics..." Talim replied instinctively.
"Besides Loenese, what other languages are you proficient in?"
"Ancient Feysac and Intisian..."
"How much do you know about history?"
"I've read
A History of the Loen Kingdom
..."
After a few rounds of questioning, Talim finally couldn't hold back anymore and interrupted, "Miss, may I ask where this is? And why am I here?"
"This is the
Golden Dream
," the woman—Edwina—explained unhurriedly, "A friend of mine introduced you to me and asked that I keep you as a crew member for a while. I agreed.
I need to assess your knowledge to determine your role on the ship and what subjects you'll need to study... That's why I was asking you these basic questions."
"The
Golden Dream
?! You... you're the 'Vice Admiral Iceberg'?" Talim stared wide-eyed at the beautiful woman before him, his face full of disbelief. "Stop joking... Miss! I was just in Backlund!"
Edwina remained silent, merely gazing at him for a few seconds before calling for Danitz and instructing, "Help him recognize reality."
"Understood, Captain!"
After responding, Danitz shot a few suspicious glances at Talim, who was only wearing pajamas, wondering why he had appeared in the captain's quarters at this hour.
...
Once Danitz took Talim away to "recognize reality," Ebner finally revealed himself and smiled at Edwina. "I hope Talim adjusts quickly."
This so-called "recognizing reality" was a rule set by Vice Admiral Iceberg for new crew members—it typically started with various kinds of labor. This method was actually somewhat similar to modern boot camp training, meant to instill obedience.
Edwina didn't continue the topic. Instead, she picked up a deep brown, leather-bound book made of parchment and then asked, "Do you remember the invitation I gave you last time—to join me on an expedition?"
Ebner glanced at the book's title and couldn't help but twitch his eyelids before cautiously asking, "Are you saying... the expedition involves entering this book?"
Edwina nodded and replied, "Yes... There is a 'world' inside this book. Its previous owners likely wandered into it and never returned... That's why, despite it being an ancient text from 3,000 years ago, its pages contain figures from various eras throughout history. But I've discovered a possible way to enter safely... thanks to a 'prophecy' given to me by Teacher Isabella..."
"What kind of prophecy?" Ebner asked curiously.
"'The Calamity Seal bestows the Northern King's Key upon the soldier's family.' That was the revelation my teacher received. The 'Calamity Seal' is probably the most beloved Sealed Artifact of Emperor Roselle that 'Lion' Leon mentioned... And the 'soldier' likely refers to the Loen soldier who was the last to enter the book... Unfortunately, after searching for over a month, I still haven't found any clues about his family..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 623: Analysis and Framing
chapters.content:
Chapter 623 - Analysis and Framing
The Calamity Seal gave the Key of the Northern King to the soldier's family?
The
Calamity Seal
again? Why does it keep showing up everywhere? Just how many schemes has it left behind... and for what purpose?
After inwardly complaining, Ebner seriously pondered the meaning of this "prophecy":
"First, that 'soldier' should be, as Edwina suspected, the Loen soldier, Longzel, who accidentally entered
Groselle's Travels
165 years ago. The timing of his entry into the book matches the period when the
Calamity Seal
was active, making him relatively easy to locate. So, did that transmigrator hand over the so-called 'Key of the Northern King' to the soldier's family?
"Second, as a transmigrator, the
Calamity Seal
might have also taken an interest in
Groselle's Travels
... After obtaining the book, it could have created the 'Key of the Northern King' through some means, essentially opening a 'backdoor' into that world. But... does a Conqueror have authority over
Imagination
?
"Wait... I remember in Roselle's diary, he mentioned that before obtaining the
Calamity Seal
, it had already appeared in his dreams... Maybe it really does have some connection to Dreams...
"Moreover, based on Xio's experience in East Chester County, I suspect that the Dragon of Imagination, Ankewelt, has already awakened within the Ancient Dragon, Ariehogg... If I were to make a bold assumption, perhaps it awoke even earlier...
"Could it have been awakened by the
Calamity Seal
? At the very least, it must have been involved...
"
Groselle's Travels
was originally conceived from the imagination of the Dragon King. He holds authority over that world, so creating a 'backdoor' should be effortless... Could the so-called 'Key of the Northern King' have simply been something He conjured at will?"Lastly... Edwina's mentor, Isabella, was able to receive such a 'revelation'. Based on my experience, this suggests she must have gathered a great deal of relevant intelligence, allowing the 'prophecy' to be so precise, with almost no ambiguity.
"And Isabella was extremely close to Roselle—in fact, I've overheard quite a bit from Leon the Lion's constant grumbling... So, if she knew, then Roselle likely knew as well...
"Could
Groselle's Travels
be part of their grand scheme? And if so, what was their goal?"
As thoughts raced through his mind, Ebner suddenly recalled that the first ship he and Xio had taken for their voyage was the Radiant Thousand Cities, captained by Aranson Edward—a direct descendant of Longzel, the Loen soldier who had entered
Groselle's Travels
!
Now that he thought about it, that journey, though originally arranged by his teacher as a way to temporarily escape the Witches, ended up leading them to numerous events related to Dreams—encountering Longzel's descendants, the Dream Labyrinth Tower, and the Ancient Dragon in East Chester County...
Was this just a coincidence? Or was it some form of convergence?
"The deeper I dig, the murkier it gets..." Ebner rubbed his temples, then, after a brief hesitation, spoke to Edwina:
"I have some clues regarding the family of that soldier in the book..."
Edwina's eyes lit up as she eagerly asked, "What are they?"
"The captain of the Radiant Thousand Cities, Aranson, is very likely a descendant of Longzel's family.
"I once sailed on his ship and heard him mention that one of his ancestors mysteriously vanished over 160 years ago... His family used to live in Backlund, and the missing ancestor was also a soldier."
At this point, Ebner recalled that the night in question was the same one when The Fool descended. He had even promised to deliver Aranson's words—"You're always welcome home"—to Longzel if possible... Though, in all likelihood, the captain himself had long since forgotten his drunken ramblings.
"The Radiant Thousand Cities..." Edwina murmured, her pale blue eyes gleaming slightly before she continued, "I'll look into it. If I find anything, I'll inform you immediately."
If it weren't for the looming threat of the Great Smog, I would've liked to personally track down Captain Aranson... After all, this concerns the
Calamity Seal
and transmigrators...
Fortunately, Edwina plans to invite me along when she ventures into
Groselle's Travels
, so I won't be missing out on anything.
Besides, Lilith warned me not to probe too deeply into these transmigrators—especially in front of demigods. So, it's best to let things unfold naturally.
After wrapping up their serious discussion, the two began exchanging stories about their past experiences. Ebner took the opportunity to inform Edwina that he had transferred ownership of his Doctor Strange persona.
However, Edwina hasn't been in the best mood lately. A betrayal had occurred aboard her ship, the Golden Dream—someone had leaked information about the massive black iron key she had salvaged, as well as her ambush on Mr. D of the Aurora Order.
To distract her, Ebner used the Scholar's Exchange Technique to invite her into his learning space, where they exchanged several arcane knowledge models.
.....
Got it! Here's the revised translation with the specified name changes:
Backlund, West District, No. 6 Edward Street.
This is the house of Patrick Jason, who is disguised as the Desire Apostle.
At this moment, the front door of the house suddenly opened, and a group of Nighthawks dressed in black woolen coats hurried inside.
Their expressions were vigilant and on edge, as though facing a terrifying enemy.
Clang, clang, clang. Leonard, fully armored in a silver full-body suit, walked in.
The armor was of an ancient design, and the left shoulder, slanting toward the lower abdomen, was stained with a patch of dark red blood that could not be cleaned off, almost like a unique and extravagant decoration.
"Captain, the demon is not here," Leonard reported after using the armor's ability to "scan" the house.
"Soul Assurer Sost spoke with a nod, then pulled out his pocket watch and glanced at it before saying:
"Switch out!
"Leonard, the hot water is ready in the master bathroom on the second floor, don't waste time. Otherwise, you'll be returning to the Goddess's embrace."
Leonard did not dare delay, quickly disassembling his armor with the help of his colleagues. But at that moment, a Nighthawk rushed in and reported:
"Captain Sost, someone has seen Patrick... no, Jason Beria, near South River Street in Cherwood Borough. Two Mandated Punishers have already gone to investigate... they hope we can offer support nearby."
Although South River Street was in Cherwood Borough, it was separated from the northern district's Nighthawk base only by the Tassok River.
"How did members of the Storm Church get involved in this case?" Sost asked, puzzled.
"A couple of the detectives' families refused protection, believing they wouldn't be implicated, so they stayed outside... As a result, they were found dead in their respective offices. One died of fear, the other from exhaustion after being overly excited.
"They were both followers of the Lord of Storms, so the Mandated Punishers formally took over the case," the Nighthawk explained.
Leonard, halfway through removing his armor, initially did not find this strange. But then, as if recalling something, he casually said:
"Already a lead just after getting involved? How 'coincidental'!"
Coincidence? Captain Sost furrowed his brow at this word.
.....
In a villa in St. George District, Baron Larry looked at the letter he received and muttered to himself:
"The butler of Prince Edessak asked to meet me tonight at the villa on Corte Street, No. 3?
"I remember that place is not far from St. Wind Cathedral...
"Could it be a trap?"
While hesitating, he took out an extraordinary item to perform a divination. Soon, the result showed it was not a "trap."
Baron Larry breathed a sigh of relief and thought:
If I can meet the prince and earn his trust, I might get the chance to meet His Majesty the King... Then I can surely clear my name!!
It's a pity my dear visited just yesterday... If only I could share this good news with her!
She truly is a good woman. If I regain power, I'll take her away from Panis...
....
At the South River Street house, where Ebner had previously set up the "Teleportation Altar," Panatia, wearing the face of the Desire Apostle Jason, placed two Mandated Punishers, both critically injured and near death, on the ground and thought to herself:
"No ambush... Looks like the mastermind's target is only Talim, and they even prepared a one-time teleportation ritual... Too bad they made the wrong choice. The curse released by an 'original' item is not something distance can erase!"
"Heh, although the item shields the aura, Roselle that dead fool once said, 'Everything that passes leaves a trace.' And I just happen to have an item with that ability."
Smiling confidently, Panatia took out a mirror and used it to look around the shattered altar. Soon, she saw a very faint, graceful figure.
"How could it be her?!" Panatia was surprised, but she quickly calmed down, thinking, "No, it's not impossible...
"As far as I know, that mother and daughter pair have recently been to Backlund... Especially Tracey, who deliberately approached Edessak...
"What are they trying to do?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 624: The Scheme Behind the Scenes
chapters.content:
Chapter 624 - The Scheme Behind the Scenes
On Thursday afternoon, Ebner finally returned to the city by carriage.
It wasn't because he had talked too long with Edwina and almost missed his timing, but because he had placed the "Teleportation Altar" in a small town near Backlund. That extra distance meant he had to spend another half a day traveling back.
—Due to the "Apostle of Desire" incident putting the official organizations on high alert, Ebner didn't dare to use the "Cloak" to fly directly into Backlund.
As soon as he stepped down from the carriage, he heard the sound of howling winds.
He instinctively looked up and saw the dim sky being torn apart by fierce gales, sweeping away the thin layer of pale yellow mist.
Leafless branches swayed, and the strong wind left a clear trail, heading straight southeast.
A few seconds later, everything returned to normal, as if nothing had happened.
This isn't an ordinary wind... It carries the familiar power of "Gale"... Did Spellsinger of God Snake go after the witch who disguised herself as Jason Beria? I'm not far from the docks, and the chase has reached this area... That means the assassination attempt on Duke Negan must have either started or is about to start...
I hope I can make it in time... If Klein fails to take him down like in the original plot, I'll step in to finish the job... I can't let that demon escape and become a threat to my teacher in the future...
With that thought, Ebner hurried toward the nearest subway station.
Without the ability to "fly," taking the "Steam Metro" was much faster than running while "invisible."
...
Inside a carriage outside the Quelaag Club.
Under the guise of "deduction," Klein relayed the information he had divined above the gray fog regarding the "Apostle of Desire" to Machinery Hivemind's deacon, Ikonsa.
However, he deliberately withheld the intelligence that the demon's target might be Duke Negan...
After all, such a conclusion would be difficult to explain through mere "deduction." If he hadn't heard Mr. Tower mention during the Tarot Club that the unmentionable organization was using the "Abyss Card" to tempt Blood Sanctify members into assassinating the duke, he wouldn't have made the connection either.
"You think we might have been misled?" Ikonsa didn't mock, dismiss, or belittle the idea. Instead, he seriously considered the issue with him.
After all, any arrogance, conceit, or bias he once had had long been worn down by Arrodes' questions...
Ikonsa pondered for a moment, his expression turning solemn. He glanced at the silver mirror in his hand, then quickly looked away before turning to his subordinates. "Continue protecting Mr. Moriarty in secret. I'm heading to the 'Night Watchers'..."
Interrogating Arrodes here could very well alert the demon. He needed the power of the Night Watchers' armor-like Grade 1 Sealed Artifact to do it safely.
"Yes, Deacon!" The two Machinery Hivemind members responded without hesitation.
Ikonsa immediately left for the Night Watchers' headquarters.
Spellsinger of God has been lured away, and the Goddess' church has deployed its Sealed Artifact... If the Apostle of Desire is going to make a move, it'll be now! I hope the official Beyonders can make it in time. I hope Arrodes provides the right answer... But this means I won't get to interfere, won't get to see that demon die with my own eyes, and won't be able to claim that suitcase stuffed with cash, gold bars, coins, and jewelry...
Klein sighed, feeling a tinge of disappointment as he watched Ikonsa leave.
As for missing the chance to act in character, he wasn't too concerned. Thanks to his performance during the "Flesh Abyss" ritual—when he had "acted" and "curtained" himself before Mr. A, the Adjudicators, and the Saints of the Steam Church—his "Magician" potion had already been mostly digested. The remaining portion had been absorbed through various minor performances over the past month...
If he had the necessary materials, he could advance to "Faceless" immediately.
He quickly regained his composure.
This is fine. At least I don't have to take any risks, and the crisis will be resolved steadily. Once I get the "Mutated Pituitary Gland and Blood of the Thousand-Faced Hunter" from Emlyn in the next couple of days, plus the "Human-Skin Phantom's Trait" Sharon promised to bring on Sunday... Maybe I can advance to Sequence 6 before the next Tarot Club! That should help mitigate the scheduling issues caused by Mr. Tower's "vacation" ending.
The only pity is that I'll never get my hands on that Apostle of Desire's suitcase, which contains all his savings as a banker—at least 50,000 gold pounds worth of gold, jewelry, and cash...
Even Lady Mary of the Air Pollution Investigation Committee, including her shares in Coyim Company, barely had such wealth!
As these thoughts ran through his mind, Klein returned to the lounge inside the Quelaag Club. After locking the door behind him, the pale-skinned, exquisitely beautiful Miss Sharon suddenly stepped out of a mirror. She remained silent for a few seconds before speaking succinctly. "Do you need me to retrieve the suitcase?"
Are you thinking about it too? Not bad, Miss Temperance, you and Mr. Fool really think alike. A promising "Blessed One" candidate!
Klein internally joked before shaking his head.
"There must be a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact there, maybe even a demigod. It's too dangerous... Forget it."
"Very rational. You understand 'Temperance' well." Miss Sharon's ethereal voice carried a note of approval before she disappeared.
Was that a reminder not to be swayed by greed, lest I fall prey to the Apostle of Desire's tricks?
Klein glanced at the mirror beside him, deep in thought, before justifying himself.
I'm not that greedy, really. Machinery Hivemind won't treat me unfairly. If this mission succeeds, my insights and suggestions will be highly valued...
And as a believer of the God of Steam and Machinery, I should receive a share of the spoils based on the churches' usual practices... With 50,000 pounds on the line, it won't be a small sum...
...
In a luxurious villa not far from the Cathedral of the Eternal Wind in Cherwood Borough—also the residence of Miss Aisha, the woman Klein was commissioned to investigate by the fake Baron Larry—
Pallas Negan, whose waist was bloated and eyes gray-blue, sat on the bed holding his mistress in his arms. She was a beautiful young lady with a touch of innocence still on her face, Miss Aisha, who had just turned twenty a few days ago.
She was the most favored woman of the Duke in the past three years.
After taking a mummified potion obtained from a certain apothecary, Duke Negan seemed to have regained the feeling of his youth—riding across vast lands, hunting with his father and elders, chasing wild beasts with hounds.
But just then, that joy and pleasure exploded within him—over and over, endlessly, with no limit or reprieve—until his heart could no longer bear it and suffered a fatal blow.
Extraordinary individuals guarding the Duke in other rooms instantly sensed a mysterious force and rushed into the bedroom.
Leading them was none other than Deacon Stewart of the Church of Storms, the "Mysticism Magister"!When the Honorable "
Spellsinger of God
" pursued Jason Beria to the dock, Stewart, having experienced similar situations before, sensed something was wrong and took the initiative to replace the original "Wind-Blessed" who had been protecting the Duke.
While mimicking a "healing" ability to repair the Duke's injuries, Stewart also used secret arts in an attempt to reflect the power the demon had inflicted back upon it—
But at that very moment, the Duke's blonde secretary unexpectedly rushed straight to the source of the mysterious force in the attic and used her ability to "seal" it off, seemingly trying to trap the intruder.
Yet by doing so, she also interrupted Stewart's secret art.
The Mysticism Magister frowned but didn't reprimand her. After all, they had never worked together before, and poor coordination was only natural.
So he chose not to interfere in her fight with the enemy, to avoid any misfire, and instead focused solely on protecting Duke Negan. He even calmed the Duke's emotions to prevent him from inadvertently giving the enemy an opening.
However, though the blonde secretary was powerful, she had clearly failed to fully contain the Desire Apostle, who relied on his unique abilities to become a shadow and slip past the attacks.
Just as the Desire Apostle planned to provoke the Duke's fear by killing his mistress Aisha, and then finish him off—Stewart intercepted in time. Using a variety of means, he instantly identified the weaknesses in the Apostle's unique shadow magic!
Seeing the holy light rapidly coalesce in Stewart's hands, the Desire Apostle was about to fall in bitter defeat—when suddenly, a man's figure appeared right beside Duke Negan. He pushed out his left palm and solemnly declared in Hermes, "Death!"
As the words fell, the man's body fused with a strange power, light of dawn bursting from his form, and he struck Duke Negan's head—blowing it to pieces!—If Duke Negan hadn't been injured, as a mid-sequence Beyonder, there was no way he would've been struck so easily. Even if he had been hit, he would've had enough time to activate his powers and mitigate the damage—he wouldn't have died immediately...
But there were no "ifs" in this world. The conservative party leader, the greatest landowner besides the king, the elder brother of the current prime minister, a genuine bigshot, and a Sequence 6 Beyonder—Duke Pallas Negan was dead.
The change happened so suddenly that even Stewart didn't have time to react. He could only watch helplessly as the Duke lost his head...
The blonde secretary who rushed in after was even more shocked. "Baron Larry?! You actually killed His Grace the Duke!"
Before her words had finished, she launched an attack in fury.
The man who had acted suddenly was indeed the kingdom's wanted criminal, Baron Larry. Looking down at his own fist as if waking from a dream, he muttered in disbelief, "What... did I do?"
He didn't react at all to the blonde secretary's attack.
But the blow missed anyway—because Baron Larry's figure vanished again, as if he had never appeared at all.
As for the Desire Apostle, he seemed to have anticipated this. Taking advantage of everyone's shock, he ignored the briefcase and swiftly left the villa, retreating along the predetermined route.
Until a vast blood-colored ocean appeared before his eyes—and at its center stood a figure clad in full silver armor!
...
At the same time, a fog of white, gray, yellow, and black colors swirled in the sky above Cherwood Borough. Since such fogs were common in Backlund, no one paid it any attention.
Within the fog, an old man dressed in a shirt, vest, full suit, and striped blue-gray trousers, with a dark red bowtie and a head full of thick white hair, clutched his head with a contorted expression. But after a moment, he lowered his hands and his demeanor returned to that of a gentle scholar.
The old man smiled faintly and looked around. His gaze soon landed on a heroic-looking young woman, who held an unconscious Baron Larry in her hands.
Seeing this scene, the old man bowed politely to her and smiled. "Your Highness Vera... Heh, I suppose calling you that now isn't a problem, is it?"
"No problem at all," Princess Vera nodded slightly and looked at the old man. "Your Highness Ariehogg."
"The persona I created is still Hvin Rambis—at most, it's a Hvin who possesses Ariehogg's memories... Please don't miscall me again," the old man—no, the fabricated "Hvin Rambis"—corrected her before continuing,
"If not for the item you planted on Larry ahead of time, plunging Herwin into extreme 'misfortune' and allowing the replacement of the persona marked by that individual, even I wouldn't have succeeded so easily...
"Even if I had succeeded, it would likely have triggered the mark left behind by that being...
"Heh, no... I should say that without your help, I definitely wouldn't have succeeded. After all, without the concealment of this fog, nothing we did would escape His notice."
This was something he gave me back then... Of course, it's useful...
Vera fell silent for a few seconds, then replied in a calm tone, "I've fulfilled my end of the bargain. When do you intend to honor yours, Lord... Hvin Rambis?"

chapters.title: Chapter 625: Tool and Scapegoat
chapters.content:
Chapter 625 - Tool and Scapegoat
"I've fulfilled my end of the bargain. When do you plan to honor your promise, Lord Hvin Rambis?"
"Not too long from now. The preparations are mostly complete. At most half a month, and you'll see the results." "Hvin Rambis," controlled by the ancient dragon Ariehogg, answered confidently.
As he spoke, his gaze shifted toward Baron Larry, who was in Vera's hands, and he asked, "May I take him now?"
"To avoid suspicion, it's better to keep him with me for now..." Vera gently shook her head, then added with hidden meaning, "Besides, we still need to leave behind traces of a struggle."
"In your hands? And still leave traces of a struggle? Yes, that's how it should be... After all, if there's no sign of a fight—or if I managed to escape with him—it would only raise more suspicion!" "Hvin Rambis" smiled as if suddenly enlightened.
"Now that's more like a royal advisor..." Vera nodded, then asked, "Since you've taken control of him, you should already know everything my dear brother planned regarding Larry, right? Care to share?"
"Of course, beautiful Princess." Hvin Rambis gave a gentlemanly bow and chuckled.
"That Baron Larry was originally just a scapegoat thrown out to divert attention, someone to shift the so-called 'Ghost Empire' clues onto other factions...
"But he got lucky and received help from Intis intelligence. Somehow, he actually managed to escape back to the Northern Continent!
"After that, due to the ambiguous attitude of the Loen military toward him, and the considerable losses suffered by various secret organizations trying to track him down, people began to half-believe he might really possess some valuable intel.
"Right then, MI9 discovered that Madam Panis—who had been sheltering Larry—was actually Bianca, the military attaché from the Intis embassy in disguise. That envoy, Mr. Owen, who belongs to the same secret organization as His Majesty and 'me,' seemed to want to use this to uncover some of Loen's secrets.
"So, on 'my' advice as royal advisor, His Majesty George III decided to adjust the plan. One part involved secretly relocating Larry, removing him from your and others' sights. The other part was having someone pose as a detective he hired, to deliberately investigate Duke Negan's mistress...
"Then 'I' suggested His Majesty arrange for Prince Edessak's butler, Finkel, to make contact with Larry, giving him a sliver of hope...
"And all of this was to prepare for pinning the blame on Baron Larry once the 'Negan assassination case' and the hidden danger surrounding the Prince exploded, and then further shifting the blame to Intis for aiding Larry.
"After all, compared to the 'Aurora Order,' who constantly talks about 'responsibility,' the narrative that Intis spies and a defected native baron colluded to assassinate a conservative Duke and destabilize the kingdom is far more likely to gain the Church's trust.
"The same logic applies to Prince Edessak... A simple tale of a prince being obsessed with a witch—even if it cost him his life—might not convince the Church. But if Intis used a traitorous baron to exploit the prince's naivety and cause disaster, then the royal family would bear less blame, and it would make much more sense.
"And evidence wouldn't be hard to find. After all, the real Madam Panis was murdered long ago. With the Church's means, a thorough investigation would definitely uncover the truth.
"Heh, thinking back now, the previous 'me' thought Larry was completely off your radar once he entered Backlund. Who would've thought you had already planned ahead and placed that item on him—ultimately helping 'me' become myself.
"Your luck was quite good, too. Your subordinates happened to 'coincidentally' discover Baron Larry's whereabouts, which also helped cover up the fact that you'd planted something on him...
"Even if
He
investigates afterward, with this fog obscuring most of the information, the one he'll suspect more is that little girl named Xio.
"What's even better is that little girl has close ties with the 'Hero Detective.' That might just divert
His
attention toward the 'God of Knowledge.'
"And in
His
eyes, you might just be an ambitious person who used a Sealed Artifact to kidnap Larry, attempting to gain the royal princess of the 'Ghost Empire'...
"That's probably another reason why you wanted to take Larry and stage a fake confrontation with me, right?
"Incredible! You even accounted for the 'God of Knowledge'!"
After speaking, "Hvin Rambis" deliberately looked at Vera with an admiring gaze, while also observing her expression.
Vera's face remained unchanged as she gently shook her head and replied, "Why would you think that our actions weren't within the 'God of Knowledge's' expectations?"
"Uh..." Although the current personality of Hvin Rambis possessed all of Ariehogg's memories—as if the ancient dragon had seized his body—it lacked the relevant memories of the "Dragon King" Ankewelt who had awakened from Ariehogg. So he didn't have the necessary understanding of that true god who once betrayed the dragon race.
"Also, you talk too much! Your descriptions are unnecessarily verbose and fragmented. That's not in line with Hvin's usual manner." Vera pointed out another flaw in his performance.
Such issues would never occur with human Beyonders on the Spectator pathway, because if their "acting" was this poor, they would have lost control long ago.
But the dragon race was born as mythical beings. Their powerful bodies allowed them to resist losing control and turning into monsters to a large extent—after all, they
were
monsters to begin with—so their performance was relatively rough around the edges.
"That's Ariehogg's habit... He likes to ramble to himself about things..." Hvin Rambis offered a simple explanation, then took out an ice-blue metal cylinder from his pocket and changed the subject:
"This is a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact entrusted to 'me' by the Psychological Alchemy Society, called 'Rotting Meteor.' Its origins are unknown, but it's certain that part of its material came from the stars!
"This ice-blue cylinder can fire special dark green projectiles. Anyone hit by them is instantly poisoned and begins to rot—even their spirit body won't be spared. It's effective even against demigods.
"Its side effect is that the holder may be watched by gazes cast down from the starry sky, unknowingly becoming corrupted. If
He
hadn't placed some seals on it, I definitely wouldn't dare to carry it with me!
"However, precisely because of
His
seal, if I use it in the future, the chances of someone detecting something unusual are quite high..."That's why I want to hand it over to you... After all, it's impossible for me to 'escape' from you without paying some price... This also makes the story more believable."
Vera accepted the metal cylinder, gave it a quick glance, then summoned the surrounding mist to wrap it up before finally looking at him and saying, "Alright, I'm going to make my move now...
"You'd better 'transform' into your dragon form first. Otherwise, with just a Sequence 4 body, you might actually die!"
...
In the dark sewer, a shadow clung to the base of the stone wall, swiftly gliding in one direction.
He was the "Apostle of Desire" who had previously attacked Duke Negan. But now he was in a rather sorry state, because just as he was about to escape, he encountered a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact from the Church of the Evernight.
It was an extremely terrifying suit of armor. Just one strike had forced him to abandon his physical body, fleeing as a shadow.
But even so, the armor was still gaining on him!
His only chance was to use the fact that the bloodstained armor was tall and heavy, making it difficult to maneuver through certain narrow parts of the sewer—and shake it off!
Or... survive until the armor's side effects erupted!
...
At the same time, in another section of the sewer.
Ebner was using the "Magic Mirror" to sense "Desire" and monitor the target's every move.
Seeing the pursuer and the fugitive getting closer and closer to his location, Ebner put away the mirror and took out a beautifully crafted card painted with a skeletal dragon. He sighed:
"The Hero Bandit 'Black Emperor' really didn't show up...
"Did he finish digesting the 'Magician' potion?
"Or is he certain that I'll make a move to help my teacher eliminate the threat?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 626: Leonard was deeply shocked.
chapters.content:
Chapter 626 - Leonard was deeply shocked.
Aside from the fact that the "Magician" potion had already been digested and that he believed Mr. "Tower" would definitely go deal with the "Desire Apostle," Ebner had more or less grasped some of Klein's other thoughts:
For example, he didn't want to expose the fact that "The World" was actually Sherlock Moriarty, at least not yet.
After all, he himself had become quite famous. If the Hero Bandit "Black Emperor" appeared and intercepted the Desire Apostle, it would be easy for the members of the Tarot Club to make the connection and turn their attention to the detective Sherlock Moriarty.
Although he himself wouldn't even need to speculate or have any doubts... because there was simply no need!
After muttering a few complaints inwardly, Ebner raised the exquisite card high in one hand and shouted in Ancient Feysac, "Blue-Eyes White Dragon!"
In an instant, a giant skeletal dragon more than ten meters long appeared in the sewer. It crouched on the ground, and in its eye sockets danced cyan flames.
If it weren't for the fact that the "Bone Dragon" was an undead creature and could spiritualize its body, the height and width of the sewer wouldn't have been able to contain it.
At the same time, a set of silver armor appeared around Ebner, draped with a hooded robe, and behind him hung the cloak-like alchemical lifeform.
He leaped onto the Bone Dragon's back and directed it to intercept the "Desire Apostle," who was just about to flee into this section.
...
Elsewhere, the "Desire Apostle" could no longer suppress his injuries and was forced to stop. He pressed tightly against the damp wall and cold pipe, trying hard to restrain the bloodlust and urge to kill within him.
Huff... Huff... His shadow-thin body heaved unsteadily, like a candle that might be snuffed out at any moment in the wind.
At that moment, he suddenly turned his head and looked toward the wall on the opposite side.
Because right there, the enormous skull of a dragon, larger than his body, suddenly emerged from the wall and entered his "sight"!
No hesitation, no words, and no delay—just as the cyan flames flickered slightly in the dragon's eye sockets, it opened its jaws and unleashed a nearly invisible breath attack.
This was a direct assault on the mind and spirit body!
The "Desire Apostle" had no time to react before large patches of black fell off his shadowy body, as if shaking off the snowflakes stained with the deepest desires.
With just a single strike, the already severely injured "Desire Apostle" was pushed to the brink of death.
In his last flicker of consciousness, he desperately tried to disperse his shadow form, transforming into inky-black liquid to escape in all directions...
Unfortunately, faced with a "Mind Dragon," even if it was undead, once the mental island's defenses were breached, he could no longer carry out his intentions.
With his subconscious "modified," he abandoned the idea of fleeing and gathered all his shadows and launched himself toward Ebner on the dragon's back for one final struggle.
While this decision didn't appear "wrong" from a subjective point of view, it nonetheless sealed the "Desire Apostle's" fate.
The "Knight" sitting atop the dragon didn't panic in the slightest. Before those viscous shadows reached him, he calmly took out a mirror with a golden frame and a pitch-black surface.
Then, a gaping maw filled with sharp teeth opened on the surface of the mirror, waiting quietly for the shadows to dive in.
Moments later, the "Magic Mirror" affectionately rubbed against Ebner's hand, signaling that it had successfully "Grazed" the Desire Apostle.
At the same time, it "spat out" a "Seafarer" characteristic and released the soul of that pirate.
As for the souls already being "Grazed" inside the Magic Mirror, except for the "Devil," Ebner didn't care which one was replaced by the "Desire Apostle." After all, he had already confirmed that none of them were good people—each one was absolutely worthy of execution.
It's worth mentioning that Ebner had the Magic Mirror "Graze " the Desire Apostle not for his "abilities" but simply to preserve his spirit for the time being.
After storing away the "Seafarer" characteristic, Ebner was about to leave when he suddenly saw a tall and heavy suit of armor charging toward him at an astonishing speed.
Its left shoulder slanted downward, stained with a patch of solidified blood, exuding an eerie yet mesmerizing beauty. With each step, the sewer pipes trembled slightly.
Ebner wasn't surprised by the arrival of the Church of Evernight's Grade 1 Sealed Artifact. In fact, he had prepared for it in advance.
He gently rubbed the "Tudor Emblem" on his robe, instantly activating a pre-arranged ritual. The armor, which was about to launch an attack, immediately froze in place.
With his face hidden beneath his hood, Ebner smiled slightly and tossed a "Tower" card onto the ground.
Only then did he command the Bone Dragon to carry him away, directly entering the dreams of a nearby resident.
...
Meanwhile, Leonard, who had been tracking the Desire Apostle in the "Armor," found himself in disbelief.
The negative effects that were supposed to erupt in about a minute were already showing signs of advancing. If not for the old man's help, he might not even have had the chance to take off the armor and soak in hot water!
"Stop dawdling! Take off the armor and get into the hot water that guy prepared for you!" Pallez's aged voice rang in his ears.
This was the second thing that baffled Leonard—the Dragon Knight had actually prepared hot water for him?!
"Old man... what's going on?" Leonard didn't dare delay, but he still asked while stripping off the armor.
"Heh, that guy used a demigod-level 'Distortion' ability to shorten the negative outburst time of the armor," Pallez explained briefly.
"I meant... why did he save me?" Leonard asked with a slight feeling of dejection.
"You've already made some guesses, haven't you? You suspect he's actually from the Church, which is why he's so familiar with this armor and held back against you?" Pallez chuckled.
"Is there another possibility?" Soaking in the hot water while removing the silver patterns on his body, Leonard caught the underlying meaning in Pallez's words and asked in surprise.
"Heh, there are plenty of possibilities! Since I could instantly recognize whose blood was on that armor, others might not be blind to it either..." Pallez paused before continuing with a serious tone, "Besides, that knight just now gave off a feeling of 'Omniscience'..."
"Omniscience?"
"The Sequence 1 of the 'Reader' pathway is called the 'Omniscient Magic Eye.'
"That person definitely isn't at that level, but if my senses weren't wrong, he's at least at the 'Insight' stage."
.....
When Red Gloves Captain Soest received Leonard's report, he was in the middle of writing an application.
He put down his pen, looked at the Nighthawk before him, and asked gravely,
"That Tarot-named organization appeared again? And they preemptively intercepted the Desire Apostle? This time, they left the 'Tower' card at the scene?"
"Yes, Captain," the Nighthawk confirmed before adding, "According to Leonard's judgment, they don't seem to be allied with the Desire Apostle."
Soest nodded thoughtfully, considering,"If they weren't there beforehand to silence him... then it's yet another coincidence...
"Coincidence..."
Mulling over the word, Soest's gaze returned to the application report in front of him:
"...Based on the series of coincidences in the Desire Apostle case, I suspect Ince Zangwill may still be lurking in Backlund...
"I hereby apply for the support of Her Excellency, 'Eye of the Goddess.'"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 627: Responses from All Sides
chapters.content:
Chapter 627 - Responses from All Sides
West Borough, Intis Embassy.
The confidential secretary, who deliberately sported a small mustache seemingly in imitation of Roselle, knocked on the office door of Special Envoy Mr. Owen.
"Sir, Duke Negan has been assassinated! The attackers were a 'Desire Apostle' and... and Baron Larry!" The secretary rushed through the report, paying no mind to the envoy's displeasure.
"What?!" The envoy immediately stood up. What shocked him wasn't Negan's assassination—after all, that had been part of their organization's long-decided plans.
What troubled Mr. Owen was that Larry had shown up at the scene and had played a major role in the operation...
After a brief pause to collect his thoughts, Owen asked urgently, "Was Larry captured? Or killed on the spot?"
"No... Word is he escaped in front of the Mandated Punishers..." The secretary didn't dare hide anything and briefly summarized what he had learned.
"He escaped even under such circumstances? Did some higher being interfere?" Envoy Owen fell into thought for a few seconds before asking again, "What about the 'Desire Apostle'?"
"That part's still unclear... But from what I've gathered, it looks like he was silenced by some other force."
The incident had only just occurred, so for the secretary to have obtained this much information already was proof of his competence.
Owen paced around the room, muttering to himself, "I might've fallen into George III's trap..." Then he gave a command:
"Immediately send someone to deal with Bianca. We can't let the Loen side get hold of any evidence that we supported Larry."
"Yes, Mr. Envoy." The secretary acknowledged, then hesitated slightly before adding, "But if this really was a trap set by the Loen side, then it's likely they already have some evidence... After all, there were other agents helping Larry—not just Bianca...
"And... it might already be too late for Bianca..."
"That doesn't matter... If the others are caught, we can completely deny them," Envoy Owen said coldly with a sneer. "If Bianca can't be silenced in time, and Loen insists on an explanation, we can hand over Sari to take the fall.
"With his status as Chief Martial Officer, his long-standing work relationship with Bianca, and his 'suspicious' friendliness with the Conservative Party nobles in Loen... he has the capacity, and he can bear the responsibility... can't he?
"After all, Intis isn't ready yet—we can't fall out with Loen now. That would make Feysac
very
happy.
"For the sake of our great homeland, this sacrifice is necessary... I believe Mr. Sari will be willing."
As he spoke, a strange gleam flashed in Owen's eyes, and he gave the secretary a meaningful look.
"I understand... I'll make sure Mr. Sari becomes 'willing'..." the mustached secretary replied. Then, almost in a daze, he murmured, "After everything's done... I'll make myself 'disappear'..."
"Good." Envoy Owen closed his eyes. "Don't worry about the Sari family's political influence back home. I'll work with the Sauron family to suppress them."
The secretary seemed to have forgotten what he had just muttered. His heart was full of excitement and anticipation—after all, Mr. Sari was his main competitor for the ambassador position.
However, just before leaving, he couldn't help but voice the doubt in his heart: "Since the entire assassination might've been orchestrated by the Loen royal family... why not expose this secret?
"Even if we don't have concrete proof, it could still cause mass panic and deeper chaos among the Loen people..."
But Envoy Owen simply shook his head without answering, silently thinking to himself:
Because that is not the choice of this era...
.....
"This
is
the choice of the era..." Duke Negan's blonde secretary, Lockhart Siacam, told himself with eerie calm after being interrogated by the Mandated Punishers and the Machinery Hivemind.
Then, without rush or resistance, he returned to the room arranged for him by the authorities and obediently accepted the outcome of being temporarily placed under house arrest.
Watching the secretary enter the room, Ikanser, a steward of the Church of Steam, finally turned to the "Mysticism Magister" Stuart, who had participated in the interrogation alongside him.
"What do you think? Could he be the mole?"
After several collaborations—and jointly suffering public humiliation at the hands of Arrodes—their relationship had grown considerably close... though Stuart was reluctant to admit it.
"I didn't sense any signs of him lying... But he might have some special means to bypass my 'Mysticism' abilities." Stuart pondered for a moment before continuing, "Still, my intuition tells me there's something off about him... After all, in our previous battle, while I may have made mistakes in coordination... the fact remains that he blocked my spell."
"In that case... it's safest to ask Arrodes," Ikanser suggested after some thought.
As soon as he finished speaking, although Stuart remained unfazed, the Mandated Punishers and Machinery Hivemind members standing behind them all instinctively took a step back in unison.
Noticing this, Ikanser sighed helplessly. "I wasn't telling
you
to ask... What are you afraid of?"
"You seem less fearful of it today?" Stuart observed with a smirk.
"Arrodes seems to be in a good mood today. Just now, a 'Red Glove' asked it about the whereabouts of the 'Desire Apostle,' and it didn't ask any overly unreasonable questions."
As he spoke, Ikanser gazed at the silver mirror in his hand and stroked its surface three times with his right palm.
After a brief two-second pause, he took a deep breath and solemnly asked:
"Respected Arrodes, my question is: In the past few months, has Lockhart Siacam had any secrets he wouldn't want others to know?"
The surrounding darkness suddenly thickened, and ripples of water-like light spread across the silver mirror's surface.
Soon, a series of images emerged within the mirror:
—Lockhart arranging for someone to monitor Miss Audrey Hall's accounts.—Lockhart meeting with a disguised individual, their face deliberately concealed, in a café.—Lockhart discussing something with a butler-like figure...
Although the scenes were silent, they were enough to show that this secretary from MI9 did indeed have some suspicious activities.
"Why not just ask whether he's the mole?" Stuart asked as he observed the images.
Previously, he had mostly used 'Mysticism' to invoke Arrodes' power. Though he had suffered greatly at its hands, he wasn't fully aware of its limitations in answering questions.
"Because if you ask a simple 'yes or no' question, it will inevitably give a definite answer. He was an MI9 agent planted beside Duke Negan—he
is
technically a mole.
"And if we ask things like 'Did he participate in the assassination?' or 'Did he betray the Duke?' the answers would likely be vague or misleading, making them highly unreliable!
"Furthermore, asking such questions would increase the difficulty and risk of both the punishment and the response significantly!
"I suspect that Arrodes dislikes straightforward 'yes or no' questions. It prefers to give prophecies or visions, like certain forms of divination."
"A 'living' Sealed Artifact, huh..." Stuart sighed, nodding in understanding. He took a moment to organize his thoughts before analyzing, "First, we need to identify the two people Lockhart met in the images...
"As for Miss Audrey Hall... I personally don't think she has anything to do with this case."
Ikanser agreed with the reasoning and was just about to respond when the images in the mirror suddenly vanished.
In their place, blood-red words slowly formed, one after another:
"Have you ever had feelings for 'Mysticism Magister' Stuart?"
Ikanser froze, utterly dumbfounded.
At the same time, the members of the Machinery Hivemind and the Mandated Punishers all turned their gazes toward him.
Some looked surprised.Some looked horrified.Some looked intrigued.Some looked as if they had just figured something out...
As for Stuart, his expression became unfocused. He had never imagined that even someone as "fearless" as himself could still fall victim to
this kind
of torment...
"Arrodes hates being asked 'yes or no' questions, but it
loves
asking them itself!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 628: Unexpected Gains
chapters.content:
Chapter 628 - Unexpected Gains
West Borough, No. 9 Hope Street, Prime Minister's Residence.
The current Prime Minister, Aguesid Negan, who seemed to have aged several years overnight, was conversing with Earl Hall.
Although he was a major figure in the Conservative Party, after his brother's assassination, the only person he could think of to discuss countermeasures with was Earl Hall...
After all, only by properly handling the aftermath could they prevent the kingdom—the heavy steam locomotive—from derailing completely!
After listening to Aguesid's account of the entire incident, Earl Hall furrowed his brows and said:
"Patrick Jason? He's been a demon disguised as a banker for decades? I recall that my Bavart Bank had just acquired his assets...
"Furthermore, Baron Larry was involved in the assassination? Why would he go that far?
"As far as I know, Baron Larry has always served in the military and had no major conflicts with Pallas..."
Duke Negan's full name was Pallas Negan.
Aguesid organized his thoughts before responding:
"That demon was a Sequence 5, yet he suddenly liquidated his assets, abandoned an identity he had maintained for over a decade, and took the extreme risk of assassinating my brother...
"From this, we can make a strong assumption that he was acting under someone's orders. Unfortunately, he was killed while fleeing... According to reports from the Nighthawks, the culprit was a high-sequence Beyonder.
"Oh, and before leaving, they also left behind a tarot card—the 'Tower' card."
"Tarot card? Is this related to that organization that opposes the Aurora Order and worships some entity called the 'Fool'? I recall reading a report about them..." Earl Hall asked after a moment of recollection.
"It should be that newly emerging secret organization... They previously sent a so-called Hero Bandit 'Black Emperor' who appeared in Backlund several times..."
"So, we're dealing with an extremely secretive organization, and we won't be able to uncover the truth in the short term?" Earl Hall asked rhetorically.
"There are actually some clues..." Aguesid retrieved a document and handed it to Earl Hall while continuing, "This is the latest intelligence from MI9. During his escape, Baron Larry received assistance from Intis spies. Even his mistress, Madame Panis, was actually a disguise—she was the military attaché Bianca from the Intis embassy, a Sequence 7 'Warlock'..."
Earl Hall paced for a moment before saying, "You suspect that the assassination was orchestrated by Intis? Or that this mysterious organization worshiping the 'Fool' is connected to Intis?"
"A secret organization that can send out Saints as soon as it emerges cannot be without backing... It's more likely an 'old friend'!" Aguesid said as he revealed another document. "This is a report submitted by the Church of Storms and the Church of Steam about the Aurora Order's previous attempt to conduct the 'Abyss of Flesh' ritual... That incident was actually resolved by the Hero Bandit 'Black Emperor.'
"And the report also mentions that an Intis envoy's bodyguard died during the incident—killed in battle against the Aurora Order's Angel...
