To be honest, over the past few months working for Mr. Bryan, although she had been quite busy and often had her spirituality squeezed dry, things had actually been fairly relaxed and fulfilling once she got past the initial anxiety and fear.
While aboard the
Black Death
, Tracy had also done her best to accommodate her needs—but would never have truly allowed her to return home...
And when she signed the contract with Detective Bryan, she had initially worried that he might go back on his word and refuse to let her go when the time came... but as they spent more time together, she stopped worrying about that.
Mr. Ebner Bryan is a gentleman who keeps his word, and he genuinely respects me... Even though he always has me working, if I really didn't want to, he wouldn't force me.
He's also incredibly powerful, completely unafraid of Tracy. Traveling with him offers great security.
That's far more reliable than trying to reach out to family friends at the Intis consulate in Bayam.
More importantly, I have no idea how many more foolish things my father has done or how many debts he's racked up during my time in Tracy's captivity... If I travel with Detective Bryan, maybe I can ask for his help later on...
With that thought, Helene convinced herself to stay by Ebner's side and nodded. "I'll go with you."
"Good. Then your wages from the past few months stored here will count as your escort fee," Ebner said as he cut into another piece of steak, giving her a look that said,
You're getting a deal.
He was a Sequence 5 Beyonder—based on Miss Temperance's rates, his daily fee would normally be 300 pounds.
Helene froze at his words and immediately retracted all the praises she had just been thinking.
This guy's a stingy penny-pincher, a 'vampire' who gives his subordinates potions from the Sleepless pathway just to exploit them more easily.
Of course, grumble though she might, she had no intention of changing her mind.
Ebner ignored her little internal complaints, took a sip of coffee, and turned to "Lion" Leon. "You've been handling my social appearances for the past month to keep up the illusion that Detective Bryan has always been in Bayam. That must've been tough... I plan to send a servant to buy tickets tomorrow. The day after, I'll publicly take a ship back to Port Priz, then follow the railway to Intis..."
"Hmm, is there anyone I should send farewell letters to? It'd be strange to just disappear without a word."
Leon blinked and grinned. "Plenty of people, actually. Like Lady Reggie, the Governor's wife. Or Miss Clay from the Southco family. There's also Madam Enno from the Trade Association... and Abby, the youngest daughter of the North Party leader..."
Ebner nearly spat out his coffee. He quickly waved his hand to stop Leon and asked in disbelief, "I thought I asked you to maintain social contact on my behalf?"
"Isn't this normal social contact?" Leon replied innocently. "That's how it always was when I was with Roselle."
Helene, standing nearby, covered her mouth and giggled, clearly enjoying the show.
Ebner stared speechlessly at him for a moment before putting down his coffee and rubbing his temples. "You didn't actually do anything... inappropriate, did you?"
"Of course not. I'm a lion. My aesthetic isn't even the same as a human's..." Leon shook his head with conviction, but just as Ebner breathed a sigh of relief, the lion squinted and added mischievously, "Though I did give them a few very vivid dreams..."
You're just like the Magic Mirror! No wonder—you were both brought out by Roselle...
Ebner silently cursed, then observed a few moments of silence for his own reputation before brushing the matter aside.
I'm about to leave Bayam anyway. Even if I come back, I won't be making a grand return. What's the point of stressing over this?
"Oh right, the others are fine, but that Abby girl—the North Party leader's daughter—might be a bit of a problem..." Leon added, as if suddenly remembering something.
"The North Party's leader?" Ebner frowned. He remembered the man—he'd once shown the Fool's honorific title during a Beyonder gathering at the Amyris Leaf Bar, even offering a high bounty for any clues about believers of the Fool.
Now hearing that his daughter was involved in something strange, Ebner asked curiously, "What's wrong with her?"
"That Miss Abby has an unknown power residing in her... I almost got caught when I entered her dream... But I did gather some intel. She's very likely connected to an organization called the 'Celestial Body Cult.'" Leon's tone turned unusually serious.
The Celestial Body Cult... isn't that the group that worships the Mother Tree of Desire?
In the original novel, the mistress of a certain admiral, Miss Cynthia, met a tragic end after joining this cult...
Yeah, I'd better report this! Next time we have a Tarot Gathering, I'll tell the Hanged Man and let the Church of the Storm handle it.
After that serious discussion, Ebner had just finished dinner. He stood up and waved to Helene, signaling her to follow him.
"Is there something you need, Mr. Bryan?" Helene asked, puzzled.
"I remember our contract runs until New Year. There are still a few days left. Naturally, you should continue your work as a 'maid'—go boil water in the basement. I've got several mystical items to craft," Ebner said matter-of-factly.
Hearing that, Helene's expression went blank for a moment, then she resigned herself and followed Ebner.
.....
Name:
Transformation Wand - Fire
Appearance:
A short rod with a deep red gemstone set at its tip.
Function:
When activated using a preset "incantation," the wand reveals its true form, allowing the user to transform into a girl clad in red tight-fitting armor. In this form, the user can access most of a "Demon's" abilities, including but not limited to: "Lava Sword," "Foul Speech," and "Sulfur Fireball."
After transformation, the user passively emits a "Charm" aura that rapidly inflates the desires of all targets within range. This can either implant seeds for future control or instantly catalyze the emotions, causing targets to lose control, be unable to resist, or suffer an overload of desire that critically injures or even kills them.
Post-transformation, the user can hide in firelight, remaining undetectable even by ordinary demigods unless they actively act. The user can also fuse "Black Flame" and "Sulfur Flame" to form a "Flame Sword," which can detonate inside a target.
Negative Effects:
After more than two minutes of transformation, the "Flame Sword" detonates inside the user, causing injuries lethal to low- and mid-sequence Beyonders.
Sealing Method:
Use the preset incantation to deactivate the transformation, then seal the wand using intermediate-level talismans from either the "Darkness" or "Death" domain.
.....
In Mr. Gaston's workshop, when Ebner, returning by sea with Leon and Helene, stopped by Damir Port and presented this new creation to the elderly man, the latter was visibly stunned:
"How did you know the 'King of the Five Seas' had placed an order with me for something like this?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 671: Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea’s Intelligence
chapters.content:
Chapter 671 - Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea's Intelligence
"Why would the 'King of the Five Seas' order something like this?" Ebner was stunned for a moment after hearing Mr. Gaston's words. His intuition told him that the so-called "White Maple Earl" might have "awakened" some bizarre preferences.
That said, Ebner hadn't crafted such an item purely for the joke—it was a method to reconcile and even suppress the influence of the "cold-blooded" trait from the "Desire Apostle" characteristic, preventing the user's temperament from drastically changing.
Mr. Gaston set down the magic wand and replied with an odd expression, "Though I don't have any proof, I suspect the real client isn't Lord Nast himself, but rather the third officer of the
Black Emperor
, Littorio... He's also the holder of the 'Transformation Wand – Wind' that I made..."
As for his motives? Most likely, he just didn't want to feel "lonely" on the ship... Had to drag someone else "into the water" with him!
I think I've heard of this person before...
Ebner thought for a moment and recalled that when he was aboard the
Golden Dream
, he had once encountered the
Black Emperor
handling an out-of-control crewmate... and the one who intervened back then seemed to be Littorio, possibly using that "Transformation Wand."
"'Witch of the Wind'?" Ebner asked tentatively. He remembered Edwina telling him that nickname.
"You know?" Mr. Gaston looked at Ebner in surprise. He had thought this guy had been so buried in women these past months that he'd lost all interest in outside matters.
—Although the "Hero Detective" topic had cooled down somewhat, there were still nosy adventurers and pirates who enjoyed spreading juicy gossip.
Come to think of it, if not for the recent "Beyonder Fog Disaster" in Backlund drawing everyone's attention, the scandal at Bayam's port—"Multiple women nearly caused a disaster bidding farewell to the 'Hero Detective'"—would definitely have made headlines.
Ebner, unaware of Mr. Gaston's inappropriate thoughts, casually said, "A sea pirate with a 9,000-pound bounty—of course I remember."
But Mr. Gaston shook his head. "His bounty's already been raised to 11,000 pounds in a single nation. That's equivalent to a pirate admiral."
"What did he do?" Ebner asked in surprise.
"They say he discovered Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea's secret and ruined his plan. The latter tried to silence him, but failed," Mr. Gaston explained.
That's impressive,
Ebner thought. Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea, Hal Constantine, was a pirate admiral whose strength exceeded most Sequence 5s... While Littorio, without transforming, was merely a Sequence 6 "Corrupt Baron," a noticeable gap in power.
"But what does that have to do with his bounty going up?" Ebner still didn't get it.
"Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea is deeply connected to Intis, and there are even rumors he's an illegitimate son of a major family in Trier... In short, the 'secret' he was hiding might also be one of Intis's secrets. That's why the 'Witch of the Wind' got a bounty increase," Gaston said. As a peripheral member of the Church of Steam—and an Intis native—his information was quite up to date.
"I see..." Ebner pondered for a bit, then asked Gaston for more details, but the gentleman only knew that much.
Ebner's interest in this was because it involved Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea. Back when he was exploring the fifth level of the
Dream Labyrinth Tower
, in the "Elven Trial" dungeon, he received a reward from the Elven Temple—a vision of the Vice Admiral sacrificing living people to a sea monster with "Prophet" traits.
At the time, he judged that this would be his opportunity to advance to Sequence 4 and deduced that the sacrifice's time and place would likely be sometime in April on a small island to the west of the Southern Continent.
Could Littorio's discovered secret be related to the sea monster sacrifice? If so... then the sea monster probably doesn't just have a master-servant relationship with the Vice Admiral—it might also have a contract with some family from Intis...
No wonder the 'Trial Temple' would give such a hint... If I just prepared to fight the Vice Admiral and a weakened sea monster, I'd definitely be walking into a trap!
With this in mind, Ebner quietly performed a
Prophecy
—and confirmed that his guess was correct. What Littorio discovered truly was related to the sea monster...
He thought for a moment, then pushed the
Transformation Wand – Fire
back toward Mr. Gaston and said, "Could I ask you for a favor?"
"You want to trade this item for intelligence from Littorio?" Mr. Gaston guessed Ebner's intention immediately.
"Exactly. The wand's main materials come from the characteristics of a 'Desire Apostle' and a 'Witch.' Before the Desire Apostle was killed, it was even tainted with the aura of an 'Ancient God's blood,' which is why it can hide within 'firelight' and not be sensed by an average 'demigod'...
"And its negative effects are still within a manageable range...
"All in all, if this were auctioned off, it'd easily be worth more than 10,000 pounds—equivalent to the bounty on the 'Witch of the Wind.' That should be enough to exchange for the information he risked his life to obtain."
As he spoke, Ebner also demonstrated the wand's firelight-concealment ability—something Gaston hadn't managed to identify earlier.
After watching the demonstration, Mr. Gaston hesitated for a moment, then finally nodded. "I'll help you get a more reasonable price... but I want an 80-20 split of the extra margin—80 for me."
"Deal." Ebner agreed readily.
After his massive gains from the
Land of the Night
, he was quite "flush" and didn't mind these petty sums. Only Elaine gave him a discreet side-eye, thinking,
If you're so loaded, why the hell are you still cutting my salary?
"You're leaving Damir soon, right? If the deal goes through, how should I contact you?" Mr. Gaston asked.
"Just send me a telegram directly. I'll be staying in Backlund for a few days to handle some other matters," Ebner replied with a smile.
.....
While Ebner was resting in the Port of Damir, the elegantly dressed Audrey stood in the royal palace's lounge, waiting for the New Year's ball to begin. However, her expression did not reveal the excitement, thrill, or joy one might expect from a girl about to receive her coming-of-age ceremony.
Before her lay a newspaper, with a headline that read:
"...According to preliminary statistics, over 10,000 people died directly in that heavy smog. The subsequent spreading plague claimed another 30,000 to 40,000 lives, including many young children and strong young men and women..."
Hoo...
Audrey closed her eyes and adjusted her emotions. Then, accompanied by her parents, she walked out of the lounge and entered the ballroom.
Finally, it was the queen herself who led her to the edge of the stage. Facing all the guests, the queen proclaimed:
"Although this is a dark time in Backlund's history, we still have a gem bright enough to illuminate the entire city. Her intelligence, her beauty, her character, and her manners are all impeccable.
"Today, I formally present her to you.
"Miss Audrey Hall."
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Outside the floor-to-ceiling windows, fireworks soared into the sky, bursting into waves of dreamlike light.
On the night of the last day of 1349, Audrey officially came of age in the eyes of high society.
.....
Afternoon of January 3rd, 1350.
In the suburbs of the East Borough, Klein, now appearing as a young gentleman with neat black hair and deep brown eyes, was strolling through a newly opened cemetery.
This was the new identity he had chosen for himself, arranged with the help of Miss "Temperance." The name was Gehrman Sparrow.
The cemetery he was in wasn't filled with traditional graves, but rather rows upon rows of cabinets holding urns of ashes—one after another, shelf upon shelf, layer upon layer.
"Mr. Corson and his wife..." Guided by his spiritual intuition, Klein quickly found the photos and memorial plaques of two familiar people.
Mr. Corson had been the president of the dockworkers' union. He once hired Klein to investigate who had "instigated" his wife to insist on leaving him...
Although the matter was eventually taken over by Steward of the Church of Storms, Klein later heard that Mr. and Mrs. Corson were going through a divorce...
Yet in the end, they were still buried together as husband and wife.
Letting out a sigh, Klein walked past their urn cabinets and soon came across another familiar name.
It was the landlord of the one-bedroom apartment Klein had rented in the East Borough. That house had been destroyed during the battle between the captain and the Aurora Order's Rose Bishop. That landlord had even kindly refunded his rent afterward...
Cabinet by cabinet, Klein looked them over. After a while, he exhaled a breath of white mist and murmured with slight relief, "Thankfully, Old Kohler was saved by Sharon...
"And Daisy and Freya, those sisters, are also safe..."
As for his informants, Klein had also asked Sharon to help relocate the child of Maric's friend to Port Pritz for care. After all, Old Kohler had been involved in several affairs with Detective Sherlock. If the authorities ever investigated Klein, they would surely find him... It was better to let him live in anonymity from now on.
While thinking this, Klein swept his gaze around, taking in the names and photos—sometimes just blank nameplates—of all the victims resting here.
Then he turned away and left the cemetery without looking back, heading for the Backlund train station.
.....
Woo—!
The steam train arrived in Backlund, bringing with it countless people filled with hope. Ebner got off the train dragging his suitcase, followed by Elaine, who had returned to her red-haired appearance. The "Lion" Leon had taken the form of an orange tabby cat, following closely beside them.
At that moment, a pair of siblings also emerged from the train station with their suitcases, blending into the crowd and walking right alongside Ebner and Helene.
At the same time, the doll-like Miss Sharon had just sent Klein off at the station and quietly parted ways with him.
As Ebner and Klein passed each other, they exchanged a glance. Both recognized one another, but silently chose not to speak.
But just as the three parties brushed past each other, the younger sister among the siblings suddenly turned her head, gave Ebner a few curious looks, and then asked hesitantly:
"Are you Detective Ebner Bryan?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 672: The Door and the Hometown
chapters.content:
Chapter 672 - The Door and the Hometown
Outside the Backlund steam train station, Benson skillfully protected both his sister and his wallet as he efficiently located the exit.
Suddenly, they both felt a gaze sweep over them.
Following the sensation, Benson and Melissa saw a young gentleman wearing gold-rimmed glasses.
The gentleman adjusted his top hat, his eyes passing over them to settle briefly on another young man walking beside them, before brushing past and entering the station.
At that moment, Melissa instinctively followed his gaze and looked at the brown-haired young man walking parallel to her and her brother. She first found him somewhat familiar, then recalled the source of that familiarity—he had been in the newspaper!
That person looked like the "Hero Detective"!
Back when Klein was still alive, we even debated whether this detective's feats were real...
If he were just an ordinary person, then his legendary exploits would naturally seem fabricated... But if he were a Beyonder, then perhaps what the reports published—along with any omissions—might not be so far-fetched...
Having personally witnessed supernatural powers, Melissa had come to Backlund with her older brother not only for school, but also with a hidden purpose—to seek out the "Beyonder world"...
And in her mind, this famous detective had a high probability of being a Beyonder.
Besides, even if he isn't... having been involved in so many bizarre cases, he must have encountered the extraordinary!
Melissa had never been a girl lacking initiative. Once the thought was formed in her heart, she immediately approached and spoke in a tone tinged with "pleasant surprise":
"Are you Mr. Ebner Bryan?"
She sounded like a fangirl who had just recognized her idol.
On the other side, Ebner, who had just crossed paths with the Fool's new alias, was withdrawing his gaze when he heard Melissa's question.
He was slightly stunned, then turned toward the voice and responded politely, "I believe you haven't mistaken me, beautiful miss."
Although it was his first time meeting Melissa, Ebner had seen her image in Xio's dream, where it was shown within the Sefirah Castle. Coupled with the current location—a well-known scene from the original work—and the man beside her with the notably receding hairline...
A few guesses immediately formed in his mind.
At this point, Benson had also stopped walking. Though slightly surprised that his sister would take the initiative to strike up a conversation, he warmly greeted Ebner:
"Didn't expect to run into you here, Detective Bryan.
"My sister and I greatly admire your heroic deeds."
As he spoke, he took half a step forward to shield Melissa behind him and extended his hand.
Ebner also reached out and shook hands with him, smiling as he said, "Thank you for still remembering this 'washed-up' detective."
After a few polite exchanges and trading business cards, they went their separate ways—one side heading toward the carriage Mr. Skard had sent to pick them up, along with Helene and Leon, and the other moving toward the smoke-emitting pillar in the central garden, eager to experience Backlund's underground transport.
Ever since Melissa had initiated the conversation, Klein—who had crouched down pretending to sort luggage—also stood up again and murmured softly, "If it's not too much trouble, please look after Melissa."
"Alright," came Sharon's ethereal voice in his ear.
—Due to having experienced the fifth level of the Dream Labyrinth Tower, which replicated the Tingen scene, Sharon knew the true background of Sherlock's original family.
.....
Having purchased second-class tickets, Benson now sat in the subway car. Watching his sister looking over the business card she had gotten from Detective Bryan, he teased with a smile, "Melissa, I thought you weren't interested in anything outside of machinery."
Melissa held the card carefully, memorizing the address on it, then suddenly asked, "Benson... where exactly is the house you rented?"
"Cherwood Borough, No. 26 Kinster Street.
"The agent said it's a nice big house, with a great environment. The neighbors are all middle-class families, well-mannered... The rent is only so cheap because of a few incidents that happened there..."
Benson responded offhandedly, but halfway through, he noticed that his sister's expression had become a bit odd and asked in confusion, "What's wrong?"
Melissa handed the business card back and pointed at the address on it.
Benson looked down and saw the words "No. 28 Kinster Street" printed on it.
"So the luxurious mansion next door the agent mentioned is actually Detective Bryan's residence... What a coincidence!" Benson couldn't help but exclaim with emotion.
Meanwhile, Melissa's heart stirred with excitement:
Is even the Goddess favoring me, letting me draw closer to the world of the Beyonders?
.....
On the other side, after boarding the carriage, Ebner heard the lion Leon click his tongue and say, "You were criticizing me for fooling around in Bayam, yet the moment you arrive in Backlund, women are already hitting on you. What I did for you back in Bayam might have been too modest."
Having experienced this lion's terrible personality over the past days, Ebner was already used to it and simply ignored his comment, changing the subject instead: "You promised to figure out the activation incantation for the 'Blasphemy Card.' Any progress?"
"You already tried 'Isabella' and 'Bruna'? Their names didn't work either?" Leon scratched his head with a paw and asked in return.
As for their conversation, Elaine, who was sitting across from them, knew nothing of it. Whether it was Ebner's "Tudor Emblem" or Leon the Lion, both possessed enough power to seal her five senses without her noticing.
"No, they didn't work... And I feel that if the answer were as simple as being the name of one of Roselle's women, Panatiya, who previously held the card for so long, would've activated it already." Ebner shook his head as he spoke.
"That makes sense... Let me think... Hmm... When Roselle forged this card, I think it was on the night of a full moon... He seemed to glance up at the moon at the time," Leon muttered after swaying his head for a while.
"A full moon? Could it be that 'Mr. Door' was involved in the creation of this card? But I already tried words like 'Crimson,' 'Bethel,' 'Abraham,' and none of them worked..." Ebner frowned, having no real leads, and could only continue speculating aimlessly:
A full moon... What else could a full moon symbolize?
Heightened spirituality? The Evernight Goddess? Lilith? Even the Primordial Moon?
Hmm... By the time the Emperor forged the Blasphemy Card, he had already set foot on the moon and realized this world was actually Earth, but he could no longer return...
Wait a minute!
At that moment, Ebner suddenly remembered another layer of meaning tied to the "full moon"—one known only to the Chinese:
"Raising my head, I gaze at the bright moon; lowering it, I think of my hometown..."
If he placed himself in the Emperor's mindset at the time—if he hadn't yet learned the truth about "transmigration"—then the authority represented by "Door" might well have been his only hope of returning home.
Unfortunately... time had already moved on...
With a sigh, a vague and inexplicable premonition surged in Ebner's heart. As a "half-prophet," he had a rough idea of what the Blasphemy Card's activation incantation might be.
"Hometown!"
After casting "Ivans' Veil of Secrecy" to enshroud the carriage, Ebner took out the Blasphemy Card and recited the incantation.
.....
At 2:55 in the afternoon, Emlyn had already come up with an excuse and left the Church of Harvest to return home.
He held his favorite doll in one arm while anxiously awaiting the arrival of three o'clock.
Soon, a burst of sudden crimson light swallowed him whole. He once again arrived in that ancient and mysterious grand hall, where many people were already seated on both sides of the central bronze long table.
Before Emlyn could look around, a lady whose face was blurred stood up on the opposite side. She respectfully bowed toward the mysterious being at the head of the table and said:
"Good afternoon, Mr. Fool."
The other members also stood up and greeted him in unison.
Only then did Emlyn belatedly realize he had missed something. Just as he was about to say something to save face and cover up his "disrespect," he heard that same woman who had first stood up speak again with a voice full of emotion:
"Praise be to you, Mr. Fool.
"You've saved Backlund once again!"

chapters.title: Chapter 673: “Moon” Debuts, and All Kinds of Wild Guesses
chapters.content:
Chapter 673 - “Moon” Debuts, and All Kinds of Wild Guesses
Huh? What? When was I saved again? Emlyn the "Moon" was completely confused. But the only major incident to have happened in Backlund recently was that one, so he quickly locked onto the outbreak of the heavy smog and plague, and guessed that the young lady across from him was referring to that.
But I heard it was caused by a "Demoness of Despair" seeking a promotion... As someone backed by his race, Emlyn was fairly well-informed, and this left him puzzled.
At that moment, he subconsciously looked around the long bronze table to observe the reactions of the other members, but quickly got distracted when he stared too long at Miss "Temperance."
Then, with a sigh full of disappointment, he looked away.
This... This kind of top-grade doll is actually a Beyonder? What a waste!
Emlyn howled in his heart. After all, he knew very well that all the Beyonders able to enter this palace were actually spiritual bodies... And if she had a spiritual body, then that meant the young lady sitting diagonally across from him wasn't really a puppet...
She... moves!
Just as Emlyn was inexplicably sinking into disappointment, "The Hanged Man" Alger, who had long since noticed the new member and was closely watching him, immediately sensed the fluctuation in his emotions.
This seems to carry a bit of "grief"... Could this new member have lost a family member in the Backlund smog disaster?
As he pondered that, he also allocated part of his focus to "Justice," "The World," "Judgement," and "The Tower," thinking they surely knew more hidden secrets and behind-the-scenes truths about the smog incident...
Also, during last week's Tarot Gathering, both 'The World' and 'The Tower' warned that a major tragedy might occur in Backlund... And now 'Justice' has just said Mr. Fool saved Backlund... This might involve a struggle between deities!
Murmuring with a touch of excitement, Alger then turned to glance at "The Sun," who remained calm and composed, clearly signaling that the exploration team from the City of Silver had broken free of the cycle of fate.
Meanwhile, after expressing her thanks to Mr. Fool, "Justice" earnestly lifted her skirt and offered a deep curtsey toward both "The World" and "The Tower," sincerely saying:
"...Mr. World, if not for your prior warning, perhaps in this smog, tens of thousands in Backlund would have perished.
"Mr. Tower, if you hadn't delayed the 'Demoness of Despair's' advance, had she been free to act as she pleased, the direct death toll in the East Borough alone could have exceeded thirty thousand, with indirect casualties being even higher..."
That gloomy guy over there... is that 'The World'? He could predict the smog disaster? He might be a high-sequence powerhouse.
And the one sitting between the big guy and the blue-haired one, who looks scholarly—that must be 'The Tower'... He could obstruct a 'Demoness of Despair'? Another demigod? This gathering really is high-tier!
Emlyn the "Moon" was both shocked and yet felt it was perfectly natural.
—After all, this is a divine assembly. For those who don't have my noble lineage and background, it's only right that their strength would be greater.
To be accurate, if I hadn't intervened, the direct death toll would have exceeded 22,000, though the indirect deaths are probably similar... After all, one, this was the result of Backlund's long-standing environmental problems, and two, later figures are always murky—likely inflated by the royals to cover up mass disappearances.
While thinking this, Ebner had no intention of claiming credit—after all, that number of casualties was still enormous.
He thought for a moment, then pointed at Xio across from him and said, "What I did was nothing much. Miss 'Judgement' also made contributions during the smog incident."
Xio actually felt quite awful about the people who died in the East Borough and at the docks. Many of them had been her friends or informants. Seeing Ebner deflect the credit to her, she merely responded calmly, "I only banished the 'vampire' shepherded by the 'Dusky Saint.'"
'Dusky Saint'?! So the 'Aurora Order' was involved in this too?
"The Hanged Man" Alger sat up straighter, visibly intrigued.
So the 'Aurora Order's' Saint was held back by Miss Xio and MI9's powerhouse...
Klein felt deeply relieved. Even a half-crippled Mr. A had nearly "devoured" him. If a full Saint had been there too, he would've been utterly doomed.
I heard that Her Highness Princess Vera thwarted the "Dusky Saint's" plot during the smog incident and was even commended by the royal family for it... Also, Princess Vera once led a team to the Southern Continent... Could Miss "Judgement" actually be Her Highness?
As these thoughts swirled in her mind, "Justice" Audrey began to scrutinize "Judgement" closely, silently wondering to herself with some uncertainty:
Their temperaments are somewhat similar... but the body shapes don't match... Could it be a disguise?
Meanwhile, "Magician" Fors felt a jolt of fear:
So many demigods were involved behind the scenes of the smog disaster... No wonder it affected a huge metropolis, a prince, and tens of thousands of lives... And I'm just a Sequence 8, yet because I joined the Tarot Club, I've gotten involved in matters far above my level...
"Dusky Saint"? Who's that again? A demigod from some secret organization? And... what vampire? Emlyn the "Moon" blurted out without thinking.
That immediately drew everyone's attention to him.
Hearing his question, Klein finally realized he had forgotten to mention a certain vampire. He chuckled lightly and introduced:
"This is the new member, Mr. 'Moon.'"This gathering is called the Tarot Club, and these are..."
Mr. "Moon"... I thought whoever picked the Moon card would be a lady...
"Justice" Audrey gave a polite nod while letting her mind wander, feeling a bit more relaxed.
Emlyn, however, didn't care about being scrutinized. He proudly lifted his head and asked, "Can you tell me more about that vam—bloodkin? Miss 'Judgement'..."
Xio glanced at him in surprise but, seeing Mr. Fool give silent permission, still materialized an image of the pus-covered "vampire."
A textbook example of a "vampire." "Sun" Derrick nodded, indicating that the vampires he'd seen looked just like this.
Emlyn immediately averted his eyes, curling his lips in disgust. "Forget it... Pretend I never asked."
Either he's a Beyonder deeply interested in vampires... or he's a bloodkin himself!
Seeing this reaction, "Justice," "The Hanged Man," and "Judgement" all came to the same conclusion internally.
"Temperance" even turned her delicate little head to look toward "The World," her eyes clearly conveying one thing:
The one from the Harvest Church?
Back when she protected Klein closely during the "Desire Apostle" incident, she had followed him to the Harvest Church.
Klein saw this and had "The World" give the tiniest nod.
Only then did "Temperance" return to her original posture.
This entire scene was caught by Emlyn, who had been secretly watching her the whole time, and it made him all the more disappointed:
She does move after all...
At that moment, seeing how the members were all modest and not vying for credit, Klein had "The World" exchange a few polite remarks as well. Then, controlling "The Fool" to lean back in his chair with a faint smile, he said:
"I only offered a tiny bit of insignificant help."
After speaking, seeing that "Justice" was about to say something else, he immediately had "The World" cut in:
"Mr. Fool, I conducted a private transaction with Miss 'Magician.' The diary pages she owed you have been transferred to me."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 674: Continued Speculations
chapters.content:
Chapter 674 - Continued Speculations
When
The Magician
Fors heard
The World
's words, she belatedly realized that the private debt transfer between her and
The World
had not received
The Fool
's approval...
Thank goodness Mr. World is a Blessed and, to a certain extent, can represent Mr. Fool's attitude... I must be more cautious when conducting trades with other Tarot Club members in the future,
Fors reflected inwardly.
Although the others were curious about the transaction between
The Magician
and
The World
, they didn't overthink it. Only
Judgment
Xio gave Fors beside her a glance, thinking that this was a situation she hadn't been aware of.
At that moment,
The Fool
nodded slightly and responded in a calm tone to
The World
's earlier "debt transfer" request: "Granted."
Seeing the topic shift to the
Roselle's Diary
,
Temperance
turned her small head toward the seat at the top and said:
"There is one page of the diary this time, credited to
The World
."
As she spoke, she looked over at
The World
. Though she said nothing, Klein still understood her meaning: she had submitted a total of ten diary pages, which should have fully repaid the cost of cleansing the pollution.
The World
also didn't speak—under Klein's control, he simply nodded slightly.
On the other side,
Justice
Audrey said apologetically:
"I'm sorry, due to the Three Major Churches and the military conducting a cleanup in Backlund, I haven't been able to acquire additional Roselle diary pages. Please allow me one more week."
"That's fine," Klein replied once more, calmly and without any emotional fluctuations.
Hearing the others speak,
The Magician
Fors snapped out of her self-reflection and quickly looked to the top of the bronze table, saying:
"Honorable Mr. Fool, I also have three pages of Roselle's diary to offer."
Not long after she agreed to
The World
's deal—exchanging a teleportation stone for her debt—she received a letter from her teacher, which included those three pages.
Fors didn't regret her trade with
The World
. After all, it was likely her teacher only had those three pages, and it wasn't nearly enough to cover the debt she owed for
seeking angelic protection
.
Still, if I had held those three pages back then, I might've been able to ask for more compensation from Mr. World... like gold pounds...
Mr. World looks like someone with money—he surely wouldn't mind spending some worldly goods.
Fors secretly speculated.
Completely unaware of what she was thinking,
The Fool
Klein nodded in satisfaction, thinking:
Not bad. The more members there are, the more channels there are. A lot of things will snowball and grow rapidly...
He transferred the four materialized diary pages to his side, then discreetly looked toward
The Tower
.
Although the diary pages the latter provided always contained some unserious content, there were occasionally high-quality entries.
Ebner, however, gave no response. He still held two pages of Roselle's diary provided by
The Lion
Leon, but after letting
The Fool
read rather indecent "short essays" three weeks in a row, it didn't seem appropriate to do so again. It was better to wait a bit longer and mix them with more proper diary entries before submitting them.
As for writing his own... Ever since learning there were other transmigrators in this world, Ebner rarely did that anymore.
Under the butterfly effect, much of the information he "knew" might no longer be accurate.
In order not to mislead
The Fool
, even if he were to make something up, he'd only fabricate some of Roselle's gossip...
But those aren't much different from the diaries provided by "Lion" Leon—so why bother making them up?
Seeing that "The Tower" didn't respond, Klein wasn't disappointed. He turned to Fors and said, "Very well... you may state your request."
Since Fors's debt had already been transferred to "The World," the three pages she now submitted should earn her compensation.
Miss "Magician" thought for a moment. She felt that not only was she still far from advancing, but she had also gotten clues to both her formula and materials. As for Xio and Ebner, they didn't need her worrying...
There didn't seem to be much worth asking for... Fors instinctively glanced around and then suddenly froze as her eyes locked onto something—there was an extra card beside Mr. Fool!
At first, the other Tarot Club members didn't notice this change due to the impact of the Great Smog incident, except for "The Moon." But now, following "Magician's" gaze, everyone looked over in surprise at the additional card—even Ebner was no exception.
Klein got one more card than in the original story? Looks like I wasn't the only one who gained something from the Great Smog incident—Mr. Fool profited as well,
Ebner thought, adjusting his sitting posture thoughtfully.
Mr. Fool gained a Blasphemy Card after the Great Smog... That definitely isn't a coincidence! My guess must be right—an event that caught Mr. Fool's attention to that extent must involve secrets on the level of gods! Hmm, when it's time to share information later, I'll ask Miss "Justice" about it... Although, she may not know much. Her position likely limits her access to real details. Still, she's very curious. She'll definitely try to get answers from Mr. Fool, from "The Tower," from "Judgment." Hopefully, I can eavesdrop...
Many thoughts rapidly crossed the mind of "The Hanged Man" Alger.
At this moment, Fors withdrew her gaze. With no pressing needs, she naturally chose to satisfy her curiosity first:
"Respected Mr. Fool, I would like to know—does the new card by your hand belong to the Blasphemy Cards? Which one is it?"
I thought Miss "Justice" would be the one to ask this. After all, her curiosity is always the strongest... But Miss "Magician" asking works just as well. Either way, I get to breeze through another question without effort...
Klein chuckled to himself and casually flipped over the new Blasphemy Card, displaying it for "Magician" to see.
"Demoness."
The "Demoness" card? How did it fall into Klein's hands? And honestly, Old Huang's image is quite seductive... How did he manage to make it so clearly recognizable as himself, and yet obviously female?
Ebner silently commented to himself before looking away.
Demoness... The main culprit behind the Great Smog was a Demoness... So it really is connected.
Another piece of proof formed in Alger's mind.
Having already learned the Blasphemy Cards' function, "Sun" Derrick felt somewhat disappointed—after all, there were no Beyonders in Silver City on the "Demoness" pathway.
"The Moon" Emlyn, however, was intrigued as he stared at the "Demoness" card for a few moments, thinking:
So this is one of Roselle's Blasphemy Cards... But who's the person drawn on the card? Quite beautiful... Is she Roselle's wife, his mistress, or his daughter?
I still don't understand in what ways these "Blasphemy Cards" are considered blasphemous... Hmm, that priest and the Iron-armed lady both have a bunch of Roselle's manuscripts... Well, now they should be called diaries. Next time, I'll bring them to exchange for answers.
Unaware that he was about to receive a batch of "low-quality" diaries, Klein flipped the "Demoness" card face-down again, then turned his gaze to the page of parchment Sharon had materialized.
This should be something Sharon had just received today—he hadn't read it in advance.
"June 6th. What happened today was simply a disaster!
"I swear this in writing:
"If I ever bring the 'Calamity Seal' to a ball again, I'll eat the shit that 'Three-Light' poops out!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 675: Diary
chapters.content:
Chapter 675 - Diary
Your Majesty, even you have started scamming food and drink?
Klein couldn't help but make a jab when he reached this point. Then he refocused on the page and continued reading the rest of the diary:
"...Liu Bo told me that it's because his current true body—that is, the 'Calamity Seal'—has been 'contaminated' by a higher-level power, which always brings 'misfortune' to those around him. That's why the Sauron family named it 'Calamity.'
"A major reason why the Sauron family has declined to its current state is precisely because they've been holding onto this 'Grade 0' Sealed Artifact for so long.
"After Liu Bo transmigrated here, he's been doing his best to 'restrain' the side effects brought by that 'contamination'... Now, it only 'activates' during banquets or balls, and that's already the result of his efforts.
"I thought about it and felt it might be because in banquets and balls, everyone wears a false mask, scheming for their own interests and those of others. Isolation, alliances, provocations, honeyed words with a dagger behind the back—such behaviors are everywhere. In a certain sense, this resonates with the 'Calamity Seal,' a Sealed Artifact from the 'Hunter' pathway. That's probably what causes the loss of control over its negative effects during those occasions.
"It reminds me of those wars in my previous life—they always began with a meeting, and ended with another meeting...
"But seriously, what kind of 'contamination' could even a Sealed Artifact at the Sequence 1 level not resist?
"Something related to fate... Could it be the uniqueness of the 'Wheel of Destiny' or something like that?
"This also solves a long-standing question that's been bothering me: for over a thousand years, the Sauron family has been unable to produce a 'Conqueror' using the traits of the 'Calamity Seal,' and it's probably because they just couldn't handle the contamination."
The Calamity Seal is contaminated too?
And it even caused the Sauron family—an angelic lineage—to fall into decline due to its side effects...
That's terrifying!
And the fact that Liu Bo could restrain such dreadful negative effects to only act up during events like balls and banquets... he clearly isn't simple either!
Still, Liu Bo didn't say that the Calamity Seal has zero side effects during ordinary times... In fact, the Emperor
did
go downhill later... though that might also have been entirely his own fault...Lastly, is the "Wheel of Destiny" the name of a Sequence 0 from some pathway?
Fate... the "Monster" pathway perhaps?
While mulling over it, Klein flipped the page to its back.
Indeed, Miss "Temperance" was more "conscientious" than the others—this kind of double-sided diary entry was still counted as just one page's contribution!
Feeling a bit of admiration, Klein lowered his head and read on:
"September 4th, the night of the full moon.
"As I stared at the crimson sky, considering whether I should 'Intis-ify' a few ancient poems to match the mood, Liu Bo suddenly began singing a Chinese song with a rather offbeat tone...
'Without the bright moon's light, how would one long for home?
Where am I going, through these glittering lights and wine?
Standing in a noisy square, a bone flute's gentle whine.
Beside me, only emptiness, a void so wide...'
"I've never heard this tune before, and the lyrics... I feel like they were written just for me!
"Since when did Liu Bo get so talented?
"And he's even been to Feysac before? He actually knows those half-giants use bone flutes to mourn the Giant Court?
"But it just made me even more upset, made me miss home even more...
"Oh, my homeland!"
Homeland...
Reaching this part, Klein—for the first time—felt a hundred percent emotional resonance with the Emperor.
The Emperor, Liu Bo, and himself...
In this world, perhaps only the three of them truly understand the emotional weight those two characters carry for someone from Huaxia!
Sighing, Klein looked toward the final paragraph on the back of the page:
"I asked him why the song only had a few lines... and he gave me this cryptic response, saying the story beyond hadn't happened yet, so naturally there were no lyrics...
"Damn it, cryptic my ass! He completely scattered all my melancholic feelings with that one line!
"Don't tell me this guy just couldn't come up with more lyrics and was faking profundity to cover it up?"
The Emperor and Liu Bo really do seem like a pair of trollish friends...
Klein even felt a twinge of envy. After all, burdened with so many secrets and such a heavy responsibility, he had always felt rather alone.
After a few seconds adjusting his emotions, Klein finally opened the diary submitted by Fors.
The first page was filled with the Great Emperor mocking a young Sauron family member named Floran, based on the fact that the "Iron-Blooded Knight" stage would turn women into men.
Klein had already learned this from Ebner, so he wasn't surprised. He just couldn't help but mutter a complaint when he saw Roselle's concern over whether the "Savant" might undergo a gender change:
Your Majesty, you didn't change genders, but you not only slept with a Demoness, you even printed the imagined female version of yourself onto a card...
Glancing at the "Demoness" card by his side—where a bandaged, female Roselle was depicted—Klein continued reading the rest of the diary:
"February 15th. The improved cannon I designed and supervised has been completed. Its performance was slightly worse than expected, but it's not a major issue. With it, and with mass production, I'll let this world and this era witness truly advanced tactics!
"To celebrate, I've decided to hold a banquet and invite those people who look down on me. Just wait to be completely slapped in the face!"
Your Majesty... treasure these days when banquets go off without a hitch...
Klein silently grumbled before turning the page.
The second page detailed the operations of the "Twilight Hermit Order" and Roselle's first encounter with Hermes.
As for the former, Klein had already deduced much of it based on various information revealed by Mr. "Tower," and had more clearly identified the mysterious gathering's convener than Roselle had at the time of writing—it was "Angel of Imagination " Adam, the offspring of the ancient Sun God, a king among angels.
As for the latter, Klein wasn't surprised either. After all, in previous diary entries he'd received, there were mentions of Roselle asking Hermes about the "Death Archon" Vicente Miranda.
But Hermes's so-called "brilliant" explanation of 'Authority' got cut off before even starting... that's just frustrating!
Klein sighed, but there was nothing he could do. After all, all Roselle's diaries available on the market were scattered, copied versions. It was normal for them to be incomplete.
He quickly flipped to the third page, which wasn't of much value. It merely contained the Emperor's account of manor life—wanting to hunt, reminiscing about delicious food, hoping to gain supernatural powers, and longing for pretty maids.
.....
While Mr. "Fool" was reading the diary, Ebner was also trying to think about some matters he had previously avoided due to the warnings from the "Pure White Eye." He had dared not think too deeply.
But to his surprise, even within "Sefirah Castle," even with the concealment of the "Gray Fog," the moment he tried to contemplate the deeper connections between the "Pure White Eye" and transmigrators, his spirituality went into a frenzy of warnings, forcing him to stop.
He even had a premonition... thinking about those things inside "Sefirah Castle" might be even more dangerous than doing so in the real world!
Ebner immediately ceased his attempt, but a hint of realization dawned within him:
Unlike the pollution risk from learning about those Outer Deities, delving into the connection between transmigrators and the "Pure White Eye" likely had consequences that didn't stem from an external source—but from the "Unknown Land" behind the "Pure White Eye."
The "Unknown Land" was directly connected to my spirit, in a bond so close it couldn't be severed... So the "Land of Hidden Night" outside my spiritual body couldn't block the internal influence on me, and neither could "Sefirah Castle"...
And once I'm affected by something from the "Unknown Land," Sefirah Castle might even launch its own counterattack... That's probably why my spirituality kept trying to stop me.
Looks like the key is becoming a demigod... Lilith once said that after I become a demigod, I'll come to understand certain things... maybe that's because divinity is the lowest threshold for carrying knowledge about the 'Unknown Land.'
Hmm, but Lilith never stopped me from collecting stories and items related to other transmigrators... so that should be fine... Once I become a demigod, I should be able to piece together part of the truth using the intelligence I've gathered.
Sighing lightly, Ebner stopped overthinking. At this moment, the "Fool" Klein had also just finished reading the diary. He leaned back slightly and smiled.
"You may begin."
"Justice" Audrey immediately looked across at "Tower," a little worried as she asked, "Mr. 'Tower,' I forgot to ask earlier... I heard that you and the Demoness who created the smog were both 'erased' by a powerhouse from the Church of the Evernight Goddess... You weren't injured, were you?"
Although Mr. "Tower" sitting here meant that Mr. "Fool" must have intervened and rescued him, Audrey was still concerned that the "hero" of Backlund might have gotten hurt... After all, in a way, it was partly her fault that the Evernight Church's powerhouse had been able to arrive so quickly.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 676: The Moon’s Discovery
chapters.content:
Chapter 676 - The Moon's Discovery
When "The Fool" Klein heard Miss Justice's question, he also controlled The World to adjust his sitting posture. He too wanted to know how Mr. Tower had escaped—could it be that the Earth Mother and the Goddess had erupted into a divine war?
Was Tower erased by a powerhouse from the Church of the Evernight Goddess?
Erased... that word is quite interesting... Generally speaking, isn't it equivalent to "killed"?
Was it Mr. Fool who saved him? The Hanged Man Alger turned his head, looking toward Tower with interest.
The others also looked over in unison—even Xio was no exception. She had recently been busy handling various follow-up affairs from the Great Smog. Though she knew Ebner had returned to Backlund, she hadn't had time to meet him yet.
Seeing that Miss Justice seemed somewhat guilty, Ebner thought for a moment and smiled as he said, "I wasn't injured. That angel merely sent me into the Land of Evernight... I even killed one of the main culprits behind the Great Smog incident there—Despair Nightingale Panatiya."
As he spoke, he obtained Mr. Fool's permission, then manifested Panatiya's Beyonder characteristic and continued, "If anyone has need of it, you can make me an offer."
That Demoness of Despair who sought advancement was killed by Tower? He really is a demigod—maybe even not an ordinary one! The Moon Emlyn didn't associate this matter with the message The Fool had him pass to Bishop Utravsky earlier. He simply marveled at how extraordinary he was—surely it was because he was special, the savior of the Blood Tribe, that he could join such a high-level gathering as a mere Sequence 7.
But The Hanged Man Alger caught the key point in Ebner's words and asked, carefully considering his words, "Land of Evernight? The one at the peak of Mount Hornacis? Wasn't that place already abandoned? I remember some documents saying that only ruins remain there, and the people inside seemed to have vanished into thin air."
As for the Demoness of Despair's Beyonder characteristic, he had no need for it, even if it was an item at the demigod level.
Ebner nodded, then shook his head and said, "It is indeed that Land of Evernight, but it wasn't abandoned—it was hidden by the Evernight Goddess."
Hidden?
The rest of the members all sensed that this "hidden" likely didn't carry its ordinary meaning, but rather a deeper and more specific connotation. But what exactly it meant, they couldn't guess. They could only speculate randomly based on the Goddess's title, Mother of Secrets.
Could it be... authority?
Klein's heart stirred. He recalled the phrase mentioned in the diary he had just read and immediately made a connection.
"Mr. Tower, could you show us a glimpse of the Land of Evernight? I'm willing to pay an appropriate price." At this point, Miss Justice had completely forgotten her original intent, asking with reserved curiosity.
Well asked!
Klein almost applauded Miss Justice.
But Ebner hesitated at this moment. Other places might have been fine, but the Land of Evernight was the Goddess's domain. Talking about it was one thing—if he were to reveal the secrets within, would he be punished by the deity?
"I'm sorry, Miss Justice... That is the Goddess's secret." In the end, Ebner didn't dare display the scenes from within the Land of Evernight, afraid of disrupting the Goddess's arrangements... This also came from a certain
premonition
of his.
Although the Goddess surely couldn't peer into the interior of the Castle of Sefirah, She was watching Klein...
"Ah... I misspoke." As a follower of the Goddess, Audrey instinctively wanted to draw a crimson moon before her chest, but quickly realized she was in Mr. Fool's divine kingdom, so instead silently offered a prayer.
Then, she sincerely said, "Mr. Tower, thank you once again for stopping and eliminating the Demoness of Despair, thereby preventing the awakening of the Primordial Demoness, and keeping the pollution level of the Great Smog within a controllable range."
As she spoke, she looked toward Judgment and The World as well, equally sincere in her tone. "And thank you both for disrupting the Aurora Order's plot, once again blocking the descent of the True Creator into the material world."
She had long wanted to express her gratitude to Tower, The World, and Judgment, but had suppressed her eagerness due to Mr. World's interruption and the sequence of the Tarot Club. Now, she naturally had to make up for it.
The Primordial Demoness wants to awaken... The True Creator attempted to descend... What exactly happened in Backlund? This is far more dangerous than I imagined!
At the same moment, The Hanged Man Alger and The Moon Emlyn had the same reaction, though their expressions differed. The former only lifted his eyelids slightly, his pupils contracting as he unconsciously leaned to the side, while the latter gave the impression he was about to leap up.
Mother Goddess—no, by the Moon above—when did Backlund become so dangerous? Two evil gods appeared during one Great Smog? That young lady must be exaggerating, right? Mr. Fool might be a suspected deity, but even he can't afford to offend two existences of that level at the same time...
Unless he is actually an incarnation of one of the orthodox gods? Or maybe he's backed by an alliance of deities?
Wait... Right after the Great Smog, Mr. Fool did have me pass a message to a priest of the Earth Mother... Could Mr. Fool be in an alliance with the Earth Mother?
And I even asked Mr. Fool to help remove the mental suggestion that bishop from the Earth Mother's Church placed on me...
No... that's not right... It was the Ancestor who told me to pray to Him for help... Don't tell me the Ancestor and the Earth Mother are also allies? That's why those old geezers in the family turned a blind eye when I became a follower of the Earth Mother?
Am I actually the liaison among all three? The Ancestor really does value me most!
The more Emlyn thought about it, the faster his heart pounded, and the more excited he became... but he still couldn't confirm anything.
—The Blood Clan having the nickname "vampires" didn't mean they had no heartbeat; it was just significantly slower. Their heart was still one of their vital weaknesses.
As expected... No wonder this event caught Mr. Fool's attention... But what benefit does He gain from foiling the evil gods' schemes? The Hanged Man Alger pondered silently as his gaze fell once more on the newly appeared "Demoness" card.
Could that be Mr. Fool's reward?
Hmm... The Blasphemy Card may be priceless to us, but to someone near godhood—or even an actual god—like Mr. Fool, it likely isn't all that valuable...
Perhaps He used this opportunity to achieve a deeper goal... like forming an alliance with a deity who loathes the Primordial Demoness and the True Creator...
Connecting this with Mr. Tower escaping from the Land of Evernight almost unscathed... Could it be the Evernight Goddess?
Alger's thoughts traveled far in that moment.
The Magician Fors, on the other hand, was once again gripped by fear. Though she had heard a few scattered hints from Xio, she never imagined that behind the Great Smog—an incident that had already claimed tens of thousands of lives—there lurked an even more terrifying truth.
Ebner, however, didn't wish to continue this topic. He turned instead to The Sun Derrick and asked, "Did you escape that cycle?"
The Sun Derrick was momentarily stunned, then gave a sincere nod. He turned toward the head of the bronze table and bowed.
"Great Mr. Fool, I am immensely grateful for your guidance. It helped me discover the key point—the Angel of Destiny—from the mural with the words 'Rose Redemption,' and assisted our Chief in breaking the cycle of fate."
Angel of Destiny? Is that the "Mercury Snake" Mr. Tower mentioned, the one who loves to paint? Half-understanding, Klein—the Fool—responded with a smile, "Not bad."
After thanking Mr. Fool, Derrick looked at Ebner and Alger with equal sincerity and said, "Mr. Tower, Mr. Hanged Man, I thank you both as well for your guidance...
"Also, Mr. Tower, I asked that little boy about the origin of the gear-shaped book."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 677: Occult Arts
chapters.content:
Chapter 677 - Occult Arts
At this point,
"Moon"
Emlyn was completely baffled. What "Rose of Redemption"? What "Angel of Fate"? What "breaking the cycle"? What "Gear Book"? Everything was outside the bounds of his knowledge. He could understand every individual word, yet strung together, none of it made sense to him.
They had just been discussing demigod-level topics—how did an angel suddenly get involved? Could it be that this seemingly young
"Sun"
, under
The Fool's
guidance, had escaped from the hands of an angel?
Emlyn tried to piece things together based on the tiny slivers he did understand.
On the other side, Ebner followed up on
"Sun's"
words and asked, "What exactly happened?"
Derrick didn't conceal anything and recounted the multiple expeditions he and his Silver City companions had taken, just like in the original story. He also repeated in full what the boy Jack from Enmat Port had said during each "cycle."
This made the other Tarot Club members—excluding
"Moon"
and
"Tower"
—both curious and uneasy. They were curious about how the "Land Abandoned by the Gods" could connect with the normal world and worried that the devouring darkness surrounding Silver City might keep spreading, eventually engulfing both the Northern and Southern Continents and all five seas.
The only difference from the original account lay in Jack's description of the Gear Book.
A fallen mountain peak, a ruined tower, and the only intact part within that tower—a Gear Book capable of resisting the cycle of fate... And Jack's father had mentioned "a group of sinners who defied the Lord" and a "Fallen Star"...
Fallen Star... Morning Star Fallen from Grace?
After hearing
"Sun's"
explanation, Ebner immediately made a few connections, then recalled the two occult techniques embedded in that extraordinary item:
"Ivans' Veil of Secrecy"
and
"Vaulite's Perfect Restoration."
"Ivans' Veil of Secrecy"
worked even better within the dark domain... and the Land Abandoned by the Gods was filled with darkness.
"Vaulite's Perfect Restoration"
could to a certain degree resist losing control and even reverse the mutations brought by contamination... In the normal world, this would just be a better kind of healing spell...
But now that he thought about it, in the
Land Abandoned by the Gods
, for the survivors forced to consume monster flesh and suffer the deformities and torment brought by corruption, this ability was nothing short of
divine magic
!
Silver City still had black-faced grass, so the problem wasn't too severe for them. Back when I introduced the
Fallen Morning Star
at the Tarot Club, I only mentioned it briefly—so
Little Sun
didn't react much... But if it had been someone from
Moon City
, they probably would've begged me for the construction method of that occult art already.
So now, I'm almost certain: these two secret arts must have come from a transmigrator who ended up in the
Land Abandoned by the Gods
. The
Calamity Seal
probably found the inheritance of these two arts from the
Unknown Lands
or elsewhere, and then passed them to Roselle to forge into an extraordinary item...
The name
Fallen Morning Star
—most likely also chosen by the
Calamity Seal
!
But Ivans and Vaulite... Which one of them was the transmigrator? Or maybe his full name was
Ivans Vaulite
?
Ebner gave a slight shake of his head and continued pondering over the circumstances in which
"Sun"
said they had found the Gear Book:
A fallen mountain peak... ruined architecture... a half-collapsed tower...
Could the transmigrator have cut out a mountain from the Land Abandoned by the Gods to build a floating city?
Could the so-called "Ivans' Veil of Secrecy" actually be part of the barrier protecting the floating city?
Just as Ebner was making unfounded guesses, Klein also thought of the "Fallen Morning Star" necklace. Although his understanding of the secret arts within wasn't as deep as Ebner's, he directly deduced that the creator of that "Gear Book," and even the so-called "Fallen Star," were all referring to "Liu Bo."
But why is Mr. "Tower" looking for the Gear Book? He even used "Prophecy"... Is it a task from the Earth Mother?
At that moment, "Sun" happened to finish summarizing what the Chief had told him about the eight Kings of Angels. He speculated that Amon might be the "Angel of Time," one of those Kings, while the one who created the "Cycle of Destiny" would be the "Angel of Fate," Ulotheus.
In response, "Justice," "Hanged Man," "Magician," and the others all nodded silently. They had already heard Mr. "Tower" speak of the Kings of Angels before. They were simply glad to have learned the name and title of another one.
Only "Moon" responded with a blank expression...
Although the blood race had a long history and long lives, and knew quite a bit about the era before the Great Cataclysms, that knowledge was mostly centered around the period before the Progenitor fell into slumber. It didn't involve the so-called "Kings of Angels."
Emlyn looked around and found that apart from "Tower," who was lost in thought, everyone else seemed to understand what was being said... He couldn't help but grit his teeth in frustration.
Once I get back, I have to get more of Roselle's diary from the priest and the Iron-arm lady. Next time at the Tarot Gathering, I have to figure all of this out.
At that moment, "The Fool" Klein noticed everyone glancing discreetly in his direction, seemingly trying to get more information about the other "Kings of Angels" from him. So he let "The Fool" speak up first and said with a faint smile, "You will come into contact with them one after another in the future."
Although I know more than you all about the 'Red Angel' and the 'Angel of Imagination,' if I only mention those two and keep the rest hidden, it'll look even more suspicious, and could make Mr. Fool look less dignified.
When "Sun" Derrick heard that, he was somewhat disappointed, but he quickly adjusted his mood. Then, as if remembering something, he turned to Mr. "Tower" beside him and said with some difficulty, "Mr. 'Tower,' although the Gear Book is currently with me, I'll definitely be subject to a thorough inspection before returning to Silver City... I probably won't be able to hide it then... And I won't have any opportunity to 'sacrifice' it to Mr. 'Fool' on the way."
Hearing this, Ebner returned from his thoughts. After thinking for a moment, he smiled and said, "No need to worry. It's fine to leave the Gear Book in Silver City for the time being.
"But just as Mr. 'Hanged Man' and I predicted, once you return, Elder Lovia, who had been imprisoned, will almost certainly be released. The supervision over you will also be relaxed—but following that, there will be plenty of tests."
"Hanged Man" Alger nodded as well. He glanced at Ebner and added, "At that time, you'll need to display some value appropriately.
"Make your Chief believe that the power backing you can truly contend with the Fallen Creator behind Elder Lovia."
"How should I show that?" "Sun" Derrick asked earnestly.
"Hanged Man" Alger didn't answer but instead looked to "Tower," confident the latter had already made plans.
Ebner smiled and said, "Start by trying to negotiate an exchange for the Gear Book.
"You can ask your Chief whether Silver City needs a secret art that can purge the 'pollution' accumulated in the body, heal deformities, and restore people to normal."
Passing secret arts to Silver City also fit with his role as the "Mysticism Magister."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 678: The Change in "The Tower"
chapters.content:
Chapter 678 - The Change in "The Tower"
After a few seconds of comprehension, "Sun" Derrick immediately became excited and couldn't help but ask, "Mr. 'Tower'? Do you really have a mystical technique that can purge madness and toxins?
"And you're willing to teach it to us?"
Although Silver City had discovered Black-Faced Grass and now had relatively safer food, they still had to hunt some monsters, collect their flesh and blood, and pick the fruits of mutated plants as supplementary food.
This was especially true during missions outside the city—since they couldn't carry too much flour ground from Black-Faced Grass, they had no choice but to hunt nearby monsters and, after identifying their characteristics, roast and eat them.
But this led to a certain accumulation of toxins and pollution, which caused both mental and physical problems. It couldn't be consumed continuously and required sufficient intervals.
Still, on every mission, there were people who lost their lives due to such mental and physical issues...
If there truly was a mystical technique that could remove the pollution and restore the body and mind to their original states, then the survival rate of Silver City's exploration teams would surely rise significantly!
Derrick couldn't help but feel thrilled.
"Don't get too excited—this is an exchange... and also just the first step in demonstrating value," Ebner said with a smile to calm him.
Upon hearing this, "Sun" Derrick took a few deep breaths to steady his emotions. Then he solemnly said, "Once I return, I'll speak to the Chief about this. I believe he'll be willing to trade that book for this mystical technique."
"The Hanged Man" Alger sighed inwardly before speaking up. "If you bring it up so directly, it'll be too abrupt. If I were the Chief, I'd definitely suspect your motives.
"You need to take it slow."
Derrick thought for a moment, then nodded, realizing that his approach might indeed seem too hasty. He earnestly asked, "Then what should I do?"
"Maintain tacit understanding, but don't lay it out too bluntly." "The Hanged Man" Alger first established the principle, then hesitated briefly before saying, "You can deliberately consume some polluted monster meat, then use Mr. 'Tower's' mystical technique to 'heal' yourself.
"That way, you'll draw the attention of your Chief or other high-ranking members. Let that be the starting point for 'contact.'"
Ebner followed up at this point, "I'll craft a charm containing that mystical technique or a one-time-use mystical item. When it's convenient, you can ask Mr. 'Fool' to pass it to you."
"Sun" Derrick nodded repeatedly, then asked, "And after that?"
"After that, it'll depend on how your Silver City leadership reacts... different reactions will require different strategies. For now, just make sure that within this week, you manage to draw their attention and display our intention to 'make contact.'
"At next week's Tarot Gathering, you can tell me and 'Tower' about their actions, and we'll guide you on what to do next."
At this point, Alger subconsciously glanced at "Tower" beside him. The reason he cooperated with the other party in advising "Sun" was to help him break free from suspicion and surveillance as soon as possible, restoring the material channel from the Forsaken Land of the Gods.
But originally, I hadn't intended to act so aggressively. I wanted to understand the Silver City leadership's attitude first before letting "Sun" display value. After all, the risks here aren't small... But "Tower" seems quite certain about the upper ranks of Silver City... Did he make a "prophecy"? Or did he confirm it by some other means?
As for the possibility that "Tower" was merely sending "Sun" into danger, Alger didn't even consider it—after all, Mr. "Fool" was present, and He likely wouldn't allow any deliberate harm against a fellow member.
Ebner had indeed "prophesied" Chief Colin Iliad's attitude based on his knowledge of the original storyline, confirming that Derrick wouldn't be in danger before presenting this plan.
At this moment, seeing "Sun" accept "The Hanged Man's" suggestion without much hesitation, Ebner added, "For this 'demonstration,' it's best to wait until you're sure that Elder Lovia has regained her freedom before taking action."
Upon hearing this, although Derrick didn't quite understand why, he still agreed earnestly. After all, in his heart, Mr. "Tower" and Mr. "Hanged Man" were both good people, and everything they said was for his own good.
That way, it wouldn't come off as abrupt, and it would also strengthen the upper echelon's confidence in their "checks and balances" strategy. Watching silently all this time, Mr. "Fool" sighed inwardly, feeling that both "Tower" and "Hanged Man" were indeed masters at manipulating hearts.
It was just that one relied on experience, and the other relied on a kind of "omniscience"... Of course, as for the difference between the two, Mr. "Fool" himself was still unaware for the time being.
"Justice" Audrey and "Magician" Fors were both left stunned as they listened, deeply feeling they had just taken another enlightening lesson.
"Judgment" Xio recalled the time she first met Ebner. How pure and sincere he had been back then... never hesitating to share any knowledge...
Yet now, after just a little over half a year, he was becoming more and more calculating!
And I'm the same... The only ones I can trust without reservation are Fors and Ebner...
Xio mocked herself inwardly.Meanwhile, "Moon" Emlyn remained completely bewildered—polluted monsters? Silver City? Chief? He understood none of it. He could only vaguely guess that the "Sun's" living environment must be very different from his own.
At this moment, "Temperance" Sharon saw that the discussion between "Sun," "Tower," and "Hanged Man" had concluded. She spoke concisely:
"I need information on high-Sequence mummies."
She didn't mention a price—after all, when it comes to information, the value depends on the specifics, so compensation should be negotiated accordingly.
Mummies? The term Emperor Roselle used to name the corpses of "pharaohs"? Hmm... "Pharaoh" was also a proper noun he coined. Also, "mummy powder" seems to be quite popular among nobles and gentlemen, though I don't know why... "Justice" Audrey recalled related knowledge she had come across, while glancing at Miss "Temperance," who looked like a doll.
Since joining the Tarot Club, this lady had always been very low-key. Other than knowing she had a good relationship with "World," Audrey knew almost nothing else about her.
"High-Sequence mummies? Ones with Beyonder characteristics?" "Hanged Man" Alger hesitated a moment, then probed.
He was quite curious about this member of the "Temperance" faction, suspected to be from the Rose School of Thought.
"No need," "Temperance" Sharon shook her head lightly.
"I'll keep an eye out for you, but there likely won't be any results in the short term," Alger replied after a bit of thought.
Demigod-level mummies generally only exist in tombs of Beyonders in the Southern Continent, and he had no plans to go there anytime soon—he could only inquire through his colleagues.
"All right." Sharon's reply remained concise, and she soon returned to her doll-like state, causing "Moon" to sigh inwardly:
If only she could stay in that later state all the time.
Meanwhile, on the other side, Ebner was thinking that once he finished his trip to Trier, he would head south to Siburn. Perhaps he'd have a chance to gather some mummy-related intel there.
But that would be at least a month or two from now... While thinking this, Ebner looked around and said with a smile:
"I have a batch of Beyonder characteristics I want to sell...
"Here's the list."
(End of this Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 679: Trade and Assassination
chapters.content:
Chapter 679 - Trade and Assassination
A series of Beyonder characteristics? A list? The moment they heard this, "Justice," "Magician," and the others were visibly shaken. Even "Judgment" and "Hanged Man" turned to look, and Miss "Temperance," who rarely made any extraneous movements, also turned her head.
"Physician," "Provoker," "Swindler," "Demon," "Navigator," "Baron of Corruption," "Demoness of Pleasure," "Faceless Man"...
When the "Tower" materialized the list and passed it to everyone, they stared at the entries ranging from the Sequence 8 "Physician" to the demigod-level "Demoness of Despair," and their shock not only failed to subside but instead deepened into disbelief.
The "Nation of Night" that the "Tower" had mentioned earlier sounded like some prison where the goddess locked up criminals... Could he have wiped out all the Beyonders there? As Alger the "Hanged Man" pondered this, he decided to purchase the "Physician" and "Navigator" characteristics.
Those two Sequences were very useful at sea. If he had Sharf craft them into Beyonder items and resold them, he could easily make a profit of over a thousand pounds.
After her initial surprise, Audrey the "Justice" felt a twinge of regret... It was a shame there were no "Audience" pathway characteristics on the list, or she could have bought one for Susie to use in the future.
Fors the "Magician" lowered her head to study the list, then looked up at the "Tower" across from her, utterly unable to reconcile this scholarly, refined man with the brutality his actions implied.
Miss "Temperance" sat there quietly on the surface, but in her heart, she gave the "Tower" a new label:
Demoness Slayer.
There were two Demoness es on the list alone, and counting the "Demoness of Agony" Ray who had previously died by his hand, that made at least three Demoness es connected to his actions in under half a year—and one of them was even a demigod!
Xio the "Judgment" was still saving up to buy the "Punishment Knight" characteristic from Jane, so after a quick glance, she lost interest.
Derrick the "Sun" didn't see anything he needed, so all that remained in his heart was admiration:
Mr. Tower is incredible.
This was Emlyn the "Moon's" first time witnessing such a scene. While he tried to maintain his composure, he couldn't help but feel a strange sense of balance—
Humans are always treating our Blood Tribe's characteristics like commodities...
Even the "Fool" couldn't help but click his tongue inwardly:
Just how many people has Mr. Tower killed? This is more than what I've collected in my "Creeping Hunger" glove...
What in the world happened in the "Nation of Night"?
Seeing the astonished expressions on the Tarot Club members' faces, Ebner finally experienced the exhilaration his teacher used to feel when showing off his collection of Beyonder items. Smiling, he added, "If you don't want the raw characteristics directly, you can also commission me to craft them into magical items. But the cost will be significantly higher, and I can't guarantee when they'll be finished."
It wasn't too bad while he was still in Backlund—he could shamelessly borrow Mr. Sarri's workshop, Fanny's grandfather. But once he went to Intis, it wouldn't be that convenient. Even the "Edwards–Blaine Teleportation Spell" couldn't bridge the distance from Trier to Bayam in one go; at least one or two transfers would be needed, which was too expensive.
Of course, the "Recorder" under Mr. A's control did have teleportation abilities, but the number of uses was too limited, and the range even shorter.
Ebner was currently focused on improving all the prerequisite knowledge. He believed that soon he'd truly master teleportation, and things would become much easier then.
Upon hearing the "Tower's" words, Xio the "Judgment" was the first to speak. "I'd like to commission a magical item crafted from the 'Faceless Man' characteristic. It must at least be able to change my appearance and body shape... As for other abilities like substitute bodies or fire control, one of them will do."
She had been wanting such an item for a while. Bringing it up now would also help Ebner by playing the role of the first buyer—a win-win.
"Alright," Ebner nodded. As for the price, there was no need to discuss it here at the Tarot Club. That could be handled privately.
Change appearance and body shape... I want one too...
Audrey the "Justice" and Fors the "Magician" had the same thought at the same time.
But while Fors only thought about it, Audrey's eyes sparkled as she spoke up, "Mr. Tower, do you have another item that can change appearance and body shape? I'd like to place an order as well!"
