At this moment, Klein had roughly finished Browse the information on the "Queen of Calamity."
Overall, there wasn't much content. After all, most of the City of Silver's information came from the kingdom of Giants, so they knew more about Giants and their arch-rivals, Dragons. As for Elves, their allies, the information was not very comprehensive, mostly preserved through oral tradition.
Among this limited content, most had already been seen in the murals "The Tower" once displayed, with only one description catching Klein's attention:
"The 'Queen of Calamity' had close ties with the 'Harvest Goddess,' who was the Queen of Giants, and visited the City of Silver multiple times... This displeased the 'Goddess of Beauty,' who had defected to the Elves. The two subordinate deities had a very poor relationship."

chapters.title: Chapter 804: The Ownership of the "Black Knight" Characteristic
chapters.content:
Chapter 804 - The Ownership of the "Black Knight" Characteristic
Based on the ancient god-related knowledge previously revealed by "The Tower" and the recent information provided by "The Sun," it's confirmed that the ancient god Lilith was once betrayed by Giant King Aurmir, who was also from the humanoid faction, falling into an ambush that ultimately led to her demise along with the Demon Wolf King and the Mutated King...
Of course, now it seems Lilith only faked her death or resurrected later using a contingency plan.
But Lilith's subordinate deity, the "Goddess of Beauty," evidently didn't know this, which is why she was displeased with the "Queen of Calamity" and the "Harvest Goddess" being on good terms?
While thinking this, and cross-referencing the currently available information, Klein developed new questions:
The Dragon race has a "Dragon of Wisdom" named Herabergen, equivalent to a deity in the City of Silver's terms; below Giant King Aurmir, there are also His eldest son, Badheil the "God of Dawn," and His Queen, the "Harvest Goddess"; the Elves, besides Elf King Soniathrym, have "Queen of Calamity" Cohinem, "Goddess of Beauty" Auernia, and the "God of Fortune" as Their subordinate deities...
Why do only the "Harvest Goddess" and "God of Fortune" lack true names?
The latter is understandable; after all, He isn't a subordinate deity of the giants, so it's normal for the City of Silver not to have records... But isn't the former the Queen of the Giant Royal Court?
"Mr. Tower" is also very interested in this period of history... Perhaps he knows something.
Thinking this, Klein leaned back, making the documents in his hand disappear as he said with a smile:
"You may begin."
No sooner had his voice fallen than Ebner was the first to rise and bow to the head of the table:
"Mr. Fool, thank you for the aid you gave me in my battle with the 'Saint of Shadows,' helping to slay him..."
Klein's spirits lifted at the remark. He adopted a nonchalant posture and chuckled lightly, "It's a small matter, and you could've defeated him on your own."
This was true; "Mr. Tower" possessed too many formidable items. Given the Saint's state after taking a "Desolation" attack, he was surely doomed.
Hearing their conversation, all the members of the Tarot Club, except for "The World" and "Temperance" who already knew, and little "Sun" who didn't understand what "Saint of Shadows" represented, were shocked by the implication of his words.
Has Mr. Fool become capable of directly interfering with the real world and slaying powerful demigods of the Aurora Order? Is it because He gained the authority of the "Sea God" and the remnants of the Queen of Calamity, leading to further recovery?
What did "The Tower" do to directly confront an Aurora Order Saint? Was it Mr. Fool's mission? And from Mr. Fool's words, "The Tower" wasn't at a disadvantage then? This is even stronger than his brief confrontation with the "Demoness of Despair" during the Great Smog incident...
Thoughts began to race through "The Hanged Man" Alger's mind. He couldn't help but glance at "The Tower" beside him, wanting to figure out what exactly had happened.
"Justice" Audrey had no doubt that Mr. Fool could kill a demigod. In her mind, if not for "Mr. Tower's" request, such a great existence wouldn't even glance at a mere demigod.
What surprised her was the frequency of demigod deaths after encountering "Mr. Tower"!
It's been less than a month, and two demigods have already died by his hand... You have to understand, the death of any such great figure is an earth-shattering event in the mysterious world!
Yet, with Mr. Tower, they died without a sound... Almost nobody even knows...
As far as I know, Detective Ebner went to Intis after leaving Backlund... So, he went to disrupt the Aurora Order's conspiracy in Intis?
Hmm, I remember Fors traveled with him... Perhaps when she and I both return to Backlund, I can ask for details.
Audrey, who had vaguely guessed Mr. Tower's identity after the Backlund premiere, thought this.
Fors the "Magician" didn't overthink it, simply being genuinely shocked by Mr. Tower's strength. She had previously thought that Ebner's power in Sequence 5 surpassed even Mr. Tower and Mr. World... Now it seems Ebner might not be able to defeat "The Tower".
Xio the "Judgment" frowned, deeply feeling that the incidents Ebner was involved in were becoming increasingly terrifying, and she couldn't help at all...
"The Tower" is very strong; after offending the Demoness Sect, he even killed people from the Aurora Order...
But what does that have to do with me? It won't affect my saving the Bloodline, nor is it anything interesting! Anyway, if there's a problem, just pray to Mr. Fool, and if this powerful individual needs to act, it can be handled through "Equivalent Exchange"!
Emlyn grumbled, disdainfully disregarding others' emotional shifts, though his red eyes were also filled with surprise.
Cattleya the "Hermit" was the most shocked person in the Tarot Club because she knew of the "Saint of Shadows" and had even been warned never to provoke him, as he could even borrow power from the "True Creator" if necessary.
Yet, such a powerful demigod was actually killed by "The Tower"? Judging by his tone and the attitudes of others, is this not his first time killing a demigod? Is "The Tower" a powerful Saint, or even an Angel?
No... that's not right, he doesn't feel like an Angel to me, he should still just be a demigod with powerful means...
Moreover, the "Saint of Shadows" was responsible for the Intis region... My previous judgment should be correct; "The Tower" is an Intis citizen, or has long been active in Intis.
This gathering is indeed not simple. I wonder if there are other powerful individuals besides "The Tower"...
And these powerful individuals are all so respectful of "The Fool"...
The more Cattleya the "Hermit" thought, the more she felt that Mr. Fool's profundity was immeasurable, just like His figure currently shrouded in dense gray fog. The clearer she tried to see, the more confused, terrified, and awestruck she became.
At this moment, Ebner cleared his throat, pulling everyone's thoughts back.
He once again "respectfully" bowed and sincerely stated: "Respected Mr. Fool, without your help, even if I could kill the 'Saint of Shadows,' it would take a very long time..."
This was the truth. Although the half-dead "Saint of Shadows" couldn't move, the remnant of Primordial "contamination" on him meant that even if he merged with the "Bone Dragon," he might not be able to eliminate him in a few seconds, which was naturally far inferior to the effect of a thunderous cleansing.
—In terms of offense, the "Tyrant" Pathway is still superior.
"Therefore, although you don't mind, I still want to offer you the 'Black Knight' characteristic." At this point, Ebner added a few explanatory words: "Previously, it was entangled with the other characteristics 'herded' by the 'Saint of Shadows,' and I paid some price to completely separate them."
Holding the "Magic Mirror," the "Black Knight" characteristic was useless in Ebner's hands. Even if he used it to forge a magical item, the side effects of something that had been "rolled" in a Primordial were definitely not small; it would be difficult for someone without a "cheat" to use.
And Ebner wouldn't feel comfortable selling such an item.
So, it was better to give it to Klein, firstly to give his "fellow countryman" some face; secondly, to allow "Creeping Hunger" to upgrade itself with it.
After all, in the current Evernight Kingdom, there was no Mr. A who had turned into a giant mushroom.

chapters.title: Chapter 805: Their Respective Transactions
chapters.content:
Chapter 805 - Their Respective Transactions
"While this distribution of spoils might seem like a loss for me on the surface, it's actually not.
"By 'arming' Mr. Fool, he'll have more tricky maneuvers at his disposal, and the development of the 'Sefirah Castle' will become more complete. In the end, I and the other Tarot Club members will benefit.
"Beyond that, with the 'Black Knight' characteristic in hand, or the upgraded 'Creeping Hunger,' Klein might develop applications for related abilities. Perhaps he could even conjure an 'Angel under the Fool' ahead of time...
"After all, a 'Black Knight' can project demigod souls it has 'herded,' and if those herded demigod souls combine with the 'Blasphemy Card' and leverage the power above the gray fog, posing as an Angel shouldn't be a problem...
"Conversely, if I kept the characteristic, it would be useless to me.
"Finally, since I've decided to give Mr. Fool a share of the spoils... anything less than a demigod-level item just wouldn't be presentable!"
All in all, giving the "Black Knight" characteristic to "The Fool" was a well-thought-out decision by Ebner. After all, one can't just watch the fun; sometimes, one has to "feed" a little "food," right?
Ebner's thinking was clear, but Klein was in a dilemma. Deep down, he didn't want to take advantage, but the reason given by the other party was hard to refuse.
And indeed, he had "stolen" the kill that day... so sharing some spoils was not unreasonable... though a demigod characteristic was a bit much...
But this was also an item for a "believer" to please a "deity." Would not accepting it make "The Tower" uneasy?
As thoughts raced, Klein had an idea. He casually tapped the edge of the ancient long table with his finger and chuckled softly, "I accept your 'sacrifice,' but because its value exceeds the reward required for my previous action, as 'The Fool' of 'Equivalent Exchange,' I will compensate you."
Saying this, he picked up the "Black Emperor" card lying face down beside him, and while briefly shielding it from others' view, he displayed the potion formulas for Sequences 9 through 3 of the "Black Emperor" Pathway to "The Tower."
As Klein knew, Mr. Tower's "friend," Miss Fanny, was a Beyonder of the "Lawyer" Pathway. The subsequent potion formulas for this Pathway would definitely be useful to him.
Moreover, Miss Judgment might even switch to this Pathway in the future.
Ebner was indeed very satisfied with this, as potion formulas beyond the demigod level, like the "Black Knight" characteristic, were already difficult to "measure" with money, unless forcibly priced using the "Quiz Labyrinth."
Even his "Pure White Eye" found it extremely difficult and time-consuming to "analyze" formulas above the demigod level through characteristics.
The demigod characteristic of "Despair Nightingale" had been in his hands for nearly a month, and he still hadn't been able to analyze it... and looking at the progress, there was little hope for at least a few years...
However, the "Black Knight" characteristic had only been in his hands for a few days, and the work of reverse-engineering the formula was already nearing completion...
"I praise Your generosity, Mr. Fool," Ebner said, bowing after noting down the formula.
"The Fool" Klein smiled slightly, "I like equivalent exchange."
No, an immediate response and direct assistance from a great existence is simply priceless!
Cattleya the "Hermit," who witnessed the entire scene, couldn't help but inwardly retort.
Although she didn't know what "The Fool" had shown "The Tower," she assumed it wasn't ordinary. This unequivocally showed how generous and indulgent "The Fool" was towards the Tarot Club members.
But were a deity's gifts truly that easy to take? Perhaps "The Tower" understood this, which is why he unhesitatingly handed over even a demigod characteristic.
However, Cattleya was still deeply envious, as she also hoped to have such "equivalent exchange" opportunities in the future, which often meant she would have an extra life compared to others!
As for the cost, that would only be a consideration if she was still alive to pay it...
Seeing that "The Tower's" matter was concluded, "The Moon" Emlyn couldn't help but look at "The Hanged Man" at the upper end of the table and asked:
"Mr. Hanged Man, I'm ready. When can you get that Bloodline Baron's legacy? You mentioned last time it was in the hands of a great pirate?"
He originally wanted to wait for the three-month period of the bill of exchange to expire before cashing it at the bank, but he soon realized that after deciding to buy the Bloodline Baron's legacy, his mood was completely different from before:
No longer doubtful, no longer hesitant, but full of anticipation, full of longing, wishing to get it immediately, just like when he used to save enough money to buy a desired doll!
He endured for over a week, finally unable to restrain himself, and resold the accepted bill of exchange.
Fortunately, after filming that movie, he passively met many wealthy people. Although their gazes made Emlyn uncomfortable, he gritted his teeth and entrusted one of them to sell it, and the loss was not significant.
Why did he have to mention the great pirate...?
Alger glanced at "The Hermit," sighing helplessly.
With "Admiral of Stars'" keen senses, even if she couldn't immediately confirm my identity, she certainly narrowed down the possibilities!
Sensing "The Hermit's" gaze sweep over him again, "The Hanged Man" felt that his worry was definitely not unfounded.
However, Alger's expression remained unchanged. He turned his head and replied to "The Moon," "I'll get it for you within this week. Finally, let's confirm the price, 4500 pounds, alright?"
Emlyn thought about the dolls in his room and began to haggle with "The Hanged Man," but he was no match for the seasoned veteran. He was naturally outmaneuvered, not only paying a high price but also feeling grateful for Alger's efforts.
An underage or newly adult Vampire, with not much worldly experience...
Cattleya the "Hermit" silently observed and made her judgment.
At this moment, Miss Temperance turned her head, looked at "The Sun," opened her lips, and spoke in a ethereal voice: "I need three petals of 'Bloody Rose Dry Petals' and 10 milliliters of 'Sangwine Thorn' fluid."
Miss Temperance has already obtained the "Marionette" characteristic, and the demigod mummy for the ritual should be completed soon... So, these are auxiliary materials? Hmm, perhaps not very valuable, but I haven't heard of these plants in the Northern Continent. Either they have alternative names, or they are monopolized by the 'Rose School.'
However, the sense of déjà vu with "Bloody Rose" and "Sangwine" is too strong... Could they also be names given by a senior Transmigrator?
As Ebner pondered, Cattleya the "Hermit" also subtly examined "Temperance," who resembled a doll, and made her guess: Either Sequence 5 or Sequence 6... Also, my previous judgment was correct; she really is from the Temperance faction of the 'Rose School'! These two plants aren't hard to find in the areas ruled by the Indulgence faction. If she were from the Indulgence faction, she wouldn't need to request them at the Tarot Club.
Derrick the "Sun" paused upon hearing Miss Temperance's words, then honestly stated: "The City of Silver has both of these materials... You can exchange them for 'Sun' essential oil and golden bergamot powder."
He had originally intended to say to exchange them for "Luminous Spirit Tree Fruits," the main material for a "Solar High Priest," but after thinking, the prices didn't match, so he switched to auxiliary materials.
"Sun" essential oil and golden bergamot were resources their City of Silver lacked.
"This is not equivalent..." Sharon the "Temperance" didn't want to take advantage. After all, her side's materials were auxiliary materials for a demigod, and even if they were relatively common auxiliary materials—the troublesome ones had all been found by her teacher—they were still much more expensive than things like "Sun" essential oil.
"Normal grain, to make up the difference," Sharon said after some thought.
"What?" "The Sun" was stunned, not reacting, but "The World" immediately "translated": "Miss Temperance means she can provide a batch of our grain to the City of Silver."
"That's great! Thank you, Miss Temperance," Derrick said, full of pleasant surprise after understanding the meaning.
Although the City of Silver had "black-faced grass," its taste couldn't compare to normal food... Moreover, with normal ingredients, perhaps the City of Silver could even reproduce Mr. Fool's Holy Communion.
"The Hermit" glanced at "The World" and "Temperance," feeling that the relationship between these two members, who didn't look alive, must be unusual.
Of course, it could also be a deliberately feigned appearance.
Just as "The Hermit" was guessing wildly, Derrick the "Sun," after finalizing the transaction with Miss Temperance, immediately raised his hand and asked:
"Who among you has 'Luminous Spirit Tree Fruits'?"
"I do," Cattleya the "Hermit" responded, then inquired what "The Sun" could offer, successfully extracting a list of common monsters in the areas around the City of Silver from Derrick.
Another one pulling teeth from an empty wolf... Are people who've spent a long time at sea all so good at shearing sheep? Or perhaps, little "Sun's" posture is just too inviting, making people want to take a shear...
"The Fool" Klein, seeing this scene, instinctively excluded himself from the "pulling teeth from an empty wolf" group.
Cattleya, however, grew more surprised the more she looked at the list. Even though she judged "The Sun" to be at most a Sequence 8, she dared not show any contempt, and finally asked Derrick for historical data of the "City of Silver."
"Mr. Sun comes from the 'Land of Abandoned Gods'," Ebner said with a smile, noticing Cattleya's aura growing heavier. Then, regardless of "Admiral of Stars'" surprise, he looked around and smiled:
"I want to sell the Beyonder characteristics of 'Mysticism Magister' and 'Demoness of Affliction'!"
"Briber" needs to be kept for Fanny, "Guardian" can be sold to Miss Gwen later, "Solar High Priest" and "Reaper" are useful for his future plans... "Telepathist" can be sold to Miss Justice's dog...
So, among the characteristics obtained from the "Saint of Shadows," only "Mysticism Magister" and "Demoness of Affliction" could be sold.

chapters.title: Chapter 806: Miss Justice’s Inquiry
chapters.content:
Chapter 806 - Miss Justice's Inquiry
Two Sequence 5 Beyonder characteristics just put up for sale? Hmm... this should be the remnant of those "herded" by that "Saint of Shadows"...
Cattleya the "Hermit," whose scalp was tingling from the shocking revelation that "The Sun" came from the "Land of Abandoned Gods," couldn't help but feel a subtle sense of empathy, as she herself was only a Sequence 5.
She remained silent for a few seconds before looking at "The Tower" and saying at a deliberate pace:
"I'll take the 'Mysticism Magister' for 10,000 pounds, or 15,000 Fels, or equivalent in gold coins."
She had noticed that previous transactions used Loen pounds, but considering "The Tower" might be an Intis native, she also offered the Intis Fels option.
"Deal," Ebner didn't haggle. With the century-long assets of three "Desire Apostles" under his command, he finally had as much confidence as Miss Justice.
Of course, transferring those three individuals' assets legally and discreetly to his name would still take some time.
"I need a few days to raise the funds, is that alright?" Cattleya the "Hermit" was originally waiting for "The Tower" to raise the price, as she had only offered the base price. Characteristics at the Sequence 5 level often had demand but no supply, so a premium was normal.
But she never expected him to agree to the transaction without hesitation...
Is "The Tower" that great banker from Intis?
Cattleya the "Hermit" couldn't help but make wild guesses.
"That's fine... if no one else bids," Ebner said, glancing around the long table and nodding.
At this moment, Klein, manipulating "The World," spoke in a hoarse voice: "I have a friend who might be interested in the 'Demoness of Affliction' characteristic. Could it be held for a while?"
The "friend" he referred to was Lina, the "Demoness of Pleasure" who had recited "The Fool's" honorific name and was currently living in seclusion with Prince Edessak in Dacey Bay.
According to Klein's plan, the identity of Dwayne Dantès he fabricated for Captain Dunn was, on the surface, a mysterious wealthy man from Dacey Bay who worshipped the Evernight Goddess. He had sold his original land and mines, preparing to seek new opportunities in Backlund, and had some interest in gaining a title through donations, but lacked the substantial financial resources, so he first considered expanding his network and making financial investments.
Klein's current abilities couldn't perfectly fabricate this resume, so he wanted to entrust Lina, a "Demoness" who already had good connections in various places, to complete it.
Although this was "The Fool's" mission, a deity who adhered to "Equivalent Exchange" couldn't go without compensation, and a "Demoness of Affliction" characteristic with a 20% discount was clearly a good reward...
Of course, Klein would also supervise Lina afterward. If she ever did anything out of line for the sake of her role-play, divine punishment would descend.
"A Demoness friend?"
Hearing his words, others immediately turned their heads, instantly recalling the story of the adventurer and "Vice Admiral of Ailment" from last week's Tarot Club...
Apart from Ebner, only Sharon the "Temperance" kept her gaze straight. She had heard the full story from Sherlock beforehand.
As for Ebner, he naturally trusted "The World's" character and vaguely guessed who Klein intended to buy it for, so he nodded and smiled: "I probably won't sell it or craft it into an item within this month."
"Thank you," "The World" Klein ignored the others' probing gazes, appearing completely unconcerned.
Seeing that the transactions between Mr. Tower, Mr. World, and Madam Hermit had been concluded in just a few words, "Justice" Audrey instinctively felt she should also buy something.
In another week or two, I'll contact the "Psychological Alchemists" members in East Chester County, inform them that I've become a "Psychologist," and exchange contributions for subsequent potion formulas. There's no need to request anything here for now... Once I know which materials are needed, I'll ask everyone for help... I can't buy any more magical items for now; one has already been reimbursed... Acquiring such rare items too frequently itself could raise many questions...
But ever since that fortunate day I entered the collective subconscious ocean and met that lady whose face was unclear, I haven't succeeded again... Perhaps I should buy a charm or a one-time item to increase my success rate?
Audrey's thoughts raced, and she formed an idea.
She half-turned her body, looked at "The Tower" across the bronze long table, and said:
"Mr. Tower, do you have a method or item to increase a 'Psychologist's' success rate in entering the collective subconscious ocean?
"For example, a charm or one of your accessories with an eight-month validity period... Hmm, if there's a ritualistic magic or 'secret technique' I can learn, that would also work."
These kinds of things shouldn't cost more than 3,000 pounds; my pocket money will be enough to buy them...
she silently added in her mind.
Although solidifying the "Dream Traversing" ability into a charm or item isn't difficult... for something that helps me role-play as a "Mysticism Magister," a secret technique is naturally the most suitable...
Even if such a secret technique doesn't exist yet, I can "develop" it quickly! After all, possessing the "Bone Dragon," I know the collective subconscious ocean very well.
Thinking this, Ebner deliberated and said, "I can provide a 'secret technique' that can be used with a 'charm'..."
"Okay, how much will your secret technique cost?" "Justice" Audrey asked cheerfully.
"Shouldn't we exchange it for the 'mysticism question' I owe you?" Ebner counter-asked.
"Let's save that question..." "Justice" Audrey smiled elegantly, thinking to herself:
Problems that can be solved with money don't require wasting an opportunity to "ask a question."
"We'll talk about it once you've learned it... And this secret technique needs some adjustments based on your situation... It'll probably be close to the weekend before Mr. Fool can give you the finished product," Ebner replied after some thought.
"No problem." Audrey wasn't in a hurry, as she hadn't yet found any records in local literature about the amnesiac lady in the "cave."
With the completion of this transaction, the palace, like a giant's abode, fell silent for about ten seconds.
Without Mr. Fool's reminder, "Justice," "The Tower," "The Sun," and others knew it was time for free exchange.
Only Madam Hermit remained in observation mode, somewhat perplexed.
"Justice" Audrey looked around, beginning to ponder whether to ask about her previous exploration of the spiritual ocean.
After all, unlike before, there was now Madam Hermit, whose personality she didn't yet understand and wasn't sure if she could trust, which made her hesitate.
After a brief deliberation, she still spoke:
"I've recently been tracing the movements of a Mind Dragon and went to a place with a custom of worshipping dragons."
She omitted the specific location and details that might reveal her identity, only describing her exploration process in detail and specifically mentioning the black-haired lady with an unclear face whom she met in the final crystal cave.
"She told me she was waiting for 'Fortune'..."

chapters.title: Chapter 807: The Joyful Deviant in the Tarot Club
chapters.content:
Chapter 807 - The Joyful Deviant in the Tarot Club
There's actually a 'person' who can live in the Collective Subconscious Ocean? What a miraculous and beautiful journey! Although Miss Justice didn't encounter any enemies or dangers, just thinking about that lady lost in the crystal cave, who knows how many years she's stayed there, just waiting for so-called 'Fortune' to return, suggests it must be a poignant, romantic, and perhaps even heartbreaking story...
Listening to Miss Justice's dream travelogue, Fors the "Magician" had one thought after another flash through her mind.
On the other side, having finished her narration, Audrey the "Justice" looked around and continuously inquired:
"Ladies and gentlemen, do you have any suggestions? Who do you think that lady I encountered truly is?
"Also, could the Dragon's 'City of Miracles,' Liveseyd, also be hidden within this Collective Subconscious Ocean?
"If I want to continue exploring, what should I be aware of? What should I prepare beforehand?"
Alger the "Hanged Man" glanced at "The Hermit," then pondered and said:
"I don't think you should continue exploring.
"This is a very dangerous endeavor.
"The lady you saw, if she can exist stably in the Collective Subconscious Ocean, and despite losing her memory, her mind is clear... that indicates she possesses sufficiently high power, perhaps even reaching the demigod level.
"Even if you obtain the secret technique for traversing the Collective Subconscious Ocean from Mr. Tower, do not attempt it rashly."
Cattleya the "Hermit" also nodded and said:
"In the Collective Subconscious Ocean, there are many dangerous things. The accumulated malice of humanity, various desires that corrode spiritual bodies, and terrifying memories from ancient times are like storms and waves on a real ocean, which can cause severe psychological trauma, or even prevent you from ever waking up.
"Moreover, that is the Collective Subconscious Ocean of all living beings, not just humans. Perhaps certain evil spirits, certain evil gods, or the consciousness of certain terrifying existences also lurk there, like giant whirlpools capable of devouring ships.
"Do not attempt a deep exploration rashly until you truly gain the Beyonder ability to walk within the Collective Subconscious Ocean.
"Finally, I believe the lady you mentioned might be more dangerous than you imagine... The title 'Fortune' might be an alias for an Angel or an ancient god..."
Audrey the "Justice," filled with anticipation, felt a wave of disappointment, yet had to admit that Mr. Hanged Man and Madam Hermit's words were very reasonable and sincere.
She silently took a breath, then looked expectantly at Mr. Tower and Mr. World, hoping they could offer more advice.
Don't look at me... I don't understand!
Klein tried his best not to let his eyes waver.
His understanding of the conscious, subconscious, and collective subconscious still relied on the theory described by "Spirit Medium" Daly, at most some common knowledge Mr. Tower had provided during their previous exploration of
Groselle's Travels
.
If you were to ask about someone invading a dream, then I'd be a professional...
Klein inwardly scoffed, but outwardly, he manipulated "The World's" hoarse voice: "I can only tell you that although the 'City of Miracles,' Liveseyd, is in the subconscious ocean... its location is quite unique."
Speaking of which, Klein wasn't without speculation regarding the identity of the lady Miss Justice mentioned. After all, he had seen the murals in the Elf Trial Temple displayed by "The Tower," and knew that before the Elf Royal Court was breached, the "Queen of Calamity" and the "God of Fortune" had broken through and escaped...
If "Fortune" refers to the "God of Fortune"... then the lady Miss Justice met might be Cohinem the "Queen of Calamity"...
Did that Elf Queen, after severing ties with the "Book of Calamity," hide in the Collective Subconscious Ocean? Is she trying to evade someone? Or was she placed there by someone?
As Klein pondered, "The Hermit," "The Hanged Man," "Justice," and others were startled by the implication of his words and couldn't help but look over.
"The World's" tone was very certain...
Does he know where the "City of Miracles," Livishead, is? Has he even been there? That makes sense, he's Mr. Fool's Blessed... And "The Fool" is a revived ancient god, perhaps very familiar with "Dragons."
"The Hermit" once again raised her "assessment" of "The World" and guessed which faction he belonged to... And from his special seating, his special code name, she vaguely felt he must be connected to "The Fool"... especially "The Hanged Man's" unconscious glance at the head of the table just now, which also revealed something.
Audrey the "Justice," after reacting, had her eyes light up. However, she saw that the other party seemed to have no intention of continuing and had specifically emphasized that he "only" could tell her this much, so she held back her question.
Perhaps it's because I'm not yet qualified to know... I need to advance my Sequence quickly!
Audrey silently took a breath.
At this moment, Ebner also returned from his contemplation. Upon hearing that the lady was waiting for "Fortune," he had a similar guess to Klein.
However, Cohinem was actually split into two parts... The part in the "Book of Calamity" was peeled off by Roselle in his later years and hidden to threaten me...
Although I still don't know why I would be threatened...
If Miss Justice truly encountered Cohinem's soul, I wonder if it was the part from the "Book of Calamity" or the part that escaped from the Golden Goblet...
Thinking this, and recalling Lilith's task to find something Cohinem had taken from the "Book of Calamity," he pondered for a moment before asking Audrey, who was currently encouraging herself:
"Miss Justice, I'm very interested in the lady you saw in your dream. I wonder if you would allow me to accompany you on your next exploration?"
Mr. Tower
is interested? Oh... if he accompanies me, then safety will be assured... I just need to check some local records again to start exploring...
But if I do that, my identity will be exposed...
Just as Audrey was struggling with her decision, Ebner seemed to guess her thoughts and chuckled: "Miss Justice, you don't have to rush your decision... Once I've perfected the 'secret technique' I'm developing for you, I'll personally visit you... You can decide then whether or not to accept my request."
Visit me personally... He... he knows who I am? That's right, Mr. Tower is very likely Ebner Brain! And that 'charming detective' has a very good relationship with Fors... Some of my disguises might work in front of Fors and Xio, but in the eyes of that famous detective, there are probably many flaws...
Especially since I also bought a "Roselle's Manuscript" from Xio, and commissioned Xio and Fors to investigate "Vice Admiral Hurricane"!
Fors even suspected I was Audrey, let alone Mr. Tower, who joined the Tarot Club much earlier... He probably confirmed my identity after the "Vice Admiral Hurricane" incident...
I should have thought of this sooner!
Audrey felt both a sense of relief and annoyance at her previous "immaturity."
Annoyed at her carelessness and lack of caution, yet relieved that Mr. Tower was ultimately one of their own, and despite some unsavory rumors, he would ultimately pose no threat to her.
Since her background was already exposed, "Justice" Audrey no longer acted coyly and said generously: "I look forward to your visit, Mr. Tower..."
She paused here, then added, "Preferably on Saturday evening."
During the day, there were too many people, and Friday and Sunday evenings had banquets and balls, so only Saturday evening was most suitable.
"No problem," Ebner responded with a smile, then glanced at Miss Judgment across the table, silently asking if she wanted to join.
After all, Xio had also fallen into a strange dream when she was in East Chester County, and this matter might be related to her as well.
Xio thought for a moment but shook her head, indicating that she had many cases recently and couldn't spare the time.
Besides, I'm only Sequence 6; I would only be an extra burden for Ebner... The top priority is to actively role-play as a "Judge" and 'digest' the potion as soon as possible!
Xio inwardly sighed.
After this topic concluded, Alger the "Hanged Man" shared the news of Kavituva's fall, emphasizing that the "Sea God's" final remnants were taken by a Beyonder suspected to be a "Demoness"... And afterward, the "Sea God's" believers heard new oracles.
Cattleya the "Hermit" immediately connected this to the staff she saw beside "The Fool" when she first came above the gray fog... And with this, she confirmed that "The World" was indeed "The Fool's" Blessed!
And the "friend" he mentioned earlier who needed the "Demoness of Affliction" characteristic must be the "Demoness" who helped "The Fool" retrieve the staff... She might be a Blessed as well, just like "The World"!
And because of Cattleya's instinctive head tilt, "The Hanged Man" and "Justice" also made similar guesses and judgments to "The Hermit."
Klein remained silent throughout, letting everyone draw their own conclusions, but he specifically observed Mr. Tower and found that he was indeed "amused" again...
This guy is always watching the fun at the Tarot Club! Now that I think about it, in previous Tarot Club meetings, he even dared to watch Mr. Fool's 'fun'... Is he confident that "The Fool" can't do anything to him?
Then, recalling one of their daily "chats" that began after the cards were laid out that day, he remembered asking Ebner how much he knew about "The Fool," and Ebner's counter-question: "Isn't 'The King of Yellow and Black who wields good luck' just 'The Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth'?"
Could The Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth truly be an ancient god? Has Lilith or some other goddess told "The Tower" about related knowledge?
While he was thinking, "The Moon" and "The Sun's" daily "clash" had also finished. This time, Emlyn the "Moon," having specifically found the history of the City of Silver and learned that the Giant Queen "Harvest Goddess's" true name was "Omibella," finally won the victory... After all, the City of Silver's records coincidentally lacked this goddess's name.
After receiving confirmation from Miss Hermit, Derrick glanced at Mr. Moon, and feeling his smugness, immediately turned his head away.
I won't let this arrogant, boastful, and strangely-flavored Vampire see my frustration!
he thought glumly.
Emlyn the "Moon," seeing this, felt utterly content, a sense of pleasure rising from deep within him.
Another one "amused" at the gathering!
Klein had just mumbled, then heard Madam Hermit ask contemplatively:
"Last week's blood moon seemed to symbolize a major event capable of affecting the world... but I haven't heard of any abnormalities occurring anywhere...
"Does anyone here know anything?"
I know, I know! Mr. Fool told me! The Original Moon fell...
Fors the "Magician" almost raised her hand to blurt out the answer.
But before she could act, everyone heard the distant, lofty figure within the gray fog chuckle:
"The 'Original Moon' fell into the Bloodline Progenitor's trap...
"Lilith has taken another step closer to complete revival."
Klein had previously confirmed with "The Tower" in their conversation that Goddess Lilith didn't mind this matter being spread, which is why he had "The Fool" state it directly.

chapters.title: Chapter 808: The Small Meeting After the Main One
chapters.content:
Chapter 808 - The Small Meeting After the Main One
The "Primordial Moon" fell into a trap? The Sanguine Ancestor revived? Mr. Fool and the ancient god Lilith are allies? No wonder there's a Vampire in the Tarot Club...
Then who could "The Fool" be? An ancient god from the Second Epoch? Is He the King of Elves, or the King of Giants? He seems to have just reclaimed the "Sea God" authority lost by the Elf Queen... Could it be the former?
Cattleya the "Hermit," who had braced herself for no response after asking the question, never expected Mr. Fool to personally provide an answer, and one so shocking that her thoughts were momentarily in disarray.
Alger the "Hanged Man," already prone to overthinking, was in a similar state. He had long guessed that Mr. Fool might have an alliance with ancient gods like the Sanguine Ancestor, who were also in the process of recovery, but he never imagined Their states would recover so quickly.
"So that's it... No wonder 'The Fool' would send Gehrman to seize the 'Sea God's' authority for Him... It must have been in preparation to help Lilith revive!
"Hmm, Mr. Fool told us about the evil god 'Primordial Moon' a long time ago. At that time, I thought He was just mentioning it casually...
"Now that I think about it, perhaps 'The Fool' had already made contact and established an understanding with the ancient god Lilith back then?
"The machinations of deities are truly unpredictable beforehand, it's terrifying!
"However, since Lilith has advanced a step further on the path to complete revival, what about Mr. Fool? What benefits did He gain from this incident?"
Unconsciously, Alger the "Hanged Man" turned his body, looking towards the head of the bronze long table.
He didn't dare look directly, only focusing on the edges.
With a glance, Alger saw two additional "Blasphemy Cards," and inwardly sighed with emotion:
Indeed, in the matter where "The Fool" cooperated with Lilith to plot against the evil god "Primordial Moon," one of them reclaimed a portion of the Moon's authority, moving closer to complete revival, while the other seized many benefits, including the "Blasphemy Cards," perhaps even recovering some power through it...
At this moment, seeing "The Hanged Man" turn, "Justice" Audrey, "Moon" Emlyn, and others also recovered from their bewildered states, all becoming alert, forming similar conjectures to Alger.
Especially "Moon" Emlyn, the excitement on his face was already overflowing. He even proudly speculated in his mind: Perhaps it's precisely because I joined the "Tarot Club" that the Sanguine Ancestor and Mr. Fool established a stable alliance, thereby aiding the Ancestor's revival... I am indeed the most special Vampire, the one most valued by the Ancestor!
As everyone was either in a daze or deep in thought, "The World" Gehrman glanced at "The Tower." After the latter subtly nodded, he carefully stated:
"'Primordial Moon' is an avatar of a powerful evil god... Although this avatar's authority has been reclaimed by the Sanguine Ancestor, the evil god's true body still exists, so be especially careful when encountering 'Primordial Moon' believers in the future."
This was information Klein had obtained from his daily interactions with Ebner. Although the latter didn't tell him which evil god it was, it didn't prevent him from offering a warning.
Before everyone could react, Ebner looked around and then at Emlyn, adding gravely: "You just need to know this; don't tell anyone else... especially 'The Moon.' Even your clan elders must be kept in the dark for now."
Although Lilith wasn't worried about her revival becoming known, Ebner didn't want the news to spread too widely, lest it genuinely create a conflict between the "Mother Earth" and the ancient god Lilith, putting those Vampires who joined the Earth Church in a difficult position.
Crucially, this dilemma was essentially a false dilemma... It would be bad if a tragedy resulted from it during this period.
"Yes, I understand!" Emlyn was first startled, then solemnly assured him.
In his opinion, such a significant piece of news as the Sanguine Ancestor's revival should be kept secret to prevent enemies from noticing.
Alger the "Hanged Man" pondered "The World's" and "The Tower's" words, his expression subtly changing to one of curiosity as he tentatively asked:
"You two seem to have been involved in this matter?"
Soon after he spoke, he saw "The Tower" stand and bow to "The Fool," then exchange glances with "The World" and "Temperance," seemingly seeking their opinion. Once they both nodded, he casually stated:
"I, 'The World,' and Miss Temperance witnessed the fall of the 'Primordial Moon.'"
The three of them are already powerful enough to participate in battles between deities? No... perhaps it's not just deities clashing, but their respective Blessed are also fighting!
Alger the "Hanged Man" thought of many things at once, feeling somewhat put out.
After all, as an elder member of the Tarot Club, he could only hear about such a major event afterward...
While "The Tower," "The World," and "Temperance" could directly participate!
Is it because I'm only Sequence 6, too weak?
Alger the "Hanged Man" felt disheartened but also somewhat fortunate.
Fortunate that Mr. Fool was indeed a benevolent deity, who didn't forcibly summon members of insufficient strength like him to participate in battles...
Just seeing the "Black Knight" characteristic "The Tower" offered was enough to know how perilous the situation was!
If I had also been forced to participate, I probably wouldn't have come back...
Alger sighed. He wasn't surprised that the "True Creator" might have also had a hand in this, as Mr. Fool had disrupted the "True Creator's" descent several times; it was only normal for the other party to send people to cause trouble.
"Saint of Shadows'" characteristic...
So the "True Creator" was also involved in this divine-level conflict?
On the other side, Cattleya the "Hermit" immediately connected this to the characteristic "The Tower" had previously handed over. She then recalled that the "Aurora Order" was the first organization to spread "The Fool's" honorific name, and nodded with a sense of understanding:
As Mr. Fool's enemy, even if the "True Creator" also harbored animosity towards the "Primordial Moon," He wouldn't easily allow the Sanguine Ancestor's and "The Fool's" plan to succeed.
I just wonder if any other deities also interfered... So the "secret event" I glimpsed in the "Blood Moon" was actually so far-reaching! It truly was an event capable of affecting the world!
—As an "Astrologer," she could glimpse certain hidden knowledge from celestial anomalies.
At this point, as "The World" and "The Tower" fell silent, everyone tacitly moved past the topic. After all, it involved deities and far exceeded the scope of "exchange."
Even though "The Hermit," "The Hanged Man," "Justice," and others were eager to know the details of this matter, they all suppressed their curiosity and didn't press further.
As for Miss Judgment, she felt she could privately ask Ebner. If it was something she was allowed to know, he certainly wouldn't be stingy.
After everyone discussed for a while longer, the Tarot Club drew to a close. Klein smiled slightly:
"Everyone, see you next week."
"As you command," "Justice" Audrey immediately rose and bowed.
The others were not much slower, including Cattleya the "Hermit."
Next, as streaks of red light engulfed the Tarot Club members, Ebner was surprised to find that he hadn't returned to reality. Instead, he and "The World" remained in the ancient palace.
He couldn't help but look at Mr. Fool at the head of the table, who had somehow conjured the "Book of Calamity" and chuckled:
"Madam Yarolam of the 'Moses Ascetic Order' requested that I pass this book to you... Liu Bo."

chapters.title: Chapter 809: Klein’s Plan
chapters.content:
Chapter 809 - Klein's Plan
Zhou Mingrui, seriously, can you stop being so cheeky? Will you only be satisfied once I've ripped off your disguise?
Ebner grumbled inwardly, then pondered the meaning behind those words.
Yalolan asked you to hand over the Book of Calamity to me?
He remembered that this pillar of the Moses Ascetic Order and the blood clan duke, Rhine Kalendia, had some kind of connection with that transmigrator senior...
Could this be part of that senior's plan?
But that senior should be truly dead. After all, his body was used by Lilith to ascend to become the Goddess of Beauty.
Hmm... Could it be that Yalolan knows I possess the Pure White Eye and is investing early?
As his thoughts spun, Mr. Fool casually mentioned that Yalolan was already a "He," and that his current condition seemed rather poor.
Not doing well... Does He need my help—or rather, help from the Unknown Land behind the Pure White Eye? Is that the real reason for handing me the Book of Calamity?
Maybe it's not that simple... But with my current understanding and control over the Pure White Eye, I have no idea how to use this book. Most likely, I can't help Him solve anything...
Quoting Roselle,
"You're too early!"
With a sigh, Ebner got up and expressed his thanks, but didn't try to take the book beside Mr. Fool. After all, he was currently in spiritual form and couldn't take it with him anyway...
Mr. Fool glanced at him calmly, then teleported several pages of parchment in front of the World before fading from view.
The World, seated at the end of the table, also rose to respectfully send off Mr. Fool. Only after that did he laugh hoarsely and ask, "You're not planning to meet with that Lady Yalolan?"
That might very well be your old flame... You just don't remember right now,
Klein added silently.
You really can act... No wonder you're digesting Faceless so fast,
Ebner muttered, then shook his head and replied, "Before becoming a demigod, I don't plan to contact Him."
Of course, if He really can't wait, they could always meet at the Church of the Earth Mother... But from the way Klein spoke just now, even though something had gone wrong, it didn't seem urgent.
Klein's heart stirred when he heard this. He guessed that Liu Bo's "cheat" might be similar to that light gate above the gray fog, requiring demigod-level power to activate...
"If you need to contact Him, come find me. I have a way to summon His messenger." Klein nodded, then handed the parchment to him. "Take a look at this."
Ebner took it curiously, glanced over it, and immediately realized it was the diary Audrey and Xio had just submitted.
Lady Julia of the Delien family might be an MI9 agent, and she got the Hunter potion formula from Roselle?
After reading the content on the parchment, Ebner's expression turned a bit odd, because from what he knew, the Delien family's current Hunter-path demigod—who had been around for over a hundred years—was named "Julia"...
Did Roselle start going off the rails in his later years?
Noticing the change in the Tower's mood, Klein asked in surprise, "What is it?"
Ebner placed the diary face-down on the table and said meaningfully, "According to the information I've gathered, the Delien family's Hunter demigod only advanced thanks to the potion formula and ingredients Roselle provided... and that demigod's name is Julia."
"You mean... Roselle turned his lover into a...?" Klein had joked maliciously about this before, but now it seemed Old Huang was even more open-minded than he thought!
As they spoke, the two exchanged a glance. Though their faces were hard to discern, they could both see the teasing smile on the other's expression.
When it came to laughing at Roselle's misfortunes, their attitudes were perfectly aligned...
A dozen seconds later, Ebner cleared his throat and asked, "Letting me read the diary so kindly... is there something you want me to help with?"
"After all, no matter how special you are to Mr. Fool, trading for a diary must still come at a price, right?"
The price is just the future embarrassment when your disguise is blown...
Klein mocked himself internally, but on the surface, he carefully explained the situation with Tracy and added parts of the reports from the Church of the Sea God's believers before finally asking:
"What do you Sugges?"
"Suggestions? Heh, how about learning from the emperor and developing a relationship with this witch? After all,
'a witch's taste is truly wonderful!'
" Ebner retorted.
"You've read that diary too, huh..." Klein couldn't help but curl the corners of his mouth, then shook his head. "But seriously, stop joking like that..."
"I get it, you're worried Miss Sharon might misunderstand." Ebner winked at him teasingly.
Klein rubbed his forehead. Now he finally understood what Roselle meant in his diary about his "troublesome friends." Mr. Tower usually acted so proper, but when he let loose, he really didn't hold back...
Maybe it's precisely this personality that drew the favor of so many goddesses throughout his many lives?
Letting out a helpless sigh, Klein, not realizing how much more at ease he now felt, began to explain his plan:
"Though I haven't met her yet, I suspect Trissy's condition must be quite bad. She'll need time to recover...
"And I still need to investigate the 'Celestial Sect' and continue my 'acting.' I can't take her along...
"Besides, she's being hunted by multiple factions on the sea. Keeping her by my side would be both dangerous and inconvenient.
"So, can you take her somewhere safe and settle her there?"
After hearing him out, Ebner didn't ask about the Vice Admiral of Ailment but instead asked thoughtfully, "Are you planning to impersonate a member of the Celestial Sect?"
Klein was surprised that Ebner understood him so well—he could guess his general plan from just a few words—but he didn't dwell on it. He nodded and replied, "Or maybe one of Trissy's mother's subordinates... In any case, I want to investigate them thoroughly while also continuing to 'act' as a Faceless."
That was a lie. His real plan was to impersonate Trissy, pretending to have been captured by members of the Celestial Sect, then infiltrate their ranks. The moment he heard that the people from the Celestial Sect were also looking for Trissy, this idea had come to him.
But that kind of thing didn't need to be shared with Mr. Tower.
"You need to be careful... The evil god behind the Celestial Sect is roughly on par with the one behind the 'Primordial Moon'... Although, right now, He doesn't seem capable of investing much power into the Rorsted Archipelago," Ebner warned.
"Don't worry. I know what I'm doing." Klein could feel the concern in Ebner's words, and his heart warmed slightly, though he maintained a confident front.
After all, with the Sea God's Scepter and the Error card, he already had some demi-god-level abilities. If needed, he could also write to Lady Yaloran or summon Miss Messenger as backup.
Especially the latter—she was Sharon's teacher, and after learning that Klein had obtained the Puppeteer characteristic for Sharon, she had agreed to be his "hired muscle," even offering a 50% discount.
Besides, a Magician never performed without preparation... Until his plan was perfected, he wouldn't take risks lightly.
"You'd best find a way to get Mr. Fool to grant you the Black Knight's characteristic. Once Creeping Hunger upgrades with it, then you can begin your infiltration," Ebner suggested after thinking it over.
"I'll consider it." Klein nodded slightly.
Only then did Ebner begin to consider how to arrange for Trissy. He thought to himself:
I'll be returning to Tosk soon to attend the Valerian family's masquerade with Helene. Maybe I can ask for her opinion...
Helene had always feared being recaptured and brought back to the Black Death, but her feelings toward Trissy were rather complicated—not entirely negative...
With that in mind, Ebner said to Klein, "I need to consult someone. If she agrees, I'll go pick Trissy up... If she's unwilling, then you'll have to figure something out yourself."
Her? Don't tell me Liu Bo and Trissy are love rivals?
Klein gave Ebner a few odd looks, then nodded. "Alright."
Just as they finalized the matter, Klein noticed the Hermit's crimson star contracting and expanding violently. Taking the opportunity, he bid farewell to Mr. Tower and severed the connection.
After receiving the offering from the Hermit—the Glorious Contract Spirit Tree's fruit meant to be exchanged with the Sun—the Fool, seated at the head of the table, finally looked toward the World seated across and asked:
"What do you think Liu Bo really knows about us?"
The World replied in a hoarse voice, "It seems like you, Mr. Fool, haven't been exposed... but I can't be sure..."
The Fool tapped his finger on the edge of the long table. After pondering briefly, he sighed and said, "Forget it. Let's just assume he still thinks I'm the Celestial Worthy...
"But then... who exactly is the real Celestial Worthy, and where is He now?"
...(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 810: Danitz’s Fear
chapters.content:
Chapter 810 - Danitz’s Fear
In Trier, within a small villa provided by the golf club for gold card clients.
After offering the Black Knight's Beyonder characteristic to Mr. Fool, Ebner received a roll of yellow-brown parchment.
He didn't open it right away, since the book contained the Beyonder characteristic of Cohinem and was at the angel level. If it made any commotion, it would be difficult to deal with should the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun be drawn over.
After thinking briefly, he extended his spirituality to the gold-rimmed glasses and spent some money in "Alvin's Question Labyrinth" to open a "storage room," placing the
Book of Calamity
inside.
After that, he tidied up the ritual items and altar in the room. Just as he finished and was putting on his coat with the help of "Chelsia" controlled by the magic mirror, ready to head out, there came a knock at the bedroom door.
Opening it, he unsurprisingly found Fors standing outside.
She was wearing a newly bought pale yellow dress, holding a novel in one hand and a cup of coffee in the other. Seeing Ebner fully dressed, she asked in surprise, "Ebner, are you going out?"
"Yes. You know, I promised Helene I'd attend the masquerade," Ebner replied with a smile.
"You're not teleporting there directly?" Fors asked in surprise.
Since they had known each other for a long time and were quite familiar, she more or less understood the extent of Ebner's capabilities.
"I'll be staying in Trier for a while, so I need to set up a more stable altar for long-distance teleportation," Ebner said as he stepped outside the small villa with Chelsia.
Fors followed him all the way to the front gate before asking again, "When will we be able to retrieve what Mr. Trun left in the bank's safe deposit box?"
Ebner turned back, recalling the newspaper he saw on the train, and said cautiously, "There's no need to rush with that... If we go to the First Bank rashly, not only might we fail to retrieve it, but we could also draw unnecessary trouble.
"You have to understand, although the First Bank's safe deposit box service is claimed to be the most secure and convenient way to store valuables, it's not without its filth.
"If a tycoon comes to retrieve their belongings, sure, no problem. But for people like us, newcomers to Trier, trying to withdraw an 'inheritance' from the First Bank's safe isn't so easy!
"There are all kinds of procedures starting from just the 'appointment'... and we might get targeted by gangs or other forces trying to seize the legacy.
"One opposition newspaper recently reported a similar case...
"Even if we're not afraid of them, handling the aftermath would still be troublesome!
"So, let me get my assets in order first, then find a lawyer, broker, and business agent. Only then will we go to the First Bank."
Though lazy about certain things, Fors wasn't lacking in worldly experience. She quickly understood and nodded, but couldn't help but grumble, "Trier used to be known as the 'financial capital,' so how did it end up like this? The bank's service is so much worse than in Backlund..."
In fact, Trier's financial industry hadn't always been so chaotic. Back in Roselle the Great's time, it
was
worthy of being called a "financial capital"...
But now, many of Roselle's regulations had been abolished, and with political strife bleeding into the financial system, the loopholes had only grown worse.
With that in mind, Ebner didn't offer further explanation. After bidding farewell to Fors, he got into the club's carriage with Chelsia and headed for the outskirts of the Semburg District.
Semburg was located on the left bank of the Serence River. Named after the ancient Semburg Castle, it was one of the most expensive areas in all of Trier. Its residents were typically famous artists, opera stars, top executives of major corporations, and newly wealthy individuals.
That ancient castle, standing since the early Fourth Epoch and weathering thousands of years, had recently been purchased by the Dorian family and converted into the Semburg Museum.
The Dorian family's current manor was located just outside the Semburg District, not far from the museum.
But Ebner wasn't heading there for them—he was going to a small estate in the same area, formerly owned by Herta, the "Mirror Apostle" who had "donated" all her assets to him.
Seated in the carriage, Ebner's facial features slowly shifted, eventually transforming into the face of a portly man in his mid-thirties.
This wasn't Herta's face but that of the identity she used in Intis—a disguise under the name "Lucen Semb," a financial tycoon.
The carriage soon stopped before an estate with a vineyard. In the form of Lucen Semb, Ebner entered the main building with Chelsia in tow—it was a four-story Intis-style house.
This place is way smaller than Fragrant Manor... and that so-called fourth floor is barely tall enough to use as storage...
Ebner curled his lip inwardly. Still, it was free, so he couldn't complain too much.
Most of the estate's servants were ordinary people. Only the steward and personal valet left behind were Beyonders—one a "Criminal," the other a "Planter," both at Sequence 9—and both were swiftly mind-controlled by the magic mirror.
After a brief interrogation, Ebner learned that the "Criminal" steward was a trusted subordinate trained by Mirror Apostle Herta, tasked with overseeing her properties in Trier.
Despite only being Sequence 9, this man had, over the years, driven more than twenty people to death through coercion and manipulation. He was a complete beast in human clothing.
In Ebner's eyes, that man had already been sentenced to "death." Once Herta's properties had all been gradually transferred under his name, he would deal with him.
As for the other "Planter," Hagel, although also trained by Herta, he had only been tasked with managing the vineyard and cultivating some "rare" grape varieties. He hadn't done anything vile.
For this man, Ebner planned to find an opportunity to take him to the Church of the Earth Mother to convert him, then use "Suggestion" to make him forget any favors he had received from Herta and continue working for him.
Since he had to attend a masquerade ball in Tosk that evening, Ebner didn't have time to explore "Ancient Vine Manor" in depth for now. After having Chelsia take control of everyone's minds in the estate, he went to the basement to set up a teleportation altar.
.....
Southern Rorsted Archipelago, Lans Island.
After returning to reality, Klein called over Danitz, who was just about to go drinking, and told him to carry a suitcase and follow him.
Although Danitz had no idea where this lunatic was going, since the captain had instructed him to follow the man for the time being, he resigned himself to the hard work of playing the "manservant."
After leaving the inn, Klein briskly walked through the port town that held no more than a thousand residents, then hiked to the edge of an uninhabited cliff on the other side of the island.
Staring down at the waves crashing endlessly against the rocky wall, Danitz looked around in confusion.
"This is our destination?"
Klein, still keeping up his Gehrman persona, ignored the question.
Instead, he first prayed to himself, then went above the gray fog and used the "Sea God Scepter" to summon a suitable nearby deep-sea creature.
Once he judged that the summoned sea monster was close, Klein pulled out a charm made of white tin and softly chanted the incantation for "Storm," activating powers like "Underwater Breathing" and "Deep Sea Water Membrane."
Half was applied to himself, and the other half to Danitz.
At that moment, a great splash erupted from below the cliff, and a massive creature resembling a whale surfaced from the ocean.
It was black-gray all over, its jaws suddenly gaping open to reveal rows of sharp white teeth and a bloody maw.
Klein stepped to the edge of the cliff, grabbed Danitz by the arm, and jumped down with him.
With the aid of the charm's power, they floated gently into the mouth of the enormous sea creature.
"Ahhhhhhhh!"
It wasn't until the monster had completely closed its mouth that Danitz belatedly screamed.
"Shut up!" Klein barked in his Gehrman tone, even as he marveled at how long Danitz's mental reaction took.
In the darkness, Danitz silenced himself, then was about to strike a fire for light—but he immediately remembered they were inside a sea monster's body and gave up. Trying to make conversation instead, he asked, "Where are we going?"
Klein didn't answer directly but countered, "Are you afraid of heights?"
"Who—me? I'm not afraid of heights! Anyone would scream if they fell from that high!" Danitz forgot his own question and snapped back.
"Hmm, so the symptoms aren't obvious..." Klein said solemnly.
This lunatic really can't understand normal conversation!
Danitz grumbled internally and chose not to argue further.
What he didn't see was Klein stroking his chin thoughtfully, a look of slight disappointment on his face.
Although there's some effect, this method of constructing an identity and slowly gaining recognition is too slow...
Similarly, truly playing a person for several years until everyone connected to that identity fully accepts it, to the point even I believe I am that person... it's time-consuming, more morally challenging, and even more twisted and maddening...
Sigh... to speed up the process, I'll have to overcome certain barriers—psychological barriers!
The role of "Faceless Man" may look simple on the outside, but the real key lies in the heart!
Who knew how much time had passed before the sea monster rose to the surface again. Ahead was a deserted island.
Using the power of the charm, Klein stepped onto the island, removed his hat, and bowed to the sea creature.
This startled Danitz, who grew increasingly worried about the lunatic's mental state.
After watching the enormous ocean creature leave, Klein led Danitz to a cave on the island.
Via "divine revelation," Klein had already instructed the fishermen who discovered Tracy to leave, leaving only a shovel standing beside the cave.
Gazing at the clearly filled-in soil, Klein pointed at the shovel and said to Danitz:
"Dig it up."
Having hunted for treasure with the captain for years, Danitz was no stranger to this kind of setup. Without any questions, he grabbed the shovel and got to work.
What kind of treasure could it be? This lunatic may be mad, but he's always generous... maybe I'll get a cut of whatever's inside?
Just as that thought crossed his mind, the shovel struck something hard—a massive crystal that looked extremely valuable at first glance!
Danitz's spirits lifted, and he dug even faster. Because the fishermen hadn't compacted the soil much, he quickly unearthed the entire chunk of crystal.
And within the crystal was the figure of "Vice Admiral of Ailment" Tracy, wearing nothing but a thin coat.
This... how are we supposed to split
this
? Danitz was stunned, his mind immediately spiraling into wild speculation:
That's... Tracy?! Did this lunatic bury a pirate admiral here?
What's he trying to do? Plant one Tracy to grow a bunch of Vice Admirals of Ailment?
But since she hasn't sprouted... will he bury me next?
The pit's already been dug for me...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 811: Tracy and Helene
chapters.content:
Chapter 811 - Tracy and Helene
Klein examined the "crystal" encasing Tracy, swiftly unclasped the citrine pendant from his left wrist, and performed a divination in a voice barely audible to himself:
"Forcibly removing the crystal around Tracy is dangerous."
After silently chanting seven times, Klein opened his eyes to see the citrine pendant spinning counter-clockwise.
This indicated that the crystal Tracy used to seal herself was purely for protection and had no offensive properties...
Thinking this, Klein caused "Creeping Hunger" to turn pale, moved his butterfly muscles on his back, and flung his arms wide before rapidly bringing them together, striking the "crystal" from both sides with the power of a "Zombie."
"Thud!"
With a dull thud, the "crystal" around Tracy's body remained unchanged. Instead, it was Klein who unnaturally shook his arms.
So hard! If I hadn't switched to my "Zombie" state, that hit would've surely broken my bones... But then again, if I didn't have the "Zombie's" strength, I wouldn't have even tried...
Klein secretly mused for a few moments, then slowly turned his head, glancing at Danitz.
The great pirate, whose bounty had already risen to 4,500 gold pounds, immediately dropped his amused expression and straightened his face, as if he hadn't seen anything.
"Use fire on it," Klein instructed him.
"What?" Danitz didn't react for a moment, looking bewildered.
"Use fire on that crystal," Klein repeated expressionlessly.
"Oh... no problem," Danitz's face showed understanding, and he conjured flames in his palm.
But just as he was about to throw the fireball, the corner of his eye suddenly lost sight of Gehrman.
Danitz turned back in astonishment, realizing that the powerful and insane adventurer had flashed ten meters away in just a few seconds.
Seeing this, Danitz asked dumbfounded, "You, why are you hiding so far away?"
"There might be danger," Klein said in a low voice, suppressing a smile.
That's for laughing at me just now; it's an equivalent punishment... After all, I'm a "Fool" who adheres to "equivalence."
He silently added in his mind."Didn't you just divine it?" Danitz squeezed out a smile and asked.
Klein replied solemnly, "Attacking the 'crystal' isn't dangerous, but that doesn't mean it won't be after it breaks..." As he spoke, he glanced at Tracy, whose eyes were tightly closed within the crystal, and added, "Besides, she's 'Vice Admiral of Ailment'!"
He deliberately emphasized the word "Ailment."
Upon hearing this, even though it was winter, Danitz felt cold sweat dripping from his forehead. He thought for a moment, then also ran back a dozen meters, simultaneously dispersing the "fireball" in his hand and changing it to "fire crows."
Quite clever!
Klein watched his actions, a faint curve to his lips.
What he didn't tell Danitz was that even if Tracy had set up "ailments" within the crystal, it wouldn't make someone gravely ill so quickly. As long as one promptly exited the range of her "ailments," there wouldn't be much of a problem.
—This was experience gained from the battle with Mr. A.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
One after another, orange-yellow fire crows, once condensed, circled and flew out, striking the "crystal" one after another.
But as the smoke from the explosions dissipated, the crystals remained completely undamaged, as smooth as new.
Seeing this, Danitz looked at Gehrman with slight nervousness, then spread his hands, indicating he was powerless.
Klein nodded slightly, calmly stating, "It seems powers below Demigod-level will have difficulty breaking through..."
Perhaps my "Burial Blade" could forcibly break it, but firstly, this weapon crafted by Mr. Tower burns money with each use, and secondly, it might destroy Tracy's protective item, which would be a net loss.
After all, in his plan, this magical item also had a significant role.
He thought for a moment, then specifically observed Tracy in the crystal, noticing that apart from her damaged jacket, she only had a bracelet on her right wrist...
That must be it!
Klein thought, and without avoiding Danitz, he constructed a spiritual wall in front of him, set up the ritual, and summoned his own spirit body.
The spirit body seemed to be composed of tiny, twinkling specks of light of various colors, sometimes forming a man, sometimes a woman, sometimes a child, sometimes a youth, and each time their clothes and appearance were different.
In Danitz's "Spirit Vision," this spirit body seemed to have some problem, forcing it to constantly "correct" its own existence.
"Error!" If he had to use one word to describe his feeling upon seeing this spirit body, Danitz would definitely choose that word... because the very existence of this spirit body seemed like an "Error."
At this moment, that "Error" spirit body, which seemed to be constantly being corrected by this world, extended its right hand and gently grabbed, and then a bracelet embedded with diamonds appeared in its palm.
Chapter 814: Tracy and Helene
And this bracelet had been on Tracy's right wrist just a second ago.
This was Klein utilizing the "Error Card," leveraging the power above the gray fog, granting his spirit body Demigod-level "stealing" ability.
After obtaining the bracelet, Klein took it above the gray fog for a brief study, then brought it back into reality before ending his self-summoning.
Next, under Danitz's terrified gaze, he calmly tidied up the ritual items, then glanced at the bewildered pirate not far away.
Sensing Gehrman's gaze, Danitz instantly shivered, then forced a smile and said, "I won't say anything."
Gehrman Sparrow truly belongs to an incredibly powerful and secretive organization! He likely summoned a Demigod just now!
Thanks to "Vice Admiral Iceberg" Edwina's strict teaching, Danitz had a decent foundation in mysticism. Even without seeing it, he knew that the existence of such a mysterious being would not have a low Beyonder characteristic!
Hearing Danitz's assurance, Klein nodded noncommittally, then put on the diamond-encrusted bracelet. His spirituality extended over it, and he removed the "crystal" from around Tracy's body.
Snap...
As the "crystal" abruptly vanished, Tracy fell directly to the ground. She laboriously opened her eyes and saw Klein nearby, wearing her bracelet.
"It's you... Adventurer..." Tracy recognized the adventurer who had saved her and immediately breathed a sigh of relief. Then her eyelids drooped, and she fainted again.
Falling into this adventurer's hands, while not the best outcome for her, was ultimately much better than other terrifying possibilities, which is why she could no longer hold on once her mental guard relaxed.
Looking at the unconscious "Vice Admiral of Ailment," Klein did not act rashly. Instead, he again took out the citrine pendant to divine, and only after confirming there was no danger did he cautiously approach, finally reaching Tracy's side.
Kneeling down to carefully examine her body, Klein found that the pirate general's condition was very poor.
Her external injuries were the lightest and had been simply bandaged, with bleeding stopped, so they weren't much of a concern.
However, the poison she was afflicted with was quite troublesome. Even without being a specialized doctor, Klein could tell from the color of her "etheric body" that the "poison" in her body was causing her continuous weakening. If it dragged on for another day or two, she might even lose control due to extreme weakness.
"This must be the drug used to 'control' her. Normally, a certain dosage of 'antidote' would be given daily to keep her in a weak, unconscious state without 'losing control'...
"But because Tracy escaped using a magical item, she didn't get the 'antidote' to relieve it, leading to this dangerous situation.
"I have no way to deal with this kind of poison... I can only wait for Mr. Tower to take over. He has the double favor of the 'Mother Earth' and Goddess Lilith.' He should have plenty of means to solve it."
With a plan in mind, Klein turned to Danitz, and said expressionlessly: "Take off your coat and give it to me."
Glancing at the somewhat tattered and revealing outer garment on "Vice Admiral of Ailment," Danitz suddenly understood. After muttering to himself, "
Why don't you take off your own?
" he obediently took off his coat and threw it to Gehrman.
Klein took the animal fur coat, which had a certain "scent," and remained silent for a few seconds. Finally, he proceeded to remove Tracy's clothes and helped her change into the "new" ones.
During this time, Klein inevitably observed some of Tracy's physical characteristics.
He forced himself not to look away, carefully recording them in his mind.
This wasn't because Klein had any ulterior motives... He was merely conducting "academic" research to avoid any flaws when "role-playing" later.
After doing all this, he picked up Tracy and carried her into the cave the fishermen used for resting.
Danitz, following Gehrman's instructions, lit a fire inside the cave and cooked some porridge using the grain stored there by the fishermen. He then couldn't help but ask, "Why aren't we going back to Lans Island? It's not far; even with my 'flying carpet,' we could get there before nightfall."
"We're still waiting for someone," Klein replied simply, then once again took out candles, essential oils, and "Amandala Pure Dew" and similar items.
He had just "notified" "The Tower," intending to use his "Nightmare" ability to enter Tracy's subconscious before that gentleman arrived, to ask about the "Demoness Sect" and the missing population in the colonies.
.....
Tosk, within the Surrey Family's underground ritual chamber.
As a circular flame door slowly formed, Ebner stepped out of it.
Immediately after, he simulated a "short-range teleportation" using his "Hand of Wisdom" glove, which he had left with Helene, quickly pinpointing her location and appearing directly inside her rented hotel room, right behind Helene.
—Since Fanny had left Tosk, Helene could no longer stay in the Surrey Family's ancestral home and had moved to a hotel.
"Sorry, I'm a little late." Hearing the familiar voice from behind, Helene, already dressed up, breathed a sigh of relief and turned around, saying, "There's still some time before the ball. Hurry and change, I've already prepared your clothes."
Ebner nodded, not dragging his feet. He took the clothes directly into the bedroom, and about two or three minutes later, he emerged wearing an exquisite black mask that only covered the part above his nose, a pirate general's hat, and a modified, exaggerated blue military uniform.
"You want me to dress up as a pirate general?" Ebner glanced at Helene, who was sizing him up, thinking:
You've been captured by a certain pirate general and developed feelings for him, haven't you...
Helene was quite satisfied with Ebner's attire. She was now wearing a white feather mask, which, combined with her bright yellow low-cut evening gown and fiery red hair, made her look exceptionally radiant and beautiful.
"Actually, I should be wearing a 'beast' mask," Ebner praised Helene at the opportune moment.
"What?" Helene blinked in confusion, clearly not getting Ebner's joke.
Did Roselle not copy that? Or was it to be reserved for Bernadette as a "Mystical Reappearance" spell, so it wasn't spread?
While pondering, Ebner shook his head at Helene and chuckled, "Nothing, just complimenting your beauty."
Helene's face flushed slightly. She pretended to glance at the wall clock, changing the subject:
"We should leave now."

chapters.title: Chapter 812: Saintess of Red?
chapters.content:
Chapter 812 - Saintess of Red?
The Valerian family's manor and the hotel Helene was staying at were only separated by two streets, so the distance wasn't too far. Thus, after merely five minutes, the carriage pulled up to a building with a distinctly Gothic style.
"The Valerian family is very fond of this style, which Emperor Roselle named 'Gothic.'
"It's said that the first truly 'Gothic' dress was specifically designed by a young Roselle to please the then-Countess Valerian...
"Of course, that's just a rumor. After all, according to our Sauron family's records, this style actually existed in the Third Epoch... Emperor Roselle merely improved upon it, modernizing it."
Helene linked arms with Ebner, handing the invitation to the attendant while quietly introducing the building.
The original novel seemed to describe the Giant King's Court as having Gothic architecture...
However, this style should be more suited to vampires, but Lilith doesn't seem to like it much... Though the Goddess's churches in the County of Winter are all Gothic.
As Ebner's thoughts wandered, he and Helene entered the ballroom together.
Since it was a masquerade ball, everyone theoretically concealed their identities, so there was no host greeting them.
Ebner and Helene simply entered the main hall led by a servant and then began to move about freely.
This was actually a common situation at private balls in Intis, as Roselle also described in his diary. It primarily served as a venue for "socializing," and the host generally did not interfere with how guests interacted.
Ebner looked around and found that, unlike the customs in Loen, the ladies and madams in Intis were much more open in their attire. Almost every gown revealed a large portion of their shoulders and fair chests, fully showcasing their beauty.
