Especially one lady who also had fiery red hair; not only did she have an impressive figure, but the low "opening" of her gown's neckline attracted the gazes of half the men present.
In comparison, Helene's long dress seemed conservative.
Of course, Ebner observed her not because he had any thoughts, but because he detected some "familiar" qualities about her.
Seeing Ebner's gaze drift further and further, Helene's brows furrowed beneath her mask. She tugged on his sleeve and said, "That woman is the adopted daughter of a wealthy man, a famous socialite in Trier."
"Which wealthy man?" Ebner subconsciously asked.
"Why are you asking about that?" Helene eyed Ebner suspiciously. In her perception, "Detective Hero" wasn't a lecherous person, and was even very much a gentleman. Otherwise, on their journey to Intis, not to mention anyone else, Miss Fanny would have "succeeded" long ago.
Ebner glanced at several gentlemen nearby who wanted to invite Helene to dance but inexplicably "forgot" their purpose after approaching. He then extended his hand to Helene and said:
"Miss, may I have the honor of inviting you to dance?"
Helene was silent for a few seconds, as if guessing that Ebner might want to discuss something while dancing. So, she placed the champagne she had just picked up back on the servant's tray and politely replied:
"The pleasure is mine."
As they stepped onto the dance floor and the music began, Ebner took the opportunity to lean close to Helene's ear and say, "That's probably a Demoness."
Having encountered several Demonesses, Ebner, even without activating his "Pure White Eye," vaguely sensed the unique "charm" aura of a Demoness through "aura extraction."
And this one was likely a High-Sequence Demoness!
"A Demoness..." Helene seemed to think of something, and her dance steps became a bit erratic.
Fortunately, Ebner adjusted his steps, timely compensating for her mistake.
At this moment, Helene recollected herself. She looked into Ebner's eyes beneath the mask and reminisced:
"Speaking of which, Madam Margaret claims she was originally a country girl, noticed by the head of the Issac family who took her in as an adopted daughter, which is how she entered Trier's social scene.
"The reason I remember her is that her hair color was once mistaken for that of a Sauron family illegitimate child... until the elders of our family personally verified that she had no relation to the Sauron family, which then dispelled the rumor.
"Additionally, this lady has been married twice. Both husbands were gentlemen of good character... but neither of her two husbands lived long... so afterward, no one was willing to marry her again."
Issac... I recall that surname. In one of Roselle's diaries, it was recorded that Great Emperor's loyal Captain Issac explored the sea route to the "Forsaken Land of Gods" and never returned... And just two months later, that captain's daughter, Miss Issac, helped Roselle 'reminisce' about his youth.
Come to think of it, Helene helped transcribe that diary before it was given to Klein... What a coincidence!
Amidst the passionate melody, Ebner pondered while expertly performing various difficult dance steps with Helene, drawing glances from other guests.
One was tall and well-built, the other slender and graceful. Though their faces were unseen, their skill and demeanor were perfectly matched, creating an aesthetic appeal.
However, their spotlight didn't last long, quickly stolen by the red-haired socialite Margaret and her dance partner with even more exaggerated movements.
Ebner remained unfazed, simply glancing at the red-haired, red-dressed socialite again, thinking to himself:
Margaret... that name has a "Camille" déjà vu... and her self-professed origin is even more similar!
The Issac family had a close relationship with Roselle, and should have been purged when the Gustav Dynasty fell... Yet this family is still wealthy... This suggests they either betrayed Roselle or received support from someone.
Additionally, Margaret is likely a High-Sequence Demoness.
In Intis, the organizations that possess High-Sequence formulas for the "Demoness" pathway are the "Demoness Sect" and Roselle's "Men in Black."
So, is this Madam Margaret a "Saintess" of the Demoness Sect, or a Saint of the "Men in Black"?
Or both?
Why would such a person attend the Valerian family's ball?
Heh, if my "gathering calamity" constitution holds true again, will the upcoming "accident" originate from her?
Though Ebner had many conjectures, he didn't intend to actively "report" her. Instead, amidst a graceful turn, he changed the subject:
"Do you want to know about Tracy's current situation?"
Of course, as he brought up this topic, he used "Evans's Secret Barrier" to prevent others from hearing.
Helene's steps faltered again upon hearing this, and she bumped into Ebner's embrace. After two seconds, she regained her composure and asked chidingly:
"Why bring her up?"
Her feelings for "Vice Admiral of Ailment" are indeed complex... But then again, Tracy, aside from forcibly detaining her, was actually quite good to her...
As his thoughts drifted, Ebner replied:
"Tracy's condition is very poor right now. Not only was she betrayed by her subordinate, but she's also suffering from a very troublesome poison, and could lose control at any moment..."
He then meticulously relayed the information Mr. World had just "sent" to Helene.
"How could such a thing happen..."
Helene's bright eyes behind the mask showed some concern. She was about to press for more details, but the music stopped at that moment.
The first dance had ended.
Meanwhile, the red-haired, red-dressed Margaret and her dance partner, under the envious gazes of many gentlemen, entered a lounge.
But as soon as the door closed, Margaret pushed her partner away, frowning as she said:
"Why are you still staying in Tosk?
"Aren't you afraid Amon will come knocking?"

chapters.title: Chapter 813: The Men in Black
chapters.content:
Chapter 813 - The Men in Black
Hearing Margaret's words, her male companion's lips curved into a smile as he said:
"Amon? Heh, I actually hope he comes! If so, he can pay back a portion of the blood debt he owes me!"
With that, he took off his mask, revealing a youthful face.
If Ebner were here, he would certainly recognize him as the so-called "Acting Commander" of the "Kaspersky" base.
"So confident?" Margaret raised an eyebrow, simultaneously slipping off her high heels and sitting on the lounge sofa.
Her waist was naturally slender, full of allure even without a corset. Even in her current rather ungraceful sitting posture, she resembled a slowly unfolding beautiful painting.
However, the young man opposite her was oblivious to this beautiful "painting." He simply poured himself a cup of black tea, sipped it, and said, "I have confidence in His Majesty... He once left a seal in my mind, telling me it would be enough to give Amon an unforgettable lesson."
"The means His Majesty left you can actually contend with Amon?" Margaret asked with considerable surprise and curiosity, "What did he seal?"
"I don't know... His Majesty only told me not to probe; the information contained within would be equally dangerous to me..." The young man put down his cup and shook his head.
"Very dangerous to you... Once Amon seizes your fate and steals your memories, He would also gain this warning..." Margaret reminded him.
"Heh, is Amon the kind of person who sees a warning and doesn't investigate? He'd probably be even more excited, wouldn't He?" The young man let out a cold laugh.
Clearly, he had a certain degree of understanding of Amon's character.
"That's true," Margaret nodded, then dropped the topic, shifting to say, "You should know why I came to see you, right? Ace of Hearts..."
"I can mostly guess..." The young man nodded slightly, "Twelve of Clubs."
As he spoke, he organized his thoughts and continued, "But I can't be certain..."
"You can't be certain? Didn't you preside over the 'resurrection' ritual?" Margaret asked with a frown.
"But something went wrong... His Majesty, well, let's call that person His Majesty for now, he awakened in the Delien family's 'Black Knight'... so I still have some doubts about his identity." At this point, the young man relayed some of his attempts at probing from that day to "Twelve of Clubs."
After listening, Margaret said thoughtfully, "It sounds fine... And that 'ancestor' of the Delien family was very close to His Majesty before becoming a Demigod. His descendants might even be His Majesty's bloodline, so it might be normal for him to revive in Sero Delien...
"But according to what you said, his personality indeed isn't like His Majesty's... Yet His Majesty had a big change in his later years, so we can't judge it's not him based on that alone..."
The young man gave a wry smile and said, "That's why I said I couldn't be certain."
"In that case... it's best if the 'Men in Black' I command don't contact him for now... If he summons for something, I'll first send people from the 'Demoness Sect' to him... until we're certain he is truly His Majesty," Margaret quickly decided.
"Heh, you've certainly done well for yourself, 'Saintess of Red' of the 'Demoness Sect'," the young man chuckled, teasing her.
The high-ranking members of the Demoness Sect all used colors as codenames, such as "Saintess of White," "Saintess of Black," and here, "Saintess of Red."
"Thanks for the compliment... but it still can't compare to you, Vice President of the 'Hermit of Fate Society'," Margaret retorted.
Afterward, the two looked at each other for a few seconds, then both laughed... but their laughter contained both mirth and a hint of sadness.
After a while, Margaret sighed and said, "Of that batch of people from over a hundred years ago, only you and I are left..."
"Indeed, the 'Diamonds' group was openly active and was wiped out by the Churches and various forces early on; the 'Spades' group was mainly responsible for foreign affairs, and also lost their protection, being dug out by intelligence agencies of various countries. The remaining members then defected to the Princess and joined the 'Dawn of Elements'..."
At this point, the young man's face showed some weariness. He repeated Margaret's earlier words: "Only we are left!"
"So, what are you waiting for? Won't you reminisce about the past with me?" Margaret suddenly untied her dress, saying temptingly.
Chapter 816: The Men in Black
The young man, however, shook his head firmly, turning away from Margaret's body as her clothes automatically fell off. He said, "Even if we are to revisit the past, it must be my main body... This avatar cannot have such a cheap pleasure."
"You still care about that?" Margaret asked in surprise.
...I don't even care.
"It's a form of respect for you... though it ultimately means nothing," the young man said, pursing his lips.
Margaret fell silent for a moment upon hearing this, then curved her eyes and said, "If I were a hundred years younger, I might even fall in love with you."
"Good thing you didn't... those who love me don't usually have good ends..." The young man grinned, self-deprecatingly.
Margaret, now re-dressed, didn't pursue that topic. Instead, she changed the subject: "Where is your main body? Did it stay in Loen after the 'Hermit of Fate Gathering' and not return?"
If it were anyone else asking, the young man naturally wouldn't answer, but for Margaret, he chose not to conceal: "I found a Jacob family Demigod in Backlund. She seems to hold the secret of a treasure and has parasitized a noble lady.
"However, that 'Parasite's' mystical knowledge is clearly incomplete, missing many important details, allowing me to easily 'influence' her without her knowing.
"She still believes to this day that she is bound by that noble lady due to a so-called 'contract'!"
.....
At nine in the evening, after the final major event of the Valerian family's masquerade ball, the screening of the new "film," concluded, Ebner and Helene finally left the luxurious manor and boarded their carriage.
—Helene had come to the ball specifically to observe the premiere's effect... It seemed their film company, Ebner's and hers, had succeeded once again!
Even before the silent comedy film began, Ebner had asked her about taking Tracy in and caring for her. After several hours of deliberation, Helene finally made her decision:
"Ebner, please bring her over... She has no one to rely on now... Consider it my repayment for her care on the 'Black Death' ship."
Without Tracy's care, one could imagine the tragic fate she would have met on the "Black Death" ship.
Ebner nodded upon hearing this, saying nothing more. He simply instructed her to return to the hotel to pack her luggage, then vanished from the carriage.
As he headed to the altar to teleport to the Rorsted Archipelago, what he was thinking was:
The entire ball went without any problems... It seems my "gathering calamity" constitution likely originates from the "Pure White Eye," as I had suspected!
The few times I've had uneventful gatherings before were also when I didn't use the "Pure White Eye" or used it very little...
Is there something behind the "Pure White Eye" that can cause "calamities"?
.....
On a desolate island south of the Rorsted Archipelago, Danitz was guarding a bonfire, bored and dozing off. But his spiritual intuition was suddenly triggered. He vigilantly opened his eyes and saw Gehrman stand up.
His heart startled, he quickly looked towards the cave entrance, only to see the detective he disliked enter, wearing an exaggerated officer's uniform.
He's dressed as if he's going to a masquerade ball... He's even more pretentious than that "Flower Tie" guy!
Danitz grumbled inwardly, then saw the detective greet Gehrman and walk directly to "Vice Admiral of Ailment's" side.
The other party briefly examined Tracy's condition, then frowned. He then picked her up horizontally and vanished from the cave with her.
Gehrman stared at the spot where they disappeared for a few seconds, contemplating something, then turned back to signal Danitz, ready to return to the hotel on Lans Island.
"Where did they go?" Danitz asked curiously after catching up to Gehrman.
"They might have gone back to Bayam first," Klein replied casually. He knew that Mr. Tower's "teleportation" distance wasn't too far; a long-distance teleportation would likely require the "teleportation altar" at "Fragrant Manor."
"Our destination is Bayam later too, right? Why didn't you let him take us along?" Danitz mumbled softly.
Because I haven't gotten my deposit back from the Lans Island hotel...
Klein glanced at him, thinking.

chapters.title: Chapter 814: The Dice
chapters.content:
Chapter 814 - The Dice
The herb shop in the alley diagonally opposite the "Red Theater" was still open. The plump apothecary, Darkwill, sat behind the counter, outwardly calm but inwardly anxious.
Ever since receiving Ebner's advice, he had frequently used opportunities to prepare potions for others to discreetly commission adventurers or pirates to inquire about his teacher's whereabouts.
Just yesterday, he finally received news from a guard at the Governor's Mansion: his teacher, Roy King, had been secretly arrested by the military and was currently imprisoned within the Governor's Mansion.
If this guard hadn't joined the "Celestial Sect" and severely depleted his body from excessive indulgence with a certain noble lady, and also lacked money for medicine, he wouldn't have risked telling the plump apothecary this information.
Of course, a more significant reason was that the Governor of Bayam was about to leave office, and the guard had lost his former deference towards him.
Darkwill had spent the entire day trying to contact known "School of Life" members through various means, seeking necessary help. However, he couldn't know who would come or when, so he could only suppress his fear and anxiety, continue to keep the shop open, pretending that nothing had happened.
"Darkwill, you're very restless," the owl perched on Boody's shoulder spoke.
"I don't need you to remind me, I'm well aware of my state," Darkwill waved his hand impatiently.
He still remembered when he was studying with his teacher, he was always warned to be wary of official organizations and true vampires. For this, Roy King gave many examples: being permanently imprisoned underground, seeing neither sunlight nor women; becoming a researcher, using one's body to test the dangers of certain Sealed Artifacts; enduring various experiments, mutating into monsters with only instinct left; or being drained by vampires and turned into puppets.
So, while he might have a foul mouth, he rarely truly caused trouble and never stayed in a city for more than three months.
Fortunately, seeing Boody's worried gaze, Darkwill, for the sake of his pride, somewhat reined in his fear and shifted his attention to what to do.
If only Ebner were still in Bayam, I could ask him for advice...
Darkwill annoyedly scratched his hair, then a flash of inspiration struck him. He suddenly remembered his last communication with his teacher, Roy King.
"He seemed to tell me to go to Mapple's Grocery Store on Enmat Street and buy a dice... I've overlooked this before, but now that I think about it, this request was a bit abrupt... Maybe there's a secret there?"
Thinking this, Darkwill mustered his courage, took the owl with him, left Boody to watch the shop temporarily, and walked out of the alley.
Next, he spent a high price of 1 gold pound at that grocery store to buy a very small ring box.
Inside the ring box was an off-white six-sided dice, with a red "4" facing up.
Afterward, he accidentally dropped the dice and encountered various misfortunes, yet fortunately rolled a "6" when interrogated by the police, safely passing through and returning to the shop.
By this time, night had fallen, and the light from the gas streetlights on either side was too far apart, illuminating only a small portion of the road.
Darkwill nervously entered the herb shop using this faint light. After briefly comforting Boody, who looked worried, he took the owl upstairs to his living quarters and repeatedly examined the ring box and the off-white dice.
Finally, he pulled out a piece of paper, folded to half the size of a finger joint, from a hidden compartment at the bottom of the ring box.
Darkwill silently took a breath and quickly read it.
It was a message written by his teacher. Besides explaining that he might have been betrayed by an insider, it also described in detail the function of the dice, stating that it had a certain living characteristic: the more it was used, the easier it would awaken, and it would even roll itself unnoticed, even without space.
When it fixed on '1', it would make people suffer more than direct death, because almost everything they did would fail!
Finally, he issued a task... telling Darkwill to take the dice to Kano the bell-ringer on Olavi Island, or to Detective Ebner Braun.
Sure enough, this dice is very dangerous...
Darkwill subconsciously sighed, then realized he had done something foolish out of good intentions.
To rescue his teacher, Roy King, he had overcome his cowardice and stayed in Bayam, sending out requests for help to the members of the School of Life he knew.
And according to the letter's content, this meant he was very likely targeted by the person who betrayed Roy King!
"Why didn't I think of buying this dice sooner! If I had bought it earlier, I wouldn't have sent messages to the traitor... And if it were even earlier, maybe Ebner wouldn't have left Bayam..." Darkwill raised his hands, pulling at the hair on the sides of his head.
However, a flicker of doubt immediately crossed his mind:
Why give the dice to Ebner? Although that detective is strong, he's only a Mid-Sequence Beyonder. Does he really have the ability to handle such a terrifying Sealed Artifact?
And this Sealed Artifact belongs to our own school; why give it to an outsider?
After thinking for a long time without success, Darkwill decided to give up. After all, his teacher was always acting mysterious; he was used to it. Besides, he had no idea where Ebner was, so his only option now was to find the bell-ringer.
He dared not linger here, deciding to move his residence tonight and take a boat to Olavi Island tomorrow morning—an island located on the "Rorsted Archipelago—Toscato" shipping route.
"My talismans, my pistol, my whip..." Darkwill busily counted items that provided a sense of security, worried about his lack of sufficient combat power.
Suddenly, he thought of Boody again, unsure how to arrange for her. Although the little girl had made significant progress recently and could fend for herself... his enemies were not ordinary people. If they couldn't find him, would they make trouble for her?
But taking her with me might be even more dangerous!
Darkwill's expression twisted, then quickly settled, twisted again, then settled again... After repeating this several times, he decided it was best to ask Boody herself, as this was a matter of life and death, and he had no right to decide for her.
She wasn't that silly bird bound to him.
Just as Darkwill, having cleared his mind, let out a sigh of relief, a knock suddenly sounded at the door.
"They're coming for me! Someone's coming for me!"
Darkwill's first reaction was that he had been exposed. Outside were either official personnel or a traitor from the "School of Life"...
The uncontrollable fear that had just subsided in his heart surged again, and he instinctively wanted to hide the dice.
But only then did he realize that the off-white dice had somehow flipped itself.
This time, a red "6" was facing up.
Is this a good omen? Darkwill clutched his chest, asking with a trembling voice:
"Who is it?"
"Boss, it's me... Boody." Boody's clear voice rang out from outside the door.
Darkwill then slumped onto a chair, feeling as if he had come back to life.
"Your friend, Mr. Ebner Bryan, has arrived with a patient," Boody's voice came again from outside the door.
"What?!"
Darkwill looked at the "6" facing up on the dice and thought:
Looks like my luck isn't so bad after all?
.....
In the courtyard, Ebner waited for Darkwill, holding Tracy, who was clad in a hooded robe.
He hadn't returned directly to Toscato or Trier because Tracy's body truly couldn't wait any longer. Darkwill's apothecary shop had a relatively complete stock of herbs, allowing him to concoct some potions to alleviate the toxins.
As for the robe on Tracy, Ebner had simply picked out a random one from the "Fragrant Manor" for her to wear.
He didn't feel there was anything to be discreet about; setting aside that "Vice Admiral of Ailment" was originally a man, he had seen Tracy stark naked when she was controlled by the "Rose School" deep in the Daniel Maze, so he had long lost any "exploratory" thoughts.
However, Boody's expression just now seemed off... Did something happen here with Darkwill?
But even with my "Butterfly effect," shouldn't there still be some time before the "Dice of Probability" storyline?
Just as he thought this, he saw a pale-faced Darkwill walk out of the house, holding an off-white dice in his palm.
Seeing this, Ebner's hand trembled, and he nearly threw Tracy out like a dice.

chapters.title: Chapter 815: Beyond the Eyes
chapters.content:
Chapter 815 - Beyond the Eyes
Ebner stared intently at the off-white dice in Darkwill's hand. Only after seeing the red "6" facing up did he breathe a sigh of relief, simultaneously recalling the original novel's description of this Sealed Artifact, solidified from the uniqueness of the "Wheel of Fortune."
"...'Dice of Probability'.
"...The highest-grade Sealed Artifact within the School of Life, with a 'Grade 0' standard.
"...It controls the probability of every event. At '1' point, it amplifies the probability of unfavorable outcomes to the extreme. At '2' points, it significantly increases unfavorable probabilities, but this doesn't mean '2' is necessarily safer than '1,' because once the probability becomes high, any accident can happen. '3' points slightly amplifies unfavorable probabilities. '4' to '6' points are the opposite.
"...To truly seal the 'Dice of Probability,' one must use specific Sealed Artifacts to isolate its connection to the spirit world, astral world, and real world."
Additionally, Arrodes had mentioned that it's a petty and vengeful fellow. While it can be intimidated by certain methods, the more often it's done, the less it's affected, and after more than a week, it will retaliate wildly... In short, according to Arrodes, it's not suitable to be a loyal servant.
Just as Ebner thought this, he heard Darkwill ask in a surprised tone: "How much medicine did you give her to make her like this?"
As his words fell, both the little girl Boody and the owl Harry looked at Ebner with wide, round eyes, as if they couldn't believe he was such a scoundrel.
—One's eyes were already round, the other's became so.
Is this the time to talk about Tracy's problems? That dice in your hand is something that can make us even worse off than Tracy!
Ebner suppressed the urge to run away directly, and with a grim expression, asked: "You still have the mood for sarcasm? Do you know how dangerous that thing in your hand is?"
Saying that, he set Tracy down, wrapped an arm around her waist to support her from falling, and with his other hand, pulled out a one-gold-pound coin. He tossed it to the little girl Boody, and gently said: "Could I trouble you to get some supper for me with Mr. Harry?"
Though his words were polite, they carried the authority of an "Arbiter," which made Boody, who took the coin, and Harry on her shoulder, follow his instructions and walk out of the courtyard with almost no hesitation.
Once Boody and Harry had left, "Fat Apothecary" Darkwill finally realized that Ebner had sent them away to avoid implicating innocents...
His lips mumbled a few times before he incoherently responded to Ebner's earlier words: "For uncontrollable matters, we must remain optimistic; for controllable matters, we must remain cautious.
"This is a proverb circulating within our school, rumored to be the famous saying of a High-Sequence powerhouse in the Fourth Epoch."
Though it makes sense, I think you're just being a smart-mouth... But this sentence sounds familiar, which Transmigrator senior "borrowed" it?
It's related to the "School of Life"... That Vampire Duke Rhine?
As Ebner speculated, he stared intently at the dice in the "Fat Apothecary's" hand, terrified it would roll on its own.
"Alright, I admit I'm very nervous, very scared, so I need to adjust with words." Seeing Ebner's displeased expression, Darkwill quickly changed the subject, raising the dice in his hand and asking, "It seems you know it?"
No wonder Teacher's note said it could be given to Ebner.
Ebner felt his heart pound with fear, yet dared not scold the other party for fear of startling him and causing him to drop the dice. He could only take a deep breath and whispered: "Stay in that position and don't move... I'll go find someone who can re-seal it for you..."
He planned to bring Klein over, as in the original novel, to invite this dice to a concert.
"You can't do anything about it either? But Teacher said I could just give it to you..." Darkwill frowned upon hearing this, muttering.
Huh?
Hearing his mumble, Ebner immediately stopped his "teleportation" action and asked with a serious expression, "What did your teacher say?"
Darkwill, seeing his solemn inquiry, quickly handed over his teacher's note.
Ebner took it and read it carefully several times. Seeing that its content was largely similar to the original novel, with only additional information about himself, he couldn't help but ponder:
Although the people of the "School of Life" are all mystics, to accurately "predict" me...
Combining that proverb Darkwill blurted out, and the "Dice of Probability" still obediently showing six points...
Could this also be something arranged by a previous Transmigrator senior?
Or perhaps it's the "little snake's" arrangement?
Hmm... the Speaker of the "School of Life," "Little Snake" Will, has always been friendly to me. During our conversation at the banquet at 28 Ginster Street, he even said he was entrusted by a friend... Who could that friend be? Rhine?
As his thoughts whirled, Ebner opened his "Pure White Eye," preparing to carefully observe this Sealed Artifact solidified from the uniqueness of the "Wheel of Fortune."
Of course, he also had an ulterior motive... After all, no matter what plans the Transmigrator seniors had, they were most likely centered around the "Pure White Eye" as their common cheat.
Just as the "Pure White Eye" opened and the passage to the "Unknown Land" formed, the off-white dice in Darkwill's hand, as if attracted by something, flew up on its own.
Then, it shot straight towards Ebner's eyes.
Having experienced similar incidents and being somewhat prepared, Ebner did not let it enter the "Unknown Land." Instead, he spent money to buy a Demigod-level "barrier" force stored in the "Quiz Labyrinth," preparing to intercept it.
But just as the dice touched the barrier, a illusory, rotating golden wheel suddenly flashed out, swiftly penetrating the barrier and entering Ebner's "Pure White Eye."
Due to the suddenness of the event, Ebner, who hadn't reacted at all, could only watch helplessly as the off-white dice fell to the ground and shattered into several pieces...
On the other side, Darkwill, dumbfounded, stammered: "A 'Grade 0' Sealed Artifact... just broke like that?"
The "Unknown Land" can block the fate of Zaratul's projected revival, so it's almost certain that it has no relation to the Spirit World, Astral World, or the real world. Otherwise, it wouldn't be "unknown"... It truly is a good place to seal it...
But why did the "Dice of Probability" rush so eagerly into a place so unfriendly to it? What exactly inside is attracting it?
Or rather, did some Transmigrator senior put something in there that even a Uniqueness would flock to?
Perhaps I should ask that "little snake"?
Ebner rubbed his forehead and answered Darkwill's question:
"Its true body has been sealed, so this dice, as the 'outer shell,' naturally broke."
Darkwill suspiciously looked back and forth between the shattered dice and Ebner several times before reluctantly accepting his explanation.
After all, Teacher told me to give it to Ebner. Even if something went wrong, it's not my responsibility...
Darkwill thought to himself, though outwardly, he finally relaxed and showed his signature ambiguous smile, looking at Tracy, who was leaning against Ebner, and said:
"Now that the troublesome matter is resolved, let's first examine the poison on this lady...
"I recognize this poison; the 'Celestial Sect' on the island likes this kind of thing. Many Beyonders even willingly drink it to pretend they're powerless to resist others... But this lady's condition is very serious, the dosage is huge... Playing so wildly?
"Uh... is this 'Vice Admiral of Ailment'?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 816: You’re awake?
chapters.content:
Chapter 816 - You're awake?
Darkwill instinctively swallowed, his gaze slowly shifting from Tracy's face. He asked in disbelief:
"The Vice Admiral of Ailment also likes the 'Celestial Sect's' style?"
Although Tracy wasn't a good person, she certainly wasn't
that
kind of person, so Ebner, after a brief thought, simply defended her: "She was ambushed."
Was the person who ambushed her you?
If it were before, Darkwill would have blurted out the question, but intimidated by the unique ability Ebner had just displayed in sealing a Grade "0" Sealed Artifact, Darkwill swallowed his words.
Next, he returned inside the shop, retrieved a prepared potion, and handed it to Ebner, implying: "You're quite lucky. I just recently prepared a similar antidote for a guard, and there's some left...
"However, her situation is different from that guard's lover. The dosage used before was too large, and she went too long without taking the 'antidote.' The poison has not only corroded her body but has even caused a certain degree of 'contamination' to her spirit...
"At most, I can only help her alleviate it for now... To completely cure it, you'd probably need someone with more advanced methods... Hmm, like my teacher."
Ebner was fully aware of Darkwill's intentions behind those words, but he currently had no desire to clash with the Loen military, and his "plan" in Trier had only just begun, leaving him no time for such extraneous matters.
Moreover, Darkwill's teacher wasn't in any particular danger being held in the Governor's Mansion. According to the original novel, he would successfully escape soon due to the chaos caused by personnel changes among the officials in the Rorsted Archipelago.
Therefore, Ebner did not pick up on Darkwill's hint. He simply took the potion, opened the cap, and poured it down Tracy's throat.
In fact, what he cared more about in his heart was the "luck" Darkwill mentioned...
"Such 'luck' feels even more like an 'arrangement'!" Ebner secretly sighed to himself, throwing the empty bottle back to Darkwill, then said:
"I don't have time to save your teacher... but I can introduce you to a formidable adventurer. Go talk to him."
Ebner was naturally referring to Klein. Since the latter wanted to infiltrate and investigate the "Celestial Sect," he probably wouldn't refuse the opportunity to rescue Darkwill's teacher from the Governor's Mansion and earn some extra cash.
Darkwill was initially disappointed when Ebner didn't reply, but upon hearing his words, he couldn't help but ask curiously, "Which adventurer?"
"Gehrman Sparrow!" Ebner replied after picking up Tracy again.
"Gehrman Sparrow? The one who hunted Steel Maveti, and helped the 'Vice Admiral of Ailment' repel the Demoness Sect... Uh." At this point, Darkwill glanced at Tracy in Ebner's arms and suddenly choked on his words.
The next second, he looked at Ebner's eyes in disbelief. Although he didn't speak, the meaning conveyed in his gaze was very clear, and Ebner easily read it using his "mind-reading" ability:
You ran off with his girl, and now you want me to ask him for help... What if he finds out and retaliates against me?!
—At this time, due to the actions of the Demoness Sect and the Celestial Sect, the identity of the adventurer who had previously helped Tracy had finally been revealed and was currently a hot topic, so even though Darkwill had been in poor spirits these past two days, he had still heard about it.
"Gehrman entrusted me to treat and look after her..." Ebner thought for a moment, then simply explained, trying to salvage his reputation. After all, this really had nothing to do with him...
"Then he must have some special fetish!" Darkwill muttered, then asked, "Where do I find him?"
"In a bit, first take Boody to the 'Amyris Leaf Bar' and find 'Sea Snake' Wave. He'll arrange lodging for you... By tomorrow, Gehrman Sparrow should be back in Bayam, and he'll come looking for you then." Ebner said this, handing Darkwill a "Badge of Courage" as a token. Wave would know it was someone Ebner arranged upon seeing it.
"And the 'Amyris Leaf Bar's' gathering is protected by the 'Mandated Punishers,' making it much safer," Ebner added after a moment's thought.
"But is it really okay for a Beyonder like me to be exposed right under the nose of the Church of the Storms?" Darkwill asked, still hesitant after receiving the badge.
"Don't worry. Your school already cooperates with the Church of the Storms... That so-called bell-ringer, Kano, rings the bells of the Storm." Ebner had learned this information back when he was on the fifth floor of the "Dream Labyrinth Tower."
"Is that really how it is? The old man never told me..." Darkwill felt like everything that had happened in the past two days was a dream.
At this moment, Boody and the owl Harry, who had gone to buy supper, returned to the shop's courtyard. Ebner took the Bayam specialty, "Teayativa," they had bought back, then bid farewell to Darkwill, Boody, and the owl, disappearing directly from the courtyard.
Although she had long known about the existence of "Beyonders," the inexperienced Boody was still startled. She couldn't help but look at her boss, who was now also wide-mouthed, mumbling, "If he had said earlier that he could 'teleport,' I should have just had him send me directly to Olavi..."
Hearing this, Mr. Harry the owl clicked his tongue twice and said, "Clearly, the woman he's holding is more appealing than you are."
Darkwill snapped back to attention upon hearing this. He silently pulled out the whip he had previously packed and said "kindly," "Come here for a moment. I have something good to share with you..."
Harry the owl, however, looked at the whip in Darkwill's hand with a mix of affection and fear. He then spread his wings and flew onto Boody's shoulder, disdainfully saying, "You can't trick me this time..."
Seeing this scene, Boody finally broke into a heartfelt smile...
How wonderful! Mr. Darkwill and Mr. Harry are back to their old selves.
Although she didn't know what had happened in the past few days, she could feel her boss's fear and unease. But now, with the arrival and departure of that detective, everything had finally returned to normal...
Truly, the Sea God's blessing... Thank you for your mercy!
.....
In the ancient palace above the gray fog.
Klein, who had just ridden the "big fish" back to Lans Island and returned to his rented hotel room, did not rest immediately. Instead, he came above the gray fog, ready to seriously study the abilities and origins of Tracy's bracelet.
Just then, the crimson star symbolizing Mr. Tower expanded and contracted.
He thought for a moment, let his spirituality extend over it, and then heard the other party's request and report.
"Please ask 'The World' about the 'Dice of Probability' from that 'Snake of Mercury' in Backlund...
"What is the 'Dice of Probability'? Is it a Sealed Artifact of the School of Life?
"Also, a plump apothecary wants to give me a commission? Go to the 'Amyris Leaf Bar' tomorrow?"
After careful consideration, Klein divined a few times, confirmed there was no danger, then left the gray fog and returned to his bedroom. He took a paper crane from his wallet, unfolded it on the table, looked at the surface that still showed wiping marks, picked up a pencil, and wrote a simple question:
"Dice of Probability."
Although it was only a noun, he believed that "Snake of Mercury" would surely know what Mr. Tower wanted to ask.
Then, he folded the paper crane back to its original form, tucked it into his wallet, and then once again walked four steps counter-clockwise, re-entering the space above the gray fog.
.....
On Tuesday morning, when Tracy felt a warmth and finally overcame her mental exhaustion, opening her eyes, she saw an unfamiliar man in her sight.
The man was handsome, with curly brown hair, and wore gold-rimmed glasses, making him appear refined and scholarly.
He seemed vaguely familiar, but her muddled mind couldn't recall where she had seen him.
Tracy was about to ask something, but then saw the man look directly into her eyes, then curve his lips, smiling as he said:
"You're awake? The surgery was a success!"

chapters.title: Chapter 817: Various Role-Plays of the Mysticism Magister
chapters.content:
Chapter 817 - Various Role-Plays of the Mysticism Magister
"The surgery was a success?" Tracy didn't grasp the meaning of Ebner's words. Still somewhat disoriented, she instinctively repeated his phrase while her rusty brain pondered philosophical questions like "Who am I?", "Where am I?", "What am I supposed to do?", and "What does he mean?"
After about a minute, she finally recalled what she had experienced.
She tried to struggle up but found herself too weak to even lift a finger. She could only ask in a hoarse voice, "Who are you... Where is this? Where's Gehrman?"
As she spoke, she used her nearly depleted spirituality to sense her body. Finding herself dressed and feeling no abnormalities, she breathed a slight sigh of relief.
"My name is Ebner Bryan. Gehrman was helpless against the poison in your body, so he transferred you to me...
"And you are currently in my Ancient Vine Manor in Trier, Miss Tracy."
Ebner Bryan answered her questions with a smile.
Speaking of which, early this morning, Ebner had gone with the "criminal" butler whose mind was controlled by the "Magic Mirror," as well as the agent and lawyer provided by the "club," to complete the property "transfer" procedures.
So, it was now legitimate to say that this "Ancient Vine Manor" belonged to him.
For this, Ebner paid nearly 20,000 Fels, but it was essentially a left-hand-to-right-hand transaction, costing only dozens of Fels in processing fees.
And now, the "Magic Mirror" was still representing him, along with the lawyer and agent, to transfer the shares of "Mirror Apostle" Herta in the shipping company and the Susit Bank.
As for her luxurious villa in Trier's Saint Laurent District, Ebner Bryan did not intend to take it over, planning to sell it directly for cash.
—After all, ostensibly, "Herta" was selling these properties because her business abroad ran into problems and she urgently needed a large sum of capital... If Ebner bought everything himself, it would look too suspicious.
More importantly, the villa's location was not ideal and did not fit Ebner's next plan.
"Ebner Bryan..." Tracy muttered the name several times. Suddenly remembering something, her eyes sharpened, and she asked in a dry voice, "Helene... is she with you?"
Although her mother, Caterina, hadn't fulfilled her promise to tell her Helene's whereabouts, the mere clues of "Bayam" and "maid" had narrowed the scope, and she had a list of suspects in hand.
"If it weren't for Helene's request, I wouldn't have agreed to save you." Ebner's impression of the "Vice Admiral of Ailment" was clearly not as good as that of the other three female pirate generals.
"Helene..." Tracy's eyes first softened, then she looked at Ebner Bryan with a complicated expression.
Though she suspected he might have been involved with Helene, he was also the one who saved her.
"Thank you..." Tracy thanked him, then struggled to raise her head to look further, wanting to see if Helene was nearby, but failed. She could only exhale and say, "Where is Helene?"
"She went home to help her father with some debts; she should be coming over soon," Ebner replied casually. At the same time, he pulled back the covers to examine Tracy's body, finding that his initial treatment last night had yielded considerable results. At least her body and spirit had stopped deteriorating.
In fact, if Ebner wanted to quickly cure Tracy, it wasn't impossible. As long as he arranged a ritual to summon Lady Helene, the problem would surely be resolved.
But Tracy had no relation to him, and Ebner Bryan had no intention of owing favors for her. So, he simply experimented on Tracy after specifically modifying the "Violet's Perfect Recovery Art." It seemed effective, and perhaps could be further adjusted.
"Learning mystical arts, developing mystical arts, teaching mystical arts..." According to the role-playing principle of a "Mysticism Magister," Ebner Bryan's plan was to research a "mystical art" specifically designed to eliminate this "toxic potion," then teach it to Tracy, allowing her to recover on her own, thus completing a "role-play."
As for the pain Tracy endured during the "experiment"... that would be her paying the price for her misdeeds... Moreover, with Helene's care, she might even willingly act as a "guinea pig."
It's worth noting that through Ebner Bryan's research, the drug provided by the "Celestial Sect" was actually quite complex. The so-called "aphrodisiac" was merely a pretext; even the "antidote" provided could only alleviate the symptoms, not truly eliminate them... Once the "antidote" was stopped, those who had taken the drug would become even weaker than the "Vice Admiral of Ailment" in a very short time!
It could be described as both a "poison" and a "curse"... It was likely something specifically developed by followers of the "Mother Tree of Desire" to control others.
The "Biological Toxin Bottle" in the original novel was a product of those guys' failed experiments. Could this potion have a similar origin?
As he pondered, Ebner heard Tracy ask in a surprised tone, "You... you two aren't living together?"
Ebner snapped back to attention, glancing at her. He naturally understood what she wanted to ask, but was too lazy to bother, simply continuing to examine her body on his own.
Tracy was initially a bit nervous at his actions, but quickly realized his eyes were clear and he was indeed only conducting "academic" research. She then relaxed.
As a pirate, and as someone who had once been male, she genuinely didn't care about minor physical contact.
After a moment, seeing Ebner cover her with the blanket again, Tracy inquired once more: "How's my condition? When will I recover?"
"Your condition is basically stabilized. Use the potions I formulated for a few days, and once you regain some mobility, I will teach you a mystical art.
"After that, you'll use the 'mystical art' yourself to continue clearing the effects of the poison. You should recover completely in about half a month," Ebner said after some thought.
"Half a month..." Tracy mused, then suddenly asked, "What was that 'surgery' you mentioned earlier?"
That was just a joke you wouldn't understand... Ebner Bryan muttered to himself. He used his "Spirit Vision" to observe her mental state, his eyes twinkling, and said with a smile:
"'Congratulations on a successful surgery, you've turned from a man into a girl'..."
"There once was an 'Instigator' who was tricked into drinking a 'Witch' potion. When she regained consciousness, someone offered her congratulations with that very joke."
Tracy froze at his words, her expression twisting slightly. It felt as though a deep-seated shame had been brutally dug out and exposed to the sunlight.
Her azure eyes immediately clouded with anger stemming from shame and irritation, and her pale, poisoned face instantly flushed red.
But, unable to even move a finger, she quickly reined in her emotions, scoffed, and said in a low, hoarse voice:
"As expected of the 'Romantic Detective,' your understanding of demonesses far surpasses that of ordinary people."
Ebner ignored her sarcasm, merely nodding with satisfaction. "It seems your mental recovery is quite good... You should know that, according to my research, this poison you've contracted amplifies emotions and desires. Once an extreme emotion arises, it's very difficult to control...
"The 'Violet's Perfect Recovery Art' is indeed very effective at removing spiritual contamination."
Tracy stared blankly. She hadn't expected that he wasn't trying to expose her past, but merely testing her mental recovery?
If that's the case, did what I just said sound impolite? Will he speak ill of me to Helene because of it?
Just as Tracy was lost in thought, the sound of the door being pushed open came, and Helene walked to the bedside.
"Ebner, how is she?" Helene asked.
"She's awake. You two can catch up now," Ebner replied with a smile, then turned and left the bedroom, only adding before stepping out, "But be moderate; don't delay the company's work."
With that, he casually closed the door.
Helene didn't reply; her full attention was on Tracy. Seeing her weak and powerless state, she felt all her fear of her vanish.
Tracy also looked at the familiar yet somewhat strange face, saying with a complex tone, "Helene, you're still as stubborn as ever, but your eyes seem much firmer... no longer so wavering..."
"This is all Ebner Bryan's guidance to me..." Helene said.
This was not a lie. Being with Ebner , she had learned many excellent qualities from him—of course, she didn't know that this was a "Mysticism Magister's" deliberate and subtle guidance tailored to her personality, also part of his role-play.
Tracy's mood immediately darkened. She felt that even if they weren't living together, their hearts had grown closer... According to Emperor Roselle's saying, she suspected her head might be a little green...
But before she could dwell on it, her chin was lifted by Helene's finger. The girl who had once been beneath her now looked down, saying:
"Everything you did to me before, I'm going to get my revenge!"
At this moment, Helene fully embodied the domineering female CEO persona from some of the stories Ebner had told her.
.....
On the other side, Ebner , having left the bedroom, directly pushed Tracy's matter to the back of his mind, turning instead to contemplate Klein's recent reply from "Little Snake" Will:
"This is the choice of destiny..."
The choice of destiny? What exactly does that mean? "Mystics" really are annoying when they speak!
Muttering inwardly, Ebner Bryan stepped out and boarded a carriage, pondering:
"The note left by Darkwill's teacher actually had two choices: one was to hand the 'Dice of Probability' to Councilman Joes Red, as in the original novel, and the other was to hand it to me...
"And the choice of destiny... does that mean the uniqueness of the 'Wheel of Fortune' ultimately chose me?
"Why would it choose me? And why did the little snake allow the uniqueness to fall into my hands?
"Could it be that other Transmigrators brought by the 'Pure White Eye' also obtained the 'Wheel of Fortune' before?
"The God of Luck?"

chapters.title: Chapter 818: The Chaotic Delien Family
chapters.content:
Chapter 818 - The Chaotic Delien Family
Aboard the "Future," Cattleya dismissed Jane, who had come to probe for information, then hesitated for over ten minutes. Finally, she took out a pen and paper, carefully writing:
"Recently, someone has been deliberately collecting the Great Emperor's diaries."
She dared not mention the Tarot Club in her letter, nor leak any information, fearing punishment from Mr. Fool. She could only start from signs that could be ordinarily discovered to provide a hint.
After writing and folding it, she took out a delicate, golden harmonica she carried, placed it to her lips, and blew a note.
In just two blinks of an eye, she saw the letter mysteriously vanish.
Even without her glasses, she couldn't detect the arrival of the messenger.
Whew...
Cattleya exhaled softly, then walked to the captain's cabin window. As she gazed at the monotonous seascape, she thought with worry:
I wonder if Mr. Fool will notice these little actions of mine...
Jane, standing on the deck, happened to witness this scene, confirming a certain suspicion she held.
.....
On a swing woven from pea vines, Bernadette, after reading Cattleya's letter, had eyes that seemed to flow with the river of fate.
After about four or five minutes, she finally murmured thoughtfully to herself, "The detective who helped Sharon kill the 'Rose School' Wraith is also deliberately collecting Dad's manuscripts..."
.....
In a coastal city in Dacey Bay, the "invisible" Lena carefully infiltrated the City Hall. In its records, she fabricated a merchant's resume under the name of "Dwayne Dantès."
This was the final step in creating this fake identity.
After she finished these tasks, returned to her safe house, and offered her identity documents to Mr. Fool, she removed her disguise, muttering to herself:
"This way, as long as I gather 8,000 pounds, I can get the 'Demoness of Affliction's' Beyonder characteristic from the 'Black Emperor'...
"Only by becoming stronger, a 'Pirate General' or Demigod-level powerhouse, can I better protect Prince Edessak, so he doesn't have to constantly wear that heavy iron mask..."
Thinking of this, Lena became troubled again: The money is easy to get... But how do I role-play 'Pleasure'?
I've already tried it; just my own 'pleasure' isn't enough... I also need to give others 'pleasure'...
This... do I really have to do that? Is there a clever method, like when Shaw role-played 'Instigator' and 'Witch'?
Sigh... perhaps Mr. Fool knows... but I dare not ask...
.....
Backlund, In a Detached House in St. George Borough
After obtaining the identity document through the "Request for Granting" ritual, Madam Daly leaned against Dunn, chuckling, "The identity document has been obtained. I'm just waiting for you to marry me, Mr. Dwayne Dantès, the wealthy magnate."
Dunn, after reading the identity document and character profile, was momentarily stunned. He murmured, "Dwayne Dantès... what a name that truly suits my intentions."
Saying this, he rested his chin on the head of Daly, who was leaning against him, and said helplessly, "But I don't know how to act like a rich man."
Dunn's funds were just barely sufficient; his "chivalrous deeds" over the past six months had brought in a considerable income.
"Aren't you role-playing 'Iron Man' under Madam Closfia? Shouldn't you be quite familiar with this? After all, 'Iron Man' is set up as a very rich playboy," Madam Daly chuckled, feigning casualness.
Dunn's heart, however, tightened. He calmly said, "I only used the name 'Iron Man' during combat..."
At this point, he carefully released Daly from his embrace, stood up, and changed the subject, "To enter the church with you as soon as possible, I need to leave Backlund now to manage 'business' and then pretend to return."
Hearing this, Daly turned and gave him a half-smile, no longer teasing her man. She simply stroked her still-flat abdomen, a happy smile gracing her face.
.....
Outside the Ancient Vine Manor
Ebner had just gotten into his carriage outside the "Ancient Vine Manor" when a figure abruptly appeared opposite him.
The person was around 40 years old, with emerald green eyes, a shapely nose, thin lips, and brilliant golden hair, making him quite handsome.
This was Serald Delien, the "Black Knight" whose fate had been taken over by the former Pope of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun.
After sealing off the surroundings with his spirituality, the former Pope immediately knelt on one knee, devoutly calling out, "My Lord."
Ebner had met him once on the way to Trier, so he wasn't surprised. He simply nodded slightly and said, "Rise."
"Thank you for your benevolence," the former Pope praised, then stood and sat in the seat opposite Ebner .
"Last time we met, I asked you to investigate the Delien family. Do you have any results?" Ebner activated his "Pure White Eye," wasting no time on pleasantries, and asked directly.
Based on his few interactions with the man, the former Pope was quite straightforward.
"Reporting, My Lord, there are preliminary results," he responded respectfully.
"Tell me about them." Ebner's spirit lifted, and he leaned slightly forward.
The former Pope, now the "Black Knight" Serald, organized his thoughts and said:
"From what I've gathered, excluding myself, the Delien family is currently roughly divided into five factions..."
Five factions...
Ebner was speechless. The internal affairs of this family were even more absurd than Intis's political landscape.
"Which five? What are their respective strengths and influences?" Ebner asked in a deep voice.
"Firstly, the most powerful of the five factions is the 'Eternal Blazing Sun' faction. They are loyal 'Sun' believers and currently have two Demigods and five Sequence 5 powerhouses.
"The two Demigods are named Hyman and Morfee. They are both Archbishops of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun, belonging to the family in name only.
"The second is the Patriarch's direct lineage. They possess some formulas from the 'Hunter' pathway. The 'Hunter' pathway ancestor, who has lived for over a hundred years, has already reached Sequence 3 and controls a Grade '0' Sealed Artifact.
"The Patriarch's faction has mysterious origins; I don't know if they have other Demigods.
"Next is the current Prime Minister's faction... This is actually a faction that has joined different secret organizations, with a very loose structure.
"This includes Prime Minister Charlie, who joined the 'Blood Worship Sect,' Owen, who joined the Psychology Alchemists, and myself, who originally believed in the 'True Creator'...
"I haven't thoroughly investigated how many Demigods are specifically in this one, but I imagine there aren't just three... There's at least one more Demigod who joined the 'Iron-blooded Cross Society'!"

chapters.title: Chapter 819: Wheat Seedling Church
chapters.content:
Chapter 819 - Wheat Seedling Church
Although Serald hadn't finished speaking, Ebner was already quite astonished. There were already seven Demigods combined; without counting the high-end Angel-level powerhouses, this number wasn't inferior to the Augustus family of Loen!
If the Delien family's many internal factions couldn't unite, the Sauron family, currently in its twilight, probably wouldn't be able to hold onto its position as the leading family in Intis.
However, the so-called "Prime Minister's Faction," while called a faction, was actually composed of members belonging to different secret organizations, likely fraught with internal contradictions. At best, they maintained a united front against other factions.
Ebner deeply felt it was a miracle this family hadn't fractured already.
"What about the other two factions?" he asked after a moment's thought.
Serald took out a booklet, respectfully handed it to Ebner, and then replied, "The remaining 'Military Faction' and 'Industry Faction' are not strong; they exist by relying on other factions... Their boundaries aren't as clear as the other factions, and their members also have their own inclinations.
"Most of them are collateral members of the Delien family, and many don't even know about the existence of Beyonders.
"I've compiled a list, recording the affiliations and inclinations of some important figures among them."
Ebner took the list and casually flipped through it while listening to Serald's explanation. On the very first page, he saw a somewhat familiar name:
Winks Delien, Rear Admiral, member of the "Military Faction," working closely with the "Prime Minister's Faction." After being killed by Lady Scythe under the "Admiral of Stars," he was transformed into a "Sea Monster" Dependent.
"Winks... isn't this the guy who put Jane on Intis's bounty list? He actually transformed into a 'Sea Monster' Dependent...
"Hmm, perhaps a state similar to the 'Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea'? Dominated by a 'Sea Monster'?"
Ebner was surprised and questioned Serald in detail about this matter.
However, Serald wasn't entirely clear about the Delien family's cooperation with the "Sea Monster." He only knew that the "Sailor" pathway Beyonders in the family, if they didn't later join the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun, all had a chance to become "Sea Monster" Dependents after death.
Ebner unconsciously frowned, pondering:
Looking at it this way, that 'Sea Monster' is indeed a bit sinister... Thankfully, I didn't rashly go 'hunting' it...
Also, is the task Lilith gave me to "investigate the Delien family's secrets" related to this?
This family is like an iceberg in the ocean; the more you investigate, the more you feel there are deeper secrets hidden within.
So the best way is to let it collapse on its own, exposing everything...
Hmm, the original dual internal and external strategy doesn't need much change; I just need to adjust the methods for dealing with its internal affairs... The many internal factions of the Delien family actually work to my advantage.
After some thought, Ebner actively ended the discussion about the "factions" and instead asked about the current political situation in Intis.
Facing Ebner's questions, Serald was clearly prepared. He organized his words and said:
"Ever since the Prime Minister pushed for the new publishing law and strict news censorship, there has been continuous opposition.
"Opposition parties, the Church of Steam and its affiliated families, and large numbers of the middle class have united, supporting public protests and demonstrations to obstruct the passage of the bill.
"Meanwhile, old noble families from the former Sauron dynasty, such as the Frays and Flonner families, have sided with the Delien family and received a certain degree of support from the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun.
"Conversely, the Sauron family, the former masters of the old dynasty, has remained ambiguous on this matter, becoming an object of contention for both sides.
"Of course, this is only a general political alignment... In reality, even within the Delien family, attitudes towards this bill are not unified.
"For example, the 'Church Faction' supports the Prime Minister's proposal, while the 'Iron-blooded Cross Society' Demigod within the 'Prime Minister's Faction' strongly opposes it..."
The "Iron-blooded Cross Society" advocates for societal change, transforming the world so that the extraordinary are no longer hidden but revealed to all, becoming true rulers. As members of this organization, they naturally vehemently oppose news censorship.
The choice of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun is not surprising either. All orthodox churches actually control news related to the "extraordinary," as knowledge in this world is dangerous. The more one knows, the more likely it is to lead to terrible consequences...
But why is that Prime Minister, as a subordinate of the "Blood Worship Sect," actively promoting this bill? Is he trying to cover something up with it?
More importantly, Lilith has noticed the hidden problems within the Delien family; has the Eternal Blazing Sun not noticed? Is He also making arrangements here?
As for the "God of Steam"... He might truly know nothing...
As his thoughts raced, Ebner chatted with Serald about several other prominent families, learning a lot of the latest intelligence:
For instance, Johnson of the Frays family was finally released from house arrest recently and reappeared at high-society balls;
For example, although the Sali family received support from the "Church of Steam," their subordinate industries are still being encroached upon, and their political influence is weakening;
For example, the Sauron family is currently offering a reward for a young man named "Whitman." Anyone providing clues can receive 100 Fels, and finding him will earn a reward of 3000 Fels.
.....
At the Wheat Seedling Church
It wasn't until the carriage arrived at Montaigne Avenue in the "Sauron District," south of the Reyne River, stopping in front of the "Wheat Seedling Church" at number 18, that Serald, the "Black Knight" whose fate was occupied by the former Pope of the Eternal Blazing Sun, saluted Ebner and then disappeared.
—The Sauron District is named because the Sauron family's ancestral home is located here. It contains many buildings such as a military academy and a military museum. The only church of the Earth Mother Church in Trier is also located here.
The Wheat Seedling Church has a total area of 1000 square meters. To the west, there is a clock tower, about 50 meters high;
To the east is the main body of the church, which has three naves inside, including a central nave and one aisle on each side.
Compared to the Harvest Church in Backlund, this one is clearly much larger and more luxurious. Its scale even rivals the "Church of Steam's" Saint Estin Cathedral in Trier.
Alighting from the carriage, Ebner paused for a moment in the square in front of the church, looking at the people entering and exiting. He thought with emotion:
The number of believers I'm seeing right now is more than all the believers in the Harvest Church before the Great Smog event combined!
However, this is not surprising. Since the Earth Mother Church in Trier is not suppressed by the Church of Evernight as it is in Loen, its treatment is naturally much better.
Entering the church, he came to the main prayer hall, found a seat near the aisle, bowed his head, clasped his hands, and began to pray earnestly and quietly to the "Earth Mother."
A short while later, a pastor came to his side and led him to a lounge at the back of the church. Madam Helene, with beautiful silver hair, was waiting there, smiling at Ebner as he entered the room.
Perhaps there's another reason why the Wheat Seedling Church has better evangelism results than the Harvest Church... A beautiful vampire woman is clearly more likable than an old semi-giant man...
Ebner muttered to himself, while politely greeting her, "Good morning, Madam Helene."

chapters.title: Chapter 820: The Evolution of Prophecy
chapters.content:
Chapter 820 - The Evolution of Prophecy
"Good morning," Madam Helene said, her silver eyes looking over as she chuckled playfully, "Next time you visit, you should consider putting 100 Fels in the offering box. That would make it much more 'reasonable' for me to have someone bring you in here."
This trend cannot be encouraged. Earth Mother Church clergy should be as simple and honest as Bishop Utravsky.
Ebner grumbled inwardly, while outwardly nodding in response, "I'll consider it next time."
Madam Helene is indeed a bit of a money-grubbing vampire... In this regard, Cullen and Lydia are completely different from her, not at all like her biological children.
"Is there something you need from me this time? Do you want me to intercept another Demigod?" Madam Helene changed the subject, asking with a smile.
Madam, do you see me as someone who constantly causes trouble for Demigods?
While complaining inwardly, Ebner shook his head and said, "I'd like to ask you to help me find a qualified and reliable butler, preferably someone with connections in the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun...
"Additionally, I need to rent a garden villa in the Sauron District. It doesn't need to be too large, but it's best if it's not far from the Sauron family's ancestral home."
He paused here, then added, "I've already been to the 'Association for Assisting Household Servants' and the 'Housing Rental Association,' but I haven't found anything satisfactory."
After hearing Ebner's requests, Madam Helene pinched her chin in thought. After a moment, she began,
"The garden villa isn't a problem. I own a house that meets your requirements. It's a four-story building with over twenty rooms, a stable, servant quarters, and a considerably large garden. It's only a street away from the Sauron family's ancestral home, and the neighbors living nearby are Intis bankers and owners of large enterprises...
"Its furnishings are very exquisite, with many famous paintings and antiques. The furniture and utensils are also top-quality items that I personally selected..."
Ebner frowned upon hearing this, cautiously inquiring, "The rent for this house isn't cheap, is it?"
He had clearly researched the market and knew that the annual rent for similar properties wouldn't be less than 3,000 Fels.
"Of course, it's not cheap. Someone offered me 5,000 Fels in rent, and I still didn't agree." Helene first established the house's value, then changed her tone, smiling, "But what can I say, you just feel so close to me? So, as long as you can help me accomplish one thing, I'll rent this house to you for free."
"What is it?" Ebner didn't agree rashly. Although Madam Helene was Lilith's favored one and theoretically wouldn't harm him, her personality was somewhat eccentric, so it was better to be cautious.
"I want you to use your detective skills to help me find someone. She used to be called 'Shirley,' but that's undoubtedly a false name... Hmm, she's a believer of the 'Primordial Moon,' currently hiding in Trier, and I'm certain she hasn't left," Madam Helene said, her expression becoming serious.
Ebner pondered for a moment, then tentatively asked, "Is that a 'Witch King'?"
He remembered Cullen mentioning that his mother had been looking for materials for his promotion to Demigod for over a hundred years without success.
"Exactly. Her mind suddenly went awry during last week's 'Blood Moon,' exposing her whereabouts. I detected her and severely wounded her.
"But she possesses a magical item that is very adept at escaping and concealing aura, so she ultimately managed to flee... I can only vaguely sense that she's still somewhere in Trier," Madam Helene said, taking out a portrait of the person and handing it to Ebner.
Last week's Blood Moon represented the fall of the "Primordial Moon"... Not directly losing control means she either wasn't a firm believer, or her belief was actually directed towards the "Mother Tree of Desire."
Ebner accepted the portrait thoughtfully. With just a glance, he noticed something oddly unsettling about the "Witch King" named Shirley. Her facial features were distinct, yet when combined, it was impossible to remember her appearance, as if one had prosopagnosia.
"Is this her innate ability, or the power of a magical item?" Ebner asked, then continued, "Do you have any of her hair or clothing?"
"Of course not. How could a 'Witch King' possibly leave those things behind?" Madam Helene shook her head, then pointed at the portrait. "I suspect she possesses a high-Sequence Beyonder item from the 'Seer' pathway, which is why she has this strange effect that can even influence portraits."
A "Seer" pathway... some ability of a "Bizarro Sorcerer"? If she truly holds such a magical item, it's no wonder she managed to escape Madam Helene and remain unfound...
However, I can try!
After a moment of thought, Ebner activated his "Pure White Eye," directly using his once-daily "prophecy" ability.
Before, such a "prophecy" with little preliminary information and an opponent capable of concealment wouldn't yield valuable insights...
But now, with the uniqueness of the "Wheel of Fortune" entering the space behind his "Pure White Eye," Ebner could clearly feel the improvement in his "prophecy" capabilities.
Moreover, the revelations he received were no longer just a few words or a sentence. More often, they would directly show relevant scenes.
For instance, at this moment, a picture of a house with a green roof appeared before Ebner's eyes.
After noting the various details of the image, he asked Helene for paper and a pen, then set up a ritual to draw the scene he had witnessed in its entirety.
Madam Helene was somewhat surprised that Ebner had a result so quickly, but after seeing the drawing, she sighed. After all, there were too many houses in Trier that looked similar to the one in the drawing, making it impossible to pinpoint which one it was.
However, Ebner, with his many methods, was full of confidence. He believed he could find the target within a day or two, and Madam Helene's mansion was definitely going to be "freeloaded" by him.
Seeing his confident demeanor, Helene didn't think Ebner was boasting. She just smiled and said, "Then I'll await your good news...
"These two days, I'll also help you find a suitable butler and tidy up that villa."
.....
In the Bedroom on the Third Floor of Ancient Vine Manor, Trier Suburbs
Helene looked at Tracy, who was flushed and panting on the bed, unable to move. She finally withdrew her hand and said with a smile in her eyes, "That's enough for today. I still have work to do.
"Besides, Ebner said that although this technique helps with your recovery, it should also be done in moderation..."
Tracy looked at a different Helene than before, biting her lip, and asked, "What... what exactly have you learned from him?"

chapters.title: Chapter 821: Infiltrating the Prison
chapters.content:
Chapter 821 - Infiltrating the Prison
At noon, Ebner, having met up with the "Magic Mirror," or rather, Chesi, who had been handling various transfer procedures, returned to the small villa provided by the "Golf Club" and shared lunch with Fors, who had remained there.
He forked a piece of pan-fried mushrooms into his mouth, chewing as he listened to Chesi's report.
"Herta's house in the Glan District, because of its good location and luxurious decoration, was ultimately appraised at 19,000 Fels. It was listed at the auction house for just over an hour before someone bid on it, with the final offer being 22,000 Fels. Additionally, his 1% share in Sucit Bank and his shipping company stocks, since agreements were signed long ago, will be transferred to your name in one or two days, at most, once the paperwork is complete."
The "Transfer Agreements" presented by Herta, the Mirror Apostle, were clearly legitimate documents, just one step away from becoming effective. Otherwise, the "Quiz Labyrinth" wouldn't have recognized their value... This certainly made things convenient for Ebner.
Ebner drank a glass of authentic Intis white wine, wiped his mouth, and then asked, "Did you get any news about the newspaper I asked you to inquire about?"
Chesi, under the Magic Mirror's control, nodded and said very smoothly, "Affected by the 'News Control' act, many newspaper offices in Trier are unsettled, and several are already selling at low prices."
"Which ones?" Ebner asked with interest.
"The
East Shore Morning Post
,
Cerenz Weekly
, and
Rhine News
... There are also some other small newspapers up for sale, but their influence is limited and doesn't suit your status, Master!" Chesi said, picking up her own Magic Mirror to display the addresses and specific details of these newspaper offices in images.
"Even
Rhine News
can't hold on?" Fors, who had been listening in, exclaimed in surprise. "This is one of Trier's top three newspapers, very influential across the entire Northern Continent!"
She was currently holding a copy of
Rhine News
, and the headline of its second-page lead story boldly read: "Escaped Convict Murders and Frames Another, Hero Detective Identifies True Culprit."
Chesi thought for a moment, and considering Fors's relationship with her master, she answered her question. "
Rhine News
' owner, Mr. Wolff, was recently sentenced to 16 months in prison for libel. Yet, after only a week in prison, he mysteriously disappeared... This incident also became the fuse for opposition against 'News Control'... And Mr. Wolff's son, young Wolff, is a conservative and never liked his family's newspaper business. Now that he's at the center of public opinion, his resolve isn't strong enough, and he just wants to leave this troubled place in Trier... That's why he wants to sell the newspaper."
"So that's how it is..." Fors suddenly understood, then curiously asked, "How did Mr. Wolff disappear?"
"This case occurred last Friday and was reportedly assigned to Inspector Russell, known for his 'uprightness,' but there's no result yet," Chesi said with a hint of meaning.
Last Friday... wasn't that when the blood moon occurred? Could Mr. Wolff's disappearance be related to the falling of the Primordial Moon? And wasn't Inspector Russell determined by Lion Lyon to be the North family's Desire Apostle? What a coincidence.
As Fors pondered, she put a piece of bacon into her mouth.
"
Rhine News
can be put aside for now. Even if its price drops, it's still worth tens, or even hundreds of thousands of Fels... You should keep an eye on the prices of the
East Shore Morning Post
and
Cerenz Weekly
later; those are my targets..." Ebner instructed the Magic Mirror after thoroughly reviewing the situation of each newspaper.
Of course, the final decision on which to buy would have to be made by Lion Lyon, as this was the newspaper he had promised to buy for it.
It was worth noting that the lion had been by Fanny's side ever since it got off the steam train, and was not currently at the club villa, which had given Fors two days of ease.
"Yes, Master," Chesi respectfully replied.
At this point, Ebner recalled the conversation between Fors and Chesi, and with a thought, he asked, "Do you know which prison Mr. Wolff was held in?"
"Kala Prison in the Northeast District... I'm sorry, Master, I don't know the specific cell number," Chesi said, lowering her head in "shame."
"It's fine, that's enough," Ebner replied, quite satisfied.
"Ebner, do you want to investigate this case?" Fors asked in surprise.
In her understanding, Ebner wasn't a detective who enjoyed solving cases... unless the case benefited him.
Ebner smiled and replied, "Mr. Wolff might have some connection to the person I'm looking for."
If he really was a follower of the Primordial Moon...
.....
On the Rorsted Archipelago, in the "City of Generosity," Bayam.
Around 11 o'clock, Klein met the plump apothecary Ebner had mentioned above the gray fog, in the lounge of the Amyris Leaf Bar.
His gaze swept over the man, and he was suddenly stunned because the timid, chubby man before him was actually someone he knew.
Isn't this the loose-tongued, sarcastic plump apothecary from the gathering summoned by old Mr. Eye of Wisdom in Backlund? I even met him at a circus once... He stopped appearing at old Mr. Eye of Wisdom's Beyonder gatherings because he left Backlund, apparently...
Klein carefully observed the man, noting his local attire of a Taraba shirt, wide-legged trousers, and a thick coffee-colored jacket. Additionally, a round-faced owl perched silently on his right shoulder, its eyes fixed on the adventurer opposite him.
This feeling is very similar to how Miss Justice observed the other members of the Tarot Club... This owl might be a Beyonder creature, a Spectator type?
Klein made his judgment internally, but his expression remained calm as he asked in a deep voice, "What commission do you have that you asked someone to find me?"
"It's like this." The plump apothecary, hearing the cold tone and recalling the adventurer's reputation, instinctively shrank his neck. After a moment, he managed to organize his words. "I want to ask you to help me rescue someone... I originally asked Ebner, but he recommended you, saying you were more suitable."
The way you put that, it's like I'm Ebner's backup... You really don't know how to talk!
Klein grumbled inwardly, yet asked calmly, "Where do I rescue them? Who do I rescue? Is there any danger?"
Darkwill's lips moved a few times before he said, "To rescue my teacher from the Governor's Mansion prison... Uh, I can't determine the level of danger... If, if the danger exceeds your capabilities, you can simply give up. This is our agreed promise now; it won't harm your reputation."
If I didn't know you always speak so poorly, I'd think you were trying to provoke me...
Klein thought for a moment and said, "What kind of reward can you offer?"
Darkwill initially wanted to state the price he had already considered, but then he hesitated. He genuinely couldn't determine the level of danger, and even with Ebner's connection, if the offer wasn't compelling enough, it would be hard to sway Gehrman Sparrow.
However, if Teacher is successfully rescued, he can pay on my behalf, right? After all, this is for his escape...
As Darkwill pondered, Klein glanced at him and said indifferently, "You can think about it first. I'll go to the washroom; tell me your answer when I return."
With that, he turned, walked to the door, twisted the handle, and stepped out.
His response seemed seasoned, possessing the casual coolness of an adventurer and bounty hunter, but in reality, he didn't truly intend to give the plump apothecary time to think. He was simply looking for an opportunity to go to the washroom and perform a divination above the gray fog.
That was the key to whether he would accept the mission—though he had long intended to feign capture and enter the Governor's Mansion to investigate, with the rescue just a convenient side task.
After a while, Klein returned to the lounge and asked, "Have you thought about it?"
He had already divined above the gray fog that this mission would not increase the difficulty of his plan.
"1,000 pounds, and our friendship—I mean, my teacher's and my friendship," Darkwill said, somewhat unconfidently.
