Klein was silent for a few seconds. "Alright. Additionally, you need to provide some intelligence on the Governor's Mansion."
Intelligence is easy enough. Guards often buy medicine from me; I know a lot about the Governor's Mansion...
Darkwill sighed in relief and nodded. "I'll organize the intelligence for you later... However, I will only prepay you 300 pounds; my teacher will pay the rest after he's rescued."
Another pauper!
Klein nodded calmly. "Deal."
.....
The Northeast District of Trier, backed by the canal, was the smallest area of the city.
Kala Prison was located by the canal, originally a baron's castle. During Roselle's reign, the baron lost his title and moved his entire family to Masik, so the place was converted into a prison.
Since it was merely a jail for ordinary people, Ebner, using "Evans's Concealment Barrier," easily bypassed the guards and arrived before a cell with a large hole broken in its ceiling.
Was this broken from the inside? It seems Mr. Wolff indeed underwent an anomaly on the blood moon night last week?!

chapters.title: Chapter 822: Bonova’s Attention
chapters.content:
Chapter 822 - Bonova's Attention
"It seems Mr. Wolff did undergo an anomaly during last week's blood moon night! After all, that hole in the ceiling doesn't look like something a human could have made..."
Thinking this, Ebner tried to use his ability to extract auras, but in the end, he only found some residual traces from the police, nothing about Mr. Wolff.
It shouldn't have dissipated so completely in less than a week... Was it cleaned up by someone?
His thoughts swirling, he activated his "Pure White Eye," using the even more powerful "Aura Extraction" ability of his "cheat" to search the cell again. Finally, he extracted a trace of Mr. Wolff's aura from around the edge of the broken hole.
Then, he immediately began "Scene Recall."
Soon, a middle-aged gentleman with striking features, a graceful demeanor, and only a slightly receding hairline appeared before Ebner.
He had been reading a magazine by candlelight in the room, but just then, the moonlight outside the cell suddenly intensified, as if stained with fresh blood. Mr. Wolff then clutched his head in pain, his teeth immediately became sharp, his skin rapidly turned pale, then rotten and oozing pus, and bat-like fleshy wings grew from his back...
In just a few seconds, Mr. Wolff transformed into a small "sun," a disgusting, pus-oozing vampire that Mr. Moon often described after joining the Tarot Club.
Once the transformation was complete, he seemed unable to bear the pain and the craving for blood any longer. He immediately smashed through the cell's roof and flew into the air.
The scene ended there.
He really is a vampire... So, it seems he's likely a follower of the Primordial Moon as well, and it's highly probable he has ties to the Witch King Ms. Helene is looking for... perhaps even a blessed one converted by her.
Then, there might be residual aura from that Witch King, Miss Silvia, in Mr. Wolff's residence! If there truly is, this matter becomes much simpler...
Ebner felt a surge of excitement. His original plan was to rely on the investigated clues and, after his "prophecy" ability recovered tomorrow, perform another "diviner" operation to determine the location of the green-roofed house he had seen earlier.
If all else failed, he could "Teleport" back to Backlund or the
Golden Dream
to ask Xio or Edwina for help in summoning Arrodes and asking the fawning mirror for the answer. This was the source of his confidence when he had spoken with Ms. Helene.
Now that he had a clue, it might not be so troublesome after all...
While he thought this, a hint of regret appeared on Ebner's face, as he had quite looked forward to Xio or Edwina "answering questions" again.
Just as Ebner was about to leave, voices suddenly drifted from a distance, growing closer. He immediately stopped, hiding in a corner of the cell using "Evans's Concealment Barrier."
Soon, the cell door opened, and five police officers entered from outside.
Among the five, one was a prison guard holding keys, whose attitude towards the others was quite fawning. Next to him was a probationary inspector, only in his twenties, whose back was ramrod straight and whose attitude towards the three behind him was neither humble nor arrogant.
Walking at the very back were two men and one woman, none appearing over thirty, dressed in inspector uniforms, with the "Seventh Special Operations Team" badge pinned to their chests.
Ebner, who was familiar with the official Intis church organizations, knew that the so-called Seventh Special Operations Team of the Trier police department actually represented a "Machinery Hivemind" squad.
It seems Mr. Wolff is a follower of the God of Steam and Machinery... That makes sense; as a vampire, even his feigned faith wouldn't be in the Sun...
As Ebner pondered, he watched the female member of the "Machinery Hivemind" squad use some kind of witchcraft, attempting to extract Mr. Wolff's aura.
But this place had clearly been deliberately cleaned, and even Ebner, with his Pure White Eye, only found a tiny trace at the broken hole, so the Witch Miss naturally returned empty-handed.
Seeing his teammate shake her head helplessly, the leader of the "Machinery Hivemind" squad, a man with short brown hair, frowned and asked, "Who else came here before us?"
The prison guard glanced at the young inspector beside him, and seeing no reaction, he carefully replied, "Only Inspector Russell brought people to investigate."
"Why wasn't such an obvious Beyonder incident reported in time?" another man with a full beard couldn't help but demand. "Our 'Special Operations Team' only found out about the change here from the newspapers! Also, where is Russell? Doesn't he know the importance of a case like this? This is dereliction of duty! Do you know that in our jurisdiction alone, at least ten people have been drained of their blood and died in the past two days?"
Seeing them insult his master and idol, the upright young man couldn't help but argue, "Inspector Russell's wife was assassinated by thugs on the train, so he took leave to handle the aftermath... Besides, the inspector judged at the time that the house was blown open by explosives and didn't involve Beyonder elements..."
"Heh, I heard about that too... If you ask me, he brought it on himself. That escaped convict's life was already on track, but he just had to interfere, ruining the man's home and family..." The bearded man clearly disliked Russell's style and scoffed.
"Hmph! The inspector was upholding 'justice'! And the facts prove that guy was a cruel murderer!" The probationary inspector snorted.
The bearded man was about to say more but was stopped by the short-haired man leading the team. "Pierre, we're here to investigate the case, not to argue."
"Captain, I feel sorry for Bishop Therese... She had clearly guided that person onto a path of goodness, and he had found happiness through effort and diligence... Everything was so perfect... but it was ruined by Russell's so-called 'justice'!" The bearded man said indignantly.
"So, he really did steal the church's golden lever back then? Heh, I knew Bishop Therese was helping him cover it up! The bishop is too kind; she doesn't know that evil people are always evil and can never turn good!" The young probationary inspector was clearly deeply influenced by the "upright" Russell and had fully adopted his ideology.
Ultimately, both sides parted unhappily, with the young probationary inspector leaving directly, leaving only the three Beyonders to continue investigating the cell.
After dispatching the prison guard as well, the captain frowned and said, "Inspector Russell might have some issues."
"What?" The most surprised was the bearded Pierre. Although he disliked Russell's methods, deep down he actually admired his adherence to "the law."
"This judgment was made by His Highness Bonova a few days ago, when he happened to hear about Russell's deeds... He said that Russell was replicating a story Roselle had told. Coupled with the fact that the aura in this cell was cleaned up very thoroughly, and the reporting time was delayed... I have reason to suspect he tampered with this case," the captain calmly stated.
"Then why not just arrest him directly?" The bearded Pierre instinctively asked.
The captain glanced at his teammate, too lazy to reply.
The "Witch" lady beside them smiled bitterly and shook her head. "There are many problematic people in Trier, even in every major family! But without conclusive evidence strong enough for a death sentence, we can't just arrest people... This is an unspoken agreement between the Church and the various Beyonder families. Although Russell's background isn't strong, the 'reputation' bestowed upon him also provides very strong protection."
Upon hearing this, Pierre immediately deflated. He pouted and casually asked, "How would a big shot like His Highness Bonova notice the affairs of a mere inspector?"
The captain was silent for a moment before saying, "Regarding that, I heard a rumor... It's said that His Highness Bonova's recent interest in Inspector Russell's matter is just incidental; what he truly wants to understand is that detective from Loen, Ebner Brain!"
Ebner, hidden in the corner, felt his eyelid twitch when he heard this. He immediately activated his "Mechanical Mind," which allowed him to stabilize "Evans's Concealment Barrier" and prevent his shock from being transmitted.
Bonova is Old Huang's angel son, right? Why is he paying attention to me for no reason?

chapters.title: Chapter 823: Lilith’s Influence
chapters.content:
Chapter 823 - Lilith's Influence
Is it because Lion Lyon has been following me?
Is it because I have Lilith's 'blessing'?
Or is it because I previously disrupted Roselle's resurrection plan, and he learned something?
Even after the three "Machinery Hivemind" team members left, Ebner couldn't determine why Bonova was paying attention to him.
After all, he was just an ordinary Sequence 5; why would an Angel pay him any mind?
Alright, I admit, I am a little bit special.
After a self-deprecating thought, Ebner didn't linger in the prison. After confirming there were no hidden observers in the cell, he used "Teleportation" to return directly to the "Golf Club."
He didn't plan to go to Mr. Wolff's house to look for clues. After the "Machinery Hivemind" got involved, that place would surely be monitored... And since even the prison cell's aura traces had been cleaned up, Mr. Wolff's house was probably tampered with too!
The "blood-sucking" incidents the "Machinery Hivemind" members mentioned earlier, however, were a better entry point. As long as he found Mr. Wolff himself, he should be able to get many clues about the "Witch King" Silvia... As long as there were enough clues, he could get a more accurate picture once his "prophecy" ability recovered tomorrow.
The location of the most recent "blood-sucking" incident happened to be on Carlot Street, not far from the "Golf Club," just one street away.
If Ebner hadn't been busy running to Bayam last night to bring Tracy back to "Ancient Vine Manor," perhaps he, remaining at the club, would have sensed the attack, and the tragedy wouldn't have occurred...
Of course, Ebner merely sighed briefly and didn't dwell on it. He had long since established his code of conduct: he would only consider helping when he encountered a situation and had the ability to help; if he didn't encounter it, and unless it was a friend's trouble, he wouldn't actively seek out involvement.
In other words, helping was a favor, not helping was his prerogative, and he only needed to have a clear conscience.
Leaving the club, Ebner changed his appearance, disguising himself as a reporter, and made his way to the house at 11 Carlot Street.
This was a detached house with a garden in the back, with an annual rent of around 250 Fels. In this area, it wasn't luxurious, but it also wasn't affordable for an average middle-class family.
It was precisely because the victim in this case was a prominent tobacco merchant that it attracted official attention, leading to a reverse investigation that uncovered several similar "blood-sucking" incidents in the East Slums.
Since the murder had occurred almost a day ago, the police had already finished their evidence collection, so they didn't stop reporters like Ebner, allowing them to interview and question the servants, only prohibiting photography.
After feigning a few uninspired questions to a distressed maid, Ebner went to the primary crime scene—the basement.
Honestly, this location confused Ebner greatly.
After all, it was strange enough for a tobacco merchant to be in the basement at night instead of sleeping. And the vampire let go of the more flavorful blood of the maids in the house to chase after a fat, big-headed merchant's blood in the basement... This was simply too bizarre!
Unless Mr. Wolff had some peculiar fetish.
As he muttered to himself, Ebner activated his Pure White Eye and began extracting auras from various spots in the basement.
Logically, a place like a basement shouldn't have too many visitors, so the auras should belong to only a few specific individuals. However, Ebner was astonished to find that the auras here were incredibly complex, with at least 100 or more people having stayed there!
Yet, it seemed that some Demigod-level power had tampered with the area, making the auras in the basement very difficult to extract. If not for the boost from Ebner's Pure White Eye, he probably wouldn't have discovered them on his own.
"Most of these auras... are from young girls..." After sifting through the auras one by one, Ebner had some unpleasant suspicions. He narrowed his eyes, mentally prepared himself, and began his "Recall."
What followed were scenes that filled him with anger.
It turned out that the owner of this house, whose identity as a "tobacco merchant" was merely a disguise, was actually a "blood slave" to vampires! He used the pretext of hiring female workers to trick young girls into his basement periodically, for his masters to feast upon and enjoy... And this had been going on for at least a year or two!
Among those masters, Ebner saw the well-dressed Mr. Wolff, the Witch King Silvia whose face was obscured, and an unfamiliar man wearing a hood.
But last night, the utterly wicked tobacco merchant encountered an accident while entertaining one of his "masters." That "vampire" seemed to have changed its taste, sparing the innocent girl and instead drinking the merchant's sinful blood, sucking him dry until he died!
Afterward, Mr. Wolff surprisingly let the unconscious girl go, sending her out of the house...
The "Recall" scene ended there.
Ebner frowned, a little surprised, as Mr. Wolff's transformation was beyond his expectations...
He had thought that the other party was not being picky because of a "loss of control," even consuming his own "blood slave."
Is this... a lingering effect of the Primordial Moon's fall?
Quite possibly... Perhaps Mr. Wolff was a devout follower of the Primordial Moon, and as its Beauty Goddess characteristic merged with Lilith, his disposition even changed in order to get closer to the deity?
Is Lilith making all Primordial Moon followers drink only the blood of "sinful" people?
Hmm, I'll investigate the East Slums later to see if those who were previously sucked dry were also villains... However, this effect should only be limited to mid-to-low sequences, and only for vampires who originally held a pure faith in the Primordial Moon...
Having made a judgment, Ebner suddenly felt that finding Mr. Wolff might not be so troublesome. If he prayed to the Earth Mother, the other party might just come to him, just like "that... undying... idiot" who sought out Klein in the original novel.
Though he thought this, Ebner first used a secret art to collect the residual auras of Wolff, Silvia, and the hooded man, keeping them for backup, before leaving the tobacco merchant's house.
Next, he changed his appearance again, rented a room in a nearby hotel, set up a ritual, prepared the "Daniel Dew," and began to pray earnestly to the Earth Mother.
Two or three seconds later, the ritual ended, the dew vanished, and the other powdered materials moved on their own, forming word after word: "Try to use 'Wheel of Fortune' as little as possible before becoming a Demigod. The more fortunate and smooth things are now, the more terrifying the bad luck will be later."

chapters.title: Chapter 824: Target Confirmed
chapters.content:
Chapter 824: Target Confirmed
Use "Wheel of Fortune" less... This should refer to the Wheel of Fortune Uniqueness after the Pure White Eye, right?
I only seemed to borrow its power during previous "prophecies"... No wonder my search for Silvia was so smooth; not only did I happen to learn about Mr. Wolff from Chesi, but I even happened to encounter the Machinery Hivemind during my prison investigation, gaining important clues...
It seems the combination of the Wheel of Fortune Uniqueness and the Pure White Eye’s own "prophecy" ability not only gives me more accurate results during "prophecy" but also keeps me at a certain level of "luck" until I achieve the purpose of this "prophecy"!
However, this "luck" obviously comes at a price... overdrafting the future!
Understanding this, Ebner decided to heed Lilith’s warning and try to use this "prophecy" ability, which he couldn’t fully control, as little as possible before becoming a Demigod, so as to avoid overdrawing the future with the Wheel of Fortune again.
Fortunately, if there was truly urgent information he needed, he could still seek divination from Mr. Fool, or have Xio and Edwina summon the Magic Mirror.
—
It wasn’t that Ebner didn’t want to summon Arrodes himself, but he had tried before, and it simply wouldn’t come, seemingly very resistant to him.
As Ebner cleaned up the ritual items and pondered, the window of the hotel room was suddenly blown open by a gust of wind. A group of ethereal bats then flew in from outside, subsequently converging into a figure dressed in a black formal suit.
It was an elegant, graceful, middle-aged gentleman with a slightly receding hairline—none other than Mr. Wolff, the owner of
Rhine News
.
As soon as he stood still, he bowed solemnly with Intis etiquette, his attitude extremely respectful. At the same time, the window closed on its own without a sound.
Ebner had anticipated his arrival, but hadn’t expected it to be so soon, so he merely paused for a moment before adopting a poised demeanor and nodding, "Wolff, you’re here."
After experiencing the humble attitudes of two former Popes of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun’s evil spirits, Ebner’s experience in "acting like a big shot" was now second only to Mr. Fool.
Wolff, the "Vampire," maintained his subordinate posture and spoke in a deep voice, "Parker Wolff has come to see His Blessedship by divine oracle. God commanded me to obey your orders and accept your arrangements from today onwards."
It’s a pity you can’t show yourself now, otherwise I would have had you offer the newspaper directly to God...
Mumbling to himself, Ebner asked, "What happened to the girl you took away last night?"
He wanted to know if the other party had truly abandoned his evil ways under Lilith’s influence...
Of course, as a former follower of the Primordial Moon, his mind was already twisted, and he probably didn’t even think he was doing evil.
"Reporting to His Blessedship... I have sent that girl back to the East Slums... Since she was unconscious the entire time and didn’t know what happened, I did not erase her memory," Wolff replied, bowing his head.
I see... Although from the results of "Mind Reading," he doesn’t seem to be lying to me, I can investigate this when I go to the East Slums later to confirm the identities of those who died from "blood-sucking" incidents.
While thinking this, Ebner didn’t forget the main task. He carefully phrased his words, "I am pursuing the whereabouts of the blasphemer who has abandoned God, the Witch King Silvia. Can you provide any clues?"
Since Lilith didn’t directly give the Witch King’s location, it means that the other party’s former faith wasn’t in the true Primordial Moon, and thus she escaped Lilith’s influence.
Hearing that Silvia was a "blasphemer," Wolff was somewhat surprised, but his face immediately showed hatred, and he said in a low voice, "So, Your Excellency the Witch King... no, Silvia has abandoned God... No wonder she hasn’t responded to my meeting requests these past few days! However, I’m sorry, Your Blessedship... I don’t know exactly where she is now, I only have some guesses..."
With that, he listed several secret strongholds, all of which he believed to be Silvia’s possible hiding places.
Ebner thought for a moment, took out the drawing of the green-roofed house he had sketched after his "prophecy" from his pocket, showed it to Wolff, and asked, "Among those hiding places you mentioned, is there this green-roofed house in the drawing?"
"No..." Wolff glanced at it and affirmed. Then he held the drawing, examining it for a long time, and then said uncertainly, "This house... I think it looks like a property of Tan’de..."
"Tan’de?" Ebner frowned, feeling as if he had heard that name somewhere before.
Wolff organized his words and replied, "Tan’de was a member of the Moses Ascetic Order. A few months ago, he protected Envoy Owen of the Delien family who went to the Loen Kingdom. Later, he reportedly died at the hands of an Aurora Order Divine Emissary.
"I was somewhat friends with him. I went to his house a few times to help him prepare potions, so I recognize this roof. Oh, right, Tan’de’s teacher is a Bizarro Sorcerer from the Moses Ascetic Order. He was going to investigate in Backlund after hearing that Tan’de died at the hands of the Aurora Order Divine Emissary... but then there was no further news."
I knew that sounded familiar! So, it was that unlucky guy who was pastured by Mr. A! That means his soul is still in my Magic Mirror... Heh, is this also "luck" brought by the Wheel of Fortune? Also, could Tan’de’s teacher have been made into a magical item by the Witch King Silvia? Ms. Helene did speculate that Silvia had a Bizarro Sorcerer ability as a Sealed Artifact...
Thinking this, Ebner, having basically achieved his goal, stood up and simulated his Teleportation ability, preparing to take Wolff to the East Slums to confirm if he had truly changed under Lilith’s influence.
If it was true, he would temporarily spare his life, let him continue to consume the blood of evil people to atone for his past misdeeds; if it was false, he would immediately add him to the Tarot Club’s "fresh ingredients" list.
Facts proved that the Beauty Goddess was indeed quite reliable in the domain of soul domination. Wolff had been completely twisted in nature on the night of the blood moon, thoroughly becoming another version of himself, so he hadn’t lied to Ebner earlier.
This implies that after Lilith reclaimed the Beauty Goddess characteristic, a considerable portion of the mid-to-low Sequence Beyonders among the original Primordial Moon followers will likely undergo a subtle change in temperament, becoming "harmless" individuals... This alone makes the "Silver Moon Project" of the Transmigrator seniors and the two goddesses worth my continued promotion!
After a few internal remarks, Ebner made an agreement with Wolff about how to meet, then let him leave. He himself teleported back to the "club" villa, and then had the Magic Mirror interrogate Tan’de, the pastured Marionettist.
Soon, the Magic Mirror’s surface displayed images formed from parts of Tan’de’s memories: He and Silvia met at a ball, and afterward, according to Intis custom, the two quickly became passionate lovers.
Silvia’s beautiful face and superb "technique" left a lasting impression on Tan’de, so much so that he even leaked a lot of information about his teacher during their intimate moments.
He hadn’t thought much of it at the time, but reflecting on it afterward, he felt something was amiss. Just as he was about to go explain the situation to his teacher, he received the mission to protect Envoy Owen Delien to the Loen Kingdom, forcing him to temporarily put it aside, leaving only a letter...
Finally, the house where he and Silvia often met had a green roof. It was located at 33 Radfang Avenue in the South District, adjacent to Brony Park.
Seeing this, Ebner understood, guessing that Silvia approached Tan’de mostly because of his teacher.
The reason Tan’de didn’t even notice such an obvious problem was likely due to Silvia’s own influence on him—as a Potions Professor at the Demigod level, it would probably be very easy for her to use drugs to bewilder a Sequence 5 without a strong background during intimate moments.
Even more ridiculously, Tan’de was completely unaware of his lover’s true identity. When he was unable to perform, he even went to Wolff for medicine...
Shaking his head, Ebner thought for a moment, then took the Magic Mirror, left the bedroom, and knocked on Fors’s door.
"Come in, the door’s not locked," Fors’s lazy voice came from inside.
Ebner pushed open the slightly ajar door and saw Fors casually reclining on the sofa, eating snacks while reading an Intis novel.
Miss Magician is getting more and more casual around me... almost catching up to Xio...
Ebner’s mouth twitched. He then walked over, took her snacks, and pulled her up, saying, "Come out with me for a walk in the park, and get your ’exercise’ for today."
This was a "supervision" task Xio had given Ebner before they left Backlund.
Fors, now standing, eyed him suspiciously for a few moments, then her eyes darted, remembering something, and she smiled. "You want me to help you provide cover?"
"That’s right," Ebner admitted directly.
If Chesi hadn’t been a follower of the Mother Tree of Desire before, "she" would actually be the best candidate, but unfortunately she was... so he couldn’t risk it.
"Then let’s go." Fors didn’t act coy and immediately got up to change clothes in the inner room.
She was thinking to herself: Ebner always helped her, and it was rare to have an opportunity to return the favor now. If she didn’t seize it, she might really have to become his lover in the future...
Soon, Fors, in her new clothes, and Ebner left together. They took a carriage to the South District of Trier, then posed as a couple and slowly walked towards Brony Park.
The reason they didn’t use secret arts or "Psychological Invisibility" to investigate directly, choosing this roundabout method instead, was out of concern that the Witch King, who might be nearby, would see through them. If that happened, while there wouldn’t be much danger, it would alert her and cause her to change her hiding place, making her even harder to find.
Ebner wouldn’t underestimate any Demigod, especially one who hadn’t appeared in the original work and whose background was completely unknown.
He let Fors link arms with him, and they "intimately" approached the bushes at the edge of the park, getting close to the green-roofed house’s courtyard wall.
Fors’s face was a little red, because she could already hear some not-so-normal breathing sounds from the bushes not far away...
—
Brony Park was a famous lovers’ park in Trier, and Tan’de’s memories included coming here with Silvia for outdoor recreation.
However, Ebner’s eyes narrowed, because through "Aura Extraction," he confirmed that the person breathing rapidly in the nearby bushes was none other than the Witch King Silvia!
At this moment, she was biting the left side of a bald man’s neck, passionately sucking his blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 825: Encounter Battle
chapters.content:
Chapter 825: Encounter Battle
Just as Ebner’s gaze fell upon the
Shaman King
Silvia, her previously intoxicated expression suddenly froze, and a pair of blood-red eyes turned to look directly at Ebner and Fors.
Then, her beautiful face twisted, and she left the bald man beneath her, shooting toward Ebner like a cannonball!
Directly encountering a "half-mad" Shaman King? Is this also good fortune granted by the Wheel of Fortune? Well, according to some novel tropes, this indeed counts as an opportunity... but I don’t want it at all! Actually, this kind of "good fortune" already has some hint of "backlash," completely unlike the pure benefits from before... It seems that before becoming a Demigod, it’s truly not suitable to use "Prophecy" combined with the Wheel of Fortune Uniqueness effect anymore.
Seeing the
Shaman King
’s attack arriving in an instant, Ebner, who had the Beauty Goddess’s blessing on him, showed no panic and even had the leisure to quip a few words.
He had prepared contingency plans for various unexpected situations before coming, and for the current situation, he had already readied his methods.
Just as the Shaman King’s sharp nails were about to touch Ebner’s neck, patterns on the latter’s forehead gradually lit up. Immediately afterward, Silvia’s hand unconsciously deviated, pointing towards herself, as if she would rather harm herself than harm the man before her.
This sudden turn of events stunned even the half-mad Silvia, but she quickly regained her senses because a scorching pure white ray condensed in the "mirror" in the man’s hand and directly struck her.
The ray then burst forth with intense light, dissolving all undeath, darkness, and evil.
The Witch King Silvia instantly ignited with whitish flames, like a paper figure held close to glowing coals.
That was indeed a paper figure, seemingly condensed from crimson moonlight.
Witch King substitution art, Moon Paper Figure!
As the paper figure turned to ash, the half-mad Shaman King reappeared on the bald man’s body, casting a cold gaze towards Ebner.
But as a Mysticism Magister, since Ebner chose to act, how could his attack be interrupted? Thus, just as Silvia appeared, a massive demon abruptly materialized behind her, followed by a "Magma Sword" burning with the smell of sulfur, mercilessly striking down from above.
—
This was a "Devil" soul released beforehand by the Magic Mirror.
Although Silvia was insane, her battle instincts were still intact. She immediately tried to create a red moon and then use the moonlight to disperse her body, dodging the attack.
But she quickly found she couldn’t do it, because a few meters around her had, at some point, been enveloped by "twisted" rules, making it difficult for the "Red Moon" to rise from within her body.
This was naturally Ebner using the Mutated Tudor Emblem to construct an environment with rules favorable to himself.
However, Silvia still managed to dodge this almost certain hit because she held a Bizarro Sorcerer sequence Sealed Artifact in her hand!
She took out a short staff and gripped it. As the gem at its tip lit up, her figure was instantly ignited by the "Magma Sword," regressing into a burning piece of paper that rapidly turned to ash.
"Paper Figure Substitution"! At the moment the Demigod-level "Magma Sword" reached her, she used "Paper Figure Substitution" just in time!
Her figure, dressed only in a white shirt with almost no other clothing, then appeared on the park wall. Immediately after, she raised her other hand and unleashed a "Blood Moon Arrow."
But Ebner had long anticipated her response. Just as her hand, which had raised the short staff, had yet to retract, the detective, in his Mechanical Mind state, gripped his cane—modified from a Harris Rapier—and unleashed a secret art he had developed: "Disintegration."
Logically, the success rate of this spell was very low and not really suitable for practical combat... But Ebner had a strange feeling that his attempt this time would surely succeed! This should be a blessing from the "good fortune" granted by the Wheel of Fortune...
While thinking this, Ebner pulled out a card and took out the
Groselle’s Travels
sealed within it.
With a "thwack," the "Blood Moon Arrow" accurately hit the book cover Ebner held against his chest, then vanished without a trace, as if it had never existed.
With another "thwack," the short staff in Silvia’s hand completely shattered, breaking into pieces of material and gems.
The abilities of a Bizarro Sorcerer were strange and varied, with extremely high life-saving capabilities, making them truly troublesome. So, before acting, Ebner had already made arrangements specifically targeting the magical item in Silvia’s hand, aiming to "destroy" it immediately!
If "Disintegration" didn’t succeed, he had also prepared a specialized method to "seduce" Sealed Artifacts into betraying their owners—
"Beloved Defection Art."
Although the original success rate of this secret art, learned from the latter half of
Feast of Blood
, was even lower than "Disintegration," it became different with the Beauty Goddess’s blessing.
After all, even a Sealed Artifact wouldn’t bear to harm the Beauty Goddess and would defect to her.
At this moment, the Shaman King Silvia saw her short staff shattered on the ground, and her beautiful face twisted even more. She stared directly into Ebner’s pure white eyes, activating the Shaman King’s unique "Dark Gaze." Then, she dug out her own eyeball and squeezed it hard, intending to inversely affect Ebner through manipulating her own eyeball.
After all, a Shaman King possessed regenerative and self-healing abilities and speed beyond imagination. After the battle ended, it wouldn’t take long for new eyeballs to grow.
But her plan was good, yet she misjudged her opponent...
How could a Demigod-level "Dark Gaze" possibly destroy something of the Pure White Eye’s caliber?
So, she suffered a terrifying backlash, and the eyeball she had just squeezed instantly burst!
"Aow!" After a shriek that was not quite human, the half-mad Shaman King Silvia seemed to regain some clarity due to the intense pain. She eyed Ebner with dread, no longer willing to fight, and directly flung two Blood Moon Arrows at Fors, who had been hiding in the corner since the battle began, hoping to interfere with the man’s pursuit so she could calmly retreat.
Ebner watched Silvia decompose into a swarm of ethereal-yet-real vampiric bats, scattering and flying away, a smile playing on his lips. He then Flashed in front of Fors, using
Groselle’s Travels
to block the Blood Moon Arrows once more.
Although Ebner, wielding a "miracle," wasn’t worried that Fors would die from this—this was why he dared to bring her to such a dangerous place—since his objective had been achieved, there was no need to let Miss Magician experience the pain of death.
This encounter, though described as troublesome, actually lasted only a minute from start to finish. Fors had just managed to pull out the Marionette Ebner gave her for self-defense and hadn’t even had time to offer help.
Now, seeing the enemy flee, she steadied herself and asked worriedly, "Ebner, aren’t you going after her?"
That was a Demigod; although she seemed to be in poor condition, what if she healed and came back for revenge?
"Don’t worry, she can’t escape!" Ebner smiled confidently at Fors, making the latter freeze, her heart pounding.
At this moment, the Magic Mirror, controlling the "Devil" soul, sent a drop of blood that Silvia had sprayed when her eye burst, along with the shattered fragments of the "short staff," near Ebner and Fors.
—
Although the Shaman King had cautiously cleaned up her blood and hair as she fled, the unexpected bursting of her eyeball and the spell’s backlash caused some blood to splash around, which the prepared Magic Mirror easily collected. It also spiritually sealed it to prevent the other party from using secret arts to evaporate and self-destruct the blood.
Speaking of which, even if Silvia hadn’t foolishly played "eye-swapping" with Ebner, the latter had already planned to spend money to "buy" a Demigod-level "Aurora" from the Quiz Labyrinth’s storage, which Roselle likely sold to the labyrinth, to bleed out that half-mad Shaman King...
"Sigh, if only the Quiz Labyrinth could pull in people of my own Sequence to answer questions, it wouldn’t be this troublesome..."
Sighing inwardly, Ebner ignored the materials containing Bizarro Sorcerer characteristics. He simply took the Shaman King’s blood offered by the Magic Mirror and smeared it onto the cover of
Groselle’s Travels
.He had never imagined that he, a mere Sequence 5, could single-handedly kill a vampire Demigod skilled at "surviving," even if the other party was briefly suppressed by him due to madness...
But a Demigod is a Demigod; their life level has the characteristics of a "God." It would be almost impossible for him to kill one on his own! What’s more, if he really pushed the other party too hard, she might disregard everything and activate her "incomplete mythological creature" form, at which point he might very well be counter-killed!
Therefore, all of Ebner’s contingency plans for an encounter battle revolved around injuring the opponent and making them bleed.
Watching the drop of blood smeared on
Groselle’s Travels
inexplicably become illusory and then disappear, Ebner opened the book. He indeed saw that the previously stuck-together pages had thinned, and the book opened two more pages.
Those two pages recounted the story of a somewhat deranged one-eyed vampire encountering the King of the North in a blizzard. They battled fiercely, with neither side gaining the upper hand.
After Silvia entered the travelogue, the sleeping King of the North indeed got up to work... Hmm, it’s best to find someone to surround and kill her before she meets the "protagonist" team!
Having made his decision, Ebner didn’t linger in the park. He grabbed Fors’s arm and Teleported them to the lounge of the Wheat Seed Church, a Earth Mother church.
Shortly after they left, a ray of light descended from the sky, forming a middle-aged clergyman wearing the robes of a Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun bishop.
He had a thick black beard, appearing somewhat aged, but it was evident he must have been a handsome man in his youth, with deeply carved facial features. This was Morphy Delien, the Archbishop of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun in Trier.
He looked at the potholes corroded by the Blood Moon Arrows in the bushes, then at the naked, half-dead bald man lying on the ground, and couldn’t help but frown.
Soon, the Archbishop of the Machinery Hivemind also flew in, using a special propulsion device, landing in the park.
Then, the Archbishop’s eyes "opened" on their own sides, and a pair of spectacles rose from within. He carefully observed the scene through his "spectacles" and asked with a frown, "I felt a Demigod-level ability erupt earlier... What happened here? It doesn’t seem to have caused much destruction or casualties."
"I don’t know, I only arrived half a minute before you," Morphy replied, then pointed at the bald man on the ground and continued, "What’s certain is that one of the parties was a Demigod-level vampire."
"An action by the Baron of Corruption?" the Archbishop of the Machinery Hivemind said thoughtfully.
"Very likely... but they won’t admit it," Morphy nodded gravely.
Although the Earth Mother church was allowed to form Beyonder teams in Trier, their jurisdiction was limited to the "Soren District," where their church was located.
"I’ll have people try to find clues. If we get conclusive evidence, we’ll pressure the Earth Mother church together," Morphy said to the Archbishop of the Machinery Hivemind beside him.
The Archbishop of the Machinery Hivemind scoffed, replying, "Don’t investigate yourselves, only to find it leads back to your Delien family!"
It seemed his relationship with Morphy wasn’t very harmonious.
Morphy was silent for a moment, then finally stated, "If it leads back to my family, we’ll still handle it officially! ’Justice’ is our Lord’s doctrine!"
The Archbishop of the Machinery Hivemind pursed his lips, revealing the "gears" at the corners of his mouth, clearly not believing him much.
.....
In the lounge of the Wheat Seed Church, Ebner, who had just teleported there, looked at the familiar figure before him and exclaimed in surprise, "Miss Chloe, what are you doing here?"

chapters.title: Chapter 826: Hidden Secrets
chapters.content:
Chapter 826: Hidden Secrets
Closfia smoothed her chestnut-brown hair and responded with a playful smile, "Why
shouldn’t
I be here?"
As she spoke, her gaze drifted toward Fors, who still looked somewhat dazed beside Ebner. With a teasing glint in her eyes, she pointed at the young woman—whose demeanor bore a faint resemblance to her own—and remarked, "If you keep flirting like this, the Countess waiting all alone at that hot spring villa in Feysac might get upset."
Countess? Wasn’t that "Greed" lady hypnotized into... well, whatever by you? What does that have to do with me?
Ebner inwardly grumbled but knew better than to engage in a battle of wits with a seasoned "Spectator" like her. Instead, he changed the subject. "Where’s Ms. Helen?"
"Helen is distributing ’Holy Communion.’ She’ll be back soon." After answering briefly, Closfia’s expression turned uncharacteristically serious. "That was just a joke. I’m actually here on a mission from the ’Mother Goddess.’"
She paused, then added with a smirk, "To put it simply, I’ve been
sold
to you..."
Ebner, long accustomed to her antics, didn’t take the bait. Closfia loved playing the coquette and had a penchant for teasing. He simply stared at her, his expression clearly conveying:
Cut the nonsense and get to the point.
"How boring..." Disappointed that she hadn’t managed to fluster him, Closfia sighed before explaining properly: "The ’Classical Alchemist’ Beyonder characteristic you offered to the ’Mother Goddess’ wasn’t free... By Her decree, I’m to protect you until you become a demigod. Only then will my task be complete."
She grinned. "During this time, I’ll follow your arrangements."
So when the Mother Goddess took the "Classical Alchemist" characteristic as payment, it was to assign me a bodyguard?
But as one of Her devout followers, Closfia wouldn’t need such incentives... Was this just to ensure her cooperation was more proactive?
Ebner didn’t doubt her words. No matter how eccentric Closfia was, she wouldn’t dare joke about the edicts of a true deity.
"I see... With the ’Classical Alchemist’ characteristic, Judy will probably advance to demigod soon," Ebner mused aloud while stepping to the door and peeking into the prayer hall. The distribution of "Holy Communion" was only halfway done.
"She’s still far from ready. Forget the ritual—she hasn’t even fully digested her ’Druid’ potion yet." For the first time, a trace of genuine maternal concern flickered across Closfia’s face as she shook her head.
After exchanging a few more words with the "Sloth" lady, Ebner realized Helen wouldn’t be free for a while. Rather than wait idly, he first teleported Fors back to the townhouse provided by the "Club," then took a moment to pray to "The Fool" and borrow the "Black Emperor Card" to prepare for his next safe entry into
Groselle’s Travels
. Only then did he return to the rest area of the Wheat Seed Cathedral.
By now, Helen had finished her duties and was sipping tea with Closfia while waiting for him.
"You came looking for me specifically... Does this mean you’ve made progress on my request?" Helen’s eyes gleamed as she guessed Ebner’s purpose.
"Exactly. I’ve trapped her inside this book." Ebner produced
Groselle’s Travels
and briefly explained its abilities.
Upon hearing that the book contained a world imagined by the "King of Dragons," Helen remained composed, but Closfia’s eyes lit up with excitement. "Can I join the hunt for that ’Shaman King’?" she asked eagerly.
"Since Mr. Bryan didn’t avoid discussing it in front of you, he must intend to bring you along," Helen remarked. Though she, too, was intrigued by the imaginary world, her primary concern was securing the "Shaman King" characteristic for her son.
"Just as Ms. Helen said, with your help, we can deal with that vampire much faster." Ebner gestured for the two ladies to take hold of him. "Time is of the essence—let’s head to a location where we can safely enter the book."
He had just checked the story’s progress and discovered that the "King of the North" was on the verge of being slain by Silviaand was currently fleeing for his life. If they didn’t act soon, the "Shaman King" might complete the adventure and escape the book entirely!
Helen and Closfia had no objections. Each took hold of one of Ebner’s arms, and in the next instant, all three vanished from the rest area.
.....
In the ancient palace above the gray fog, Klein couldn’t help but chuckle to himself after listening to "The Tower’s" report about the "Shaman King" and lending him the "Black Emperor Card."
"The Tower" has really found some... creative uses for that book.
Not only does he use it as a shield, but he can also trap enemies inside its imagined world by using their blood...
Now
that’s
what I call an unorthodox strategy!
If it were me, I wouldn’t dare treat such a high-value mystical item so casually...
His gaze then drifted toward the pile of miscellaneous items in the corner, and he immediately reconsidered.
...Okay, maybe I would.
Shaking his head, Klein dismissed the thought and focused on locating the ship carrying the "Demoness of Affliction" who had been tracking Tracy.
—He planned to disguise himself as "Tracy" to infiltrate the "Celestial Sect." Most of his preparations were complete; the only thing missing was the abilities befitting a "Demoness" to maintain his cover. Thus, he intended to use "Creeping Hunger" to enslave a "Demoness"—preferably at least a "Pleasure"-sequence one.
Such "Demonesses" were usually hard to find, but currently, a ship full of them from the "Demoness Sect" was cruising near the Rorsted Archipelago. As the "Sea God," tracking them down was child’s play.
With a thought, the sapphire at the tip of his "Trident of the Sea God" glowed brightly.
Simultaneously, schools of fish of various species rose to the water’s surface.
They caught the faint, misty light that spilled from nowhere, circled once, then dove back down, each heading in different directions.
Whew... This is quite draining...
Klein rubbed his temples with his left hand.
His manipulation of marine life hadn’t been simple—he’d imbued them with traces of supernatural spirituality, enabling them to transmit visual information back to him through prayer should they locate the target vessel.
While this posed little difficulty for the "Sea God Scepter," the strain on Klein himself was considerable.
Having completed this task, he didn’t even bother returning the scepter to the pile of miscellaneous items. Instead, he immediately returned to the real world, removed his coat, and collapsed onto his bed. He then attempted to meditate on layered spheres of light to soothe his physical and spiritual exhaustion before drifting into sleep.
.....
In the ritual chamber beneath the ancestral home of the Surrey family in Tosk, Helen and Closfia watched as Ebner used two books and two cards to open a door that seemed to exist between reality and illusion, their eyes filled with awe.
Unaware that this was one of Roselle’s arrangements, they assumed it was Ebner’s own handiwork.
—Since there was no longer any need to "steal" miracles,
The Book of Fortune Stealing
and the "Error Card" were no longer essential for opening the "door."
The trio quickly stepped through the boundary between reality and illusion, entering the treasure hoard of the "King of the North." This time, however, the frost dragon wasn’t sleeping atop its golden mountain.
"It’s almost indistinguishable from reality... The power of ancient gods is truly formidable!" Closfia picked up a gold coin, studying it with admiration.
Helen, however, had no time for such reflections. After closing her eyes briefly to sense their surroundings, she pointed southeast. "Over there—about 150 miles away!"
No sooner had she spoken than she flew out of the dragon’s cave.
Exchanging glances, Ebner and Closfia promptly employed their own means to follow.
—Ebner naturally had no trouble, capable of simulating flight himself while also possessing a "Cloak of Flight." As for Closfia, being the wife of a "Classical Alchemist," she certainly had no shortage of flight-enabling artifacts.
Soon, braving the snowstorm, the three approached the battlefield where the "King of the North," Yulisan, was locked in combat with the "Shaman King," Silvia.
From a distance, the towering, ten-meter-tall reptilian beast appeared utterly wretched. Not only was one of its massive, membrane-covered wings severed, forcing it to grapple with the vampire on the ground, but the beautiful, crystalline scales covering its body had also been torn away in large patches, leaving bald, exposed sections.
Had it not been for the frost dragon’s thick hide and incredible resilience—and Silvia’s lack of armor-piercing techniques—the "King of the North" would have fallen long ago!
Spotting the trio’s approach from the air, Silvia immediately halted her assault on the dragon. Recognizing them instantly, she wasted no time attempting to disperse into a swarm of spectral bats and flee.
She knew all too well how terrifying the silver-haired, silver-eyed woman was. Even with the aid of a "Bizarro Sorcerer"-grade mystical item last time, she’d barely escaped with her life. Now, without that artifact, she dared not linger.
And that infuriatingly alluring young man with his arsenal of powerful items was here too!
Yet just as she was about to make her escape, a new thought struck her:
In this bizarre world, running might be futile. Why not gamble—take one of them hostage to force the others to let me go?
The silver-haired woman was too strong, and the bespectacled young man seemed equally troublesome. That left the chestnut-haired woman, who appeared comparatively frail—even her "flight" relied on external means.
Perfect target!
No sooner had this thought formed than a crimson moon rose within Silvia’s body, and in a flash of moonlight, she materialized directly in front of Closfia.
They didn’t react in time!
Ecstatic, Silvia prepared to first incapacitate the woman with a "potion" before taking her hostage.
What she failed to notice, however, was the slight curl of Closfia’s lips—or the pity in Ebner’s eyes.
This fool, her mind already warped by worshiping an evil god... Her mental island may look more dangerous, but to a "Dreamweaver," it’s full of holes.
Thus, Closfia effortlessly "manipulated" Silvia, weaving for her a "beautiful dream" in which she successfully took a hostage and fought her way free.
Alas, just as the dream-Silviawas about to escape this strange world, her "hostage" transformed into a dragon even more colossal than the "King of the North"!
Hiliya jolted awake—only to despair upon discovering she was
actually
pinned beneath a dragon’s claw, moments before a torrent of "dragon’s breath" engulfed her face.
Then she "awoke" again, trapped in another "beautiful dream" with an equally gruesome ending...
A demigod with mental vulnerabilities truly suffers at the hands of a high-sequence "Spectator"...
As Ebner attempted to cast "Violet’s Perfect Restoration" on the barely breathing "King of the North" to prevent its immediate demise, Closfia suddenly let out a soft exclamation.
"What is it?" Ebner asked. He knew the "Sloth" lady was currently subjecting Hiliya to various scenarios to extract hidden secrets—had she discovered something?
"In a dream scenario involving the Delien family, I found her memories had been tampered with."
"But the moment I touched them, they self-destructed... Only two phrases remained, the ones that had left the deepest impression on her."
Here, Closfia donned Silvia’s "persona mask" and replicated the vampire’s tone verbatim:
"The Deliens are not truly devout to the Mother Tree..."
"...A strange spirit that emerged from a box—high in rank, yet lacking Beyonder characteristics to sustain it."

chapters.title: Chapter 827: The Witch Concentration on the Black Emperor
chapters.content:
Chapter 827: The Witch Concentration on the Black Emperor
"The Deliens are not truly devout to the Mother Tree..."
"...A strange spirit that emerged from a box—high in rank, yet lacking Beyonder characteristics to sustain it."
After reciting these two fragments from Silvia’s memories, Closfia’s face twisted in pain. The "persona mask" she had just donned shattered violently, and Silvia’s spirit itself was extinguished.
"The seal on these memories was stronger than I anticipated! Even disguised as herself, this was all I could retrieve..." Closfia massaged her temples before adding, "Also, I vaguely sensed these were remnants of a conversation she had with an angelic-level entity... from eleven years ago."
The Deliens aren’t devout to the Mother Tree? Well, of course—with that family’s complicated allegiances, how could they be? So does this "Delien" refer specifically to the Prime Minister? As a follower of the "Blood Sanctity Sect" and a lackey of the Nox family, is he also duplicitous?
And what about that "high-ranking entity from a box"... What box is this referring to? Closfia confirmed this was a dream involving the Delien family... Could this box be the hidden secret mentioned in Lilith’s mission?
Also, eleven years ago... angelic level... Does the Delien family harbor an angel? No, Silvia said it lacked Beyonder characteristics...
The Delien family’s waters run deeper than I thought!
As Ebner’s thoughts raced, a gemstone coalesced from Silvia’s corpse—a fist-sized crystal formed of condensed blood, radiating a crimson glow like a miniature crimson moon.
The "Shaman King’s" Beyonder characteristic.
Just as Helen reached for it, Closfia snatched it up first. Smirking at Helen’s empty grasp, she teased, "I did most of the work here. If you want this characteristic, shouldn’t you offer something in return? After all, my Judy could also switch pathways and advance to ’Shaman King.’"
Helen, clearly familiar with Closfia’s antics, rolled her eyes. "Out with it. What script do you want me to act out this time? What role am I playing?"
Closfia’s lips curled as she leaned in to whisper into Helen’s ear. The latter’s expression visibly contorted.
"Closfia... your third-rate playwright skills are getting more outrageous by the day!" Helen groaned, pressing a hand to her forehead.
"Do you want it or not?" Closfia dangled the glowing gem.
"Fine! I agree!" Helen gritted her teeth.
Only then did Closfia hand over the crimson-hued crystal, adding cheerfully, "Don’t act so put upon. You never held back when teasing me as a child!"
"Besides, this benefits you too, doesn’t it?"
Helen stashed the characteristic, refusing to acknowledge Closfia’s triumphant smirk. After disposing of Silvia’s remains, she surveyed their surroundings and turned to Ebner. "Is this world nothing but ice and snow?"
Closfia perked up at the question. "Since this is a world created by the ’Dragon of Imagination,’ could its vanished divine kingdom—the ’City of Miracles,’ Liveseyd—be hidden here too?"
Ebner, who had been thoroughly enjoying the ladies’ banter and was about to subtly probe for details about Closfia’s script, froze at the question. Internally, he groaned:
What, do you two also want to experience the "Hall of Truth" and die of embarrassment?
Of course, he had no intention of actually taking them there.
Both were Sequence 3 Saints—without "cheats," approaching the "Chaotic Sea" posed significant risks.
After a moment’s thought, Ebner pointed at the frost dragon cowering motionlessly on the ground and carefully replied, "This is the territory of the ’King of the North,’ Ulyssan, so naturally it’s all ice and snow... But farther out, human cities and villages should exist."
—Giant Groselle and his companions had initially traveled through such settlements before their party grew and the "story" reached its climax on these snowy plains.
Closfia’s eyes lit up. "Can we visit one of this world’s cities then?"
Now in possession of the characteristic, Helen also gazed at Ebner with interest.
Having rushed through his last visit, Ebner hadn’t explored the book’s urban areas either. The idea appealed to him too, so he vaulted onto the now-recovered frost dragon’s back and gestured to the ladies. "I don’t know where the cities are... but it can guide us."
Groselle’s Travels
chronicled the giant Groselle’s quest to slay the rampaging dragons, so this "King of the North" would surely know their locations.
The "King of the North" dared not resist, allowing the three to mount its back before carrying them toward distant city-states.
.....
Only after they had been gone for quite some time did a five-member team arrive at the scene. After carefully surveying the area, they finally reached the spot where Silvia had died.
—Despite Helen’s disposal of the body, numerous traces remained due to their hasty cleanup.
"It seems our new companion was unlucky enough to encounter Ulyssan," remarked the giant leader, leaning on a greatsword wider than a human door panel with regret.
Similar incidents had occurred before, so he wasn’t particularly surprised.
"Not so fast, Groselle... At least four people were here just now, including three demigod-level beings!" interjected a peculiarly dressed man in his thirties who radiated unease. "As a former ’Cryptologist,’ you should trust my professional judgment."
"Demigods... Enemies beyond Ulyssan? Or new allies?" asked the Loenese soldier Ranzel, cradling his longsword.
"Unknown... But I suggest we return to camp immediately," said the unsettlingly attired man—Viscount Mobet Zoroast of the Solomon Empire—with unusual gravity.
"Why?" inquired the elf Siatas beside him.
"Groselle was right earlier... Our unfortunate new companion is already dead, which means we’ll likely fall dormant again soon. I’d rather not sleep directly in the snow, though it won’t kill us," Mobet explained wearily.
.....
Above the gray fog, a refreshed Klein reviewed the "images" transmitted by marine life and finally pinpointed the "Demoness Sect" vessel pursuing Tracy.
"That ship has numerous Beyonders. A frontal assault might not succeed, let alone achieve my goal of enslaving a witch...
"Better to use the ’Sea God Scepter’ for a long-range strike based on those prayer images, make them think the Church of Storms attacked, then pick off isolated witches..."
After strategizing, Klein materialized a citrine pendant with pen and paper to divine his plan’s viability. The results indicated manageable risk.
Returning to reality, he boarded a "giant fish" summoned by the "Sea God" to approach the Demoness Sect ship before re-entering the gray fog.
Exhaling slowly, Klein observed the vessel rocking in dark waves and raised the "Sea God Scepter."
The sapphires encircling its tip blazed to life.
Suddenly, a colossal lightning bolt illuminated the surrounding sea, striking the ship’s upper deck!
BOOM!
As electrical serpents scattered and wooden structures burst into flames, the thunderclap finally reached the sailors’ and witches’ ears.
More jagged silver lightning followed, transforming the sizable sailboat into a forest of electricity.
Just then, a massive ice barrier materialized, blocking the converging bolts—but lasted mere seconds before shattering. Lightning ravaged the deck, charring unfortunate sailors black as burnt timber.
However, those critical seconds allowed several witches and other Beyonders to abandon ship in different directions.
—Exactly as Klein predicted: believing a Storm Church demigod had attacked, they fled separately, each praying not to be pursued.
Klein quickly locked onto a "Demoness of Pleasure."
His choice was deliberate: first, he’d battled her on Symeem Island and knew her capabilities; second, her sequence was higher than other witches but lower than the leading "Demoness of Affliction"—ideal since the latter would take too long to subdue, risking complications.
While strategizing, Klein returned to the "giant fish’s" mouth to prepare a ritual. He then summoned his spirit—fused with the "Demoness Card"—and flew toward the target armed with "Burial Blade" and "Creeping Hunger."
—Using the "Demoness Card" maximized the "Convergence Effect" to prevent mishaps.
Yet just as Klein finally succeeded in enslaving the "Demoness of Pleasure" with "Creeping Hunger," an enormous black-hulled ship materialized in the distance.
Nearly 100 meters long with towering sails and rows of cannons, the vessel cast darkness over surrounding waters despite maintaining distance!
Recognizing it immediately, Klein terminated his summoning and retreated to the gray fog.
But confusion lingered:
Why did using the "Demoness Card" attract Nast’s "Black Emperor"? The fog should block the "Black Emperor Card’s" convergence...
Unless... something high-sequence from the Black Emperor pathway was in those waters?
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 828: Klein’s Confidence
chapters.content:
Chapter 828: Klein’s Confidence
On Thursday morning, at the Surrey family estate, the slightly overweight, forty-something MP Surrey had just finished breakfast when his butler informed him that Mr. René was already waiting in the study.
MP Surrey’s brows immediately furrowed. As the family’s professional asset manager overseeing the majority of the Surrey finances, Mr. René had brought nothing but bad news ever since the family’s archbishop in the Church of Steam and Machinery had passed away.
Sigh... No matter how much I dread it, I can’t avoid this... Let’s hope it’s not too disastrous this time...
With a heavy sigh, MP Surrey followed the butler to the study, where he found a weary-looking Mr. René with dark circles under his eyes.
The financial manager, only thirty years old and in his prime, had been so strained by the pressures of the past month that streaks of white had begun to appear in his hair.
When MP Surrey entered, René was downing cup after cup of coffee, desperately trying to replenish his depleted energy.
The sight made Surrey’s heart sink, but he maintained a calm tone as he asked, "René, has something else happened?"
"Yes... I’ve just received news that is extremely unfavorable to us..." René replied, dabbing his forehead with a handkerchief—perhaps due to the heat of the coffee.
"What news?" MP Surrey asked, sitting on the sofa and forcing himself to remain composed.
With the recent barrage of bad news, he had grown somewhat numb.
"Mr. Henry, the second-largest shareholder of Suhite Bank, has sold all his shares to the Flessey family..." René answered cautiously, trying not to agitate the MP further.
"What?!" Surrey shot up from his seat, disbelief written across his face. "Henry sold his shares?!"
"Yes... According to my sources, he’s been negotiating with the Flesseys for nearly a week. It may already be in its final stages..." René wiped his sweat again, delivering what felt like a divine punishment to MP Surrey.
Suhite Bank was the Surrey family’s most vital asset. As its largest shareholder, the family’s lifeline was inextricably tied to the bank.
Henry had been their staunchest ally, and together, their combined shares exceeded 50%, securing the Surreys’ operational control.
Previously, the Flesseys had acquired scattered minor shares, but the Surreys hadn’t been concerned—those couldn’t shake their foundation.
Now, however, if the Flesseys succeeded in acquiring Henry’s stake and rallied other small-to-mid shareholders, they could genuinely overturn the Surreys’ absolute authority over Suhite Bank!
"No... The Flesseys must have already swayed some shareholders... If the shares under their control surpass ours, even the neutral third-largest shareholder—Count Hall of Loen—and the other minor shareholders will side with them..." Surrey felt his legs wobble, but he steadied himself and ordered the butler, "Arrange a meeting with Henry—today at noon!"
The butler gave his employer a concerned look but bowed. "At once, sir."
MP Surrey then turned back to René. "Are there any neutral small-to-mid shareholders we can still win over?"
René, having done his homework, retrieved a document from his briefcase and handed it over. "Sir, among those worth approaching, Mr. Monet and Berlat Steel remain our best options. They supported you during the Flesseys’ and Deliens’ previous pressure campaigns, so they may assist again. However..."
"However what?" Surrey pressed, uneasy.
Truthfully, he had never understood why those two had helped before—their intervention had been abrupt and unexplained. Whether they would do so again was anyone’s guess.
"I met with their representatives earlier... They informed me they’ve received orders from above to defer future decisions to Mr. Ebner Bryan’s recommendations," René explained.
"Ebner Bryan... Who is that?" The name rang a faint bell, but Surrey couldn’t place it.
"After checking, I found he’s a new shareholder of Suhite Bank, holding a 1% stake..." René pointed to a line near the bottom of the document.
MP Surrey stared at the name for a long moment before turning to the butler. "Isn’t Ebner Bryan that friend of Fanny’s? The one from Loen?"
"Yes, sir. Detective Bryan is indeed Miss Fanny’s friend. He escorted her all the way back to Trier and has since settled here, establishing several businesses—including real estate and a newspaper... Additionally, he’s a devout follower of the Earth Mother Church and maintains good relations with Archbishop Helen." The butler, having thoroughly investigated Ebner due to his connection with the young lady, provided detailed information.
"So Detective Bryan is Miss Fanny’s friend! That explains why those two parties helped us before!" Mr. René’s face lit up with realization, and he grew visibly excited. "If that’s the case, even if Mr. Henry sells his shares to the Flesseys, we might not lose! In fact, our chances of winning are quite good!"
"How so?" The MP’s spirits lifted as well, and he pressed for details.
"Detective Bryan hails from Loen, where he enjoys considerable fame and influence. He might even be acquainted with Count Hall! If we can secure the support of the third-largest shareholder, our crisis would be averted...
"Even if we merely ensure Count Hall remains neutral, this battle is far from over!" Mr. René suddenly felt reinvigorated.
Having been under constant pressure recently, he was eager for a chance to fight back.
After seeing the newly motivated Mr. René off, the MP hesitated before addressing the butler again. "Have I been neglecting Fanny too much?"
"Miss Fanny bears no resentment toward you," the butler replied tactfully.
This was true—Fanny’s thoughts were now largely preoccupied with Ebner.
Closing his eyes briefly, the MP finally said, "Send for Fanny... I’d like to speak with her."
"At once, sir." The butler bowed and withdrew.
.....
Meanwhile, in the ancient palace above the gray fog, Ebner frowned at "The World" Klein seated below him and cautiously advised, "Given your... unique circumstances, infiltrating the ’Celestial Sect’ could be dangerous!"
"I’m aware... Lady Yalolan warned me as well." Touched by the concern, Klein explained, "I’ve reported this matter to both ’The Fool’ and the Goddess. I’ll have some protection."
So now that you know the Goddess is a "fellow traveler," you’re getting bold, huh? But the "Mother Tree of Desire" isn’t to be trifled with—this will leave quite an impression on you!
Still, with the Goddess watching over him, the risks should be manageable...
With that thought, Ebner ceased his objections and simply nodded. "If you need help, summon me through ’The Fool’... I’ll teleport over immediately."
"Don’t worry. I’ve prepared extensively for this infiltration. There might be danger, but it should be within controllable limits."
After exchanging some recent experiences, the two concluded their regular "fellow traveler" meeting.
.....
Back in reality, Klein remained silent for a long while before closing his eyes. His facial contours softened, his irises turned blue, his eyebrows thinned, and his lips pressed together slightly—in mere moments, he had transformed into Tracy’s likeness.
"Not bad... It’s not so different after all. Maybe because I’m not cross-dressing? It feels similar to becoming Gehrman Sparrow or anyone else—just prettier and with some... extra weight up front. If I’d looked like this back on Earth, I wouldn’t have struggled to find a girlfriend." He smirked self-deprecatingly.
Even this simple gesture, ordinary on Gehrman Sparrow, now carried an unsettling charm.
Damn it!
Klein cursed inwardly, quickly adjusting his mindset as he immersed himself in the role.
As time passed, he found his psychological barriers genuinely fading, replaced by relaxation and calm—bringing him closer to harmony with the potion.
Which meant faster digestion.
Well, I’ll be damned... This actually works.
Silently marveling, Klein rose, took four steps counterclockwise, and returned to the gray fog to reconfirm the mission’s risk level.
Back in reality, reviewing the collected intelligence on the "Celestial Sect," he ultimately couldn’t bring himself to don their near-nudity attire...
In this moment, he gained deeper self-awareness: some lines he simply couldn’t cross.
Little "Sun" said to remember it’s just acting...
Sighing, Klein retrieved the mystical item taken from Tracy’s wrist, planning to seal himself within it before having Danitz or Darkwill discreetly deliver the "crystal" to the Governor’s Mansion.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 829: Ebner’s Scheme
chapters.content:
Chapter 829: Ebner’s Scheme
Trier, Sauron District, outside the luxurious villa at 22 Saint Martin Avenue, a gentleman who appeared to be in his forties stood waiting to welcome his master.
With strikingly deep light blue eyes and neatly combed dyed black hair, his elegant and refined demeanor made him the type who could still turn women’s heads despite his age.
This gentleman was Bowen Bennett, the butler candidate Helen had selected for Ebner based on his requirements.
Though a devout follower of the Earth Mother, Bowen had an adopted son who had joined the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun and risen to the position of bishop. Thus, in Helen’s eyes, he perfectly met Ebner’s criteria of being both reliable and well-connected within the Eternal Blazing Sun Church.
—After their recent tour of the city-states within
Groselle’s Travels
, Helen had lent Ebner this lavish mansion, conveniently located near the ancestral home of the Karon family, free of charge.
Now, Ebner entered the third-floor study of the mansion with "Chesia" and Butler Bowen in tow.
"Sir, as per your instructions, I have hired ten maids, nine footmen, one chef, two gardeners, one coachman, and a coachman’s assistant...
"The weekly expenditure for these staff members amounts to 20 fer.
"Additionally, the ’Domestic Servants Assistance Association’ has provided a list of candidates for the housekeeper position. You may make the final selection yourself."
With that, the butler handed Ebner a booklet. He tactfully omitted mentioning a valet—Chesia’s presence suggested the master might prefer a lady’s maid.
Ebner skimmed the booklet before setting it aside. On paper, the candidates seemed equally qualified.
"Do you have any recommendations?" Ebner asked with a smile.
Butler Bowen appeared prepared but still took a moment to consider. "Jennifer appears experienced, but as a follower of the Lord of Steam and Machinery, her previous roles leaned more toward mechanical maintenance. Her financial management skills are merely passable.
"Caroline’s resume seems flawless, but from what I’ve gathered, she’s more interested in seducing male employers than actual work..."
Here, Bowen discreetly glanced at Ebner’s expression and, detecting no particular interest, continued, "Finally, there’s Ancath. Her reputation is impeccable. She married and moved to Rite City in the east a few years ago but has since returned to Trier for unknown reasons. In terms of professional competence, she undoubtedly surpasses the other two."
Ebner easily discerned Bowen’s bias but didn’t mind. Even if Bowen and this "Ancath" were to collude in embezzlement later, did he lack the means to recover his losses?
Given that, he might as well choose the most professionally capable candidate.
With that thought, Ebner tapped Ancath’s name on the list and declared, "Her, then."
"Very well, sir. I’ll have the legal team draft the contract immediately." Butler Bowen bowed and, seeing his employer had nothing further to add, tactfully withdrew.
The moment the study door closed, Closfia materialized beside Ebner. After admiring the opulent decor, she asked with a smile, "You specifically requested this house from Helen to ’legitimately’ engage with the Sauron family and ally with them to crush the Deliens, didn’t you?
"However, I should warn you—the Saurons haven’t been as arrogant or foolish as they were a century ago since the Roselle incident. Manipulating them won’t be easy."
—Having accepted the Earth Mother’s mission, Closfia had naturally moved into Ebner’s residence to serve as his on-call enforcer.
"Yet the Saurons’ greatest threat still comes from the Deliens. If internal cracks appear in the latter, they won’t hesitate to strike... My role is merely to provide intelligence, enabling them to act swiftly." Ebner pulled out a newspaper and pointed to the headline. "Besides, the opportunity has already presented itself."
Curious, Closfia glanced at the article, which primarily detailed the romantic escapades of a Trier socialite, only briefly mentioning how she had been startled by protesters during an outing. While seemingly innocuous, the report elaborated extensively on the protest’s origins and political demands.
As a former member of the Feynapotter royal family, Closfia was politically astute. After a brief contemplation, she uttered a single word: "Press censorship?"
"Exactly. Resistance to ’press censorship’ is snowballing. It’s clear the bill will never pass Congress... The Prime Minister won’t tolerate that. Before the April elections, he’ll inevitably dissolve the current Congress, reorganize it, and force the bill through." Ebner spoke with unwavering confidence.
Even if the Prime Minister didn’t conceive of this himself, Ebner would ensure Seyrou Delien—whose fate had been altered—would plant the idea in his mind.
"Once Congress is dissolved, the accumulated tensions will likely erupt, potentially spiraling out of control... Would the Prime Minister truly go that far?" Closfia paused mid-sentence, then added, "And don’t expect me to ’hypnotize’ him—someone in his position undoubtedly undergoes regular inspections by the Eternal Blazing Sun Church. There’s no way to deceive them."
"I understand. But this isn’t about the Prime Minister lacking political acumen—he’s being forced into a corner... Which gives us ample room to maneuver." Ebner rose and walked to the window, gazing toward the Sauron family’s ancestral home in the distance. "Do you think the Saurons would pass up a chance at restoration?"
"They could never succeed..." Closfia shook her head.
After all, the Churches would never allow it, and the Saurons remained too weakened to oppose them.
"Which is why I need to give them an extra ’boost of confidence.’" Ebner smiled.
"What kind?" Closfia asked curiously.
"A secret." Ebner replied mysteriously, refusing to elaborate—a small revenge for her previous schemes against him.
Closfia gave him an amused look but didn’t press further, instead remarking, "I recall you have a ’friend’ from the Sauron family... Won’t manipulating her kin cause issues?"
"Helene is just a branch family member. If we don’t deal with those main lineage figures, how can she rise?" Ebner said matter-of-factly, thinking of the diligent "Scarlet Maid" managing his "film company."
Just then, a knock sounded. Closfia vanished as Fanny entered with an orange cat in tow.
—Before moving in, Ebner had instructed the staff to admit Fanny, Fors, Helene, or Helen directly to his study without announcement.
The cat—Leon the "Lion"—sniffed suspiciously upon entering, glancing around but finding nothing unusual.
Fanny, as warm as ever, greeted Ebner with an embrace before getting to business: "My father would like to invite you to dinner this Friday evening, to thank you for taking care of me during our journey..."
She handed him an exquisitely crafted invitation.
"Your father... inviting me? Is there something beyond gratitude?" Ebner feigned surprise, though he’d already guessed the reason.
Truthfully, if genuine thanks were the purpose, the invitation should’ve come much sooner—not delayed by a week.
Perfect timing though... I need the Surrey family’s cooperation too. Even if the MP hadn’t reached out, I’d have visited him soon anyway...
As Ebner mused internally, Fanny replied, "It’s probably about the Suhite Bank shares..."
Just as I thought.
The moment he heard this, Ebner grasped MP Surrey’s mindset.After all, in a way, the crisis threatening the Surreys’ hold over Suhite Bank was of his own recent design.
Who could’ve guessed that Henry, the bank’s second-largest shareholder, was actually an agent of the "Men in Black"?
Through Seyrou’s indirect command, Ebner had instructed Henry to signal his willingness to sell shares to the Flesseys.
As for manipulating Fanny’s father? Ebner felt no guilt—consider it payback for Fanny’s sake!
—Only after arriving in Trier had Ebner learned why Fanny had lived with her grandfather in Backlund: after her mother’s accidental death, her father remarried a widow, making Fanny increasingly alienated from the new family of four.
.....
Bayam, Governor’s Mansion backyard
A Celestial Sect cadre gazed greedily at the beautiful figure encased in "crystal," asking the soldier who delivered it:
’Well done! Where did you find her?’
"Some fishermen discovered her and planned to sell her... I took her instead." The soldier grinned, counting himself lucky to have stumbled upon such a prize while visiting that fat apothecary.
"Excellent! Name your reward," the cadre said.
The soldier stared at the slender silhouette in the crystal, swallowing hard. "I... could I have her for one night after you’re done with her?"
The cadre nearly laughed aloud.
A mere mortal daring to touch a Demoness? Does he want to die of plague?
Outwardly, he smiled and nodded: "Granted!"
The soldier practically danced with joy.
Meanwhile, Klein—pretending to be sealed and unconscious—fought waves of nausea. Though he knew the soldier’s desires targeted Tracy’s body, not his true form, goosebumps still erupted across his skin.
This... definitely reinforces my self-awareness.
Elsewhere, after dismissing the soldier, the cadre urgently directed subordinates to transport the crystal to the dungeons while sending word to the "Apostle of Procreation."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 830: Klein’s Discovery
chapters.content:
Chapter 830: Klein’s Discovery
Bayam Governor’s Mansion.
It took nearly an hour for Klein, carried by two Celestial Sect members through an extremely deep passageway, to finally enter the labyrinthine underground prison.
No—"prison" wasn’t quite accurate. This was more like an underground town, reeking of alcohol and forbidden drugs, teeming with crowds indulging in unrestrained debauchery...
Soon, the crystal encasing Klein was placed inside a heavily warded structure. Several cultists immediately attempted to breach its absolute defense using flames, blunt force, and other methods.
Unfortunately, attacks below demigod-level couldn’t even leave a scratch. Cursing, they abandoned their hopes of "claiming first blood" and left, sealing the room temporarily.
