When only Klein remained in the warded cell, he finally opened his eyes inside the crystal.
Channeling spirituality into a playing card beside him, he pierced through layers of bestial cries to arrive in the mysterious space above the gray fog.
This was his latest application of the "Error Card"—using this Blasphemy Slip to leverage the gray fog’s power, "stealing" both the ascension process and his self-summoning ritual, then "returning" them when needed. This allowed access to the ancient space without requiring a bathroom or the four-step counterclockwise ritual.
One of Klein’s prearranged plans involved using the crystal’s absolute defense to protect his physical body while deploying a special spirit form—one that could instantly retreat to the gray fog—for reconnaissance.
Seated in The Fool’s position, Klein laid out several Blasphemy Slips before ultimately selecting the "Demoness Card" for fusion.
After all, the "Demoness" spirit offered optimal stealth for investigative work.
Soon, an alluring female spirit with provocative attire materialized in reality through the "Summoning Gate."
Klein immediately activated invisibility. After studying the cell’s wards, he found them strong enough to withstand three or four full-power "Lightning Strikes" from a "Sea Chanters"—but their spiritual defenses were lacking...
"Good. Otherwise I’d need the ’Error Card’ to create a backdoor first!" Slightly relieved, Klein phased through the wall into the underground town’s streets.
Surveying the orderly buildings and crowds mindlessly indulging their desires, Klein realized the Celestial Sect’s surface-level harmlessness masked a deeply corrosive influence.
"But this underground space doesn’t feel like true reality... Some spatial-type mystical item?
"Aside from newer constructions, most structures resemble my prison cell... Probably Bayam Governor’s original supernatural prison, now hijacked by the Celestial Sect!
"If I’m right, Darkwill’s teacher should be imprisoned here too..."
While analyzing, Klein’s "Demoness" spirit drifted into a distinct building—an archives.
The administrator lay entangled with a woman, oblivious to the intruder.
"Lax security... Then again, how could Celestial Sect members stay disciplined with their doctrines?
"No wonder Darkwill’s guard friend constantly buys potions—such unrestrained indulgence must have wrecked their health!
"Worse news: every Governor’s Mansion guard and Beyonder has likely been corrupted. Otherwise authorities or the Storm Church would’ve been alerted.
"Thank goodness I accepted ’The Tower’s’ invitation. Had I attended that banquet, I’d be another mindless rutting zombie by now.
"For now, I’ll investigate their operations here—ideally uncovering all their hidden bases. When that so-called ’Apostle of Procreation’ returns, I’ll arrange for someone to expose them in one fell swoop."
With this plan in mind, Klein quietly pulled a file from the shelves, masked by the administrator’s heavy breathing.
A quick scan confirmed this was an archive holding prisoner records of Beyonders.
"’Tatsumi, Sequence 9 ’Sailor’... 100 pound bearer check... withdrawal cipher...’"
Huh? They even keep interrogation records? Including sequence formulas and ritual magic setups... Pity the checks and valuables were long since claimed...
Klein flipped through several pages, noting all financial entries marked with an "X"—denoting their depletion.
As for formulas and magic, interrogators had left them untouched, unable to verify authenticity...
Unlike ’Judgement,’ who can consult Ebner or ’The Fool’ to confirm her interrogation findings.
Klein rapidly skimmed files like those "quantum speed-reading" scams from his past life—he didn’t need perfect recall, just impressions to reconstruct via divination later.
"’Roy King, Councilor of the Fate Council in the School of Life... demigod... detained in Zone A, Cell 1...’" Finally locating Darkwill’s mentor’s records, Klein noted he was the prison’s sole demigod inmate, housed in their most secure area.
No rush to rescue him yet. Before leaving, I’ll just hurl a lightning bolt at his cell—he can handle the rest...
The real question is: with demigod prisoners, are there demigod guards? Could even they be corrupted by the Celestial Sect?
Or did the sect use the Governor to transfer high-level guardians away?
My divination suggests the latter... Otherwise I’d be fighting for my virtue right now!
After this dark humor, Klein replaced all documents. Hovering midair, he mockingly bowed to the post-coital administrator before phasing through walls toward another distinctive building.
The decor instantly signaled this belonged to a high-ranking female member. A search revealed little beyond recreational tools and potions—except one valuable diary by a woman calling herself "Abby."
"I keep this diary so I won’t forget who I am."
The first page’s declaration gave Klein pause. After pendulum-divining its safety, he continued:
"It all began with that experiment in February 1339..."
"300 subjects... Only I, Bianca, and Lofia survived..."
1339? Eleven years ago?
....
Trier
After touring several newspapers for sale with Fanny and Leon the "Lion," Ebner returned to his mansion to find Butler Bowen escorting a plain-looking woman in her forties into his study.
"Sir, this is Ms. Ancath. She’s signed the contract and can begin her duties as housekeeper tomorrow," Bowen introduced.
As Ancath curtsied, murmuring "At your service, Detective Bryan," Ebner nearly dismissed them—until her aura triggered familiarity.
One quick "analysis" later, his gaze sharpened. This was no "Ancath"—but Bianca the "Wizard," former military attaché at the Intis Embassy in Loen!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 831: Bianca
chapters.content:
Chapter 831: Bianca
This woman posing as housekeeper Ancath was actually the "Wizard" Bianca?
Ebner maintained his composure on the surface while remaining inwardly vigilant. He adjusted his glasses, discreetly activating his "Pure White Eyes" to scrutinize the "plain-looking" woman before him.
Soon, through his "Mystic Art," he detected traces of a mystical item around her facial area.
This "Mystic Art"—called "Object Detection"—was developed by Ebner based on the abilities of a "Cryptologist." It could locate mystical items on a person’s body, serving as a preparatory skill for "Disintegration."
When combined with the two "Amon’s Monocle Lens" fragments in his possession, the effectiveness of this "Mystic Art" improved significantly—even some concealed "Grade 1" sealed artifacts couldn’t escape detection.
Inside the study, despite confirming the housekeeper’s true identity, Ebner chose not to expose her outright. Instead, he calmly offered a few words of encouragement before instructing Butler Bowen to introduce her to the other household staff.
After they left, Ebner took a sip of coffee from his desk and sank into thought:
"Over a month ago, when Klein, Sharon, and I met with Medici, we inquired about the transmigrator predecessor ’Giuseppe Castilla’—the one Lilith referred to as ’Felipe.’
"The ’Red Angel’ told us what stood out most was that man’s abnormally peculiar luck. Moreover, Medici recently detected a similar yet distinct aura reminiscent of that anomalous luck passing by.
"Later, Hugh mentioned that the owner of that aura was likely this very ’Wizard’ Bianca!
"I recall performing a ’prophecy’ at the time to locate Bianca, which pointed me to ’Trier’...
"Now, encountering her so soon—is this her own agenda at work, or some form of convergence?
"Could her peculiar trait of bringing misfortune to her lovers truly be connected to that transmigrator predecessor?"
As he pondered, Ebner mimicked "The Fool’s" habit of tapping the edge of his desk. After a moment, he decided to keep the "Wizard" in his household for now, using the opportunity to investigate her background.
But first, he needed to determine her purpose in becoming his housekeeper...
With this in mind, Ebner turned his head toward an empty sofa and politely said, "Miss Closfia, could you examine this housekeeper’s psyche? I’d like to know if someone is scheming behind her to target me."
"Very well," a languid voice replied. The study door then opened and closed by itself without a breeze.
While "Sloth" appeared lazy, she was actually quite diligent—perhaps why she could wield the power of "Persona Masks" without suffering significant backlash?
As his thoughts wandered, Ebner continued sipping his coffee while picking up a document on his desk—a detailed report on various newspapers compiled by Butler Bowen.
As a local, his information was naturally more accurate and comprehensive than what "Chesi," controlled by the "Magic Mirror," had gathered.
"So Lyon ultimately set his sights on the Loen Times... But that one is really quite expensive... Looks like I’ll have to go talk to that Mr. Wolfe who was successfully brainwashed by Lilith...
"Or maybe I just shouldn’t buy it at all? Just have that ’lion’ hypnotize Mr. Wolfe’s son... After all, it just wants to publish some of Roselle’s dirty laundry... There’s no real need to actually own shares...
"Besides, based on the information gathered so far, young Mr. Wolfe, while not a Beyonder, isn’t exactly a good person either—his hands are just as bloody as old Mr. Wolfe’s before Lilith ’reformed’ him...
"The only real issue is that since Mr. Wolfe’s disappearance, the ’Machinery Hivemind’ has been keeping a close eye on the Loen Times. If young Mr. Wolfe suddenly has a drastic change in attitude, it might draw the attention of the official Beyonders..."
Just as this thought crossed his mind, the study door swung open again, and Closfia’s figure appeared before Ebner.
—Miss "Sloth’s" Sequence 3-level "Psychological Invisibility" still couldn’t evade Ebner’s "Pure White Eyes."
"Any results?" Ebner inquired.
"Your housekeeper is indeed problematic... She was sent here by Inspector Russell of the Police Department," Closfia replied with a peculiar expression. "But this wasn’t the housekeeper’s own intention—she was coerced into coming."
Inspector Russell? Isn’t that the ’Desire Apostle’ from the Nox family who used Les Misérables as a script to advance to ’Devil’?
He’s controlling Bianca, sending her here to spy on me... Is this revenge for me ruining his plans on the train?
Hah, I didn’t actively go after you because I didn’t want to be ’sensed’ by you too soon, and now you’re coming after me instead?
Wait—could this be due to Bianca’s debuff effect? Very likely! So Russell, whose plans went flawlessly for years, had them ruined by me, got noticed by Bernoît, and now is making such a stupid move by provoking me, someone protected by a Saint and armed with multiple demigod-level methods?
At this realization, Ebner’s expression also turned peculiar. Shaking his head, he asked again, "What’s her objective?"
"She was ordered to gather as much information about you as possible and, if necessary, provide Inspector Russell with personal items like your clothing or hair.
"But this young lady, whose real name is Bianca, doesn’t seem to actually plan on doing it. She’s just waiting for Russell to meet his downfall so she can break free from his control." At this point, a hint of teasing amusement flashed in Closfia’s eyes before she continued, "From the fragments of memory I saw in her mind, every ’master’ she’s ever had has met with misfortune and lost their lives... So you should be careful too!"
"I have no interest in being her ’master,’" Ebner emphasized first, then asked thoughtfully, "How was she captured by Russell? And what’s controlling her?"
"Her capture was just a coincidence... or, as she herself puts it, when she doesn’t have a ’master,’ her luck tends to be terrible. Not long after arriving in Trier, she got caught up in a murder case, where Inspector Russell noticed her and planted a ’Seed of Desire,’ turning her into his servant."
As she answered, Closfia repeatedly applied "Psychological Hints" to herself to prevent her "hostility" from being detected by Inspector Russell. "Also, while it was the ’upright’ Inspector Russell who sent her to spy on you, Bianca suspects he didn’t originally plan this—it was only after a secret meeting with a member of a certain major family that he assigned her the mission."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 832: Klein Under the Influence
chapters.content:
Chapter 832: Klein Under the Influence
A major family member? Connected to the "Blood Sanctify Sect" and the Nois family... It must be the Delien family, right? The Prime Minister still hasn’t given up on dealing with me? But Seyrow doesn’t seem to have received any related information...
Ebner continued tapping the edge of the desk with his fingers, deciding to take advantage of the Russell situation to scheme against the Delien family... However, he refrained from planning specific details to avoid being sensed by the "Demon" if a real threat emerged.
"Are there any other noteworthy things in her memories?" Ebner asked again after collecting his thoughts.
"Regarding the origin of her ’misfortune’ constitution, she has some speculations herself—it seems to stem from an experiment eleven years ago... However, she doesn’t know the specific details of the experiment. It was only after encountering a member of ’Elements Dawn’ later that she realized she might have been specifically marked by the ’Hidden Sage.’" Closfia pondered for a moment before adding somewhat uncertainly, "But I could sense a deeply buried secret in her heart... I didn’t probe further because that memory felt dangerous!"
At this point, she suddenly glanced at Ebner and added, "It felt very similar to the warning I get whenever I try to peek into your thoughts."
So the reason you’ve never probed my thoughts is because it’s dangerous? Is this protection provided by the ’Pure White Eyes’?
Also, is Bianca’s dangerous memory the source of her peculiar luck—the truth behind that so-called experiment? And are these connected to the transmigrator, to the ’Pure White Eyes,’ which is why Closfia gets a similar feeling when probing me?
Of course, it’s also possible that the memory involves an existence with a status equivalent or similar to my ’Pure White Eyes’...
Lastly, a dangerous memory... eleven years ago... When Closfia probed the mind of the ’Shaman King’ Silvia, there was also a mysterious memory from eleven years ago... Is this a coincidence, or are the two somehow connected?
Thoughts racing, Ebner formed a conjecture:
That person or experiment from eleven years ago is likely the so-called ’secret of the Delien family’ that Lilith tasked me to investigate!
Even if not, it must be related!
After all, many of the people and events he’d encountered since arriving in Intis coincidentally intersected with this matter. If it wasn’t deliberately arranged by someone, then some form of underlying "convergence" effect must be at work.
Moreover, Lilith had entrusted him with this mission likely to exploit these connections... Otherwise, it could have simply sent an angel or even a demigod—far more efficient than a mere Sequence 5 like him.
What the Delien family is hiding must be anything but simple!
Come to think of it, the fact that so many organizations tolerate this family’s two-faced behavior suggests they possess some inherent value, doesn’t it?
Perhaps those organizations are cultivating insiders to uncover that secret...
And something that could interest organizations backed by true gods... There are only a few possibilities...
With this in mind, combined with the intelligence Closfia had intercepted from the "Shaman King" Silvia’s mind, Ebner began forming vague conjectures.
...
In the underground prison of the Governor’s Mansion in Bayam.
Klein carefully read through the diary of the lady named Rabi. By just the third page, he was shocked to find himself gradually overcome with excruciating pain - the oppressive sensation alone was enough to drive an ordinary person instantly mad.
This... this feels somewhat similar to when I read "The Magician" Miss’s submitted "Spirit World Observations"! Though reading "Spirit World Observations" gave me a feeling of "mania", while this is "pain"...
Hmm, the words themselves aren’t spiritual, the paper is completely ordinary, it can’t be a sealed artifact... So the words she recorded inherently contain some kind of ’power’? And my current spirit has already fused with the "Blasphemy Card", with sufficiently high status! Even so, it can affect me this strongly - one can imagine what would happen to others...
No wonder it’s left completely unprotected, as if inviting people to read it. Anyone who peeked at it before must have either gone mad or mutated into monsters on the spot.
With this thought, Klein closed the notebook, planning to leave it here for now. When his summoning ended, he would take it up to the gray fog to read.
However, from the three pages he had just read, he roughly learned that eleven years ago, a certain existence took something out from a box and conducted experiments on a group of people using it.
In the end, only five of these experimental subjects survived, then escaped the laboratory.
Miss Rabi was captured by members of the "Rose School of Thought" shortly after escaping, becoming a believer of the "Mother Tree of Desire"... Although, in her own self-awareness, she never actually worshipped that existence, yet still received its favor, becoming a so-called "Apostle of Proliferation".
The tragedy was, her "proliferation" only brought "pain" to others.
While Klein sympathized with Miss Rabi’s plight, he was also determined to grant her release as soon as possible!
After all, her actions over the years had far exceeded the limits of what Klein could tolerate. Compared to her, even "Vice Admiral of Ailment" Tracy seemed as pure as a saint.
Looking through the account books found in her room, Klein felt they were nothing less than ironclad evidence of the blood debts owed by Rabi and the "Celestial Sect".
Having collected the evidence, specific locations of Celestial Sect bases, and a list of key members, Klein felt his reconnaissance mission was now complete. He returned to the previous room, grabbed the diary, ended the summoning, and had his spirit return to the ancient palace above the gray fog.
Next, he first manifested an image of "The World", having it assume a posture of praying to "The Fool" as he passed the collected evidence and name list to "The Hanged Man" and "Judgment", tasking them with reporting it to the authorities.
After completing these actions, he simulated the sensation of falling, returning to his physical body in the real world.
Yet the moment his consciousness returned to his body, a series of indescribably lurid thoughts instantly flooded his mind.
Suddenly, naked images of "Demoness of Pleasure" Sharon Snow, the tearfully smiling Triss, the scholarly Lena, the innocent and lovely Shoko, the academically inclined Tracy, and the exquisitely doll-like Miss Sharon appeared before his eyes one after another, extending to him certain irresistible invitations... followed by disrobing and passionate entanglement...
But at this moment, the "Error Card" in Klein’s hand once again emitted a radiant glow. Immediately after, the phantom of a twelve-winged archangel appeared before his eyes, embracing his spiritual body and sweeping away all those "wonderful" scenes.
—This was another ritual Klein had preemptively "stolen" using the "Error Card" - the "Purification" ritual! All to prevent anyone from tampering with his body while his spirit was away.
Is this the Celestial Sect’s method? An influence permeating the entire underground space that imperceptibly draws people into carnal desires? So subtle I didn’t even notice earlier...
Or is this the so-called "Mother Tree of Desire", having detected my infiltration, secretly influencing me through its believers?
Similar to how I use the "Sea God Scepter" to see through fish eyes and smite "Savant" ships with lightning?
As he speculated, Klein couldn’t help but complain internally:
Why is it that in these illusions, apart from Miss Sharon, all the women entangled with me are demonesses?!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 833: Sudden Change and Calling for Backup
chapters.content:
Chapter 833: Sudden Change and Calling for Backup
Klein suppressed his stirring blood, initially planning to maintain his current state and wait for the authorities to arrive. He could then take advantage of the chaos to rescue Darkwill’s teacher and escape this underground prison.
However, at that very moment, unrestrained moans of pleasure suddenly came from outside his cell door. Soon after, an intoxicating scent that quickened heartbeats and inflamed desires seeped through the barriers and crystal walls, invading Klein’s nostrils.
This involuntary flood of sensations brought back vivid images of those wanton scenes from his earlier hallucinations...
Is this... the "Mother Tree of Desire" shifting from covert manipulation to an outright assault?
But doing this will inevitably trigger the prison’s alarms. Not only might it draw military demigods, but escaping will become exponentially harder!
Before Klein could finish this thought, the cell door was violently breached. Several humanoid monsters covered in brown woody tumors, with branches sprouting from their bodies, charged inside.
Like symbiotic plants, they entwined their branching limbs in intimate embrace while fixing their greedy gazes on Klein. In unison, they moaned:
"We want you to bear our children!"
The sheer lust and possessiveness in their voices sent a wave of visceral disgust through Klein. His entire body broke out in goosebumps, every hair standing on end.
This grotesque spectacle surpassed even the most twisted human imagination—something he’d never encountered even in nightmares.
Had this happened back in Tingen during the Megose incident, such sights would have paralyzed him with terror...
But after all his experiences, he was now a battle-hardened veteran. The instant those words reached his ears, he swiftly manipulated his bracelet to retract the crystal barrier. Simultaneously, the glove on his left hand darkened into a mesmerizing yet sinister black—activating "Creeping Hunger" and channeling the soul of the "Demoness of Pleasure" he’d previously subjugated.
Using "Tracy’s" alluring appearance and charm, he immediately
"Instigated"
:
"There are so many of you... Who should I choose? Why don’t you fight it out first?"
The moment these words left his mouth, Klein burned with shame, feeling like an actual siren sowing discord—so much so that his potion digestion seemed to progress noticeably.
If I actually helped the winner bear a child, maybe my "Faceless" potion would fully digest instantly... But I’m not actually Tracy, and I certainly lack the... necessary equipment!
As Klein internally facepalmed, the arboreal monstrosities predictably turned on each other with vicious fervor, tearing apart their previously amorous partners...
Their obsession with making me "bear children" is terrifyingly absolute!
Just as Klein prepared to eliminate these intruders, his spiritual intuition screamed in warning. He barely dodged sideways as—
THOOM!
A massive brown branch smashed through the ceiling, impaling the spot where he’d stood. At its tip bloomed a grotesque flower oozing viscous fluid, its maw wide enough to swallow a grown man whole.
Though Klein had never seen the man-eating flowers of the southern rainforests, he was certain nothing could be more terrifying or exaggerated than this!
Snap! Snap! Snap!
Branches of the same kind pierced through the walls, floor, and doors, their moist flower-tipped appendages chasing Klein from all directions.
Klein tried his old trick again, using "Instigation" on those branches and flowers, but was shocked to see their movements remain completely unaffected!
The "Instigation" clearly succeeded... Could it be because those flowers no longer have human forms and can directly resist such influence?
Without hesitation, Klein activated the "Burial Blade" hidden in his sleeve. Swinging the scythe, he swiftly severed the encroaching branches before leaping up onto the ceiling.
Only then did he realize the entire space had descended into chaos. Nearly all members of the "Celestial Sect" were sprouting woody tumors and branches, while the more devout leaders had mostly transformed into those man-eating flower branches, hunting down the few remaining normal people and escaped prisoners.
At the very center of the space, a grotesque brown tree was rapidly growing by absorbing desires and emotions!
Seeing this, Klein abandoned all hope of handling this himself. Knowing this was beyond his capabilities, he immediately took out a golden leaf and blew on it.
—Of course, he had already reverted to his Gehrman Sparrow appearance beforehand. Since the clothes he wore while impersonating Tracy were rather gender-neutral, the transition wasn’t too jarring.
Within seconds, the space rippled like water as a silver-haired, red-eyed lady appeared before Klein, her face obscured as if veiled from perception.
This was another contingency Klein had prepared.
Before the operation, he had summoned Lady Yalolan using the golden leaf and requested her to remain nearby, allowing her to descend into this underground space along with the messenger now.
As for why he didn’t call upon the "Messenger Lady"... Firstly, summoning Her without anchoring the ritual to an object would be troublesome; secondly, this infiltration involved the "Mother Tree of Desire," making his own "Messenger Lady" potentially more dangerous than himself.
"The Mother Tree of Desire..." Yalolan frowned at the grotesque brown tree in the distance, remarking to Klein, "I’m starting to regret promising you one free intervention..."
Klein gave an awkward chuckle, worried she might leave upon sensing the danger, and quickly explained, "You just need to stall it until the official demigods arrive."
"If it fully matures, even ordinary demigods would be in danger..." Yalolan shook her head initially, but after scrutinizing the tree for a few seconds with her "Eyes of Mystery," she smiled. "Fortunately, it’s still gathering strength, so dealing with it won’t be too troublesome."
Before finishing her sentence, she raised her wooden staff-like scepter and pointed at the distant tree, murmuring softly:
"Mystery Reenactment — Wu Gang Chopping the Laurel Tree."
As her spell took effect, a mysterious force enveloped the grotesque tree, abruptly slowing its growth. While it continued absorbing desires and emotions, those "nutrients" now seemed to inexplicably leak away...
Wu Gang Chopping the Laurel Tree? Is this an cultural idiom Liu Bo taught Yalolan?
Can "Secrets Supplicant" pathway Beyonders actually turn stories into abilities?!
No wonder Lady Yalolan previously said she could exchange knowledge for secret stories...
Perhaps "secrecy" is one of the prerequisites for this ability...
As Klein’s mind raced with wild speculations, Yalolan casually destroyed all remaining sealed prison cells, freeing the inmates.
Soon, a neatly combed, bespectacled young man emerged from Cell Block A.
Appearing scholarly and refined, he deftly avoided several branch attacks before approaching Klein and Yalolan, bowing respectfully:
"Thank you for your rescue... Ah!"
Before he could finish, his eyes inadvertently landed on Klein. He suddenly screamed, clutched his eyes in agony, and collapsed unconscious...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 834: The Scapegoat
chapters.content:
Chapter 834: The Scapegoat
Backlund, East Borough, Daravi Street, in a cramped but lively tavern.
Xio walked up to the counter, rapped her knuckles on the wooden surface, and said directly to the bartender, "Any valuable intel today?"
If it were anyone else, the bartender would have insisted they order a beer first... but upon recognizing Miss Xio, he thought better of it. After all, doing so might cost him more in the long run.
Not to mention the rumors of her collaboration with MI9.
"Same as usual, 2 shillings per piece of intel... There are 10 in total today," the bartender took a deep breath and quoted his price.
Xio didn’t haggle, simply placing a 1-pound coin on the table.
Only after collecting the money did the bartender produce a piece of parchment covered in writing and hand it to Xio.
Taking the parchment, Xio skimmed through it rapidly, quickly spotting her target in the last entry:
"Governor’s Mansion underground prison in Bayam has been taken over by the ’Celestial Sect.’ Many guards and officers have become cultists."
Pointing at this line, Xio feigned ignorance and asked, "Who provided this intel?"
The bartender glanced at it but remained silent until Xio produced another pound coin, then answered, "A man around 1.6 meters tall... He looked scholarly but had sharp eyes that made him seem unapproachable.
"Even though the intel couldn’t be verified, I still paid him 2 shillings."
Liar! You only gave me 10 pence!
Xio grumbled internally.
Indeed, that so-called scholarly, sharp-eyed man was actually her using the "Hundred Faces Silk Garment" to disguise herself.
After receiving the "reporting" mission from Mr. World, she had pondered how to "legitimately" obtain and report this incident.
Ultimately, she came up with this method—selling the intel to herself.
Looking back, half a year ago she wouldn’t have been this scheming. These tactics were all learned from Ebner and the other members of the Tarot Club.
Of course, Detective Isengar also played a big role—she would never forget the "art of reporting" he taught her during the "Demoness of Affliction" incident.
While her thoughts wandered, Xio maintained a serious expression and asked, "Can you draw his portrait?"
The bartender thought for a moment, then confidently replied, "Yes!"
Without asking for additional payment, he immediately picked up his pre-prepared sketching tools and began drawing.
Is drawing his hobby or dream?
Xio mused as she watched, thinking this wasn’t bad—people needed dreams, unlike Fors who had none.
But when the bartender slid the finished sketch over to her, Xio nearly fell off her barstool...
This is the person I disguised as? You just described him as scholarly—how does this look like a thug?! And to borrow Ebner’s words, this drawing emphasizes ’concept over form’...
Where did you get the confidence to just start drawing?!
Suddenly, someone like Fors didn’t seem so bad after all...
Taking a deep breath to stop herself from cursing, Xio consoled herself that this made it even harder to trace back to her, then pocketed the drawing.
Only then did she turn her attention to the other nine pieces of intel. Most were irrelevant, but one caught her eye:
"’Bryan’s Film Company’ completes nationwide theater rollout; free school students first to benefit..."
With so many free school students nationwide listening to Ebner’s lectures, his potion digestion must be progressing well... Meanwhile, my "Judge" advancement is still sluggish...
Sighing, Xio left the tavern without further delay. Taking the intel and portrait, she boarded a carriage and hurried back to MI9 headquarters in West Borough, reporting directly to Princess Vera.
Of course, during her report, she subtly emphasized the "coincidental" nature of how she obtained the intel.
Princess Vera glanced at her, the corners of her lips curling slightly as she pretended to buy the story. After sharing and filing the report, she immediately went to MI9’s underground sealed artifacts vault to requisition a teleportation-enabled mystical item.
—Her authority had increased significantly since the Great Smog incident.
Then, taking Xio with her, she "traversed the spirit world" and arrived in Bayam.
...
Meanwhile, The Hanged Man Alger found Mr. World’s request rather troublesome. Having already reported issues about the Governor’s Mansion to the church once, doing so again might arouse suspicion—especially since his sources couldn’t withstand scrutiny...
After studying the materials provided by "The World" and pondering for a while, Alger decided to spread a rumor among the sailors: joining a certain club established by the Governor’s Mansion could grant them nights with noble ladies and wealthy merchants’ wives...
After a day or two, he could report the Governor’s Mansion’s issues to the Church again under the pretext of "missing sailors"!
His plan seemed sound, but just as the rumor began circulating among dockworkers, he received a summons from the "Church of the Waves."
Though startled, Alger dared not delay and hurried to the church, where he was personally received by His Excellency "Sea God" Kotman.
"Where did you obtain your previous intelligence about the Governor’s Mansion?" The towering, broad-shouldered Storm Church cardinal and senior "Mandated Punisher" executive stared directly into Alger’s eyes.
Though feeling the pressure, Alger remained calm—"Sea God’s" presence paled in comparison to "The Fool’s." Still, he feigned nervousness and excitement as he answered, "From a man wearing a monocle..."
He described none other than "The Blasphemer" Amon. From fragments of information shared by "The Tower," Alger knew this "Angel of Time" was utterly unpredictable—capable of anything.
This would absolve him of suspicion...
After hearing his account, "Sea God" Kotman remained silent for a moment, then produced a portrait. "Is this the person you saw?"
A portrait? Where did this come from?
Alger wondered as he respectfully accepted it, only to see a highly abstract, ferocious face...
"This... The portrait is rather impressionistic... I can’t be certain," Alger "truthfully" replied.
"If it truly was Him, failure to recognize Him is understandable—He could be anyone," Kotman remarked without disappointment, retrieving the portrait.
Sensing something amiss, Alger cautiously asked, "Your Excellency, has something happened at the Governor’s Mansion?"
Kotman didn’t conceal the truth. "A evil god’s will manifested in the Governor’s Mansion’s ’Nonexistent Prison,’ causing heavy casualties. Even outgoing Governor Larry, his wife, and daughter perished there... Not to mention numerous wealthy merchants’ wives and daughters..."
"The World’s" report didn’t mention such devastation! What happened afterward? Was there truly a evil god behind the "Celestial Sect"? Or does "evil god" refer to "The Fool"?
Maintaining his composure, Alger inquired, "Was it ultimately suppressed by the military?"
Kotman scoffed. "The Moses Ascetic Order’s angel delayed the evil god’s descent. In the end, Her Highness Vera teleported from Backlund to resolve the situation... Regardless, Bayam’s military failed catastrophically—even Admiral Emlyn faces dismissal for negligence..."
The Moses Ascetic Order’s "Pillar"? That Yalolan who submitted the "Book of Calamity" to "The Fool"? Now I understand! Clearly, after providing me the information, "The World" encountered an accident that triggered the evil god’s manifestation. He must have sought "The Fool’s" help, who then dispatched an angel to rescue him!
Excellent—this confirms that among the angels serving the reviving ancient god "The Fool," there exists the Moses Ascetic Order’s "Pillar"...
Where there’s one, there may be others... Perhaps other organizations harbor...
As Alger feigned shock while internally speculating, Kotman continued:
"From surviving cultists, we learned that before the incident, a guard captured ’Vice Admiral of Ailment’ Tracy...
"My water mirror divination revealed traces of that ’demoness’ spirit who stole Kavitua’s relics in the prison.
"I suspect she’s either Tracy herself or closely connected to her!"
Tracy? Did "The World" investigate the "Celestial Sect" to rescue her? That female spirit might be another of "The Fool’s" blessed...
But why is His Excellency sharing this with me?
As Alger prepared to ask, Kotman anticipated his question:
"Tracy’s ’Black Death’ has been seized—she’s currently isolated and vulnerable. I want you to infiltrate her ranks and uncover that peculiar spirit’s identity and her patron."
...
Trier, in the third-floor bedroom of "Ancient Vine Manor," Tracy—barely able to sit up—suddenly sneezed, startling Ebner who was teaching her "rehabilitation techniques."
"Does the ’Vice Admiral of Ailment’ catch colds now?"
Tracy shot him a glare. "In my condition, isn’t that normal?"
Despite her retort, she psychically examined herself, then added uncertainly, "I think the weakening agent’s effects are fading—that’s why I sneezed just now."
Fading? Did Klein wipe out the "Celestial Sect"? Even the "Mother Tree of Desire’s" power is receding?
Activating his "Pure White Eyes," Ebner thoroughly examined Tracy, confirming the residual corruptive energy was weakening—yet not gone, liable to resurge anytime.
A latent threat... Only specialized techniques can fully purge this...
If I can detect it, the Churches certainly can... Many "Celestial Sect" victims must need such techniques now...
This is my chance to digest the potion!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 835: Alliance
chapters.content:
Chapter 835: Alliance
Ebner was deep in thought when Tracy, who was sitting on the bed, suddenly noticed some movement outside the door. Her eyes shifted, and she immediately assumed a pitiful posture, drawing a sorrowful smile as she said:
"You can do whatever you want... I have no ability to resist... There’s no need to use ’inspection’ as an excuse..."
Hearing this, Ebner came back to his senses. He too had noticed the presence outside the door, and couldn’t help but feel a little speechless.
Since the "Vice Admiral of Ailment" learned that Ebner knew she had once been a man, she seemed to have completely let loose, convinced that he wouldn’t actually do anything to her. She kept changing her methods daily to display her charm and tempt him, hoping that he would make a fool of himself in front of Helene, thus driving a wedge between them.
Has she awakened some innate talent for court intrigue? But you’ve got the wrong role for that...
Ebner internally ridiculed her and then decided to give Tracy a deep lesson.
So he used the secret technique "Charm Humans" he had learned from the latter part of the
Feast of Blood
, and, with the enhancement from the "Goddess of Beauty’s Blessing" on his forehead, he instantly threw Tracy into a daze. Her eyes filled with obsession as she stared at Ebner. If she could move, she would likely have lunged at him right then.
At that moment, Ebner canceled the secret technique, and Tracy immediately came to her senses. She turned her head stiffly to see Helene standing at the door with an expression of utter disbelief. Just as she was about to explain, Helene suddenly vanished like an illusion...
At the same time, "Chesia" pushed open the door and entered, reporting to Ebner about the scheduled meeting with the manager of the First Bank the following morning. She gave a slight bow and turned to leave the bedroom.
It wasn’t until this moment that the dumbfounded Tracy finally realized that she had been played with from beginning to end...
She suddenly gritted her teeth and snapped, "What was that ability just now?"
"’Charm Humans,’ a type of secret technique," Ebner glanced at her and explained without hiding anything. "Actually, the technique isn’t that high-level. If your strength was fully recovered, you likely wouldn’t have been so completely charmed."
"You’re immune to my temptation... is that also because of a secret technique?" Tracy seemed to recall something and asked again.
"No... that’s because I’ve seen what true ’beauty’ is."
With that simple response, Ebner heard a knock at the door — this time it was truly Helene.
He greeted his personal "Red Maid" and left the room. After all, Helene’s "rehabilitation massage" for Tracy wasn’t something he felt it appropriate to watch.
After he left, Tracy finally snapped back and felt that she had just been insulted by Ebner:
He’s seen true ’beauty’? So I fall that short, and that’s why I can’t seduce him?
Hmph! Once I recover my ’Pleasure’ ability, I’ll make sure he thoroughly embarrasses himself!
But as soon as she thought that, Helene pressed a few "sensitive" points on her body, and she couldn’t help but moan out loud...
Helene glanced at the completely helpless Tracy, then turned back to look toward the door, and for some reason, sighed.
...
In the living room of a luxurious villa in Bayam—
Princess Vera stepped out from the spirit world and walked through the empty room to the wall on the other side.
A painting hung on the wall, depicting a lavish banquet scene—not particularly original in content.
However, in a corner of the scene, by the dining table, a silver-haired, red-eyed lady was raising a cup of black tea, seemingly extending an invitation to whoever viewed the painting.
Princess Vera thought for a moment, then touched the surface of the painting with her hand. In the next instant, she vanished from where she stood, and a moment later, the banquet scene in the painting gained a beautiful, valiant-looking woman.
Inside the painted world, Yalolan waved at Vera upon seeing her appear. After rejecting a few invitations from gentlemen, Vera finally walked over to Yalolan.
"Mystery reborn? This scene... doesn’t seem very proper..." Vera glanced at the men and women who were occasionally holding hands and heading to the lounge and frowned as she asked.
"This place is called the ’Wall Painting.’ I can’t tell you much about it, but in its original legend, it was indeed somewhat improper... Still, it’s safe enough. If you have something to say, just say it." Yalolan chuckled lightly and took a sip of her black tea.
"You don’t look too well." Vera sat across from her, lifted a cup of black tea, and said while drinking.
"You’re not much better yourself. You hold the position of an angel, yet can only exert the strength of Sequence 3. If it weren’t for the help of the ’Mist of Uncertainty,’ you probably wouldn’t have been able to deal with the divine power of the ’Mother Tree of Desire’ just now." Yalolan gave a small laugh.
"You know what I mean. The pollution of the ’Hermit Sage’ isn’t so easy to overcome. You were fine before only because you became a demigod using Rhine’s blood and gained a sliver of his authority over the ’Unknown.’ That’s how you maintained balance...
"But the fall of the ’Original Moon’ earlier implies that Rhine’s body has now become the ’Goddess of Beauty,’ and She has completely inherited the authority Rhine left behind. You can no longer share the power of the ’Unknown.’" Vera looked at her and spoke in a low voice.
Yalolan scoffed, "The ’Hermit Sage’ is troublesome, yes, but the will of the Outer One in the ’Mist of Uncertainty’ is even more terrifying. Even with both the barrier and Rhine’s methods suppressing it, if you can’t recover to your peak soon, you’ll end up worse off than I am.
"As for the aura of the ’Wilderness of Knowledge’ drawn in by the ’Hermit Sage’ from who-knows-where, I can at least hold out for another year or two. I’ll find him again... Besides, when he was still the ’Wanderer,’ he gave me another possible solution."
But I’ve already found him...
Vera thought to herself, while on the surface she asked thoughtfully, "Fool?"
"That’s right... and Fool will be his dearest friend." Yalolan replied with a smile.
Vera fell silent for a few seconds before finally saying, "I’m here to form an alliance."
"Didn’t you already gather the ’Dragon of Fantasy’ and Hermes as allies?" Yalolan asked in surprise.
"The ’Dragon of Fantasy’ is more like a disposable distraction released by the God of Knowledge or ’Him’ to mislead the divine child’s attention—though that old dragon doesn’t see himself that way...
"As for Hermes... I still don’t know His intentions or goals to this day... That one is incredibly enigmatic!"
Yalolan straightened her posture, thought seriously for a moment, then asked solemnly, "Then tell me—what benefits does this alliance bring you? And what benefits does it offer me?"
...
In the "Amyris Leaf Bar," Klein looked coldly at the master and disciple pair, Darkwill and Roy king, in front of him and said, "It’s time you paid the remaining balance."
They had promised a thousand pounds, but so far had only paid a three-hundred-pound deposit.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 836: The Fool of Nass
chapters.content:
Chapter 836: The Fool of Nass
Upon hearing Klein’s words, Roy King’s expression shifted several times. Then, placing a hand on his chest, he offered a formal bow: "On behalf of our organization, I thank you for your assistance. Personally, I also thank you and that highness for the rescue..."
After finishing, he opened his eyes and looked toward his student, Darkwill, silently asking what was going on.
Darkwill took the cue and said, "His fee was 1000 pounds... but I only had a little over 300, so that’s all I could pay upfront. The rest is up to you..."
Roy King’s lips twitched as he replied, "I don’t have any money on me either..."
Just as Gehrman’s expression grew colder by the second, the demigod of the School of Life seemed to remember something and suddenly said, "But I can pay in another way..."
"What way?" Klein didn’t want to pressure a demigod too much, even if the other party knew he had an angel behind him, even if the chairman of the School of Life’s council might have to call him "uncle"...
If it weren’t for maintaining Gehrman’s persona, he might’ve allowed the man to owe him temporarily.
"It’s that I..." Roy King suddenly recalled the terrifying scene he had glimpsed in Klein earlier and immediately swallowed his words. He hesitated for a moment, patted Darkwill on the shoulder, then dragged him to the window and pointed at a narrow alley outside. "Go down to that alley now. When you see the first person enter it, use your ’talent’ to insult him a few times, then bring him upstairs."
"Teacher, what is this for?" Darkwill was completely confused, not understanding his teacher’s intentions, to the point that he forgot to protest against the mention of his so-called "talent."
"Just do as I say, go!" Roy King snapped.
"Yes." Darkwill didn’t dare talk back. He grabbed his whip and pistol and went downstairs.
Roy King closed his eyes again and turned back to Klein. "Please wait a moment. Your reward will arrive shortly."
Klein didn’t know what he was planning either, but he gave a barely visible nod and said, "Alright."
Watching all this unfold, Danitz glanced at Roy King’s refined face and muttered softly, "Pretty boys like him can’t be trusted... should I remind that lunatic so he doesn’t run off..."
At that moment, under the watchful eyes of Klein and the others, a fierce-looking man with greenish-black tattoos covering his arms, shoulders, and cheeks dragged a little girl into the alley.
Seeing the girl’s mouth stuffed and her struggling desperately, Klein furrowed his brow and was about to step in.
But before he could act, Darkwill mustered his courage and began mercilessly taunting the brute.
The man was stunned for a moment, then his entire face twisted in rage. With a loud roar, he threw the girl aside and lunged forward.
Though Darkwill was a bit useless, he was still a Sequence 8 Beyonder. His basic combat instincts were intact. He immediately raised his pistol with one hand and wielded his whip with the other, ready for battle.
Yet in the very next moment, the brute tripped and fell flat on his face right in front of Darkwill... leaving him frozen in place, whip mid-air, while Klein and Danitz, who were about to use their abilities upstairs, also halted.
After more than ten seconds, the man still lay motionless in a collapsed position... Darkwill recalled his teacher’s words and cautiously squatted beside him.
Out of caution and habit as an "apothecary," he checked the man’s body slightly, and to his surprise found that the man was already dead... The cause of death was cerebral hemorrhage...
So... he had a pre-existing condition, drank a lot of alcohol, was excited, and then, provoked by my words, his brain blood vessel burst? Judging by his speed earlier, he seemed to be an extraordinary being...
Is this bad luck for him, or good luck for me?
Darkwill thought of the slap from his teacher and knew it was probably the latter.
After having a clearer idea, Darkwill first untied the girl who had been thrown aside and let her go, then followed his teacher’s instructions to carry the man’s corpse upstairs.
Because it was dark and there were few people near the inn, his actions fortunately went unnoticed, and he successfully returned to the room where Klein and the others were.
Danitz looked carefully at the burly man under the room’s light and said:"This is ’Walrus’ Anson, the first mate of the Bloodsword Pirates, bounty 500 pounds, suspected extraordinary being on the ’Warrior’ path."
In the pirate world, bounty is an important indicator of identity and status. A 500-pound bounty ’Warrior’ shouldn’t exceed rank 8... Klein, who knew this well, was silent for a few seconds and then asked:"Bloodsword Pirates?"
Danitz casually answered:"A mid-sized faction. Their captain, ’Bloodsword’ Larson, has a bounty of 800 pounds. They operate long-term in the Suniya Sea, reportedly backed by the Feysac people."
Klein nodded, thinking that even if he collected the bounty himself, such a faction wouldn’t cause him trouble. Or rather, he somewhat hoped someone would come for revenge.
Roy King smiled and said:"Even after the cut, a 500-pound bounty should net you at least 300. Adding his ’Warrior’ trait, it should be worth around 700 pounds."
Klein calculated and approved of this "payment" method.
Hearing this, Roy King slightly relaxed. He also didn’t want to offend someone backed by an angel and whose fate was so "terrifying."
He thought for a moment, then took out a round ornament made of golden gears covered by transparent glass and said:"Thanks again for your rescue... Though I already paid you 1,000 pounds, that sum is far less than the value of my life... So, I want to give you this item as my personal token of gratitude."
Klein didn’t take the ornament directly but divined it on the spot. After confirming it was safe, he signaled Roy King to continue explaining its origin.
"This item comes from a real ’alchemist’ and is his token. Holding it allows you to make a request to that master." Roy King stroked the glass surface of the ornament and recalled, "I got it because I helped that master complete one of his proudest works."
Seems luck is needed for that to succeed... Klein murmured internally, then finally took the ornament and asked:"Who is that master, and where is he?"
Please don’t tell me he’s at the Steam Church headquarters...
"He lives in Nas, the capital of the Gargas Archipelago. I don’t know his real name, but people call him the ’Fool of Nas’... because he’s obsessed with researching the impossible ’floating city’...
"Oh, he loves canned wolffish. If you visit, it’s best to bring him a can..."
As Roy King said this, Danitz, who had been listening in, couldn’t help but gag.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 837: The Box
chapters.content:
Chapter 837: The Box
Wolf fish canned food? I remember hearing from a security guard of a ticketing company back at Port Pritz that it’s a kind of food popular along the eastern coast of Feysac and in the Gargas Archipelago. It’s made by salting wolf fish but retaining the blood, and the smell is extremely pungent—both stinky and disgusting...
Recalling this, and glancing at Danitz, who had already dry-heaved just from hearing that someone liked the taste, Klein gained a new level of understanding of how "terrifying" that canned food was. At the same time, he felt a trace of curiosity about its flavor.
"How can anyone like that stuff!" Danitz grabbed a wine bottle from the table and took a swig before calming himself down. "That so-called master known as ’the Fool of Nass’—is he really reliable?"
"Wolf fish canned food is a commodity. If it’s being produced, then there must be a demand for it..." Roy King replied indifferently, then added, "That master’s residence isn’t hard to find. Because of his eccentricities, quite a few people in Nass know about him—it’s just that they don’t realize he’s actually a demigod on the Savant pathway."
Klein stored the accessory properly and decided that when he set out in the future to search for the mermaid and passed by the Gargas Archipelago, he would pay that master a visit along the way and inquire about upgrading the "Creeping Hunger."
—He had originally planned to entrust this to Mr. "Tower," but Ebner declined on the grounds that his current level wasn’t sufficient to craft a true demigod-tier item.
With the matter of compensation settled, Klein stowed away the trait extracted from the "Walrus" and had Danitz carry the corpse, finally preparing to bid farewell to the master and disciple before him.
However, before leaving, he hesitated for a moment and eventually asked Roy King a question that had troubled him for a long time: "Mr. Roy, what did you see on me back then?"
Roy King’s expression stiffened when he heard the question. Only after a long pause did he squeeze out a single sentence: "Indescribable..."
Indescribable? Is it that you can’t—or that you don’t dare? Klein mulled it over silently but didn’t pursue the matter further. He politely took off his top hat and gave a slight bow, then left the room together with Danitz, even closing the door behind them.
After they left, Roy King dazed out for a while, lost in thought. When he snapped back to reality, he nudged his apprentice with his foot and said, "Aren’t you going to go gamble while your luck is still good and earn us the travel expenses?
"After all, I’m afraid you’re going to be extremely unlucky for the next month... It won’t be fatal, but making money from selling herbs will be out of the question!"
"What? That just now was me burning through my luck?!"
...
In Trier, in front of a small villa at the golf club.
Because he had scheduled a morning appointment with the manager of the First Bank, Ebner, after breakfast, took along the lawyers, accountants, and other personnel he had recruited recently, picked up Fors, and headed straight for the headquarters building of the First Bank.
In the carriage, Fors—finally about to open the "treasure"—was a little excited. She couldn’t help but fantasize about what that Mr. Tren might have left her:
"Could it be a generational gemstone? Or some extremely valuable piece of art?"
That was the usual trope in her novels.
Ebner, however, shook his head and rained on her parade in advance: "Since Mr. Tren mentioned Benjamin before his death, and only decided to give you the code after hearing your name... the contents of that safe might be important, but their value might not be that high."
According to his speculation, this was very likely an item or information Roselle had left behind for Mr. Fool.
After all, Benjamin Abraham had been one of Roselle’s subordinates, and the latter had probably heard the name "Fors" from the "Seal of Calamity," which was why the former had left something behind...
Heh! Yet another scheme that appeared to be orchestrated by Roselle, but was actually being manipulated from behind the scenes by the Seal of Calamity!
As his thoughts churned, Ebner saw Fors bring a small piece of cake to his mouth. Without thinking much, he leaned in to take it.
But at that moment, Fors flipped and twisted her wrist, and the cake in her palm turned into a long, hard Intis-style baguette.
"Surprised?" she asked with a smile, then added, "Did you feel a bit disappointed after the surprise? That’s exactly how I feel right now."
"You’re digesting ’Trickmaster’ quite well..." Ebner’s mouth twitched slightly, feeling that he had let his guard down after being fooled by this "slacker"...
After making the bread vanish, Fors said smugly, "Of course. When I was in Tosk, I went out to perform with that ’Lion’ whenever I had free time..."
She had completely forgotten the grief she’d felt when she was dragged out of her room by the lion during the cold winter.
As the two chatted and laughed, the carriage arrived in front of the First Bank’s headquarters building, where a man in his early twenties was already waiting.
He was a client manager at the First Bank, named Aran. Though young, he had already been with the bank for over five years and was considered a rising professional.
And Mr. Ebner Bryan had recently been acquiring properties in Trier on a grand scale. He not only had ample funds and numerous allies but also had the backing of a true god’s church...
In Aran’s eyes, this made him a truly high-quality and distinguished client—someone not to be slighted.
So, upon learning that Ebner wanted to retrieve something a "senior" friend had left in a safe deposit box, Aran had taken the initiative to handle all the preliminary procedures and had come personally to receive this rising star in Trier’s game of power.
Thanks to this internal professional’s prior arrangements, Ebner and Fors quickly made their way into the heavily guarded underground vault and arrived in front of Mr. Trun’s safe deposit box.
Ebner gave the area a brief scan with the "Pure White Eye" and discovered eight hidden Beyonders nearby. Three of them seemed to be bank security and weren’t much of a threat... but as for the other five, he couldn’t tell which faction they belonged to!
Looks like my recent high-profile activities have indeed drawn attention from interested parties. But that’s fine too—what I’m using is a strategy out in the open. I don’t need to hide anything.
At that moment, Fors, under the guidance of bank staff, arrived in front of a very complex-looking locker and recited the incantation Mr. Trun had given her.
Soon, the safe was opened, and its contents were revealed to Fors, Ebner, and the hidden Beyonders.
It was a box—made of crystal, with its lid open, yet completely empty inside.
And other than being made of precious materials and resembling an antique, the box had no extraordinary properties... it was just an empty box!
Realizing this, most of the hidden Beyonders immediately left. Aside from the security, only one person remained completely still, continuing to wait there.
At that moment, Ebner found the box increasingly familiar. After a brief moment of thought, he recalled:
"The box that the ’Goddess of Fortune’ opened in the final mural of the ’Trial Temple’ corridor looks a lot like this!
"This must be the item the Elf King ordered the ’Queen of Calamity’ to deliver to the Western Continent, right? Why is it completely empty now?"
(end of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 838: The Salty Fish Strikes Back
chapters.content:
Chapter 838: The Salty Fish Strikes Back
What was Roselle—or whoever’s really pulling the strings—trying to achieve by leaving this empty box here?
Given that it was specifically meant for "Fors"... they likely know about the "plot," meaning the real target might be "The Fool"...
With an artifact personally crafted by the Elf King, Klein could undoubtedly divine significant clues from it...
Is Roselle sending a message to "The Fool"? Or is the "Seal of Calamity" using Roselle as a conduit?
Pondering this, Ebner activated his "Pure White Eyes" again, attempting to extract residual traces from the box. Unfortunately, time had eroded all meaningful imprints—unless his "Retrospection" evolved into "Insight," recovering useful information seemed impossible.
Meanwhile, Fors showed no disappointment toward the empty box. On the contrary, she examined it with keen interest, already weaving potential backstories in her mind.
It wasn’t until their return to the club’s villa that she snapped out of her reverie, announcing to Ebner:
"Now that I’ve received Mr. Teron’s bequest, there’s no need for me to stay in Intis. I’ll depart for Loen tomorrow."
"I’m heading back to Loen tomorrow too—I can teleport you directly..." Ebner offered, recalling his promised "dream adventure" with Audrey from the last Tarot gathering.
Fors shook her head. "No need. I’ve joined a traveling circus troupe that tours major northern cities, with Backlund as their final stop. Perfect for ’acting’ while sightseeing."
The salty fish is actually putting in effort? What sparked this?
Ebner’s astonishment manifested as him reaching over to feel Fors’ forehead for fever.
She instantly decoded the gesture, indignant. "Do you really see me as that lazy?"
"Yes." He didn’t hesitate.
If I don’t push myself now, you and Xio will leave me completely behind... Same goes for the Tarot Club...
Fors swallowed the thought as Ebner withdrew his hand, producing a bell from his pocket.
"This summons my messenger. If you encounter trouble, write to me—I’ll teleport over immediately."
"Got it." Fors accepted it, only then realizing how intimately casual his forehead touch had been... and how she’d grown accustomed to such contact without a second thought.
...
Beneath St. Samuel’s Cathedral, Backlund.
What began as a perfunctory investigation into ’Fool’-related incidents to buy personal freedom had unexpectedly borne fruit. Through dream-walking interviews with figures connected to the ’Lanevus Case,’ ’Capim Case,’ and ’Flesh Abyss Incident,’ Leonard Mitchell uncovered disturbing patterns.
"Both the Lanevus and Capim cases involved that private detective—Sherlock Moriarty—and his journalist friend Mike Joseph. While peripheral, they’re viable leads... As for the ’Flesh Abyss,’ I attempted entering Reverend Hael’s dreams but got forcibly ejected..."
"...From what I’ve learned, Sherlock Moriarty also appeared during the Duke Negan assassination, providing crucial leads..."
"Come to think of it, he looks familiar... Is he some wanted criminal in disguise?"
Leonard recalled the faces from his dreams, put on his red gloves, and stepped out of his office to brew some black tea to clear his mind.
Just then, a colleague approached with a thin invitation in hand.
"What’s this?" Leonard asked, puzzled.
"It’s an invitation to Ms. Daly’s wedding..." The colleague looked visibly dejected.
Though Ms. Daly often made people uncomfortable with her teasing jokes, she was quite popular among the Backlund Nighthawks. The thought of her marrying someone else clearly bothered him.
"Oh, a wedding invitation..." Leonard began with a smile, then froze mid-sentence before exclaiming, "Wait, whose wedding?!"
Misinterpreting his reaction as shared heartbreak, the colleague patted his shoulder sympathetically.
"Ms. Daly’s wedding... Hard to accept, but it’s true."
"Who’s the groom?" Leonard forced a composed smile.
"Some merchant named Dwayne Dantès, just returned from overseas in his forties..." The Nighthawk grumbled, "No idea how he charmed Ms. Daly."
After his colleague left, Leonard’s smile faded into solemnity.
He knew all too well about Daly and Captain Dunn’s relationship—he couldn’t believe she’d consider marriage before avenging the captain...
Either this Dwayne fellow used underhanded methods to deceive her...
Or Daly has discovered something and is using him!
...
Stoen City, capital of East Chester County, Kingdom of Loen.
After socializing with local nobles at the villa, Audrey received a message from "The World."
Glancing at her maid Annie supervising the servants nearby, she crouched beside her golden retriever by the wall, eyes sparkling as she whispered:
"Susie, you’ll be getting a gift soon. Excited?"
The old Audrey would’ve blurted,
"Susie, your gift is here!"
—risking the dog deducing she could materialize objects indoors (a clear hint at ritual magic to the mysticism-studying retriever).
This rephrased version suggested Audrey had merely received word of an impending delivery, leaving countless plausible explanations.
Reading her mistress’s genuine joy, Susie nearly vocalized a question—but noticing Annie’s approach, she defaulted to tail wags.
Then, a man’s voice abruptly echoed around them:
"Ma’am, your ’Psychiatrist’ characteristic delivery has arrived..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 839: The Hand of Lyon
chapters.content:
Chapter 839: The Hand of Lyon
The "deliveryman" who spoke was none other than Ebner.
After leaving Fors earlier, he had attended a dinner party hosted by Fanny’s father, Councilor Surrey. Ebner had expected the councilor to bring up the Susit Bank matter, but the seasoned politician proved more patient—the entire evening was spent building rapport and showcasing the "close ties" between the Surrey family and Ebner, without any overt negotiations.
Clearly, Councilor Surrey was a masterful player, adept at tailoring his approach. Upon learning from the butler about Ebner and Fanny’s "relationship," he had immediately shifted to emotional appeals...
Meanwhile, he strategically leaked mixed truths about the dinner, deliberately shaping perceptions of Ebner’s "alignment" to reassure the Surrey faction’s minor shareholders.
Though Ebner later discerned some of these machinations, he wasn’t displeased—this aligned perfectly with his own plans.
The Surreys want to borrow my influence? Well, I need their Church of Steam connections!
Despite the late Archbishop Surrey’s demise, the family retained considerable influence. Ultimately, Ebner stood to gain.
Moreover, as their collaboration deepened, Fanny’s standing within the Surrey family would rise accordingly. Ebner had already positioned her as his political proxy in Intis—even investing her with a "Briber" characteristic to navigate those waters more smoothly, given his foreigner status inherently limited his own ceiling.
—This particular "Briber" characteristic had come from the "Shadow Saint," purified by Lilith and left in Ebner’s possession.
After the dinner, Ebner stayed overnight at the Surrey residence. At dawn on Saturday, he bid farewell to Fors at the circus troupe before teleporting directly to Bayam to host a Beyonder gathering at the "Amyris Leaf Bar"...
There, he met Klein—currently roleplaying as a "janitor" mopping toilets—and accepted the commission to deliver the "Psychiatrist" characteristic to Miss Justice.
—After subjugating the "Demoness of Pleasure," Klein had released both a soul and this characteristic, which coincidentally matched the needs of Miss Justice’s dog.
Ebner speculated Klein’s roundabout delivery method stemmed from the other man’s recent studies of certain mystical notes that periodically drained his spirituality—making it unreliable to respond promptly if Miss Justice requested the item via prayer...
Compounded by Miss Justice’s restricted movements at her ancestral East Chester estate, missed connections would require rescheduling entire rituals.
In any case, immediately after the tavern gathering concluded, Ebner teleported back to Backlund with the characteristic, then used his spell "Ebner’s Spirit Stroll" to reach East Chester’s capital—where traces from his previous stay with Xio provided anchor points.
Locating the Hall family castle needed no elaboration; as nominal lords of East Chester, their residence was common knowledge.
Thus, Ebner materialized abruptly behind Audrey and Susie.
Startled by his voice, Audrey instinctively gripped "Lie," while Susie arched her back into combat stance—until recognition dawned.
"It’s alright, he’s not an enemy," Audrey assured, though Susie remained wary.
"Are you certain?" The retriever’s gaze stayed fixed on Ebner—his undetected approach marked a security failure, and he knew her biggest secret.
Audrey hesitated only briefly before nodding firmly.
"Alright... woof." Susie relaxed with a bark.
"Miss Susie, might I borrow Miss Audrey privately? Would you mind guarding the door?" Ebner suggested amiably.
That smile reminded Susie of a certain portly man she’d once encountered in Backlund’s West District Park, sending an involuntary shiver down her spine. The golden retriever glanced back at Audrey for confirmation.
After brief consideration—aware of Detective Bryan’s questionable reputation but lacking evidence of outright impropriety, plus the implicit safeguard of "The Fool’s" oversight—Audrey nodded. "Do as Mr. Bryan says."
With a tail wag and final sniff of Ebner’s scent, Susie exited, nudging the door shut with her hind leg.
Alone, Audrey ventured cautiously: "’The Tower’?"
"’Justice,’" Ebner acknowledged with a slight nod, making no effort to conceal his identity. After all, "Ebner Bryan" had nothing to hide beyond some gossip.
So it really is Mr. Tower!
Though she’d suspected, this confirmation solidified matters.
"You’re early—we agreed on nighttime." She gestured to the wall clock.
After a pause, Ebner explained: "Time zone difference." Having just returned from nighttime in Bayam, his timing was off.
Audrey blinked before laughing. "We’ll need to clarify time zones for future appointments." Smoothly shifting topics, she asked, "You mentioned a ’Psychiatrist’ characteristic... Is this from Mr. World?"
"Correct." Ebner produced a metal case from his coat.
As Audrey inspected it, Susie’s urgent barking interrupted—their private window closing.
"As you see, my social obligations continue. We’ll speak in detail tonight." She pocketed the case.
"Of course. Rest assured, your father’s Beyonders won’t detect me." With a bow, Ebner dissolved into the air.
That somehow makes me more nervous...
Audrey mused, though thoughts of "The Fool" steadied her.
Within the hour, she excused herself to her private chemistry lab, arranging the characteristic and supplementary materials across the workbench.
"Susie, remember the potion preparation steps?" She straightened proudly, relishing her mentor role.
"Woof! Yes!" Tail wagging furiously, Susie finally understood her gift.
"Try preparing it yourself."
Susie stared at her paws. Silence.
Audrey froze mid-smile before catching herself.
"No need to say it—I know you’re thinking ’I’m just a dog, how can I mix potions?’" she preempted smoothly while internally cringing.
Then Ebner’s voice reappeared: "Actually, there’s a spell called ’Hand of Lyon’ that would enable Miss Susie to brew it independently."
Seizing this "spreading the mysterious" opportunity, Ebner enthusiastically demonstrated—
"Woof?" Susie tilted her head. "Why develop such a spell when your hands work fine?"
(Truthfully, the technique originated from a certain lion’s adaptation of "Mystery Pryer" abilities...)
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 840: Abby’s Diary
chapters.content:
Chapter 840: Abby’s Diary
"This is a secret technique developed by a big cat named ’Leon’ to assist in experiments. It’s essentially a refinement of some ’Witch’ spells, allowing Beyonders of other pathways to perform them... Specifically, it uses a ritual to give one’s ’astral body’ the ability to interfere with reality to a certain degree..."
While explaining, Ebner demonstrated the technique a few times in front of Audrey and Susie.
In his view, the secret technique wasn’t particularly complicated. Even some Sequence 9s with decent spirituality could pick it up quickly—let alone a "Psychiatrist" and a "Telepathist" standing right before him.
Audrey gave it a try but found it much more difficult in practice than Mr. Bryan had described...
Her spirituality was sufficient, but the precise control over her mental and spiritual body’s power wasn’t her strength. Forget finely manipulating it into a "hand"—even barely shaping it was a struggle.
Seems I’m not a genius in this area either... Fortunately, I already have real hands, so this secret technique isn’t essential...
Suppressing her slight frustration, Audrey turned her emerald-like eyes toward Susie, carefully observing her. She was prepared to console Susie with her own failure the moment the dog gave up, so it wouldn’t get disheartened by the gap between expectations and reality—a disparity that could very well cause psychological issues!
"But that’s alright. Miss Audrey the ’Psychiatrist’ is always ready to provide ’soothing’! Hmm, I prefer the term ’psychoanalysis’—it sounds more professional."
As Audrey’s thoughts drifted, Susie’s voice suddenly sounded by her ear:
"Audrey, I did it!"
As she spoke, several glass containers moved in the air under Susie’s control, floating and assembling themselves.
"This is just a bit harder than using spirituality to vibrate the air and speak. I had to try three times before I succeeded." Susie set the items down, turned her head, and wagged her tail.
"..." Audrey was momentarily at a loss for words.
Was Miss "Justice" just... outdone in a
Versailles
way by her own dog?
Ebner, who had been watching with amusement from the side, instantly felt a surge of "delight." He thought this moment definitely deserved to be "recorded" so he could share it later with Xio and Fors.
Still, seeing Audrey so shaken she was beginning to doubt herself, Ebner "kindly" offered a word of comfort: "This secret technique was developed by a Beyonder creature, after all. It’s only natural that one of its kind would learn it faster."
Hearing this, Susie said in surprise, "Audrey, you haven’t mastered it yet? Hmm... I can demonstrate it a few more times for you..."
"That won’t be necessary for now. We’re short on time. You should start preparing your potion first." Audrey smiled gently after a brief pause.
Then she turned and looked seriously at Ebner. She suddenly felt that the scholarly, generous, powerful, and mysterious image of "Mr. Tower" in her heart had just crumbled.
But she had to admit—this version of him felt more real, less like a bundle of neatly stacked "labels" as he’d seemed during the Tarot Meetings.
...Then perhaps my previous judgments of Mr. Hanged Man, Mr. World, Miss Hermit, Miss Judgment, and Miss Temperance weren’t entirely accurate either...
Maybe beneath Mr. World’s cold exterior lies extreme gentleness; maybe under Miss Temperance’s icy appearance burns a passionate heart; maybe behind Mr. Hanged Man’s calculating, self-serving shell, there is sincerity and principle; maybe beneath Miss Judgment’s mature facade, there is still innocence and naivety...
After all, people are complex. Everyone has many different "sides"...
Recalling the private conversations and thoughts of the manor’s servants that Susie often shared with her, Audrey came to a new realization.
Come to think of it, among the Tarot Club, the only ones I feel confident I can truly see through, besides The Moon and The Sun, are the ones I know best—like The Magician, Fors...
As Audrey sighed, Susie had already finished preparing the potion herself and began licking it.
Thanks to her relatively low profile, she was able to roam freely throughout the manor and villa, eavesdropping on private conversations and "reading" the true thoughts of the maids. Her "acting" was extremely convincing, so there were hardly any abnormalities when she advanced—Susie successfully became a "Psychiatrist."
At the same time, Ebner received the corresponding feedback. His digestion progress increased once more.
...
Meanwhile, in the mysterious palace above the gray fog, Klein was enduring mental "torment" as he read the diary of a lady named Abby.
"All five survivors of that experiment gained some sort of ’special’ ability.
"Abby’s was the power to cause ’pain’... As long as she made physical contact with someone, they would experience immense ’pain’ in the days that followed... This pain could be physical or emotional—it wasn’t fixed...
"As for another survivor, a lady named Bianca, her ability was unclear. But according to Abby, anyone who tried to ’bully’ her or use mind control on her ended up in a very bad situation.
"Lofia’s whereabouts are unknown, but her ability was extremely unusual—she could restore destroyed objects within a certain range during moments of extreme emotion.
"As for the remaining two survivors, Abby didn’t know their names or powers, but during a chance encounter with the ’Pale Admiral,’ she vaguely sensed something familiar..."
At this point, Klein had to close the notebook. The accumulated "pain" had reached a level even his spiritual body couldn’t endure, forcing him to stop for now.
He rubbed his temples and thought to himself,
The ’Pale Admiral’ Maria... I recall she may have some connection to Roselle. At the very least, her signature saber, ’Pale Justice,’ was forged by him...
Could she also be a product of that experiment? Or rather, was the experiment itself orchestrated by Roselle—just like the ’Dream Labyrinth Tower’? Could it have been one of his posthumous arrangements?
Hmm, next time during the Tarot Club’s usual "after-meeting," I’ll show this notebook to The Tower. Maybe he’ll know something about it.
Also, when I met the ’Pale Admiral’ Maria aboard the Future, she gave me the summoning method for her "messenger"...
And that "Messenger of Reproduction," Miss Abby, hadn’t been in the governor’s prison previously, so she escaped the purge...
I could write to Maria and ask her to send someone to intercept Abby. Perhaps we can learn more from her.
Speaking of which, Maria’s twisted and extreme sense of "justice" really isn’t normal... Anyone else trying to "act" in such a way—channeling desire to that extent—wouldn’t have succeeded at all.
...
Late at night, without daring to bathe and still wearing her day clothes, Audrey lay pretending to sleep—when she heard a knock on her bedroom door.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 841: Audrey’s Dream
chapters.content:
Chapter 841: Audrey’s Dream
"Who is it?" Audrey called out, even though she was already sure in her heart that it could only be Mr. Tower outside her bedroom. After all, no one else would knock at this hour.
"It’s me, Miss Audrey... May I come in?" Ebner’s deep voice came from outside.
Audrey was startled—she hadn’t expected him to answer so loudly... But after a dozen seconds passed without hearing any scolding from her servants or bodyguards, nor Susie’s barking, she understood that Mr. Tower must have used some method to keep their movements unnoticed.
Honestly, Mr. Tower’s abilities were truly frightening... Fortunately, even though his reputation wasn’t the best, he was still a fairly upright person. He never used his "invisibility" to stalk a lady, and even before entering my room at night, he courteously asked for permission...
That made sense. If he were really some kind of creep, Xio and Fors wouldn’t be so close to him.
While thinking this, Audrey straightened her clothes before standing up and saying toward the door, "Come in."
As soon as her voice fell, a figure phased through the wooden door and entered the bedroom.
"Mr. Tower, it seems like you’re quite experienced in knocking on a lady’s door in the middle of the night." Audrey’s eyes twinkled with humor as she teased, easing the awkwardness of meeting her "internet friend" in person.
"No, quite the opposite. Usually, it’s the ladies who come knocking on my window at night..." Ebner replied "sincerely."
It was, after all, the truth.
"Xio or Fors?" Audrey asked meaningfully, probing for Mr. Tower’s attitude toward her two friends and trying to find out which one he liked.
"Both," Ebner replied simply, offering no further explanation.
Even though Fors hadn’t knocked on his window, she had teleported onto his bed before...
Audrey discreetly activated her Telepathist ability but couldn’t glean any emotional leaning from Ebner. Realizing that he had methods to suppress the powers of the Spectator pathway, she stopped pursuing the question and instead asked, "Mr. Tower, when did you realize I was ’Justice’?"
I knew even before I transmigrated...
