"But the black mist Vera displayed earlier in the underground theater didn’t seem like a Mist Monster... Did Owen mistake it?
"No... in his memory, the mist he saw around Vera before wasn’t the one I saw earlier...
"Vera can control multiple types of mist? Variable in form?
"Hm... variable... Vera likely belongs to the Tamara family... the Uncertain Mist?!"
At that thought, he felt he had touched upon Vera’s secret and guessed at the reason for her friendliness.
The "Uncertain Mist" and the Tamara family were supposed to appear only near the original story’s end, after Earth’s barrier grew weaker—this shouldn’t be the right time.
So, Princess Vera was over 90% likely to be a "butterfly" from a previous transmigrator... as I guessed before, she probably recognized the "Pure White Eye" like Lilith and the Goddess, which is why she trusted me so much?
Everywhere I go, I find traces of my predecessors... they’re even more present than Roselle!
After a few wry thoughts, Ebner resealed the box containing the Eyes of Asmo and stored it in the Quiz Labyrinth.
Come to think of it, after making Owen into an avatar and verifying the perfected secret technique, Ebner could have, once Owen outlived his usefulness, let the avatar perish and extracted the "Manipulator" characteristic for a cross-path advancement.
Unfortunately, many hidden deities—and likely previous transmigrators—wouldn’t allow it. After all, they wanted to cultivate a Saint, even an Angel, of the
Reader
pathway!
Moreover, "Dreamer" ingredients and characteristics were even harder to obtain. Even Owen had despaired of finding them and considered switching to Cognizer...
But for me, as long as I stick to the Reader pathway, the road to at least Angel is already paved...
With a sigh, Ebner studied the necklace-shaped Sealed Artifact known as the "Proof of Lost Mind" for a while longer before leaving the chamber and sealing it again.
As for other Beyonder items? Nothing remained...
Owen had spent his entire fortune on this plan to ambush Vera, consuming years’ worth of accumulated ingredients, items, and even personal favors to secure the help of "Pride," "Greed," and "Sloth."
Hiring an angel to oversee things had even wiped out all the contributions he’d accumulated in the Psychological Alchemists over the years!
"And then there are all the conditions he agreed to with George III... Just thinking about it is headache-inducing—what a mess!
"Fortunately, according to my plan, the Delien family will soon fall into decline, and when those conditions can’t be fulfilled, it won’t be my fault..."
With a trace of melancholy, Ebner stepped from the living room into the bedroom. The moment he opened the door, he saw Princess Vera waiting—already out of her evening gown, golden hair loose, clad only in a silk robe as she approached.
Unlike Xio’s simple look in a robe, this princess’s form was elegantly contoured. Though she didn’t reveal much fair skin, she was still undeniably enticing.
Seeing this, even with Owen’s memories, Ebner didn’t quite know how to respond for a moment.
After all, those memories felt more like third-person "short films" than anything with real emotional weight.
And this wasn’t like researching "academic" matters, where he could remain perfectly calm...
Vera, however, seemed unconcerned, smiling as she said, "In fact, according to Owen’s habit, you should be preparing another outfit for me to wear when I leave tomorrow.
"As for my gown from earlier, you should tear it a bit so as not to raise suspicion."
Miss, you understand Owen’s habits even better than I do with his memories! As expected of the head of MI9—you’ve investigated everything down to the last detail...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 876: A Fleeting Tarot Gathering
chapters.content:
Chapter 876: A Fleeting Tarot Gathering
Vera’s beautiful golden hair hung down in slight disarray, part of it spilling over her back, the rest drifting over her chest. It added a hint of allure to her otherwise heroic features.
Ebner’s gaze unconsciously followed those strands of hair into the collar of her silk nightgown, where whiteness and shadowy valleys entered his eyes at the same time...
He had to admit, whether it was her figure, her looks, her aura, or her personality, Princess Vera matched several of his favorite types. She was very tempting to him.
And before they had acted together, she had already said she would fully cooperate in his "acting" as Owen. Even if he wished to display "lust," she would comply... judging from her current attitude, she had no intention of going back on that promise either...
But Ebner still suppressed that "desire," and did not go any further.
It was not because of some moral scruple. To be honest, if it had been someone he was familiar with—Xio, Fors, Jane, Edwina, Fanny, or even Helene or Gwen with their seductive charm—he would not have withstood the temptation...
But this Princess Vera before him, he had only met her a few times, and knew nothing of her background! And the normally reserved and dignified princess described by Xio was showing such initiative before him... This instead raised great wariness and concern in his heart.
After all, in such a mysterious world, reckless indulgence might bring about a tragic end.
Whether it was the
Demoness of Affliction
Ray or the
Saintess of White
Katarina, both had fallen prey because of this very aspect...
With so many negative examples, Ebner naturally dared not attempt such intimacy with Vera before he had fully understood her purpose and background, before he had established a strong bond with her.
Not even with an avatar!
Vera, watching him, easily guessed what was on his mind. A faint smile appeared on her lips. She actually hadn’t intended to really go further with him just yet either—the timing was not right, it was still too early.
Moreover...
At that thought, Vera glanced out the window at the red moon and the stars hanging in the night sky.
Next, instead of moving closer, she simply motioned for Ebner to sit on the bed. She herself sat down on the other side, smiling as she brought up serious business: "How do you plan to deal with the
Saintess of White
Katarina? She is still trapped in the dream woven by ’Arrogance,’ but as a
Demoness of Unaging
, that dream can at most restrain her for a day."
Seeing her cease her "offensive," Ebner exhaled in relief, though he couldn’t help feeling a little regret and disappointment.
As a man of normal desires, he actually somewhat enjoyed such close contact with a beautiful woman...
Steadying himself, he thought for a moment before replying: "Since I am now Owen, I’ll temporarily maintain ’control’ over her. That Sealed Artifact, the
Proof of Heartloss
, still holds sway over her.
"After all, if we release her now, and she guesses that ’Owen’ failed in the previous ambush, it could ruin our plans.
"And if she doesn’t guess, then she will inevitably seek revenge on ’Lust,’ which would still be troublesome.
"As for killing her, that would certainly draw the
Demoness Sect’s
investigation. I had previously leaked to the higher-ups of the
Demoness Sect
that Katarina might be under Owen’s control... As the prime suspect, I would suffer the witches’ retaliation.
"So it’s best to keep her in her current state for now."
Clearly, Ebner had thought this through in advance. His explanation was well-structured and clear.
Vera nodded after hearing him, then added, "I’ll have ’Arrogance’ plant in her a memory where ’Lust’ emerged victorious... though I’ll need you to provide the outline. ’Arrogance’s’ own scriptwriting is... crude! It would surely be seen through."
As she said this, she couldn’t resist grumbling about her collaborator.
Ebner’s lips twitched, but in the end he had no choice but to agree to her request.
After that, while drafting the script, Ebner also discussed matters concerning the
Mist Demon
with Vera. To his surprise, she suddenly chuckled and said with a smile:
"So that’s why Owen kept making moves on me... all for this. Though his reasoning was full of errors, the conclusion was right—I do indeed know the whereabouts of the
Mist Demon
."
Hearing this, Ebner quickly set down his pen and looked up at Vera, hoping she would share more.
But Vera only gave him a playful glance and said with a laugh, "When you truly become a
Prophet
, and bring me something that moves me, then I’ll tell you."
...
The night passed. After sending Vera away, Ebner left a message for George III using the contact details in his memory, then used the excuse of a family summons to depart Backlund.
Not long after leaving the city, however, he "switched accounts," letting Owen enter the
Quiz Labyrinth
to escape MI9’s surveillance.
Afterward, Ebner returned to Backlund, planning to attend the Tarot Gathering before using the
Teleportation Altar
to travel to Trier.
During this, he discovered another drawback of his refined mystical art: the Owen avatar could not stray too far from his main body. At most, they could operate simultaneously within the same large city; otherwise, the "signal" would cut off...
...
That week’s Tarot Gathering was similar to the last three. There was no Roselle diary, hardly any transactions, and very little information shared.
The only notable thing was that Mr. World had successfully hired the
Hermit
Cattleya. In a little over a month, at the capital of the Gargas Archipelago, the White City, Nas, he would meet her and board the ship of this
Admiral of the Stars
to sail to the far eastern edge of the Sonia Sea—toward that nearly illusory and perilous ocean, in search of the wild mermaids that dwelled there.
The
Hermit
Cattleya seemed interested in meeting the Tarot members in reality. After only a few seconds of thought, she agreed to Mr. World’s request. But given the danger involved, she set a relatively steep price:
3000 pounds!
Klein’s first reaction was to give up and instead take Mr. Hanged Man’s
Blue Avenger
, or Admiral of Stars Maria’s Pale Saintess.
But considering that Mr. Hanged Man’s ship had many sailors from the Church of the Storms, limiting his freedom, and that the easternmost Sonia Sea was indeed extremely dangerous; while Admiral of Stars Maria rarely ventured near the divine war ruins and was unfamiliar with that region...
In the end, Klein still accepted the Hermit’s terms. She would wait for one month near the Gargas Archipelago starting in early April. If he missed the deadline, the deal would be canceled.
After this transaction was settled, the Tarot members shifted into free discussion. Everyone shared bits of local news, and then Mr. Fool declared the meeting over.
As the scarlet light swallowed the figures of the others, dissolving them into the mysterious space above the gray fog, Klein, seated at the lowest place, turned toward Ebner and said simply:
"Maria succeeded in capturing Abby!"
Ebner’s spirit stirred at once, while a trace of surprise flashed through his thoughts:
Huh? Didn’t you say Abby was on the Black Death with the witches of the Demoness Sect, making it difficult for the Pale Admiral to strike?
I remember I even thought of tossing Tracy back into the sea as bait to draw them out...
Wait, could it be that Klein actually adopted that plan, disguising himself as Tracy to lure Abby out, and that’s how he succeeded?!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 877: Klein’s Compatibility
chapters.content:
Chapter 877: Klein’s Compatibility
Noticing the strange look in the "Tower’s" eyes, Klein couldn’t help but ask aloud, "What’s with that expression of yours?"
"Nothing..." Ebner definitely wouldn’t voice such a guess that might make Mr. Fool fly into a rage from embarrassment. He shook his head, pushed aside the messy thoughts in his mind, and instead asked, "Are you on the Pale Holy Maiden right now?"
"No... but I’ve already arranged to meet with Maria tonight near Oravi Island. I plan to take her ship to another island." Klein paused for a moment before adding, "If you want to take Abby away, it’d be best if you come before ten o’clock tonight..."
I don’t just want to take Abby away. I also want to take the Pale Admiral with me... Unfortunately, we don’t have a deep relationship, so she most likely wouldn’t agree to let me ’study’ her...
Besides, that "Pale Justice" sword in her hands is extremely dangerous, and her body is sealed with the characteristics of a Devil... Even with Owen as a Manipulator avatar, it’s still impossible to hypnotize her quietly...
What’s more, she’s also a friend of Klein and Edwina. I can’t put them in a difficult position... Forget it. There are still other survivors from the experiment eleven years ago waiting to be studied. I’ll set Maria aside for now and wait until my strength improves further, until I can handle her the way I secretly handled Bianca.
As his thoughts turned, Ebner gave a slight nod and asked, "Where should I find you?"
"Sweet Lemon Bar," Klein answered.
Thanks to his time exploring the fifth level of the Dream Labyrinth Tower, Ebner still remembered the layout of Oravi, including the location of that bar. So he directly said, "Let’s meet at eight."
After that, the two exchanged some information and ended their usual "Transmigrator’s Meeting," returning to reality.
In a hidden basement beneath a hunter’s cabin on the outskirts of Backlund.
After retracting the "Wall of Spirit," Ebner activated the "Teleportation Altar" set up there, opening a portal leading to Bayam’s "Fragrant Manor."
Since the Tarot Club operated on Backlund time, it was nearly seven in the evening in Oravi. Ebner didn’t dare delay. After arriving at Fragrant Manor, he immediately wore the "Azure Shadow" ring, transforming himself into a special spiritual body. Then, with the help of the "Door" card, he invoked the secret technique "Ebner’s Spiritual Stroll."
His figure gradually faded and disappeared into the void.
Everything around him became like an illusion—colors deepened, overlapped, and swiftly receded.
Although Ebner hadn’t yet mastered the ability to position himself during Spirit World Travel, unable to locate Oravi Island precisely within the chaotic layers of colors...
Klein, however, carried with him the hilt that could manifest the "Burial Blade." This wondrous item bore the power Ebner had imbued through the "Pure White Eye," and could naturally serve as a locator.
So, after just a dozen minutes, Ebner walked out of a secluded alley, put away the "Azure Shadow" ring forged from Wraith characteristics, and returned to corporeal form.
After a moment’s thought, he swapped places with Owen’s body, then used the "Marionettist" nurtured in the magic mirror to cast the Faceless Man’s power, transforming into the "Professor."
This way, even if someone stripped the "Professor" disguise, what would appear underneath was still Owen—nothing that pointed back to Ebner...
Thinking this, he glanced at the signboard outside the alley. It read: "Oravi Medical Aid Foundation, 10 Blackwood Street."
"Isn’t this the place where Mr. Fool volunteers?" Ebner muttered softly before pushing open the door into this charity with the Church of the Evernight Goddess backing it.
The female receptionist, flipping through a newspaper, looked up as he entered. She hurriedly approached with enthusiasm. "Do you need something, sir?"
—Her warmth was clearly thanks to the "Professor’s" exceptional appearance, refined bearing, and tasteful attire.
Ebner didn’t answer. He merely locked eyes with her, and she suddenly "remembered," saying, "So it’s you... Please, follow me. Mr. Sinbad Wallent is in Ward No. 2..."
—Sinbad Wallent was the alias Klein used during volunteer work.
An actual demigod’s hypnosis is far stronger than the ’pirated’ version I simulate with the Pure White Eye!
Sighing inwardly, Ebner soon followed the receptionist—who introduced herself as Juana—to the door of Ward No. 2. As soon as it opened, he saw a man in his twenties cleaning up vomit with tools.
When the "Professor" walked in, the man’s impassive face twitched slightly before he carried on as if nothing had happened.
Klein naturally recognized the "Professor’s" appearance and knew it was one of the "Tower’s" disguises... Or rather, since the healing ritual for Celestial Sect remnants had spread, "Professor" had become famous throughout the extraordinary circles of the Rorsted Archipelago.
Many who had suffered were finally able to rid themselves of weakness and return to normal thanks to his contribution. So even though the navy and the Church of the Storm wanted to uncover his true identity, they had only released sketches, not a bounty.
In fact, thanks to the spread of this restorative ritual, as well as Mr. Bryan’s "teaching videos" widely adopted in free schools across Loen and Intis, and the occasional tutoring of Tarot members, Ebner had digested nearly all of the Potion of the "Secret Arts Tutor." By his own estimate, one or two more effective and complete acts of "role-playing" would be enough to finish the digestion.
After nearly ten minutes, Klein finally finished his work. He washed his hands in the bathroom while saying to Ebner at his side, "Aren’t you worried about using this face? What if someone recognizes you?"
"As long as I don’t run into a Saint or Angel by bad luck, there’s no problem. Ordinary people can’t even remember seeing me." Ebner explained with a smile.
The two chatted as they left the Oravi Medical Aid Foundation, had dinner at the Sweet Lemon Bar, and then headed together to a small town outside Oravi.
At exactly ten o’clock, inside a cargo warehouse in that small town, Ebner followed Klein to meet the Pale Admiral Maria, who had long black hair, brown eyes, and fine yet striking features.
Beside her lay an unconscious girl. She was beautiful, but even in unconsciousness her brows furrowed tightly, as though enduring some hidden pain.
That should be Abby...
Ebner thought just as Maria, clad in heavy armor, walked toward them with clanking steps. She first offered Klein a knight’s salute and exchanged a few polite words, then turned her gaze to Ebner and greeted, "Hello, Professor."
After Ebner nodded in return, Maria paid him no further attention, focusing instead on her conversation with Klein.
Seeing this, Ebner absentmindedly stroked his chin and grumbled inwardly:
I recall that the Pale Admiral, like Miss Temperance, is also a Wraith...
Could it be that Klein has the best compatibility with Wraiths? Fated to attract ’ghost women’?
Hmm, come to think of it, his favorite and most cooperative puppet in the future is also a Wraith.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 878: Ebner’s Speculation
chapters.content:
Chapter 878: Ebner’s Speculation
Backlund, East Borough, in a room with heavy curtains where only faint candlelight illuminated a corner.
Sitting at the head of the bed, Tracy tidied her jet-black curls, her eyes fixed on the clock hanging on the wall without blinking.
When the hour hand pointed to ten, she quickly stood up. Under the candlelight, her slender and graceful figure swayed as she walked enchantingly to the full-body mirror. Then she stretched out her right palm and brushed it over the surface of the glass.
A layer of black flame ignited, quietly burning the air before quickly extinguishing without a trace, leaving the mirror dark and profound.
Within the mirror, shadows and light rippled and soon revealed a vast hall, its floor paved with deep-black stone slabs, and eight columns of the same color rising high.
This was a scene within an underground ruin, the place where Tracy and her mother tacitly exchanged items.
Before long, a figure in a simple and pure white robe appeared in the ruins. It was the Saintess of White Katarina. She tilted her head toward Tracy’s direction, her gaze meeting her daughter’s for two seconds, before smiling faintly like a living masterpiece.
Suddenly seeing her mother appear, Tracy was startled. After all, in previous communications, she had never seen anyone show up.
But Tracy quickly reacted, a trace of joy flashing in her eyes. She parted her lips impatiently and asked:
"Mother, did you successfully break free of the control?"
In her view, her mother did not seize her and even chose to appear in person for contact—this already explained everything.
Katarina, however, gently shook her head and spoke in a teasing tone: "No, I lost... I came to find you because my master ordered me to."
At these words, Tracy’s heart skipped a beat, nearly breaking contact and fleeing. Yet, as a pirate admiral with much experience, she forced herself to remain calm, recalled her mother’s temperament, and tentatively said, "Mother, don’t make this kind of joke..."
"I’m not joking... I’m still under my master’s control!" As she spoke, she displayed the red gemstone that had already lost its luster. She continued, "Although the stone you found is indeed useful... my master also had helpers. My struggle failed."
Seeing that Katarina’s words didn’t seem like a lie, Tracy’s face turned grim. With some despair, she said, "So, you’re going to capture me? And make me, together with you and Mother, serve that so-called master?"
She no longer tried to escape. In the same Backlund, her mother, who was directly related to her by blood, could easily find her. Escape was impossible.
"You should feel fortunate. My master has recently found a new ’plaything’ and has lost interest in you... Moreover, he has already left Backlund." Katarina’s lips curved into a faint smile. "But you must pay the price to redeem yourself, otherwise I’ll send you to my master’s bed right now."
Hearing this, Tracy was shocked by the shamelessness of her mother and that master, her hands trembling with anger.
So the meaning is—because he doesn’t ’play’ with me, I should be grateful?
Disgust filled her, yet in this nearly hopeless situation, she had no choice but to bow her head. Enduring the humiliation, she asked in a low voice, "What must I pay?"
"A task." Katarina’s eyes shifted as she glanced at her daughter. With a soft laugh, she said, "In Backlund, find a certain person. A woman in her twenties, whose defining trait is an uncontrollable desire for knowledge and secrets."
Tracy originally wanted to wait for her mother to finish before speaking, but after waiting more than ten seconds without more detail, she asked uncertainly, "That’s it? Nothing else?"
"That’s it!" Katarina nodded firmly. "Only these traits. You must do your best to filter those who match and report once a week."
When will this task ever end?
Tracy took a deep breath and secretly decided to complete the mission while also seeking help to escape from that so-called master once and for all.
But who can I ask for help? Not only am I surrounded by enemies, but the Demoness Sect has also branded me a traitor... Hmm... maybe I can find Gehrman. He seems to have a powerful organization backing him... And there’s Ebner... He can easily summon demigods, so his background must not be simple. But he’s the last person I want to beg from!
While Tracy was calculating inwardly, outwardly she accepted the task. She then shifted the subject and asked, "What about Mama? If she continues to hunt me desperately, it will interfere with me completing the task."
"Your mama has already taken command of the Black Death and will soon become a new pirate admiral under our sect... However, she has decided to keep using your name." Katarina spoke with a voice as beautiful as a song.
At these words, Tracy’s expression darkened, a storm brewing in her eyes. The momentum of a pirate admiral emanated from her, but soon she deflated, for she could do nothing about it.
"Alright, don’t be angry... As your mother, I can provide you with an idea to complete the master’s task." Katarina smiled with her lips pressed together.
"What idea?" Tracy asked, her voice slightly hoarse.
"Simple. Reveal the location of the ruin I’m currently in—the one from the Fourth Epoch United Empire. If the target truly cannot resist her thirst for knowledge and secrets, she will surely come!"
...
Deep within Groselle’s Travels, in the central hall of the City of Miracles, Levished.
Just as he had with Bianca earlier, Ebner, after borrowing the Black Emperor card and the Error card from Mr. Fool, bade farewell to Klein and Maria. He then carried the unconscious Abby and "teleported" to the ritual space beneath the Surrey family manor in Tosk.
After that, the two of them entered the imagined world within Groselle’s Travels through the "back door."
By using the Error card’s elevated version of the "Underwear Stealing Technique" several times to steal protections outside of "secrets," Abby’s hidden condition was finally revealed under the gaze of Ebner’s monocle.
Combined with the earlier "academic" physical examination of Abby, Ebner gained new understanding of the experiment eleven years ago:
As I suspected, Abby is like Bianca, also polluted by the power of five different primal essences. But unlike Bianca, her pollution is dominated by the Shadow World.
Her special ability is the Curse of Pain—by enduring her own constant pain, she curses others, forcing them to feel the same agony!
Because this pain comes from the Source of Curses, it is almost impossible to dispel... Anyone who has had relations with her will be cursed, and one day in the future, that pain will erupt...
And after she curses someone, her own pain will temporarily lessen... though it soon returns. For the sake of that brief respite, she chose to join the Celestial Sect, using her beauty to constantly alleviate her suffering.
That said, the path she chose is actually the "Demoness." She is already Sequence 6, the Demoness of Pleasure...
This is the first time I’ve seen a Demoness who was originally a woman. The constant "pain" she feels unexpectedly fits the pathway...
But in this case, the aftermath in Bayam involving the Celestial Sect may still hold hidden dangers... Once the curses Abby left behind erupt, my Secret Restoration will be useless...
Because that curse comes from pollution by primal essences, it carries the power of authority itself, which is why it cannot be cleansed. Only authority can counter authority! Hmm, when I return, I’ll pray to Lilith and ask her to send that angel fused with uniqueness to eliminate this hidden threat.
Within the echoes of the Hall of Honesty, Ebner opened the Pure White Eye and observed Abby once more, then began summarizing:
Comparing Bianca and Abby... I can draw some common points...
First, both are women... and this applies to the other three survivors as well... But why did only women survive? Or was it that the experiment originally only chose women as subjects?
Second, whether Bianca or Abby, their special abilities manifest only through intimate relations... Is this coincidence, or some inherent attribute? As for the other three survivors, Lady D of the Aurora Order remains unclear, and the one in Backlund hasn’t been found yet, so I won’t consider them for now...
But the Pale Admiral doesn’t seem like someone like Bianca and Abby, right? In the eyes of outsiders, she is as pure and upright as a saint...
Though within her body, she sealed a demon Te-...
At this thought, Ebner’s heart suddenly stirred. He immediately connected it with Inspector Roselle’s carefully crafted image of "justice," and with the Fountain of Youth lie woven by the Undying King Agaritou. At once, he had a flash of insight:
Perhaps purity and justice are what Maria’s ritual requires?
When those who yearn for her justice and purity ultimately discover her evil and corruption... the ritual would then be complete, wouldn’t it?
Her "justice" is easier to understand—after all, that is her "evil." By using primal essence, she twists extreme "justice" into "evil"! But purity... Maria doesn’t seem like that kind of person... Though it’s not impossible—she may have an unknown side to her...
Right, Bianca and Abby’s special abilities are triggered through intimate relations... Maria very likely is the same! And her sword, Pale Justice, carries an abnormally powerful force that requires periodic release of power... Its method of judging "sins" is also similar to an authority projection from the Nation of Disorder...
Could it be that her special ability is triggered through... that?! By the way, wasn’t that sword crafted and later modified by Old Huang? What painstaking effort indeed!
Writer’s block... finished only at this hour, time to sleep.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 879: Deep Sea Festival
chapters.content:
Chapter 879: Deep Sea Festival
If my guess is correct, then the "Pale Admiral" should be the more special one among the five survivors...
After all, Abby and Bianca were both unable to control the powers they gained from corruption, but Maria could turn hers into a controllable force by relying on the "Pale Justice"...
This must have been something Roselle prepared beforehand. He really was key to that experiment eleven years ago!
The only thing I don’t know is what his goal was...
But all five survivors are women... And their power could only be triggered through the act of "reproduction"...
Was it the influence of the "Brood Hive" or the "Mother Goddess of Depravity"?
Yet none of them carried the contamination from those two sources...
Perhaps their origins themselves were problematic?
Of course, some of these guesses still need to be verified... After all, the contents decrypted from "Amon’s Monocle" may not necessarily be accurate.
As his inner voice echoed around him, Ebner bent down, picked up Abby, then simulated the ability of "Dream Traversal" and left the "City of Miracles."
However, he did not immediately depart from the illusory world within
Groselle’s Travels
. Instead, he found a city and placed Abby inside it.Abby was, after all, different from Bianca. After joining the Celestial Sect and becoming a believer of the Mother Tree, she had stained her hands with the blood of countless innocents. Ebner hadn’t killed her outright only because he considered that the survivors of the experiment might still be of use.
And since she had been marked by the Mother Tree of Desire, keeping her imprisoned in the outside world would easily draw the attention of its believers, who might not only rescue her but even endanger Ebner in return...
Thus, after some consideration, Ebner decided to imprison her inside
Groselle’s Travels
.
First, the place was hidden enough. Even the Mother Tree of Desire, before the Earth’s barrier vanished, was unlikely to gaze inside... and Abby herself could never leave.
Second, the illusory world lay close to the entrance of the "Sea of Chaos." With some arrangements, it could suppress the "Pain" in Abby’s body. Ebner planned to integrate it into a "Secret Technique," then teach it to her. That would count as a relatively complete enactment of the "Secret Technique Mentor" role.
Lastly, keeping Abby, the "Source of the Curse," isolated near the "Sea of Chaos" would delay the outbreak of curses on those who had once been with her.
So, when Abby awoke from her coma and opened her eyes, she saw a young and handsome gentleman. She instinctively thought she would face something she had long grown used to, especially since she could already feel her undergarments had been removed...
Yet just as she prepared to offer no resistance and accept her fate, the man tossed her a reading list, then pulled out a blackboard and began giving her lessons...
This turn of events left Abby utterly dumbfounded. She suspected something about the way she had woken up was terribly wrong.
...
Fog Sea, Isaca Island.
Named by Emperor Roselle after the great explorer under his command, Captain Isaca, this island lay far from trade routes and was poor in resources. It had long since become a private pirate port and a hub for smuggled goods.
Thus, its only port town appeared bustling, filled with adventurers, pirates, profiteering merchants, spies of various nations, prostitutes, and all manner of people.
Though there were no official authorities in town, the public order was relatively decent. At the very least, shootouts over a single argument were rare.
That was because the town’s master, the controller of the private port, was a mid-sequence Beyonder. His guards not only had guns and cannons but even an old military airship!
Rumor had it that this dockmaster was a "Wind-blessed" and had deep ties with a certain great family of Intis...
In addition, his twelve-man elite guard, though rarely seen, had been recognized by the observant as former crewmen who once served under the "Admiral of the Deep Sea."
Inside a lounge of a tavern in town, the blue-haired Tran youth was reporting his gathered intelligence to his captain, Miss Gwen.
After months of sailing and adventuring, Gwen, Lydia, and Tran had finally reached the Fog Sea, where they discovered Emperor Roselle’s treasure—a complete ghost ship, the
Black Throne
!
But because of this ship, many pirates coveted them, and even a fleet from the "Admiral of the Deep Sea" had been drawn in.
Fortunately, Roselle had left behind a powerful Sealed Artifact on the
Black Throne
. With its aid, Miss Gwen, a "Weapon Master," displayed strength approaching Sequence 5. She truly carved out her own reputation, making the title "Lady Dragonmight" resound even in the Fog Sea. Even the "Admiral of the Deep Sea" acknowledged her strength and withdrew his fleet.
Of course, since the factions vying for the
Black Throne
included the Intis military, Miss Gwen naturally found herself on the wanted list, with a bounty of 10,000 filkin.
As for why the trio came to Isaca Island, it was to trace the whereabouts of a slave ship.
Although the northern continent’s nations had abolished the slave trade, slavers at sea never vanished completely. They had merely become rare. Yet for some reason, the black-market slave trade had revived recently.
Normally, this had nothing to do with Miss Gwen. When she first started roaming the seas, she might still have had compassion, but over time she inevitably grew numb.
This time was different. On a ship from the northern Fog Sea, one mainly selling bankrupt Feysac farmers, Miss Gwen spotted her uncle.
Her maternal family had been particularly unfortunate these past six months.
Her uncle had first lost his government job after being targeted by Lord Panin of the Church of the God of Combat due to Gwen’s involvement. Later, gangsters forced her grandfather to sell their family’s hot spring inn at a cheap price.
Fortunately, a countess intervened, offering a good price that convinced them to leave Indo Harbor and move far from Panin’s old sphere of influence, relocating to Viborg, a coastal city in the Feysac Empire.
To avoid spending their savings idly, Gwen’s uncle had used the money from the inn’s sale to start a trading company, engaging in maritime trade between Feysac and Intis.
But on one voyage, his ship veered off course and, by ill luck, ran into a mid-sized pirate band...
The result was predictable: not only were his goods stolen, but Gwen’s uncle was captured and sold to slavers.
When Gwen received the news, passed on through great effort by her grandfather, she began tracking the slave ship and eventually found clues near Isaca.
After sighing over her family’s misfortune, Miss Gwen composed herself and asked the Tran youth, "Did you find out where the batch of slaves sent ashore was taken?"
Tran shook his head, replying awkwardly, "Slaves seem to be taboo on this island. I didn’t dare probe too deeply, or it would surely draw suspicion... It wasn’t always this sensitive, but a few months ago, after the ’Admiral of Stars’ intercepted a shipment of slaves, things here became increasingly secretive."
He paused, then added, "But I overheard someone slip up once, saying only a small portion of the slaves are sold to the northern continent. The rest are sent to some small island off the western coast of the southern continent.
"They say it’s under the orders of the ’Admiral of the Deep Sea’..."
The Admiral of the Deep Sea?
Miss Gwen nodded thoughtfully, while also making up her mind.
...
March 11th, Friday.
Intis, outskirts of Trier, top floor of the Delien family castle.
Driving Owen’s body, Ebner knocked on the door of the Prime Minister’s office. After being permitted, he entered.
The Prime Minister, seated behind his desk, waved him to sit and then said with a smile, "Owen, the annual ’Deep Sea Festival’ is about to begin. You know of it, yes?"
The so-called "Deep Sea Festival" was actually a ritual offering live humans to the sea monster "Segust," which had deep ties with the Delien family, to ensure it continued to guard their merchant ships and strike at competitors.
Of course, that was what Owen’s memory contained. Ebner suspected it was only the surface explanation.
"Yes, it will be held between April 1st and April 10th on Sili Island, off the southern continent’s western coast, to help it maintain its sanity and resist madness," Ebner replied cautiously with a nod.
"Normally, the ritual is co-hosted by the ’Admiral of the Deep Sea’ and myself... But as you know, the political situation in Intis is unstable. I cannot leave, so I want you to go in my stead!
"Lord Elvonos has always taken this matter very seriously. You must complete this mission," the Prime Minister said sternly.
Elvonos was the "Grand Duke of Blood," one of the three great demon families of the Nos line.
Ebner had long intended to seize this mission. After all, the sea monster’s "Prophet" characteristic was the advancement material he had "reserved." He hadn’t expected the task to fall into his lap so readily.
Recalling the identity implied by that name, Ebner carefully asked, "What do I need to be mindful of?"
The Prime Minister gave him an approving look, then used spirituality to seal the room before explaining, "The offering ritual’s effect of helping the sea monster maintain sanity is only superficial... In truth, it subtly allows it to make contact with a certain existence, awakening that existence within it.
"That’s why in its early years, the creature needed a sacrifice only once every ten years. Now it requires one annually!
"Your true mission is to use an item to observe its condition after the ritual. If you detect changes, you must immediately recite Lord Elvonos’s honorific name and report to Him!"
So that’s it... No wonder the Delien family would go to such lengths to conspire with a sea monster!
Who do they want it to connect with? The "Tenebrous World," or the "Mother Tree of Desire"?
Hmm, most likely the former... If I’m not mistaken, that sea monster once fused the "Tenebrous World" imprint stripped from the God of Luck by Adam! Perhaps it has become the Mother Tree of Desire’s tool to tempt the Tenebrous World...
While Ebner pondered, the Prime Minister pulled out a telegram and handed it to him, continuing, "By the way, a slave ship transferring through Isaca Island has drawn the attention of the newly active ’Lady Dragonmight’...
"Though the ’Admiral of the Deep Sea’ should be able to handle it, judging by the timing, you might arrive in time. You could lend a hand in capturing that lady, ensuring the slaves’ safety.
"Heh, I hear ’Lady Dragonmight’ is a beauty. If you manage to capture her, she’s yours to deal with as you please."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 880: Fanny’s Revenge
chapters.content:
Chapter 880: Fanny’s Revenge
Ebner flipped through the telegram in his hand, then picked up a photo that had obviously been secretly taken of Gwen and Lydia. He appeared to show interest in "Lady Dragon Might," but in his heart, he couldn’t help worrying about her.
After all, judging from the report sent by the manager of the Delien family on Isaca Island, even though Miss Gwen and Tran had disguised themselves, they had been noticed immediately upon disembarking. The information they had obtained was all deliberately leaked by that manager...
If Miss Gwen really acted on such intelligence to intercept the slave ship, she was bound to fall into an ambush!
Fortunately, that manager in Isaca Town, intimidated by the reputation of "Lady Dragon Might," did not act rashly. Instead, he wanted to wait for Vice Admiral Deep Sea’s fleet to arrive, or for the navy of the Delien family’s military faction to come, before beginning the plan to capture Gwen alive.
Miss Gwen probably didn’t know that this batch of slaves was connected to the Delien family and the Sea Monsters’ "Deep Sea Sacrament." She thought they were just ordinary slave ships; otherwise, she would not have been so careless...
But this small mistake might very well bring her an extremely tragic fate!
There should still be time!
Ebner silently calculated the distance and timing, and made his judgment.
At the same time, he pretended to accept the task "with pleasure," smiling as he said, "You really do know me best."
The Prime Minister smiled "kindly" at these words, then said with some playfulness, "Speaking of which, you’ve been back in Trier for two days, yet you haven’t met with your old ’friends’... Just how charming is that Ruen princess, that you’re so infatuated with her?"
So, in your eyes, the strange thing is that I didn’t go and ’comfort’ those friends? Although, judging from Owen’s memories, you’re not wrong...
It seems I really do have to leave Trier soon... Otherwise, Owen’s change in behavior toward women will eventually arouse suspicion, and I can’t possibly ’hypnotize’ them every single time!
Besides, as the leader of the Psychological Alchemists in Trier, I had many subordinates across various industries, and almost every pretty woman among them had been involved with Owen...
If I continue to stay in Trier, it’s inevitable I’ll cross paths with them... What then? Facing a group of psychology experts, even hypnosis at the demigod level could only fool them for a while. The flaws would eventually be exposed!
And I could never bring myself to indulge in ’lust’ the way Owen did...
Ebner sighed inwardly, but on the surface, he gave no answer to the Prime Minister’s indecent question. He only put on a smile that looked meaningful but in truth meant nothing at all.
The Prime Minister had only asked casually, so he didn’t press further. He raised his teacup, took a sip of black tea, and signaled the end of their talk, instructing Ebner to call Seyrow in before leaving.
More than ten minutes later, the "Black Knight" Seyrow Delien left the Prime Minister’s office. He then went straight to an inconspicuous standalone house, where Ebner was already waiting.
"My Lord!" After sealing off the space with spirituality, Seyrow immediately knelt on one knee and greeted him respectfully.
"There’s no need for so much formality..." Ebner waved his hand, then asked, "What did he want with you? Was it about the conflicts with the Flais and the other noble families?"
"Yes, just as you foresaw. Although each clash was small, over the past month, the Prime Minister has clearly sensed those allied families gradually distancing themselves from him. He asked me for details.
"As per your instructions, I shifted the blame to Johnsen of the Flais family... In truth, he deserved it. Of late, he has caused the most trouble, dragging several families under the Flais into constant disputes with Delien." While replying, Seyrow stood up and personally brewed a cup of Duke’s Black Tea for Ebner.
—After a period of observation, he had confirmed that Ebner preferred the taste of Duke’s Black Tea to Queen’s Black Tea.
"So, his order to you has to do with Johnsen?" Ebner took a sip of tea and asked.
"Exactly! He told me to kill the ’Guardian’ bodyguard protecting Johnsen, as a warning to that young master and the Flais family behind him." Seyrow nodded as he spoke.
Although Johnsen was a "spiritual contamination compatible vessel" with demigod characteristics of the Flais family, and thus enjoyed certain privileges, there was no way the family would have a demigod personally guard him!
So the Flais had spent considerable resources and favors to hire a powerful Sequence 5 "Guardian" to protect him.
With the Guardian’s "shield" present, few below the high sequences could break through that defense, no matter the form of attack.
Currently, Johnsen’s house arrest had been lifted, but he was only allowed to move within Trier’s city limits. As long as the Guardian blocked one or two attacks, the family’s demigods could rush in for support at any time.
It had to be said, the Prime Minister’s choice of target was indeed very clever. Killing a hired Guardian would not create a blood feud with the Flais, but it would intimidate their mid- and low-sequence Beyonders and ordinary members... Even Johnsen himself, though resentful, would probably be too afraid to leave home for some time, let alone make trouble for Delien.
Ebner had been in Intis long enough to be well-informed about these matters, so he asked straight to the point, "When and where do you plan to act?"
"Tonight!
"From what I’ve learned, Johnsen intends to lead a few friends in attacking a Delien family member’s residence at No. 112, Florent Street. They plan to steal back the Sun Priest characteristic that was forcibly bought at the last auction, and then present it to his ’Lightprayer’ lover." Seyrow had guessed what his master intended and gave a detailed report.
"Tonight... Florent Street, No. 112..." Ebner repeated the address, feeling a strange sense of fate.
Florent Street had been named by Roselle to commemorate the Soren family member who had once wanted to recruit him as a younger brother.
That man had also been "similar" to their ancestors... And now, today, Johnsen—the "compatible vessel" of another ancestor—was destined to fall on this street named after Florent.
...
Meanwhile, in Trier’s Soren District, at the mansion on 22 Saint Martin Street.
Ebner’s true body was in a meeting with Helene and Fanny, discussing the upcoming weekend premiere of
Roselle Gustav
.
"Lion" Leon squatted in the corner, listening in. The "Magic Mirror" was controlling "Chesia" to take notes. As for Krosfia, as usual, Ebner had sent her out to keep tabs on the major families.
"Once the film premieres nationwide this weekend, the subtle messages within it will stir up a storm within a week, reaching a climax over the next one or two months... Of course, that requires the cooperation of the newspapers and media!" Ebner paused here to glance at the Lion in the corner, and only when he nodded did Ebner turn to Fanny. "This is also your opportunity. If you seize this wave in advance, you can quickly raise your renown, and in turn, increase your standing in parliament."
As she listened to Ebner speak so eloquently, Fanny found him utterly captivating. Her gaze unconsciously carried admiration. Only when the subject shifted to herself did she come back to her senses and answer seriously, "I will seize this chance."
"You too," Ebner said, turning to Helene, "As the producer of a film under such scrutiny, your pressure will be great... but so will the opportunity."
Helene nodded solemnly, her eyes full of determination.
She suddenly felt that her life had a true goal, and working toward that goal brought her far greater joy than making money through business ever had.
Just as Ebner was about to give a rousing speech and paint a big picture for his employees, he suddenly frowned, then quickly smoothed it over, smiling at Fanny as he said:
"Your chance for revenge has come!"
To be honest, the true culprits behind the death of Fanny’s grandfather, Mr. Surrey, were the Saintess of White Katarina and "Lust" Owen. But one of them was now Ebner’s own avatar, and the other was not suitable to be killed yet... More importantly, Fanny could never kill a Demoness of Unaging, even if she didn’t resist.
Thus, Johnsen Flais became the target Ebner prepared for Fanny’s revenge. After all, he was not innocent in Mr. Surrey’s death, and Fanny had always believed him to be the true culprit.
Back then, he had indeed been in intense conflict with Mr. Surrey over the Intis ambassador position.
"Really?" Fanny was first stunned, then overjoyed. She rushed over to Ebner.
...
That night, at No. 112 Florent Street.
When Johnsen and his three friends carefully sealed off the area with a ritual to prevent the Delien family member from escaping or calling for help, then kicked open the door—
They were stunned to see six mechanical puppets aiming twelve gun barrels straight at them.
The next instant, twelve steam-powered machine guns spewed out demon-hunting bullets, weaving lines of "flame" across the space.
(The End of the Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 881: Boom!
chapters.content:
Chapter 881: Boom!
Faced with such a "lavish" attack, Johnsen and his three friends had no time to react before they were each struck by dozens of demon-hunting bullets.
Among his three companions, the strongest was only Sequence 7, while the other two were of lower sequence. They were instantly torn apart by the bullets.
As for Johnsen, a layer of green radiance flared around him first—his extraordinary clothing had detected the deadly danger and automatically formed a "barrier."
But the "barrier" was not high-grade. It only blocked the fiery serpent of bullets for one second before being breached.
Yet that single second was enough for him to respond!
Faced with the threat of death, Johnsen displayed the composure expected of a mid-sequence Beyonder. He neither flew into a rage nor panicked. Instead, he calmly activated two charms—one forming a "shield," the other hardening his skin to steel—while solemnly proclaiming to the bullets about to strike him:
"God said, null and void!"
Normally, counting the already-damaged barrier from his clothes, three layers of defense plus "Judged Invalid" should have been more than enough to block the barrage of demon-hunting bullets, allowing Johnsen to calmly search for the assailant or prepare other countermeasures...
But Johnsen quickly realized he was wrong. The bullets tore through the shield’s defense, and as more slammed into the same spot, they pierced even his "steel skin"!
With a crisp crack, the gemstone ring on Johnsen’s finger shattered of its own accord, and his figure "blinked" three meters away.
It was obvious that another life-saving magical item had just activated.
Even so, Johnsen’s face looked grim. He had already guessed the reason why his "Judged Invalid" had failed.
"Briber!
"My ambusher is a Briber... the bullets acted as bribes, weakening my defenses!"
The thought had barely flashed across his mind when the gun muzzles of those mechanical puppets swiveled, aiming at him again.
Not daring to waste another moment, he quickly drew out a badge and rubbed it desperately between his fingers.
The badge, called "Return Path," could open a teleportation gate to a preset location... but the range was no more than ten kilometers, and activation was troublesome—it required ten rubs back and forth.
As the fiery tongues of bullets were about to lash at him again, Johnsen finally succeeded in activating the gate. But when he stepped into it, he passed straight through... teleportation failed!
Only then did he recall—before attacking the Delion family member here, he had arranged a ritual around the house...
That ritual not only blocked sound, sight, and spiritual fluctuations, but also screened teleportation!
Damn it...
Before Johnsen could think further, a fresh barrage of bullets struck him, shattering the other identical ring on his other hand. Once again, he "blinked" three meters away.
I only had two rings... that was my last Blink...
Johnsen admitted to himself inwardly. Without hesitation, he tore off the protective amulet he carried close and crushed it.
It was his final life-saving measure. Inside was sealed a trace of power from his granduncle. Crushing it would alert its owner.
And Johnsen’s granduncle was an archbishop of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun, a true demi-god who could reach anywhere in Trier within moments.
Johnsen prayed desperately that he was close by, and could arrive as soon as possible!
Yet just as the thought settled, an invisible mechanical puppet suddenly appeared behind him and fired a "Flesh Bomb."
Caught unprepared, Johnsen failed to evade. With no more magical items left, he suffered a heavy wound immediately.
—That invisible puppet was the unfinished work once left behind by Mr. Sari. For some reason, it had appeared here.
Fortunately, Johnsen himself was an "Arbiter," naturally resistant to the filth and corrupting powers inside a "Flesh Bomb," so no severe negative effects lingered.
But this strike crippled his leg, drastically reducing his mobility. He could only watch helplessly as the puppets all aimed at him and opened fire again!
"Ah!" Terrified to the extreme, Johnsen shut his eyes. Yet after several seconds, no pain came. Confused, he opened them—only to see the surrounding scene shatter abruptly.
Then he awoke.
"That was just a dream? A ’Nightmare’ or a ’Dreamweaver’?" Johnsen felt no relief at this escape. Instead, dread grew—his enemy might be far scarier than imagined.
I should have noticed earlier... The ritual I set up could never block teleportation. That level of effect was beyond my ability!
And when I crushed the amulet, the power’s feel was wrong too...
The enemy manipulated my thoughts... plus had dominion over dreams... A demi-god on the Audience pathway? But why would a Saint personally deal with me? And in such an insidious way!
While resentment surged within, Johnsen discovered he couldn’t move at all, as though pinned by sleep paralysis. Meanwhile, his three companions—like possessed corpses—approached with vacant eyes, stripping away his clothes, rings, charms, amulets, badge, and even a revolver, delivering them all to a man and a woman stepping out of the house.
Johnsen recognized them both. The man was Trier’s rising star, Ebner Bryan—the very one whose interference had ruined his Suhit Bank acquisition plan...
The woman was Fanny of the Sari family... He had taken part in killing her grandfather.
She’s here for revenge? How dare she?!
But... where was the demi-god on the Audience pathway?
On the other side, Ebner, monitoring Johnsen’s thoughts, received the items from the three mind-controlled men. Adjusting the golden-rimmed glasses on his nose, he paid the "hosting fee," then tossed everything into the "Answer Labyrinth."
—Those three had their minds ensnared by the Devil; they were nothing but puppets now.
After all this, Ebner smiled at Fanny beside him and asked, "Feeling better?"
The one who had struck Johnsen in the dream was Fanny. Ebner had not given her much direct aid, only six endlessly-loaded mechanical puppets and a recreated version of Mr. Sari’s unfinished assassin puppet.
This not only let her vent her rage but also tested all of Johnsen’s hidden trump cards.
After all, as the scion of a centuries-old family, personally valued by his clan, it was natural he’d have numerous life-saving measures.
The reason Ebner had her act in a dream was to avoid leaving too many traces in reality, which investigators could later uncover.
Fanny, thrilled to have personally defeated her grandfather’s killer, also understood Ebner’s intentions. She nodded seriously and said, "It’s enough. Kill him."
Hearing this, Johnsen desperately wanted to cry out a warning—that killing him would make the Flais family pursue them without end!
But his body was powerless. He couldn’t even open his mouth. He could only watch as that woman, Fanny, stacked explosives inscribed with magical runes atop him and set a thirty-second timer.
Ebner walked to his side, squatted, and cut open his finger, taking a drop of blood.
When only three seconds remained on the timer, Ebner quickly smeared the blood onto the cover of a deep-brown book.
Johnsen barely glimpsed the ancient Fusac words:
"Grossel’s Travels"
The next instant, he and the explosives vanished from the spot.
...
Meanwhile, in the World of Imagination, before a snowbound cave, the "King of the North" Yurisian had just stepped outside when a "meal" appeared at its feet.
It was not surprised. In the endless years, unlucky outsiders often stumbled upon it right away.
But this "meal" was not only stripped bare but also piled with strange items on its body...
What’s this? Smells odd... spices?
Lowering its head, its violently glowing blue dragon eyes peered closer for a better look.
And in the next moment—
"Boom!"
—— Auspicious Chapter Number
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 882: Conspiracy
chapters.content:
Chapter 882: Conspiracy
The White Horse Manor was located in the northern suburbs of Trier. It was one of the ten most famous wineries in Intis, and also served as the residence of the Flais family in Trier.
At this moment, many family members who worked and lived in the capital were summoned there.
The initiator was Mr. John Flais, the current patriarch of the Flais family and the Speaker of the National Assembly.
This Speaker was forty-eight years old. Although he was only a Sequence 6 "Conspirator," due to his superb skills and sharp political instincts, he held great prestige within the family.
Even the two family demigods who were already archbishops of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun respected him greatly, canceling their original schedules to answer his summons.
At this time, Speaker John Flais, seeing that everyone had arrived, did not bother with preamble. He directly instructed his assistant to bring in a corpse.
It was the corpse of a half-giant nearly three meters tall. His figure should have been extremely robust, but at this moment he appeared emaciated, as though his flesh and blood had been devoured by something.
"This is... Bors? Wasn’t he Johnson’s bodyguard? How did he become like this?" A family member examined it for a while, suddenly recognizing the corpse’s identity, and said in shock.
"If Bors ended up like this... then what about Johnson? Has something happened to him?" Other family members reacted, realizing the patriarch’s intention in summoning them.
They all looked toward the patriarch, trying to read something from his expression. After all, Johnson was not only the family’s cultivated demigod candidate, but also Speaker John’s son...
Archbishop Drew Flais of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun examined Bors’s wounds and then spoke with certainty: "He was killed by the ’Black Knight.’"
"Black Knight? Did the Aurora Order make a move?"
"Why would they do this?"
"Perhaps Bors accidentally offended them?"
"Not necessarily. As far as I know, several families have secretly cultivated ’Shepherds.’"
Just as the room fell into an uproar, John, who had remained calm, finally spoke: "Bors’s body was returned by the Delien family... Their message is clear. They are threatening us!"
With those words, everyone fell silent. After all, the Delien family’s power was immense, faintly surpassing the Soren family, showing signs of becoming Intis’s foremost family. Moreover, the two families were allies, their interests already deeply intertwined. Thus, no one dared rashly slander them.
After a long silence, an elderly gentleman of high seniority tapped his cane and asked, "What about the boy Johnson? How is he?"
As long as Johnson was safe, reconciliation was still possible.
Speaker John shook his head and said gravely: "We don’t know... According to the investigation reported by the Machinery Hivemind, last night Johnson originally went with his friends to teach a lesson to a member of the Delien family who had previously clashed with him.
"He had arranged a ritual in advance to block sound and spirituality... His friends’ testimony confirmed this.
"But the strangest thing is that Johnson completely disappeared afterward! Those few friends said that as soon as they entered the house, they lost consciousness and knew nothing of what happened.
"In the end, the three of them were awakened by the very Delien family member they intended to attack, who then reported the matter to the Machinery Hivemind.
"Later, the Machinery Hivemind confirmed that those people had not lied. However... all of them bore traces of being possessed by a ’Devil.’"
The residence of that Delien family member, a church appointee, was within the jurisdiction of the Church of Steam, which was why the Machinery Hivemind had handled the matter.
As for why a believer of the Eternal Blazing Sun lived among the congregation of the Church of Steam, it was because he had been preaching in the area, attempting to "lure" the followers of the God of Steam and Machinery to the side of the Eternal Blazing Sun.
After the patriarch gave a simple account of the incident, the elderly gentleman frowned and muttered to himself:
"I’ve heard a rumor that the Delien family has a secret connection with the Nos family, one of the three great demon families... I wonder if it’s true."
Speaker John and the elderly gentleman exchanged a subtle glance, then John nodded: "It’s true. I accidentally learned this intelligence from the patriarch of another demon family, Andrelad. Later, after investigation, it was confirmed."
The family members were once again in an uproar, exclaiming in disbelief:
"What exactly does the Delien family want?"
"Did they kidnap Johnson to force us to stand firmly on their side?"
"This is going too far. Wasn’t our previous support enough?"
While everyone was indignant, the elderly gentleman once again tapped his cane on the floor and sternly asked:
"Can it be confirmed that the Delien family did it? And, is Johnson kidnapped or already dead?"
This question struck at the heart of the matter. The others also looked intently at the patriarch, waiting for his answer.
"According to the Machinery Hivemind’s report, there were no traces of battle at the scene, and aside from Johnson’s disappearance, no one was harmed... He is very likely still alive... because I can’t think of any benefit in killing him... But when members of the Machinery Hivemind attempted to use prophecy, divination, and other means to locate Johnson, they failed." Speaker John turned his head to his uncle, the other family demigod of the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun, and requested,
"I recall you sealed some of your power in an amulet... And since that amulet has no unusual appearance, perhaps those who abducted Johnson did not destroy it... Could you use it to determine his location?"
This saint of the Eternal Blazing Sun was named Gis. Hearing the patriarch’s request, he remained silent for a moment, then nodded: "I can try."
He set up a ritual and began his probing.
The others watched without blinking, waiting for the result.
About two minutes later, Saint Gis furrowed his brow and said heavily: "I received no response when seeking Johnson’s life or location... But the amulet imbued with my power is in the Delien family’s ancestral mansion!
"Johnson is likely confined in their treasury, personally guarded by that member of the Delien family... In all of Trier, apart from some places of the churches, only there has ever given me such a feeling."
Hearing this, Speaker John murmured: "That old monster of the Delien family... a Grade 0 Sealed Artifact... No wonder the Machinery Hivemind couldn’t prophesy!"
At this point, the family members also united in indignation, all voicing their desire to pressure the Delien family to return Johnson.
Their unity stemmed from a relatively optimistic view. After all, the Prime Minister’s current situation was difficult, and he could not afford to lose the support of the Flais family. He would surely return Johnson obediently... perhaps they could even extract some benefits in the process.
Speaker John had convened the family meeting precisely for this effect. So he immediately gave the order to suspend all cooperation with the Deliens!
"Until Johnson is returned!"
.....
Meanwhile, inside the Delien family’s castle, the Prime Minister was also caught off guard by this sudden incident. He muttered in puzzlement:
"Who exactly is framing us, sowing discord between us and our allied families?"
He pondered for a moment, then asked the "shadow" in the corner: "Can you confirm that after Sero killed the ’Guardian’ Bors last night, he left immediately without any further action?"
"Confirmed. After killing the half-giant, he dealt with the corpse and never approached Florent Street again," the shadow replied with certainty.
"I see..." The Prime Minister frowned and continued, "And he didn’t notice anything unusual nearby after the killing?"
"The ritual Johnson and his companions set up was extremely intricate. Even I sensed nothing... let alone him!" The shadow was clearly confident in its abilities.
"I wonder where Johnson learned a ritual of that level..." The Prime Minister sighed.
The shadow fell silent for a few seconds, as if "listening" to something, before replying: "According to his three companions, it was a ’Professor’ who taught them the knowledge."
"Professor? Who is that?" The Prime Minister clearly had never heard the name.
—Bayam was far from Intis, and since the Church of the Storms and the Loen military had not publicized the bounty, the deeds of the so-called Professor had not yet spread to Intis.
The shadow fell silent again, seemingly unsure how to answer.
The Prime Minister did not expect an answer. After a while of contemplation, suspicion grew in his heart:
"In Trier, the only ones who could do this, and have reason to frame us, are the churches and the Soren family!
"But the churches are unlikely to use such means...
"So... is it the Saurons?
"Is this the former angel family’s expression of dissatisfaction at our Delien family’s rise to become Intis’s number one family?"
.....
Outside the Soren family manor, Helene carried a film reel of Roselle Gustav as well as a prepared public opinion guidance plan, and requested an audience with the patriarch from the butler.
Due to Ebner and the film company’s growing influence, her request was granted.
An hour later, Helene walked out of the manor’s gates full of excitement, then boarded a carriage toward the Assembly, intending to discuss the next steps of cooperation with Fanny.
But when she arrived, she was informed that Miss Fanny had taken the day off.
.....
At Lant Port, a small naval port in southern Intis.
After avenging Fanny, Ebner had hurried here and boarded a large steam warship under complete control of the Delien family, bound for Isaca Island.
On the ship, Ebner flipped through the sea monster information provided by the Prime Minister while fiddling with a monocular telescope.
This telescope was the mystical item the Prime Minister had mentioned for observing sea monsters.
"So that’s it... This thing was made from the ’Eye of Secret Peeping’ of some unlucky ’Astrologer,’ wasn’t it?
"No wonder it can observe the state of sea monsters..."
After a few words of wonder, Ebner recalled the "feedback" he had just received and thought:
It seems the ’Barrier’ ritual I taught truly played its role of misleading and concealing, perfectly matching Johnson and the others’ original intention in learning it...
Of course, only their original intention.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 883: Lady of Dragon’s Might
chapters.content:
Chapter 883: Lady of Dragon’s Might
The Black Throne was a ghost ship left behind by the Solomon Empire. Its design was ancient and imposing. Except for the fact that the left and right sides of the hull were in completely different styles, making it look awkward to the eye, it was still quite striking.
Originally, this ship had been hidden at the edge of the Sea of Mist, among the Oradek Islands, but more than a hundred years ago it was discovered by Roselle, who used it as his vessel during his explorations.
Unfortunately, because Roselle drove the Black Throne into the Abyss, the ship was polluted. Its "spirit" fell and was eventually erased.
Now, it could no longer be called a ghost ship, but was instead a large mystical item with many extraordinary abilities.
Even so, in the eyes of many pirates, the Black Throne was still an unspeakable treasure. Miss Gwen had been able to keep it only because of a mystical item Roselle had left on board that looked like an ornament.
This item could be mounted on her Golden Serpent Sword, and from there it borrowed the power of the Black Throne, clothing her in a manifested suit of armor that allowed her to display power on the level of a Chaos Mentor.
If she was willing to pay a certain price, she could even unleash a single strike that carried the effect of a demigod-level "chaos."
However, while this item was powerful, it could only transform her into an armored warrior within a nautical mile of the Black Throne, and its side effects were frightening. It could gradually erode the user’s mind, and once the armor was worn for more than thirty seconds, the corruption became irreversible, causing the user to slowly degenerate into a "cold-blooded one" comparable to a demon.
If it were another pathway’s Beyonder, it could only be used to fight desperately in dire straits. But as a Weapon Master, Gwen could effectively reduce the harm from its side effects. For her, the limit could surpass two minutes.
If she prepared in advance with defensive potions or items for the mind, she could even use it for more than three minutes.
It could be said that, aside from the somewhat embarrassing appearance of the armor, Miss Gwen was extremely satisfied with this newly acquired mystical item...
And the prior recognition she had received from the Admiral of the Deep Seas had made her a little arrogant, which was why she made the decision to intercept a slave ship without much planning or investigation.
As was only natural, Miss Gwen and her crew paid the price for this—she fell into an ambush, surrounded by both the Admiral of the Deep Seas’s fleet and warships from the Intis military.
Even though the Black Throne’s abilities were not bad, without its "spirit" it could not display its full power... In a sense, Roselle had created the item that allowed one to "transform" using its power precisely to make up for this flaw.
And the Admiral of the Deep Seas, a pirate admiral famed across the Five Seas, was powerful in his own right. His subordinates were all experts of the middle sequences, and his vessel, the Dominator, was itself a bizarre ghost ship. So the moment the battle began, Miss Gwen’s side fell into disadvantage.
Even when Miss Gwen transformed into the Lady of Dragon’s Might and entered the battle, she only managed to temporarily drive back the encirclement and open some distance, but she still could not break through.
After all, upon "transforming," Gwen radiated the majesty of the Black Emperor pathway, which made the living beings around her unconsciously lower themselves, yearning to submit. Because of her moniker, people called this form of hers the Lady of Dragon’s Might or the Warrior of Dragon’s Might.
When Ebner’s warship reached this sea, what he saw was Gwen, in her desperation, unleashing a demigod-level chaotic power that caused several blocking warships to inexplicably shatter and sink into the sea.
"This strike was indeed powerful. It even frightened Admiral of the Deep Seas Hal Constantine for a while. But from my observation, Gwen’s spirituality has probably been drained dry, and the mental corruption is severe. The fact she hasn’t immediately lost control is already sheer luck...
"Tran and Lydia’s states don’t look very good either. The former may have advanced to a Wizard, but in naval combat his usefulness isn’t much—Lydia’s dark spells are more practical.
"As for the rest of the low-sequence crew, the fact they haven’t betrayed her on the spot shows that Gwen’s prestige has usually been solid..."
"They’re barely holding out, but they won’t last much longer... The next attack may be the end for them!
"Rather than let the pirates make a move and cause needless slaughter, I should take this chance, while they’re cowed by Gwen’s strike, to act myself. If I capture Gwen now, it’ll also count as protecting her and her crew.
"At the same time, I can build prestige among the pirates and the Delien family’s private forces, seizing the initiative for what follows."
In the span of a thought, Ebner made his decision. Relying on the "Wind-blessed" he had shepherded through the Magic Mirror, he stirred up a gale, lifting himself into the sky and swiftly closing in on the Black Throne.
After dodging several magical and sorcerous attacks, he directly unleashed his demigod-level Dragon’s Might.
In an instant, the crew and officers aboard the Black Throne found their bodies, minds, and spirits all out of their control. Some stood frozen, trembling in place. Some fled blindly and irrationally. Some soiled themselves and collapsed weakly to the ground. Some fainted outright into unconsciousness. Others wore feverish expressions, becoming Ebner’s fanatical followers.
Only Miss Gwen, Lydia, and Tran resisted the effect.
But one by one, virtual personalities had already slipped silently into their mental islands, beginning to "manipulate" their actions.
Of course, this incursion from Ebner was genuine only for Gwen. For the other two, it was a mere touch and nothing more.
He did this because he discovered that the price Gwen had paid for that last strike was even greater than he had imagined. Without immediate "psychological treatment," she might be in real danger.
Even so, Tran completely lost the ability to act, seized by crew members who had been subdued by the qualitative Dragon’s Might and turned into Ebner’s zealots.
As for Miss Gwen, her mental state was in such bad shape that Ebner had no choice but to support her personally, treating her closely.
Fortunately, this matched the persona of "Owen," so it aroused no suspicion.
Of the three, only Lydia, aided by Ebner’s deliberate leniency, managed to activate a mystical item and then leapt into the sea.
As expected of Lady Helene’s daughter—though this level of "psychological stealth" couldn’t fool me, in the boundless ocean she’d have little problem slipping past the encirclement.
Ebner gave a quiet note of admiration in his heart. Looking around, he saw that several of "his side’s" ships were already drawing near. Leading them was a large warship whose deck sprouted strange wooden tentacles—the flagship of the Admiral of the Deep Seas, the Dominator.
Ebner glanced at the man standing at the bow of the Dominator—a blond-haired, blue-eyed man in his early thirties, wearing a long coat, a cigarette dangling from his lips.
Without any intent to meet him, Ebner simply scooped Gwen up in his arms and flew back to his own warship.
Before bringing Gwen into his cabin, he instructed his own captain, Intis Navy Lieutenant Colonel Darren Delien:
"Don’t kill the crew of the Black Throne. Just confine them on board and put people to watch them... So many ready-made sacrifices are perfect to take along for the Deep Sea Sacrament.
"Also, the Black Throne is our spoil of war. I won’t allow those pirates to board and plunder my property.
"Finally, speed up. We dock at Isaca tonight."
As a formal officer, a member of the Delien family’s military faction, the captain naturally looked down on the pirates brought by the Admiral of the Deep Seas, even though they were temporarily cooperating.
So, after receiving the Saint’s orders, he immediately stood at attention and replied solemnly: "Yes, Lord Owen! Your orders will be carried out to the letter!"
Ebner nodded in apparent satisfaction, then carried Gwen into his cabin.
Afterward, he sealed the room with spirituality, treating Gwen’s mental injuries even as he released his true body, which slipped through the cabin walls and into the sea.
On the other side, the pirates were extremely displeased with Owen’s commands. After all, they had suffered heavy losses before and had been waiting to vent their anger on the crew of the Black Throne...
But dissatisfaction was one thing; they had no choice. This was a demigod’s command, and no one dared defy it.
.....
Out at sea, Lydia looked around at the endless horizon, and her heart sank into despair.
She had lost her sense of direction!
Back on the ship, navigation had always been Tran’s job. She had never worried about it. Now, with only herself left, it was fatal.
Lydia could swim, and even briefly transform into a bat to fly, but neither could last long. If she couldn’t find land, once her strength and spirituality ran dry, she’d drown!
And drowning was hardly fitting for the elegance of a vampire...
"Papa, Mama, Brother... someone come save me!"
With three demigods as close kin, Lydia had already, right after falling into the ambush, written a letter via messenger to summon "reinforcements."
Perhaps her prayers had worked... The next moment, Lydia felt herself pulled out of the sea. Countless shifting color blocks slid past her eyes, and when she came back to herself, she was already on a small island.
Lydia finally let out a sigh of relief, then turned to look at the figure who had saved her.
"Detective Bryan, what are you doing here?" When she saw who it was, Lydia asked in both delight and surprise.
"Lady Helene asked me to come help you," Ebner answered with a smile. "And I just happened to be nearby."
This wasn’t a lie. Ebner had known back in Trier that the Delien family intended to capture Gwen. Of course he had told Lady Helene.
The latter clearly trusted him greatly, and so entrusted the matter fully to him.
So it was Mother who contacted Detective Bryan... Lydia nodded thoughtfully, recalling her brother and mother’s usual praise of the detective’s abilities. She quickly grabbed his hand and pleaded:
"Detective Bryan, the captain and Tran have been captured by the pirates... Please, you must find a way to rescue them!"
She then explained the enemy’s situation in detail—including the demigod who had appeared at the end!
"Don’t worry. They’ll be fine. I’ll have them out tonight."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 884: Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea
chapters.content:
Chapter 884: Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea
In the evening, at the dock of Isaca Port, the "Dominion," Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal Constantine stood on the bow deck with a cigarette in his mouth, taking a deep drag before exhaling a smoke ring. He watched as the officers of another navy warship, surrounded by the administrators of the port town, headed straight toward a luxurious manor in town.
Among them was His Excellency Owen Delien, the demigod, who also disembarked with the group.
At that moment, one of Hal’s subordinates ran over and said angrily, "Captain, those navy bastards have gone too far! They’re off to the town for fun, but ordered us to guard the ’Black Throne’ and those prisoners..."
"Was it His Excellency Owen who gave the order?" Hal flicked the cigarette in his hand, watching it fall into the sea, before asking calmly.
"Yes..." the subordinate answered reluctantly.
"Since it is a Saint’s order, we have no room for objection," Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea said indifferently. "Just do your part. When this mission is over and we are away from those navy men, we won’t have to look at their faces anymore."
"That’s all we can do. I’ll arrange for men to patrol the ’Black Throne’ so those bastards won’t find another excuse to trouble us!" The subordinate sighed as he spoke, then said regretfully, "It’s a pity that beauty called Lydia ran away. Otherwise, we could have had some fun with her."
As for Lady Dragon Might Gwen, since she had already entered the Saint’s bedroom, he dared not harbor any thoughts.
Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal glanced at his first mate without showing anything on the surface, but he sneered inwardly. From his investigation, Lydia’s background was likely the most dangerous among the three captured on the Black Throne!
