To touch her would be far more disastrous than daring to covet Lady Dragon Might.
Even His Excellency Owen Delien deliberately let Lydia go while keeping Lady Dragon Might...
Hal did not believe that a mere Sequence 7 vampire could escape from the hands of a demigod!
Of course, there was no need to explain these things to his men. After sending them away, Hal returned to the captain’s cabin, smoking one cigarette after another, lost in thought.
No one knew how much time passed before Hal suddenly stood up and looked through the cabin’s glass window at the sky. The red moon had risen from behind the clouds, bright and flawless.
March 17th, it was the night of the full moon!
Seeing the red moon, Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal’s lips curved slightly. He quickly put on a hooded robe, hiding his face in the shadows of the hood.
He then left the cabin at great speed, using his familiarity with the crew to evade all patrols silently, until he reached the Black Throne.
In the days leading up to every "Deep Sea Festival," the sea monster Segust’s condition would worsen, often falling into madness. That made its domination over Hal Constantine show cracks.
This was especially pronounced on the night of the full moon!
When the full moon rose, spirituality surged, and the sea monster’s madness reached its peak, leaving no attention to its dominated followers.
As long as he did not directly do anything harmful to it, he would be ignored.
This was the experience Hal Constantine had discovered and summarized over the years of attending the Deep Sea Festival.
However, in past festivals, he had never used this to betray the sea monster, not even to test its limits, always waiting cautiously.
He was waiting for the perfect moment to completely break free from the monster’s control!
As the illegitimate son of the Delien family, he had signed a contract with the sea monster in the past to gain power for his revenge against the family.
But who could have known that his so-called chance, his so-called choice, had all been arranged by the Delien family? Their true purpose was to make him willingly become a follower of the sea monster, obtain its bloodline, and merge the blood of Delien with the monster, completing some kind of covenant.
He was a sacrificial offering created by the Delien family to present to the sea monster!
He was also the "bridge" of their cooperation, the foundation of trust...
How ironic it was! All his youthful efforts were nothing but a joke in the eyes of the Delien family’s rulers!
How could Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea ever accept that?
Even though he was dominated by the monster, the creature could only imprison his heart and control his body, but it could not change his will and faith!
Though Hal Constantine had rebellious intentions, he was extremely patient, waiting silently for the right chance. He knew there would only be one!
And as the Deep Sea Festival grew more frequent in recent years, Hal knew his time was running short.
The covenant between the sea monster and the Delien family clearly had problems... no, it was likely the ritual of the Deep Sea Festival itself that was deeply flawed!
So whether the monster struck back in desperation and ruined the Delien family’s schemes, or the Delien family succeeded and gained something from the monster, he, the "bridge," would lose his value...
Therefore, when Hal accidentally learned of Gwen, Lydia, and Tran’s backgrounds, he made his decision. On the previous full moon night, he orchestrated the pirate attack on Gwen’s uncle’s merchant ship, ensuring she would end up enslaved and transported to Isaca Port.
As for afterward, his so-called "recognition" of Gwen’s words that made her feel proud, followed by the ambush on the Black Throne to capture two and release one...
These were all preplanned rehearsals!
Because these schemes targeted insignificant people, they posed no threat to the sea monster and even provided more sacrifices, Hal did not have to hide them.
Owen’s unexpected involvement did not obstruct his plan but instead made it even more perfect!
At least I no longer need to find an excuse to let Lydia go...
Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea muttered in his heart as his body moved like a ghost, avoiding every guard until he reached the room where Tran was imprisoned aboard the Black Throne.Since Tran and the other officers were Beyonders, they were confined separately. Their rooms had ritual setups to suppress their powers.
Hal, his face hidden in shadows, easily broke the ritual and stood before Tran.
Tran sensed the seal on his abilities vanish. After thanking the stranger before him, he still asked cautiously, "Who are you?"
"Just a kind man... Don’t ask too much, leave quickly. Now is the time when the defenses are weakest..." Hal deliberately used an urgent tone.
"What about my companions? And where is the captain?" Tran asked instinctively.
"Your companions were suppressed by the demigod’s Dragon Might, they won’t recover soon...
"As for Lady Dragon Might... she has already been taken by Owen Delien. She is now kept on the navy flagship.
"Even if His Excellency Owen is not there, the defenses of the flagship are tight. Besides, it is very likely that he has set things upon Lady Dragon Might. If triggered, we will be facing a demigod!" Hal answered in a low voice.
"The captain... she was actually... damn it!" Tran bit his lip, his eyes full of fury. He knew well that the captain was a conservative person. Such an ordeal would leave her with wounds beyond imagination.
"So your top priority is to escape!
"Only if you escape will there be a chance to rescue your companions and captain!
"Whether you call upon the strong ones of your family,
"Or find Lydia and ask her elders for help,
"Or tell Ebner Bryan, that well-connected detective, to save his woman...
"In short, before they become sacrifices, you must find someone to stop all this!"
After Hal incited him with the aid of a mystical item, he quickly left the room without giving Tran another chance to ask.
Find my ancestors... find Lydia... find Ebner... Tran repeated in confusion, but his gaze soon grew firm. He felt the mysterious man was right. Only by escaping quickly could he find help to save the captain!
Yet just as he resolved himself and turned, he froze in shock!
Because Lydia and Ebner were standing on the other side of the room, quietly watching him.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 885: Ebner Who Actively Played His Role
chapters.content:
Chapter 885: Ebner Who Actively Played His Role
Ebner and Lydia had already slipped inside when the hooded man unraveled the ritual binding Tran, but they both tacitly kept silent, wanting to see what exactly the man intended to do.
Moreover, since the "Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea" had only made a rather crude disguise, Ebner could recognize him easily even without drawing on his aura.
Maybe he did this on purpose... wants Tran’s elders or Lydia’s family to more easily trace the one who helped him? This Vice Admiral seems to have some hidden plans of his own...
While pondering, Ebner suddenly heard Tran’s delighted and emotional voice: "Lydia, it’s so good you’re safe!"
After that, he threw himself into Lydia’s arms and said, a little choked, "I thought I would never see you again..."
Lydia stroked his head gently and said warmly, "Don’t be afraid, now that I’m here, everything will be fine."
Listening to their exchange, Ebner glanced back and forth between the two with confusion, feeling that the roles they were "playing" didn’t seem quite right... Wasn’t this reversed?
Sensing Ebner’s gaze, Tran finally realized someone else was present. Embarrassed, he scratched his head, and after Lydia quickly whispered her experiences to him, he said sincerely, "Mr. Bryan, thank you so much for saving Lydia and also for coming to save me..."
If you really want to thank me, first get your face out of Lydia’s chest. Shoving dog food like that is not the right attitude for gratitude.
Ebner muttered in his heart, then waved his hand and changed the subject:
"Now isn’t the time to talk. First, you two rescue the rest of the crew from the Black Throne. Once I bring back Gwen from the navy flagship, we’ll seize the chance when the pirates are distracted and set sail immediately.
"Ah, before we came here, Lydia and I already dealt with the guards on the Black Throne, but you still need to be cautious while rescuing the others—avoid making too much noise."
If there was too much commotion, then even with the Vice Admiral as an insider, it would be hard for him to turn a blind eye.
"But... but that mysterious man just said the crew are all suppressed by the Demigod’s ’Dragon’s Might’ and can’t recover for the time being..." Tran said anxiously.
"He can’t, but that doesn’t mean I can’t! Don’t worry, before coming here I already performed spiritual therapy on the people aboard this ship. They’re fine now," Ebner answered with confidence.
He certainly had confidence—after all, he was the one who had "suppressed" them earlier, and he had held back just the right amount. By now, the "influence" had faded away almost completely.
Hearing this, and recalling Mr. Bryan’s past miracles, Tran finally relaxed and said gratefully, "That’s a huge help, thank you..."
Then he remembered what the mysterious man had said about their captain being seized by the Demigod and having something placed upon her. Biting his lip nervously, he asked, "And the captain..."
Ebner knew what he wanted to say, so he waved his hand and smiled. "Don’t worry, I’ll make sure not to trigger any methods that Demigod may have left on Gwen... Also, rest assured, I’ll ’suggest’ to her to forget some unpleasant things. You must be careful not to bring them up in front of her in the future."
When he had treated Gwen’s mental state before, she had been unconscious the entire time, so naturally there was nothing unpleasant in her memory.
"Mr. Bryan, you’re truly a gentle man." Lydia and Tran both sighed with emotion at the same time.
Once the three had agreed on their plans, they split up. Leaving Tran and Lydia aside, Ebner used "Evans’ Hidden Barrier" to pass unimpeded aboard the navy flagship and located Owen’s cabin.
Though the cabin was guarded by a ritual, what sort of ward could stop its own creator? Silently entering, Ebner found Gwen lying on the bed where he had placed her earlier, and immediately lifted the "Virtual Persona’s" control over her.
Gwen quickly regained consciousness. At first dazed, she blinked and, recognizing who was before her, asked instinctively, "Ebner, why are you here?"
Smiling, Ebner replied, "Lydia asked me to come save you."
"Save me..." Gwen then recalled what had happened earlier, her face instantly turning pale. She quickly examined herself and found no abnormalities, finally letting out a small sigh of relief.
"That Demigod could return at any time. Let’s get out of here first." Ebner spoke as he picked up from a table a belt inlaid with ornaments and handed it to Gwen.
"Good!" Gwen was always decisive and quick to act. Seeing the "belt," she exclaimed with joy, "The Golden Serpent Sword! Excellent, it wasn’t taken away!"
With the Golden Serpent Sword in hand, she could "transform" into her armored warrior state, gaining battle strength nearly equivalent to a Pirate Admiral.
In fact, Ebner had already studied the sword’s ability during Gwen’s earlier treatment. Overall, it had inspired him quite a bit.
After all, if a ship of Sequence 3 strength could lend its power in this way, why couldn’t the Pure White Eye? True, repeated transformations could cause pollution and risk of domination—just like Gwen’s side effects—but as long as he controlled the time each use, the problem wouldn’t be too severe...
And the principle feels familiar... hmm, the body Duke Rhine left Lilith works in a similar fashion... Did Roselle get the inspiration from here? Or maybe from a certain tokusatsu show.
While letting his thoughts wander, Ebner led Miss Gwen by the hand, carefully avoiding patrol soldiers until they returned to the Black Throne.
By this time, Gwen’s crew had been rescued by Lydia and Tran. Seeing their captain return, they were overjoyed, nearly cheering out loud.
Lydia rushed forward and hugged Gwen tightly, seemingly to comfort her. But she then sniffed lightly, eyes flashing with surprise and doubt. When she noticed Ebner smiling calmly at Gwen’s side, her expression turned to realization, and she couldn’t help but admire his thoughtfulness.
Being stared at like that, Ebner felt baffled. Only after simulating a "mind-reading" ability for a while did he shake his head helplessly.
Turns out the girl thought he had erased certain traces from Gwen to cover up her being "violated"...
Ignoring their little misunderstandings, Ebner reminded everyone they weren’t safe yet and told them to set sail at once.
...
Back in the captain’s cabin of the Dominator, Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal Constantine waited for his men to report Tran’s escape.
But after quite some time with no word, just as he was about to investigate again, piercing whistles suddenly rang out, followed by shouts from all directions: "The Black Throne has weighed anchor and escaped!"
"The Black Throne ran? Looks like I underestimated the descendant of the Angel of the Morse Ascetics!" the Vice Admiral muttered to himself. Still, he thought this outcome acceptable. Though inwardly pleased, he kept his face stern and ordered his men to give chase.
But since they raised anchor late and their speed was no match for the Black Throne, his fleet lost sight of the enemy after barely a dozen nautical miles and had to turn back.
On returning to port, since his men had been responsible for guarding the prisoners last night, the Vice Admiral naturally bore the brunt of Lord Owen’s harsh reprimand.
Only then did he learn that even "Lady Dragon Might" had been rescued.
"The only ones who can undo a Demigod’s arrangement are Demigods themselves... meaning last night, those three’s elders or friends must have come.
"From the timing, they likely heard my conversation with Tran as well...
"And since I made no effort to disguise myself, that Demigod surely knows who I am. Now it depends on whether they want revenge...
"If they do, they’ll probably shadow our fleet—and then discover the Deep Sea Sacrificial Rite!
"Looks like I’ll have to gamble...
"Sigh, if things had gone according to my plan and Gwen or the others were still captives, then they’d definitely follow...
"Unfortunately, Owen Delien is useless trash!"
As he endured Owen’s rebuke, the Vice Admiral weighed his future moves. He wasn’t afraid of the man probing his thoughts, for as a scion of the sea monster, anyone wishing to invade his mind first had to overcome the monster’s will.
Only after Owen waved him off in disgust did he salute expressionlessly and return to his ship.
The Vice Admiral’s sailors, seeing their captain pale-faced, angrily protested, "It was those damned navy men who went to the town for fun, leaving the defenses thin and letting the enemy escape... yet they pushed all the blame onto us! A bunch of dogshit!"
Hal smirked faintly, then returned to his cold demeanor. "They have a Demigod," he said lightly before entering his cabin.
At that, the pirates fell silent, swallowing their anger before dispersing.
Inside the cabin, the Vice Admiral gazed through the window at his men and murmured, "The deeper their resentment festers, the easier it will be to use...
"Because there is a Demigod, they endure.
"But what if there isn’t?"
Suddenly, he froze. Something felt wrong. Aside from the full moon nights before the Deep Sea Rite, he should never have such thoughts.
Even when scheming, his ideas only ever came in fragments. Under the monster’s domination, he could never piece them together like this!
What was happening?
Just as he thought that, he was startled to find a stranger had appeared before him.
It was this man’s aura that had blocked the sea monster’s control.
"If you wish to escape your bonds, then learn the secret art on this," the man said, adjusting his glasses as he placed a slip of paper and a rune-covered charm on the desk.
Then he vanished.
The Vice Admiral warily waited for a long time before slowly picking up the slip. After a moment, he put it down again, murmuring,
"Land of the Unknown? What is that?"
...
Meanwhile, back in his own cabin, Ebner shifted back into Owen’s appearance, rubbed his chin, and mused:
"Once Hal uses that secret art to free himself, my Mysticism Magister potion should be fully digested, right?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 886: Tran Turns the Tables
chapters.content:
Chapter 886: Tran Turns the Tables
On the "Black Throne," after Miss Gwen had comforted her crew who had just survived a great ordeal, she returned to the captain’s cabin and expressed her gratitude to Ebner, who was waiting there reading.
Perhaps feeling that words alone lacked sincerity, Miss Gwen walked to the bed, pulled out a folded piece of parchment from a hidden compartment under the mattress, and handed it to Ebner. She said solemnly, "This is the only thing I can offer right now. Please don’t despise it."
Ebner accepted the parchment with some surprise. When he unfolded it, he found it was actually a map. He couldn’t help but ask, "What is this?"
"This might be the most valuable thing left here by Emperor Roselle, besides the ’Black Throne’ itself!" Miss Gwen first teased a little, then asked, "Do you know of the ’Sunken Laurel’?"
"I do. Among the many rumored treasures at sea, that’s the one most likely to be real.
"They say that over a hundred years ago, the ’Sunken Laurel’ was carrying gold, jewels, and other precious items that the Loen Kingdom had acquired from East Balam. It deviated from its course and sank somewhere between the Furious Sea and the Sonia Sea. To this day, it hasn’t been found.
"And the total value of the items on board was said to be several million pounds!" Ebner nodded. Whether in his previous life or this one, he had heard of this treasure. He paused, then asked naturally, "So, this map points to the ’Sunken Laurel’?"
Miss Gwen gave a slight nod and said, "Together with this map was a stone sealed with a message from Emperor Roselle, giving a brief explanation of what it pointed to... Unfortunately, that stone turned to powder and vanished after the message was released."
I recall that the Laurel sank around the same time Roselle was assassinated... So in his last few years, while scouring the world for traces of other ’Travelers,’ he happened to find it, then deliberately drew a map, turning it into the ’Golden Serpent Treasure’ as a joke? That would make sense. At that time, Roselle probably no longer cared about wealth at all. Several million pounds would have been no different from wastepaper to him... After all, he owned an industrialized nation. Money? Just have the banks print more. As for the resulting inflation, he could always force other countries to ’foot the bill’...
But Lilith once said that before Miss Gwen and her people found this ship, Lady Helen had already ’cleaned it out’ once—even taking away the second half of Roselle’s translation of Feast of Blood that was kept here...
With Lady Helen’s greedy nature, how could she not have taken this map? Something feels wrong...
Did she not notice it at the time? Or was Roselle’s arrangement conditional?
Thinking of this, Ebner asked, "Where exactly on the ’Black Throne’ did you find this parchment?""You might not believe this..." Miss Gwen hesitated, then answered somewhat embarrassed, "It was when I combined the ship’s accessory with my ’Golden Serpent Sword’ for the first time, and borrowed the power of the ’Black Throne’ to ’transform’ into the ’ship-girl’ described by Emperor Roselle, that this parchment and stone suddenly appeared out of nowhere..."
After all, the armor Roselle designed for those transformations, while powerful, was rather... embarrassing.
So ’ship-girl’ was the real name of that armored warrior... Roselle, you really knew how to have fun!
Ebner mocked inwardly while also resolving his earlier doubts.
Lady Helen’s advance sweep of the "Black Throne" had only been to prevent the spread of its "pollution." She had no intention of taking it away. So she didn’t care about things that combined with the Golden Serpent Sword to enable transformation, and naturally never tried. That was why the "Laurel" information was left behind.
Having thought it through, Ebner shook his head and told Miss Gwen, "Something worth several million pounds is far too valuable. I can’t accept it."
"Ebner, I don’t mean to be arrogant... but in my eyes, my crew’s lives and mine are worth no less than several million pounds. So please, take it!" Miss Gwen looked at Ebner stubbornly, her expression solemn.
Seeing her so determined, Ebner thought for a moment before nodding. "Alright, I’ll accept it."
Hearing this, Miss Gwen seemed to let out a breath of relief. Her tone grew lighter, and she smiled. "Actually, you might still be at a loss. The map is real, but after more than a hundred years, the treasure could already have been found and secretly taken away."
"Something hidden by Roselle isn’t so easily found!" Ebner chuckled, shaking his head. Though he had only glanced briefly, he had already noticed that the place marked on the map was connected to a treacherous area of the Furious Sea. Without guidance, it would be nearly impossible to find.
At this point, Ebner took out a card and drew from it a sealed Beyonder characteristic.
Gwen gazed at the characteristic and felt a strange attraction toward it. Coupled with what she had read in the mysticism texts left on the "Black Throne," she blurted out, "Aggregation of characteristics... This is the ’Dawn Paladin’s’ Beyonder characteristic!"
This characteristic had come from the fleet commander, the "Gray Giant" Gravina, whom Ebner had killed when intercepting the "Undying King’s" squadron.
At the time, he had thought of selling it to Gwen...
But first, Gwen had just advanced to "Weapons Master" back then, with neither the funds nor the need.
Second, if Ebner had immediately brought out a "Dawn Paladin" characteristic right after the Gray Giant’s death, it would have seemed far too suspicious.
So only now did Ebner take it out. Smiling after hearing Gwen’s words, he asked, "You should have fully digested your ’Weapons Master’ potion by now, right?"
Even if her progress had been slow before, after using the "ship-girl" armor to fight across sequences so many times, her advancement must have been astonishing.
"I’ve digested it..." Gwen nodded, then said helplessly, "But I can’t afford it now..."
"That’s fine. Consider it a loan from me. Pay me back when you can. Of course, I can also accept you completing a task for me in exchange... Don’t refuse. In my eyes, our friendship is worth far more than a single characteristic." Ebner used wording almost identical to Gwen’s earlier words, blocking her refusal in advance.
The reason he so generously gave the characteristic in advance was because the "Laurel’s" value was indeed immense. Without giving Gwen something in return, he would feel uneasy.
After all, if no one else knew, he at least knew just how much of that "rescue" earlier had been his own arrangement...
Miss Gwen was silent for a long while after hearing this. In the end, she accepted the characteristic, sealed it with spirituality inside a container, and stored it.
Her gaze toward Ebner now carried a subtle change—gratitude mixed with something indescribable. She then asked, "What’s the task?"
"Help me keep watch on Lady D in Corsica... Don’t approach her, and don’t try to investigate her. Just attend her gatherings regularly and confirm that she’s still on Corsica Island." Ebner explained.
For Gwen, this task wasn’t very difficult, but it wasn’t entirely without danger either... Compared to a Sequence 6 characteristic, however, the danger was trivial.
"No problem." Gwen agreed readily, and inwardly resolved to complete the task for Ebner—and also to repay the money later.
After that, the two of them chatted idly until Ebner sensed an inexplicable fluctuation of spirituality coming from the deck. Only then did he stop and leave the captain’s cabin.
As soon as Ebner stepped onto the deck, he saw a handsome young man emerge from the void, led by a powerful spirit.
That man was none other than Viscount Cullen, long unseen... and the spirit was Tajik, the "bodyguard" Mr. Azik had given him, one who took lifespan as payment.
No, now he should be called Count Cullen! Nearly two months earlier, the demigod vampire hunted by Ebner, Helen, and Closfia in Groselle’s Travels had clearly served as Cullen’s advancement material.
"Ebner, thank you for saving my sister." Cullen first gave Ebner a solemn bow. Then he pulled Lydia and Tran over and said sternly, "We need to talk."
At that moment, he glanced at Tran again and added, "Your strength is still too weak... No wonder Lydia was worried about you..."
Hearing this, Ebner almost burst out laughing.
Because whether in tone or in choice of words, this was exactly the same as when Mr. Azik had spoken to Cullen in front of Silica!
He wondered if Cullen would also take something out to give Tran for protection.
...
(End of this Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 887: The Decision of Vice Admiral Deep Sea
chapters.content:
Chapter 887: The Decision of Vice Admiral Deep Sea
March 28th, Monday.
After many days of sailing, Ebner’s fleet finally arrived at a small island in a hidden sea region west of the Southern Continent, guided by Vice Admiral Deep Sea.
Normally, if they had taken the proper route, it wouldn’t have taken over ten days. But since what they were doing couldn’t be seen in the open, they had long since deviated from the Roselle Waterway, braving the raging seas and harsh environment to take a route several times longer before finally reaching this secret island.
Seems like the ships that transported slaves before also came this way... Sigh, who knows how many people died along the journey? No wonder the Delien family still hasn’t gathered enough people for the festival in a whole year. The losses must far exceed the safe arrivals...
Damn it!
And who knows how Miss Gwen’s uncle is doing now... It’s a pity that his group had already been secretly shipped away before I arrived at Isaca Island. Miss Gwen only ever received false information, all to lure her into that ambush...
Otherwise, I definitely would’ve helped her rescue them first.
Standing at the bow of the ship, having just finished attending the Tarot Club, Ebner sighed a few times as he gazed at the island now appearing in sight.
Speaking of which, the recent Tarot Gatherings hadn’t brought up anything particularly noteworthy. Miss Justice was still carrying out the tasks of the Psychological Alchemists while secretly probing for the whereabouts of the Queen of Calamity.
Miss Magician was still traveling with the circus, and had just entered the territory of Loen.
Miss Judgment had completely digested her Judge potion and, through Ebner, bought the Disciplinary Paladin characteristic from Jane. She only needed the military to approve her ritual application before she could complete her advancement.
Miss Temperance still hadn’t completed her demigod ritual and remained absent.
Lady Hermit, as always, drifted apart from the other members—observing more than speaking.
The Sun was accompanying his chief, exploring the path to the royal court, but so far hadn’t discovered much.
Mr. Moon, meanwhile, was once again showing off at the gathering. He claimed that without much effort, he had already digested part of his Potion Professor potion. But according to The World, this was probably because he frequently lectured the common believers in the Harvest Church on herbalism, and even some special combinations of potions.
Besides collecting marionettes, researching history, and volunteering at the Church, he also loved studying different potion formulas for use in combat situations. That was why his digestion progress was so impressive.
The World—Klein—had nothing unusual either. Other than occasionally hearing that he had taken down another pirate to claim a bounty, only Ebner knew that most of his time was still spent sweeping floors and scrubbing toilets...
Mr. Hanged Man had, by providing intelligence, support, and fencing services to The World, finally accumulated enough funds from his share of the bounties. He bought from Miss Magician the eyeball of a Three-eyed Thunderbird, thus obtaining both main ingredients needed for the Ocean Songster potion... Unfortunately, the Obnins sea monster required for the ritual was still missing.
Although Ebner roughly knew its location from the original timeline, that would only be months later. And a sea monster didn’t just stay in one place, so it was completely unreliable.
As Ebner recalled the Tarot meeting, the naval fleet had already docked at the pier, mooring by a simple wooden jetty.
Snapping back to reality, Ebner entered a seemingly plain yet lavishly decorated manor under the welcome of the staff stationed there.
No sooner had he settled in than his Owen avatar requested to first inspect the slaves that had been brought here.
The request wasn’t unusual—after all, Owen was sent to oversee the ritual, and ensuring the "sacrifices" were intact was only natural.
Very soon, under the lead of the managers stationed there, he entered a secluded area deep inside the island.
Ebner originally thought the slaves brought here would be penned up like livestock, surviving only on the bare minimum, surrounded by scenes of misery...
But reality was the complete opposite!
The moment he entered, he saw a town with a polished, glamorous facade.
The streets bustled with people, shops lined the roads with plentiful goods, and restaurants sent out streams of smoke carrying mouthwatering scents...
At first glance, aside from its smaller size, the town was no different from the bustling commercial districts of cities like Backlund.
But soon, Ebner realized something was wrong. Some people weren’t paying when they shopped; they simply took things. They beat and cursed the shopkeepers, even ripping off women’s clothes in the streets to satisfy primal urges...
Those being robbed and violated clearly seethed with hatred and rage, yet endured in silence, as if resigned to fate.
Frowning, Ebner turned to the manager beside him.
He hadn’t known anything about this place beforehand, and couldn’t understand why the "sacrifices" lived like this.
The manager quickly explained, aware of his guest’s confusion—it was the same with everyone seeing it for the first time:
"This is the rule of the town—’Joyous Town’... We provide every slave who arrives here with everything: fine clothes, comfortable housing, exquisite food... With only one exception—they may not kill. Otherwise, they can do whatever they wish!
"But there is one condition: before they can enjoy, they must first serve others for a week. Only then can they earn a week of ’joy’!
"During the service, they must accept anything and everything demanded of them. No resistance allowed—otherwise they lose their chance at ’enjoyment.’
"This place is both paradise and hell."
So that’s it... But this isn’t ’Joyous Town’ at all—it’s a City of Desire, a City of Demons!
The "servers" endure suffering, harbor hatred, and curse the "enjoyers." Then, once they become "enjoyers," they vent everything they endured upon the next "servers"...
Indulging in desire, unleashing malice, enduring pain, and cursing others, over and over again...
As I guessed, this is about cultivating suitable sacrifices for the Shadow World. The so-called ’Deep Sea Festival’ is really a means to use sea monsters that once bore the imprint of an Origin characteristic to communicate with the Shadow World...
And these managers aren’t just supervisors—they, too, are part of the sacrifices. Manipulating hearts and desires is also a trait of the Shadow World. Without them, the ritual couldn’t be complete.
Glancing at the manager, who was still speaking with enthusiasm, Ebner shook his head inwardly.
This fool probably doesn’t even know the fate awaiting him.
But why forbid killing here...? Hmm, if killing were allowed, the number of sacrifices would quickly drop—that does make sense. Still, "killing" is also a form of desire. Forbidding it seems detrimental to the ritual...
Wait... The pirates under Vice Admiral Deep Sea, and the navy soldiers I brought... I see now—they too are part of the sacrifices!
Of course. With so many witnesses to this ritual, keeping the secret would be impossible. Yet over the years, so little information has leaked... Heh, that must be because, apart from Vice Admiral Deep Sea and a few supervisors like me, everyone else became part of the ceremony.
In fact, if this really is the final Deep Sea Festival... then Vice Admiral Deep Sea and I might also be sacrifices...
No wonder Harl dared defy the sea monster, trying to draw in the powers behind Gwen, Lydia, and Trun. He must have sensed danger.
And while the Prime Minister being too busy to preside over the ritual seems normal... think carefully: when has a Prime Minister ever not been busy? Why could he always make time before, but not this time?
Did he sell out Owen?
Does he think the ritual lacks Lust, and so placed Owen on the altar? Or perhaps Owen’s dealings with George III crossed his bottom line?
If I really were Owen, I might only realize at the very last moment...
As these thoughts raced, Ebner felt that his previous preparations weren’t secure. If this truly was the final Festival, then the hidden big shots—such as the Grand Duke of Blood or the Mother Tree of Desire—might have other means!
And his own preparations had only been arranging meetings with Cressfia, Helene, and even Karen aboard the Black Throne...
But now it seems that’s far from enough. At the very least, I need an angel to hold the line!
Yet I don’t know many angels... Who should I turn to, and how would I persuade them?
Should I directly ask the Mother Goddess or the Goddess?
Not impossible... True, once I entered this island, I sensed it was covered by some force cutting off prayer to true gods...
But that’s nothing—I can always "wall-hop" through Mr. Fool to connect!
As he calculated inwardly, Ebner continued strolling through the town with the manager.
He found the facilities here far more complete than expected. There were teachers instructing etiquette, cosmetics, and deportment, able to turn a shabby female slave into a passable "noble lady" in just days.
There were also mentors in literature, painting, and music, generously teaching those eager to learn.
In short, the range of instructors was so extensive it rivaled a comprehensive university—if not even more complete!
"Human desires are diverse. Some don’t like women, some don’t like pleasure, some don’t like venting... So we also fulfill their spiritual desires," the manager added with a smile.
This is... absurd.
Ebner suddenly felt the situation surreal.
These demons and cultists are actually doing better in education than the great cities of the Northern Continent. They invest freely, and completely cater to the desires of those being taught...
Yes, he could see the teachers’ true nature. They were all sea monster dependents, long since turned into aberrations wearing human skin. Yet in life, each must have been an expert in their own field.
So they aren’t teachers—they’re the sea monster’s "priests." While teaching knowledge, they guide those not ruled by bodily lust into giving their faith to the sea monster. Truly insidious!
Suppressing a shudder, Ebner played along with the manager’s chatter. Soon, they encountered the latest batch of slaves to arrive.
With the ritual imminent, these hadn’t had the chance to "serve" or "enjoy." They were isolated, left to stew in fear of the "servers" and envy of the "enjoyers."
This state too, naturally, fit the ritual’s requirements.
Ebner scanned the group and quickly spotted Miss Gwen’s uncle. Having been educated, he wasn’t as numb as the others, but he was still shocked by what he saw, his emotions deeply conflicted...
Remembering his agreement with Gwen aboard the Black Throne, Ebner quietly inserted a virtual persona into the man’s mind to monitor him and prevent any accidents.
With that done, he left the town and returned to the seaside manor with the manager.
...
Meanwhile, after fierce inner struggle, Vice Admiral Deep Sea Hal Constantine finally made his decision and uttered the honorific left behind by that mysterious figure:
"The Unknown Land Connected by the Pure White Eye..."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 888: Calling in Favors
chapters.content:
Chapter 888: Calling in Favors
When "Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea" Hal Constantine recited the honorific name of the "Land of the Unknown," Ebner, who was resting in his bedroom, instantly received the relevant information from the "Pure White Eye."
Just the name, without using the secret technique I taught? Testing me?
Ebner quickly guessed what the other was thinking. After a moment of consideration, he simulated the Nightmare’s ability, forcibly pulling Hal into a dream, while commanding his avatar Owen to change into the appearance of the "Professor" and silently enter the dream.
On the other side, Hal, who had just finished reciting the honorific, felt a brief daze. But he quickly regained clarity and, based on past experiences, knew that he was now inside a dream.
—That "Segust" sea monster was also a master at creating dreams. Every time it issued a mission, it dragged him into a massive dream palace.
Glancing warily around, Hal realized that unlike previous lucid dreams, this time he was standing in his childhood town—the town where everyone bullied him and his mother, leaving only endless humiliation and hatred in his heart...
The very town he had sacrificed to the sea monster in exchange for the power of a "Favored of the Sea"!
"Why create this scene?" Hal guessed the existence who pulled him into the dream was nearby, and he asked with a touch of dissatisfaction.
Ebner strolled leisurely out of a house and answered with a smile, "This wasn’t created by me. It’s simply the place most deeply imprinted in your mind."
"Is that so?" Hal was silent for a few seconds, then said, "The being behind you was able to bypass the sea monster’s spiritual brand and invade my mind... Now I believe He truly can help me get rid of it."
If not for your prayer to the Land of the Unknown, I wouldn’t have been able to leverage its power to descend into your psyche at all...
Though this was his true thought, Ebner only gave a slight, inscrutable smile, wearing the look of
my Lord’s normal operation
.
Seeing that the other party wasn’t going to reveal much, Hal felt regret but also knew his counterpart was a seasoned player. He didn’t beat around the bush and asked directly, "That ’talisman’ and the secret technique you gave me—I’ve studied them.
"The secret technique is simple in structure. Its main effect seems to rely on the existence I pray to... But the talisman, with its complicated patterns, I couldn’t make sense of."
Because there is no meaning. That talisman is merely a ’key,’ just like the pendant Roselle left Miss Gwen that could be used for ’transformation.’ Stained with the aura of the Pure White Eye, it allows me to locate you and project power.
The essence of the secret technique I hastily created is still you using that card resembling the "Fortune Stealer" talisman, connecting to the Land of the Unknown through ritual and incantation. Then the Land of the Unknown relays to you the power I pried from Klein’s "Sefirah Castle" using the genuine Fortune Stealer talisman. With it, your "controlled" fate is temporarily shifted to someone else... or rather, shifted to Owen, making him the sea monster’s "favored" in your stead, and in its weakest moment, delivering a fatal strike.
As for whether Owen would also be controlled by the sea monster, I had my concerns. But since the Land of the Unknown’s power could so easily bypass the sea monster’s use of "primordial residue" to control minds and invade your psyche as Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea, it shows the Land’s authority far surpasses the sea monster’s dominion. And it’s far more domineering.
His thoughts turned rapidly, but Ebner didn’t explain any of this to Hal. He only replied flatly, "That talisman—or rather, card—is a token of my Lord.
"With it, the ritual succeeds.
"But the timing of activation is up to my Lord."
Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal Constantine had clearly anticipated this and nodded. "I’m willing to be this chess piece..." He paused, then asked, "Aside from this, what else must I pay?"
"I need all the intelligence you have on the sea monster and the ’Deep Sea Sacrament.’" Ebner smiled as he stated his request.
"That’s all?" Hal frowned in disbelief. "You don’t need me to do anything else?"
What could a Sequence 5 even do?
Ebner sneered inwardly, then said with a half-smile, "I’ve no intention of deceiving you. Once you’ve uttered His name, you’re under His gaze. You cannot betray Him."
"I know... But is it only the gaze?" Hal stared seriously at Ebner.
"Just the gaze. Even if there’s a task, my Lord won’t force anyone. ’All is voluntary, and all effort shall be rewarded’—that is my Lord’s creed." Ebner knew Hal feared falling from one swamp into another, so he casually spoke words of reassurance.
And indeed, this wasn’t a lie... for that was his own principle of conduct.
Hal studied him for a long while before finally nodding. "I believe you... And if it’s only like this, I can accept!"
In truth, so long as it wasn’t as domineering as the sea monster’s control, he could tolerate even something like the True Creator forcing believers to listen to its ravings.
And this "Unknown" was offering terms almost too good to be true.
In the past, he would never have believed so easily... But now, he had no choice.
With a sigh, Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea Hal Constantine organized his words and began to recount what he knew.
"The sacrament always starts on April 1st and ends before May 1st. During this time, the island is completely sealed. One can enter but not leave... At least ordinary demigods cannot leave.
"From the 1st to the 10th is when the sea monster accepts sacrifices. All offerings must be delivered before the 10th, or else the sea monster goes mad and destroys the island.
"There was once an incident when there weren’t enough sacrifices, and that forced the Delien family to change the ritual location.
"Normally, all the slaves, administrators, the pirates I brought, and the navy soldiers of the Delien family were sacrifices.
"But this time, the Delien family suddenly changed the overseer. And with certain changes in the details of the sea monster’s dream... I suspect the Deep Sea Sacrament will end entirely within one or two more iterations. By then, both I and that demigod named Owen may be the final sacrifices.
"Whether it’s this time or the next, I don’t dare gamble... That’s why I took the risk.
"I hope to break free of it completely—or even kill it!
"But even in madness, that sea monster still has powerful divination abilities. Your intervention may alert it.
"Though it won’t abandon the Deep Sea Sacrament, it will surely call for aid."
Hearing this, Ebner interjected, "What existences do you think it would call?"
"It doesn’t need to call. Once it feels unease, terrifying beings will descend...
"To my knowledge, at least one angel of the Rose School of Thought and one angel of the Nors family. As for demigods, they’re impossible to predict." Hal’s voice was heavy.
This level of power had once driven him to despair. But thinking of the backgrounds of the three aboard the Black Throne gave him a shred of confidence.
As long as both sides clashed, no matter who won, his plan was to flee as soon as he was free.
Ebner, however, sighed softly and thought:
All subordinates of the Mother Tree of Desire... That makes sense. Aside from the one hidden in the Tenebrous World, only She would care so much about matters of the Shadow World...
The fact that She indirectly controlled the Delien family’s cult faction to repeat the ritual was likely just to conceal Her true intent from the orthodox Churches. But now, at this critical step... She’ll surely mobilize both the Rose School and the Nors family in full!
With this in mind, Ebner ended the dream meeting with Vice Admiral of the Deep Sea, then had his true body slip out of the ritual zone before the island was fully sealed, going into hiding. Meanwhile, through Mr. Fool and his own demon wolf messenger, he began calling in favors.
...
On the Black Throne in the Sea of Mist.
Cullen looked at Mr. Azik emerging from the void. Unlike his earlier arrogance when lecturing Tran, he now said respectfully, "Ebner Bryan requests your aid. The price is a manuscript concerning the Death God."
The "Saintess of White" was still under Ebner’s control. Retrieving the manuscript that Trissy had handed to the Demoness Sect was no difficult matter.
Mr. Azik accepted the manuscript and letter Cullen handed over, remained silent for a few seconds, then nodded. "I will be there on time."
...
On Yes Island in the eastern Rorsted Archipelago, Klein blew his harmonica, summoning the messenger lady carrying four heads. He conveyed Ebner’s request to her.
"Ebner... request... I will... accept...
"But... need... ten thousand... gold coins..." The four heads answered one after another.
Without hesitation, Klein replied, "Ebner will pay for it!"
...
In the MI9 headquarters office, Princess Vera received a letter passed on by Xio. After pondering a while, she took out the Sealed Artifact capable of "spirit world travel" and teleported directly before Lady Yalolan.
...
In the basement of the Harvest Church, Lilith, who hosted the container of the Goddess of Beauty, smiled at an exquisite puppet. "I need to keep an eye on Seer, so I can’t go help him. You, as his angel, go in my stead.
"Don’t worry, it won’t delay your ’birth.’
"In fact, with all those gazes drawn elsewhere, your ’birth’ will even benefit."
The puppet nodded silently, then looked down at its broken finger and decided to "buy" a new one first.
...
In a luxurious house in a city of the Feysac Empire, a young man with a wicked smile was sipping tea.
Suddenly, an ordinary-looking old man appeared before him.
"Hermes, do you bring good news?" The young man didn’t seem surprised and asked directly.
The old man smiled. "Duke of Terror, your opportunity has come."
...
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 889: Beginning of the Great Battle
chapters.content:
Chapter 889: Beginning of the Great Battle
On a deserted island hundreds of nautical miles away from the festival islet, Closfia took the letter from Ebner handed over by the demon wolf messenger. After carefully reading it several times, she finally spoke to Madam Helen and to Lady "Greed" Ksenia not far away:
"He requests that we take action at dawn on April first, to block the ’Rose School’ and the ’Nors Family’ demigods from entering the island’s range..."
Pausing here, she turned to Lady "Greed" and added, "You should hide in the shadows as support... unless absolutely necessary, do not make a move."
"Greed" Ksenia nodded at these words without objection. After months of subtle "hypnosis," she now regarded Closfia as her closest person, even closer than her own sisters of the clan.
.....
At the same time, "Prophet" Taylors, disguised as a senior member of the Secret Order, and Princess Isabella, the former princess of Lenburg who was traveling aboard the "Golden Dream" in search of something, simultaneously felt their "Towers" being touched, and then received an oracle.
Immediately afterward, Taylors swiftly left his stronghold, flew dozens of miles to a small port, and intercepted the patriarch of one of the three great demon families preparing to set sail—the head of the Beliya family, the "Whisperer," succubus Yarubede Beliya.
"Beautiful lady, may I slow your steps and invite you to a romantic encounter?" Taylors smiled and extended his invitation.
According to the "prophecy" given by the deity, this head of the Beliya family, though subordinate to the Nors family, was not firmly loyal.
Yarubede studied Taylors with dazzling golden eyes, then nodded, apparently satisfied with his appearance. With a faintly enchanting smile, she said in a voice brimming with seduction, "That depends on whether you can please me."
She had never intended to risk her life for others; she had only joined in because she dared not defy the will of the Nors family in a matter she understood nothing about.
But now that someone was blocking her, she had an excuse. Naturally, she was happy to "fight" in another way.
Taylors also showed a sincere and charming smile, confident as he said, "I will certainly satisfy you."
.....
Meanwhile, Isabella ordered "Admiral of Iceberg" Edwina to suddenly change course. After about an hour of sailing, they just happened to block the path of a massive ship nearly two hundred meters long, its prow and stern curved high like a crescent moon, its sails painted with black tombstones.
That was the flagship of the "Undying King" Agalito—the "Death Announcer"!
At the moment when all the crew, including Edwina, were treating this as a great threat, the "Death Announcer" suddenly turned and sped away at unprecedented speed.
It ran, it ran away... The crew aboard the "Golden Dream" were briefly stunned.
Soon, the "Death Announcer" vanished from their sight.
Princess Isabella couldn’t help sighing, "As expected of a Beyonder of the ’Demon’ pathway. I had only just formed the thought, and he already noticed it."
"Agalito never fights true demigods..." Edwina murmured thoughtfully to herself, then turned to her teacher, a flash of curiosity in her pale-blue eyes. "Teacher, why did you block the ’Death Announcer’s’ course?"
"Merely to make him take a detour, so he’ll cross the ’Raging Sea’ one or two days later... As for the exact reason, I don’t know."
After all, one cannot casually guess at the will of the gods...
Isabella silently thought.
Seeing her teacher’s evasive look, Edwina more or less guessed the reason. After all, she too had once received an oracle.
Could this be related to Ebner again?
The thought flashed through her mind. Without hesitation, Edwina ordered the "Golden Dream" to sail at full speed, "biting" the "Death Announcer" and delaying it a few more days.
.....
At dawn on April first, the clone "Owen" stood on the manor’s top floor, gazing at the moonlit sea dyed with a dark crimson hue, quietly waiting.
Very soon, the calm sea began to surge violently. In less than a minute, huge waves battered the beach and harbor, and the water level rose rapidly.
Within five minutes, seawater had flooded the main buildings of the manor where Ebner was, and it continued to rise.
But at that moment, the sea suddenly receded, replaced by a sea monster larger than the manor’s main building appearing on the shoreline.
The creature was entirely blue, its body covered with black eyes, and in the void behind it faintly appeared shells containing strange "seaweed." It was exactly the same scene Ebner had seen in the "Dream Labyrinth Tower’s" fifth floor, within the elven trial temple.
Back then, Ebner had not known what those "seaweed" shells were. But thinking now, they were most likely its ascended "learning spaces." The so-called "seaweed" was actually stored knowledge!
"It seems my guess was correct. Before demigodhood, the ’learning space’ becomes, after Sequence 4 advancement, part of its incomplete mythical form...
"This sea monster revealing even part of its mythical form indeed shows its condition is poor!
"Fortunately, most of those shells remain phantasmal, showing only form without substance... Otherwise, anyone who saw them would die instantly or mutate.
"Even so, the low-Sequencers and ordinary people who see it will find their spirits and emotions unstable."
Thinking this, Ebner observed the navy soldiers outside the manor and the pirates farther away. As expected, they were becoming restless. Just a spark, and their emotions would explode.
The first group to "welcome" the sea monster on the beach should have been the island’s slaves... but since neither Ebner nor Harl wanted the festival completed smoothly, they naturally needed to first deal with the unstable factor of the soldiers and pirates...
Moreover, Ebner had already confirmed that each one of them deserved death!
Only such people could serve as sacrifices filled with the desire for "slaughter."
"Admiral of the Deep" didn’t fully understand what the new overseer of the Delien family was plotting, but he was content to comply.
As for the sea monster, it didn’t care whom it devoured first... so it wasn’t alarmed.
Seeing the sea monster in place and the ritual ready to begin, Ebner exchanged a look with "Admiral of the Deep" Harl Constantine outside the manor. Then he used his "Marionettist" ability to "infect" the restless minds of the sailors, making them instantly bloodshot and attack the pirates.
At the same time, "Admiral of the Deep" Harl fanned the conflicts he had stirred along the way, igniting the pirates’ impulsive tempers, and they charged ferociously at the navy.
As the two sides clashed and the first death—or rather, the first sacrifice—occurred, the islet suddenly seemed cut off from reality, shrouded by a layer of "shadow."
.....
In an undersea cavern outside the islet, Ebner’s true body activated the "Pure White Eye," carefully "analyzing" the shadow outside the island.
After a long while, he withdrew his gaze, frowned, and murmured silently:
"So the whole island has been pulled into a projection of the ’Tenebrous World’... separated from reality, yet not completely separated...
"In that case, entering only requires crossing the boundary of reality and shadow—it’s not difficult.
"But leaving will not be so easy!
"Unless one wields the corresponding authority, or possesses equivalent ’primordial quality,’ even an angel will find it hard to escape.
"It seems my clone won’t be able to leave until May first... After all, he lacks the ’Pure White Eye’...
"Still, this is good. Reinforcing angels and demigods won’t step in easily, so no one will know what happens inside...
"When the time comes, if everything is blamed on ’Admiral of the Deep,’ perhaps I won’t even need to discard Owen’s identity!"
Just as this thought arose, the "Pure White Eye" conveyed a message: "Admiral of the Deep" requested to use the "secret technique" that freed him from control.
After brief thought, Ebner granted permission, then took out the "Fate-theft Talisman" made from Amon’s "Worm of Time." He set up a ritual with it, praying to Mr. Fool for a temporary boost of its power.
On the gray fog, Klein had long been waiting. Upon seeing the ever-expanding "crimson star," he unhesitatingly used the "Error card" to pry open the power above the gray fog, granting it to Mr. Tower’s talisman.
.....
Within the island, just before being drawn into his "master’s" mind to preside over the Deep Sea Festival, "Admiral of the Deep" completed the secret technique taught by the mysterious man.
Then, an ethereal voice sounded in his ears, speaking in ancient Hermes:
"Fate!"
As the prolonged, difficult word echoed, "Admiral of the Deep" Harl suddenly felt unprecedented ease in his spirit.
No, not unprecedented—this was the feeling he had before sacrificing his hometown.
This was freedom! It truly succeeded! Praise the "Unknown"!
A tear fell from Harl Constantine’s eye, but he wiped it away quickly and ran inland without looking back.
First, he wanted to avoid the sea monster, lest its rage capture him again and drag him into the imminent battle...
Second, he wanted to protect Lady Dragonmight’s family! Although the mysterious man hadn’t asked this of him, this powerful outside aid was obtained through... in Emperor Roselle’s words, through "crashing into" the Black Throne trio...
No matter what ties existed between that being and the trio, it would surely be right to protect their family. And staying by their side might even be safer.
As Harl rushed inland, the clone Owen, whose fate had been "stolen" and placed upon himself, suddenly entered a phantasmal space.
Looking up, he found himself in a mythical city.
Without needing to sense, Ebner naturally knew the name of the city—"R’lyeh."
The corner of Ebner’s mouth twitched as he thought,
When the God of Luck stuffed that characteristic into this sea monster, did He also imbue it with strange knowledge?
Still, it was oddly fitting.
I recall "Admiral of the Deep" Harl mentioned this sea monster excelled at dreams... and "R’lyeh’s" other name is the "City of the Abyss," matching its role of once housing the imprint of the Tenebrous World...
Before Ebner could finish his thought, the scene abruptly changed. The city vanished, replaced by a small town.
Clearly, the sea monster had noticed its vassal being switched and was trying to trap him in its mental world, corrupting and reshaping him like "Admiral of the Deep."
But Ebner only looked around calmly, then shook his head and chuckled, "Heh, Innsmouth... You think you can trap me with such a scene?
"Hmph, if not for the ’Unknown Land’s’ protection, by now I would indeed have lost my mind, forgotten everything, and truly become your vassal here...
"But too bad... Tsk, I hold in my hands the ’Book of the Dead’ once wielded by a fellow transmigrator. Your characteristic is destined to be mine!"
.....
Just as the sea monster realized something was wrong in its spirit, within the battle between pirates and sailors, an officer’s aura suddenly changed. His body swelled, horns sprouted on his head, bat-like wings unfurled from his back, and he transformed into a towering four-meter-tall demon.
At the same time, anyone who looked upon him—pirates or sailors—found their desires uncontrollably swelling, until their entire bodies exploded.
He—no, it should be called He—after completing His descent across space, reached out to seize Owen in the manor and Harl fleeing into town.
No matter who had caused the crisis, as long as He regained control, the problem would be solved.
But before His move completed, black mist enveloped the area.
And then, that demon saw a woman in her twenties, with full lips, deep gray eyes, and striking beauty, wearing a distinctive armored gown.
"Tamara? Leticia Tamara? You still exist?!" The descended Demon-pathway angel’s voice was filled with disbelief.
The woman in the black mist gave a soft laugh, but her tone was cold. "Long time no see, Ayer Nors... You still look as disgusting as ever."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 890: Mutation
chapters.content:
Chapter 890: Mutation
Facing the mockery of the woman hidden in the black fog, the "Blood Grand Duke" known as Earl von Nois showed no fluctuation of emotion. As a cold, keen, and cunning "Devil," he was the very model of a high-intelligence being. How could he possibly be provoked by mere words? On the contrary, he sensed the other party’s bluff.
Thus, after narrowing his eyes, he smiled elegantly and said, "So, you are not at your peak. You should have only recovered to the level of Sequence 3! Let me guess what gives you confidence. Is it this black mist? It feels somewhat dangerous to me, probably a Grade 0 Sealed Artifact... With your current strength, how long can you control it?"
As a former "Devil," Earl von Nois instinctively tried to influence the opponent with words, gradually lowering Leticia’s ability to think clearly, making her careless and prone to mistakes...
But the woman within the fog merely watched his performance quietly, even making a sarcastic remark. "Do me a favor and remove your ’Devilization’ while trying to appear elegant. Otherwise, you’ll only seem more nauseating."
Seeing Leticia completely unaffected by his abilities, though he had half-expected it, the "Blood Grand Duke" Earl still found the situation troublesome. Surrounded by black fog, he had lost all sense of the outside world and had no idea what had become of that sea monster.
Thinking of the Mother Tree’s mission, his expression twisted into ferocity. He raised his hand and unleashed a "Blade of Terror" toward the woman hidden in the mist.
Since the "Heart Devil" had no effect, then he would let her experience the true power of the angelic "Body Devil"!
Yet the woman within the mist remained unflustered. Her fair palm thrust forward as she proclaimed in ancient Hermes, "Balance!"
The moment the word fell, she felt her physique, her recovery ability, and her sensory perception all rapidly rise, reaching parity with the "Blood Grand Duke" within seconds.
She then drew a longsword, struck aside the "Blade of Terror," and, smiling, charged at Earl von Nois. "Let me see if your swordsmanship has improved at all over these millennia!"
.....
Meanwhile, on the sea surface near the small island, a terrifying, dread-inducing figure suddenly emerged from the void.
Its mere presence made Ebner’s true body, hiding in a cave at the seabed, feel stabbing pain in his spirit. Only by reopening the "Pure White Eye" did he ease it somewhat.
Yet the fish, shells, and even sea plants around the cave were all infected by that aura, mutating into all manner of grotesque monsters...
It was the descent of the true body of the Rose School angel, "King of Curses" Barranca!
But just as his tumor-covered, organ-laden arms began to enter reality, an ethereal female voice echoed at the perfect moment. "Mystery reappears, source of peach blossoms!"
In an instant, a barrier cut off from the outside world and difficult to pierce blocked Barranca’s step into reality. The one who had released the fairy tale magic, Lady Yaloran, immediately dissolved her body into streams of knowledge, transforming into a pure creature of information flow. She lunged forward and pushed Barranca back into the spirit world.
— Curses had no effect on information.
.....
Dozens of miles away from the ritual island, above the sea, Reinette Tinekerr, in her intricate black dress and holding four heads, was fighting side by side with Mr. Azik, dressed in a black long coat with bronze skin. Together they blocked a revolting monster covered in pustules.
Hideous though it looked, that monster was the Sequence 2 "Life-Giver" of the "Moon" pathway. It continuously created nauseating creatures, intending to bog down Reinette and Azik while it rushed to the island where the Mother Tree’s mission was unfolding.
But its plan clearly failed. Though not in peak condition, the two angels were not foes that mere numbers could restrain.
One of the heads carried by Reinette Tinekerr opened its mouth in a silent scream. Instantly, the monster’s creations froze and then strangled themselves, twisting their own heads off.
Azik was even more at ease. While he kept his eyes locked on the "Life-Giver," towering skeletons kept emerging around him, each nearly four meters tall, their eye sockets burning with black flames. There were more than a hundred of them!
Without waiting for his command, the hundreds of pairs of black flame-lit eyes simultaneously fixed on the created monsters. The two sides immediately clashed.
Seeing its strategy fail, the "Life-Giver’s" scant rationality was drowned in fury. It was about to transform into its Mythical Creature form to crush the two detestable foes before it.
But at that very moment, the "Full Moon" that had accompanied it since its arrival suddenly vanished without a trace. Its strength plummeted, and worse, a new restriction emerged: without a full moon, it could not transform into its Mythical Creature form...
This shift in Authority clearly came from the apex of its pathway!
"Night! Lilith!" the monster roared, its voice filled with hate.
Both Reinette and Azik were experienced angels. At once, they noticed the enemy’s predicament and shifted from defense to offense, pressing the "Life-Giver" into disadvantage.
.....
While the angels fought, a massive melee broke out on the other side of the island.
Cullen and his mother, Lady Helen, joined forces with Closfia in her dragon form, together blocking the four demigods of the "Rose School," led by the "Silent One" Mahmosi and the "Shaman King" Klarman, preventing them from advancing closer to the island.
The three "Devils" of the Nois family were barely held back by Ebner’s "Magic Mirror," the temporarily teleported "Black Knight" Selo, and the external support of Klein’s "Sea God Scepter," but they would not be restrained for long...
Fortunately, the "Lady of Greed" still lurked in the shadows, ready to provide aid at any moment, which allowed Ebner some measure of relief.
Good thing the Nois family still has Andrelade as a nemesis. They can’t spare too many people right now... And the Rose School has extensive holdings in the Southern Continent. It’s impossible for them to truly send everyone here. Otherwise, I could only pray for the Goddess to descend...
Ebner sighed inwardly, holding off on acting personally for now.
Though he possessed a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact of the "Lawyer" pathway, "Tudor’s Mutated Emblem," it would be of little use in this demigod battlefield. It was better for him to remain in the cave and play a supporting role.
After all, while he retained a few means of harming demigods, he himself was fragile. Once the "Goddess of Beauty’s Blessing" was expended, he would not necessarily die—he still had one "Miracle"—but suffering grievous injuries was very likely.
Thinking this, and seeing the demigod battlefield locked in stalemate, Ebner shifted most of his attention to his avatar, hoping he could end the fight with the sea monster quickly and thus finish this war.
.....
Within the mental world of the sea monster "Segust," Ebner, relying on his rich experience, easily dismantled scene after scene, advancing from the outskirts of its mind-island toward the core.
The closer he came to the center, the more clearly he perceived the sea monster’s "corruption."
Indulging desires, toying with minds, cursing others, stirring malice... Tricks emerged endlessly, both to hinder and assimilate intruders and to mirror the state of its heart!
The erosion of the Tenebrous World... This sea monster is beyond saving... How can it still be called a "Reader"? When knowledge has become a tool for "desire" and "manipulation," the power it embodies has already been corrupted... You haven’t studied or taught new knowledge in a long time, have you? I see... you’ve already lost control long ago. Now you’re barely keeping sane by leaning on the mark of the Tenebrous World. No wonder you didn’t resist when the Delien family used you to contact the Tenebrous World... because that was exactly what you wanted! But it’s nothing but drinking poison to quench thirst...
As soon as his words fell, a furious scream echoed in his ears.
Perhaps his words had pierced the other’s heart, or perhaps he had already peeled away too many layers of its psychic defenses. In any case, the mythical city appeared before Ebner once more, with the palace in its center shrouded in shadow.
Without hesitation, Ebner made his Marionettist avatar assume the form of a dragon, unleashing a breath upon the palace.
Earlier, due to the sea monster’s special condition, Ebner had been cautious. Not understanding its mind well, and wary of giving the Tenebrous World an opening, he had painstakingly dismantled its protective scenes one by one.
But now that he faced the very core of its mental island, as a "Spectator" demigod, this was his battlefield. Even if the shadow appeared unusual, with "Uncharted Domain" backing him, Ebner was confident enough.
So, he chose the most direct method.
As a nearly invisible breath of transparency descended, the shadow that coiled around the palace immediately stirred in reaction. While resisting the breath, it extended back toward the dragon, trying to seize control of Ebner’s avatar’s mind.
But having dismantled the earlier layers, Ebner already understood this shadow’s essence. It was only a projection: faint traces from the sea monster’s brand, plus the sacrificial ritual’s shallow projection of the Tenebrous World itself, tenuously linking to its sealed body on the Western Continent.
Though high in nature, it was greatly constrained.
It might have been irresistible to ordinary Beyonders, but against Owen under the secret art’s control, it had found its nemesis.
This semi-finished secret art, refined by generations of transmigrators, essentially used the "Uncharted Domain’s" pollution, combined with Shepherd and Marionettist abilities, to latch onto the subject’s miraculous resurrection process. A patched-together experiment, yes, but it had worked well enough so far.
Its core was "pollution," pollution of the "Uncharted Domain"!
Even though this pollution had no root and could not truly connect to the Uncharted Domain, it still was not something that a sliver of Tenebrous World’s shadow power could easily taint.
Thus, a ring of golden light formed around the dragon, entwining with the shadows, both locked in a stalemate.
Ebner did not sit idly by. He swelled his maw once more, readying another breath for the palace.
His goal was clear: destroy the sea monster’s mind. Its death would strip the shadows of their host.
But just as he was about to exhale, a brown light suddenly shot from his body and plunged into the shadows wrestling with the gold.
Unprepared, the shadow swelled, and from its formless mass sprouted a brown branch!
The branch was quickly suppressed back into shadow, but almost immediately, a withered twig broke out from another side.
Again and again this happened, until finally the shadow violently expelled the brown light and fled the sea monster’s mind. But the brown light clung to it relentlessly in pursuit.
The sudden development left Ebner gaping, forgetting even to close his dragon jaws after exhaling his breath.
When he collected himself, his thoughts spun swiftly, and he understood what had transpired.
That brown light was the Sealed Artifact "Testimony of the Lost Mind" Owen used to control Katarina... It was actually the hidden move of the Mother Tree of Desire... and I never noticed! I’ve been tricked... The Mother Tree of Desire didn’t want to stop me from destroying the Deep Sea Festival ritual. It had already calculated everything, only waiting for my "Unknown" and the shadow to clash, so it could strike from the dark and pollute the Tenebrous World! The angels and demigods of the Rose School and the Nois family outside... they were bait. They were unwitting "actors." They were merely props to earn my trust!
(End of this Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 891: The Conclusion
chapters.content:
Chapter 891: The Conclusion
Taking a few deep breaths, Ebner gradually calmed down. He carefully reflected on everything he had seen and heard since getting involved in the "Sea Monster" incident and suddenly sensed that something was off.
Recalling his earlier speculation, he thought to himself with a touch of self-mockery:
Heh, when did I become so narcissistic?
Even if the Mother Tree of Desire disguised and deceived in this matter, it was to conceal things from the three gods behind me, not from me...
That "Proof of Lost Mind" necklace—I had examined it several times with the "Pure White Eye." Under its "analysis," the result was that everything appeared normal... Just like in Owen’s memory, it was in a "sealed" state, with only limited abilities available.
And the one who "sealed" it... although Owen did not know the name of that existence, without a doubt, it was Adam!
Did Adam and the Mother Tree of Desire join forces? So at the critical moment, the seal was lifted to deceive me, deceive the Evernight Goddess, deceive Lilith, and even deceive the God of Knowledge?
Well, Adam probably wouldn’t be that crazy... but Amon might...
Heh, it seems that while the space behind my "Pure White Eye" might have a high rank, its "analytical" ability also has limits... At least, it couldn’t pierce through the misdirection of the Mother Tree of Desire...
But that wasn’t strange. After all, in the original work, the Mother Tree of Desire could even interfere with Klein’s divination inside the Sefirah Castle!
In any case, being misled by the Mother Tree of Desire was beyond doubt...
Then, the next question... Did Lilith, the Evernight Goddess, and the God of Knowledge also get deceived?
Hmm, after I went to Intis and Lilith assigned me two tasks, she never used a "vessel" to meet me again... She only conveyed oracles through Bishop Utravsky...
I had thought this was normal before... but now, thinking back, it did feel a little strange... After all, she didn’t avoid meeting me in such a manner previously... Unless it was deliberately staged for someone to see...
If I make a bold guess, if the Mother Tree had been plotting since that time... does it mean Lilith deliberately avoided meeting me?
So that when I later obtained the "Proof of Lost Mind," I wouldn’t show it to her? Because if she failed to expose it, it would look fake, alerting the Mother Tree?
As for the Evernight Goddess and the God of Knowledge—I had too little contact to judge... but with their wisdom, it was hard to imagine they noticed nothing...
Hah... then, let’s suppose the three gods had already known about the Mother Tree’s plan, yet all pretended to be deceived, silently allowing me to carry the "Proof of Lost Mind" into the Sea Monster’s mind, letting the Mother Tree of Desire successfully infect the Tenebrous World...
What was their purpose in doing so?
Perhaps... the Tenebrous World was actually a trap? Or maybe they intended to use the Tenebrous World to tie down the Mother Tree of Desire’s attention, achieving another goal?
After all, there was still the barrier outside Earth, and the Tenebrous World was still sealed by the gray fog within the Western Continent. It was impossible for the Mother Tree of Desire to seize that primal source in a short time. At most, it would gain an advantage when the apocalypse arrived...
Perhaps there were other reasons as well... The thoughts of gods were truly unfathomable...
Sighing, although he had no evidence, Ebner was convinced that Lilith, the Evernight Goddess, and the God of Knowledge must be "in the know." After all, even if others didn’t understand, did he not know how much they valued him?
Even if it was just his avatar carrying an item tainted by the Mother Tree, could they really fail to notice? That would be a joke!
They must have had their own plans, which was why they pretended not to see through the Mother Tree’s deception.
While Ebner’s true body was hiding in the seabed cave outside the island, pondering all this, he did not forget to direct Owen’s avatar to launch a final assault on the mind of the Sea Monster "Segust," which had lost the protection of the Tenebrous World.
"Mind Deprivation," "Mental Plague," "Psychic Breath"...
Owen’s avatar, controlled by Ebner, wantonly ravaged the Sea Monster’s mind. Already weakened after losing the Tenebrous World’s power balance, it collapsed completely!
For ordinary people or Beyonders, a collapsed mind could easily lead to mutation into monsters... but this Sea Monster was already a "monster." Thus, like the Sea God Kalvetua, its soul quickly perished entirely amidst the collapse, and its body crumbled apart with a loud crash...
It had fallen!
Or rather, it had long been due to fall. For so many years, it had barely lingered on with the power of the Tenebrous World. Now that it lost its support, and with Ebner giving it one last push, it naturally could not escape its fate.
Ebner exited from its mental island and came to its massive corpse. While "collecting" useful materials, he waited for the trait’s extraction.
.....
Before the Sea Monster’s death, as the power of the Mother Tree of Desire pursued the fleeing "Shadow," the angels and demigods of the Rose School and the Nois family outside the island seemed to sense something. They were first stunned, revealing inner unease, then each used their means to flee the battlefield.
The three "Devils" who had been blocked by the "Magic Mirror" and Serro were the first to withdraw. They already held the upper hand, with the initiative in their grasp, and Devils excelled at survival. They vanished swiftly without a trace.
The four demigods of the Rose School fighting against Cullen, Helen, and Closfia were not as fortunate. Among them, the "Silent One" Mahmosi and two other "Puppets" could use "spirit world traversal," making pursuit difficult for Helen and the others... but the "Shaman King" Klarman was intercepted by Miss "Greed," who had been lying in ambush nearby for support.
This "Shaman King," who had been active in the Southern Continent since the early Fifth Epoch, had already suffered a great decline in state after Lilith reclaimed the "Goddess of Beauty" authority of the Primordial Moon.
After all, the reason Klarman had remained vigorous and active even at nearly 1,400 years old was thanks to the blessing of the Primordial Moon.
Normally, the natural lifespan limit of a vampire earl was only about 1,200 years.
Seeing himself surrounded by four demigods, Klarman, with his disheveled black-and-white hair, wore a grim expression. Suddenly, his right shoulder squirmed, something tearing his black robe as it emerged.
It was a finely crafted male doll, only palm-sized, dressed in a dark red suit embroidered with golden patterns. Its eyes had been gouged out, leaving only two black holes.
This doll sat upon Klarman’s shoulder, raising both hands. Its ten fingers pressed and tapped, as though playing an invisible instrument.
Miss "Greed," who had transformed into a dragon, immediately felt severe restraints. Her form shrank rapidly, forcing her to revert back into a human.
On the other side, Cullen also felt his clothes tighten suddenly, binding him tightly.
His bow tie even came alive, attempting to strangle him mid-air.
That doll was a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact given to Klarman by the Rose School, called the "Eyeless General." It was formed from the corpse of a Sequence 4 demigod of the "Aberration" pathway who had died unexpectedly.
It had the characteristic of being alive, capable of attaching to animate things or awakening inanimate objects in accordance with its owner’s will. However, its owner had to feed it with their own flesh and blood, or else it would gradually grow eyes.
And once this Sealed Artifact became whole, it would transform into a vengeful spirit that hunted down its original owner and hated all humans.
Seeing this, Helen had no choice but to "summon" a beam of light that enveloped her son, dispelling all shadows and evil. Although this harmed Cullen somewhat, as someone who had long possessed a Sealed Artifact of the "Sun" pathway, he was already accustomed to such injuries. Taking the chance, he transformed into moonlight and escaped the influence of the "Eyeless General."
Meanwhile, "Greed," with the help of "Sloth" Closfia, also dispelled the Sealed Artifact’s possession.
But by then, Klarman had already muttered an indistinct word with a cruel smile, stretching his hands forward, attempting to forcibly open a "Gate of Summoning"!
This was an ability only the Sequence 3 "High Summoner" of the "Moon" pathway could wield. Yet after defecting to the Mother Tree of Desire, Klarman had received her "reward," allowing him to pay a price to use this power beyond his level.
But his cruel smile froze instantly—for he had shamefully failed...
"How... how could this be?!" Klarman was shaken, unable to believe the Mother Tree of Desire had abandoned him.
